News.content:

MONSTER QUAKE Huge 7.7 magnitude earthquake strikes near Panama Canal as tsunami warning issued for Central & South America







Next

A MONSTER earthquake has struck near the Panama Canal as tsunami warnings have been issued for Central and South America.

The US Geological Survey recorded a magnitude of 7.7 with a depth of 10km, as tremors were reported along the southern coast of the Central American country.



The epicentre has been located at 120miles from Panama City and around 14km south-west of the remote community of Pitaloza Arriba.

Visibly shaken residents have been seen evacuating buildings and gathering on city streets following the quake.



Videos circulating online show construction workers backing away from an industrial site as the steel frame shakes and cranes move precariously.

Another shows people fleeing from a warehouse as its roof trembles.





The famous Panama Canal – an artifical 82km waterway – neighbours the capital.

The quake has triggered the US tsunami warning system, with hazardous waves possible along the coasts of Costa Rica, Ecuador, Peru, Nicaragua, Guatemala, El Savador and Mexico.

Chile has now also issued a tsunami warning.

Authorities have warned that Hawaii may be at risk too.

News.title: Woman on her way to work is held at gunpoint then dragged into alleyway & raped as registered sex offender found guilty
News.content:
HORROR ATTACK Woman on her way to work is held at gunpoint then dragged into alleyway & raped as registered sex offender found guilty







Next

A WOMAN was held at gunpoint then dragged into an alleyway and raped – with a registered sex offender found guilty of the vile attack.

The victim reported the assault to a bus driver at a stop in Catford, south-east London, who went on to alert cops at around 6.55am on April 12.

Melbourne Thompson, 41, of Eltham, was convicted of rape and robbery at the Old Bailey on October 9.

He was remanded in custody and will be sentenced at the same court on December 4.





The woman initially told the bus driver she had been the victim of a robbery.

She told officers that she had been on her way to work when the unknown man shouted at her to stop and started following her.

He then punched her in the head and threatened her with claims he had a gun.

As she attempted to cry for help, he covered her mouth and dragged her into a side alley off Minard Road, where he committed the assault.



After the horror attack, he then snatched her phone from her jacket pocket.

The woman was taken to a specialist Haven sexual assault referral centre where she continues to be supported by specialist officers.

Her stolen mobile was tracked down to an area around 30 minutes’ walk from where the incident took place – four minutes from Thompson’s home.

The vile sex offender was convicted in 2005 for the indecent assault on a woman two years beforehand – with the Catford attack matching his previous offending pattern.



He was identified in CCTV footage by a police officer who had previously monitored him after his 2005 conviction.

Thompson was arrested on April 28 and charged to appear at Bromley Magistrates’ Court on Wednesday, 29 April, when he was remanded in custody.

Cops are currently investigating whether he might be involved in any other incidents.

Detective Constable Charlie Lockett, who led the Metropolitan Police investigation, said: “I want to pay tribute to the victim-survivor for reporting this unimaginably distressing incident.

“My team and I are working tirelessly to tackle violence against women and girls through victim-led approaches that ensure survivors are supported by specialist officers throughout investigations.



“Thompson is a dangerous offender who targeted a lone woman as she walked to work early on a Sunday morning. I am pleased that the jury saw through his claim that he was not responsible for this appalling attack.

“The Met remains committed to investigating all reports of rape and serious sexual offences.

“Any victim-survivors who come forward will be treated with dignity, compassion and sensitivity at every step of the way.”

Cops are urging anyone with information about Thompson to contact police or submit reports anonymously via Crimestoppers.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Victims of sexual assault are advised to reach out to the 24/7 Rape & Sexual Abuse Support Line, which offers free phone and online chat for anyone aged over 16 in England and Wales.

News.title: Man, 38, charged with murder of woman, 46, after late-night ‘axe attack’ in seaside town as victim is pictured
News.content:
MURDER CHARGE Man, 38, charged with murder of woman, 46, after late-night ‘axe attack’ in seaside town as victim is pictured







Next

A MAN has been charged with the murder of a woman after an alleged late night axe-attack in a seaside town – as the victim is pictured.

Emergency services descended on a property in Dartmouth, Devon, at around 9.20pm on Tuesday where a woman in her 40s was found dead.



Devon and Cornwall Police say they have now charged a 38-year-old man with murder.

Luke Rigby, 38, is due to appear before Plymouth Magistrates’ Court on Saturday accused of the murder of Rebecca Grass, 46, known to her friends and family as Bex.



The shocking incident also saw a man, 46, raced to hospital with facial injuries as Rigby is also charged with assault occasioning grievous bodily harm.

He faces three further alleged offences – assault by beating, a racially aggravated public order offence and assault on an emergency worker.

Rigby currently remains in police custody.

Miss Grass’s family have been informed and are being supported by specially trained officers.



Her son, Reece Romeril, paid an emotional tribute to his mum in a heartbreaking post online.

He wrote: “As many of you have been informed, on Wednesday morning I had CID turn up to my work to inform me with some bad news.

“In Dartmouth, there was a murder of a 46-year-old woman on Tuesday evening… my own mother.

“How someone can brutally kill my mother in such a horrible way is absolutely terrifying to think about.

“Dealing with this is something I would have never expected in life, and times have been difficult lately for sure.



“My thoughts are with the ones who loved her and my family. We are taking this very seriously and working with detectives and the CID.”

Mr Romeril said a GoFundMe page has been set up to raise money for the “send-off the kindest of souls deserves”.

He ended his tribute with the words: “RIP MUM, I love you so much and miss you already”.

Police have not released details of a suspected weapon or a possible motive for the killing and are not currently seeking anyone else in connection with the death.

Locals said “someone with an axe” had attacked people, adding that they had never seen such a large police response in the quiet town.



One neighbour said previously: “It was mayhem last night. Paramedics and police doing a fab job and thoughts and prayers with the victims.

“I’m shocked. I have never heard of anything like this in Dartmouth. My thoughts are with anyone caught up in this.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Dartmouth is home to Britannia Royal Naval College, the Royal Navy’s initial officer training academy.

King Charles trained there, following in the footsteps of his father, Prince Philip.

News.title: Company director WINS bitter neighbour row to keep huge cutting-edge golf simulator built in garden without warning
News.content:
ON THE GREEN Company director WINS bitter neighbour row to keep huge cutting-edge golf simulator built in garden without warning







Next

A COMPANY director has won a bitter neighbour row to keep his huge cutting-edge golf simulator built in his garden without warning.

Pete Bransky, 51, spared no expense on the state-of-the-art timber building to play indoor golf at the bottom of his garden in Highcliffe, Dorset.



Mr Bransky, who runs a printing business, bought the house in the affluent Highcliffe area of Christchurch, about a decade ago.

The timber building takes up the entire width of the back garden, has acoustic sports panels fitted to the walls and ceiling and soundproof carpet tiles on the floor to reduce any noise.



He has also put in a rubber anti-shock and noise reduction framed base to reduce sound when he strikes the balls and installed a high-end quad layered pro golf simulator impact screen so the balls will not be hitting any walls.

But neighbours complained the huge shack was much bigger than permitted development allows, created a fire hazard as it was too close to their fences and damaged surrounding tree roots.

They also accused him of being dishonest after he wrongly stated on the plans the height of the cabin was 2.4m, just under the 2.5m allowed under permitted development.

One neighbour claimed they used a laser measuring device to show the overall height is 4m to include the central glass canopy or about 3m to the eaves.



Mr Bransky later revised the height of the 23ft wide and 13.5ft long building on the plans.

Despite this he has been granted planning permission to keep the golf cabin as the local council wanted to take a “positive and proactive approach focused on solutions” to the matter.

But angry neighbours have called the planning process “pointless” and said the local authority, BCP Council, had let Mr Branksy “do what he wants”.

One neighbour, who wanted to remain anonymous, said: “If Mr Bransky wants to whack away in his black plastic shed then that’s no one’s business but his.

“The problem is the honesty of the application and the credibility of BCP Council to govern it.



“It seems strange that you can put in at least three separate plans all with different measurements on a structure that already physically exists.

“It seems bizarre that you can put in a drawing with half of the false information removed and then get it passed when the historical anomalies are there in black and white.

“This is despite potentially damaging nearby protected trees and the parish council representative vehemently objecting based on size and overdevelopment.

“It is obviously very good news if you want to build anything you like, there’s not much point in the planning process as you can obviously make it up as you go along.”

Mr Bransky, who is a member of Brockenhurst Manor Golf Club in the New Forest, said he had not complained about work his neighbours had done to their homes and said they should live and let live.



He said: “The next door neighbour is complaining about loss of light, but he put a six metre extension on the back of his house that blocks my light and I didn’t complain about that.

“And the guy behind took out a load of trees and put in an outbuilding at the end of his garden and I didn’t complain about that.

“Lots of people have got garden buildings, yes this is slightly bigger than some but it needs to be to have the space to swing the clubs.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“It doesn’t affect anyone, I think we need to just let people have what they want. It’s all properly insulated and we’re not out there all the time.”

In approving his plans, BCP Council advised Mr Bransky to have a reputable tree surgeon check the health and stability of the trees that might be affected by the building within the next two years.

News.title: How neo-Nazi ‘cult’ leader forced Brit girls into twisted sex acts for online paedos with chilling ‘manipulation manual’
News.content:
EVIL ACTS How neo-Nazi ‘cult’ leader forced Brit girls into twisted sex acts for online paedos with chilling ‘manipulation manual’







Next

EVEN by the horrifying standards of violent sex attacks on schoolgirls, the crimes are gut-wrenchingly grotesque.

Youngsters as young as 12 from countries including Britain and America were forced to strip naked, perform depraved sex acts and self-harm in front of leering neo-Nazi paedophiles watching online.



The ringleader of the abuse was a self-styled “sadistic psychopath” Adolf Hitler fan who lured victims into a web of evil by posing as a 14-year-old boy with a pixilated face.

Rohan Rane, who is in fact an Indian aged 28, this week went on trial at the Paris Special Assizes – a highly secure court in France’s capital.



During a committal hearing in March at the Paris Criminal Court he admitted, “I am guilty, I take full responsibility”.

Saying that he was “devoid of all emotion”, he added: “I am sorry for what I did”.

Despite this, and in line with French criminal law, he is entitled to a full trial, while facing charges including “torture and acts of barbarism”, “inciting a minor to submit to sexual mutilation”, and “possessing and distributing child pornography”.

If convicted, Rane could spend the rest of his life in an isolated cell with sex offenders and others who are vulnerable to attack by other inmates.

The X-rate evidence against him is so graphic that judges ordered the Paris trial – at which Rane is the only defendant – to be held behind closed doors.

But The Sun has seen prosecuting documents outlining the case, while sources involved in a three-year investigation have also provided full details of the allegations against Rane, and his group, which was dubbed CVLT, and pronounced Cult.



Rane moved to the south of France from Mumbai, India, on a student visa in 2019, and enrolled at a business college in the seaside town of Antibes, near Nice.

An investigating source said: “He appeared to be a hard-working young man who wanted to become an entrepreneur.

“He made money as a part-time fitness coach, but otherwise appeared to be concentrating on his studies.



“Other students in his hall of residence complained about his personal hygiene – he could be very smelly – but otherwise he didn’t seem to be annoying anyone.”

In fact, Rane was leading a double-life exploiting children online through an American social media platform that has more than 200million users.

It offers access to a range of services including free messaging, video calls, and chat rooms accessed by invitation links.

Rane is first said to have set up CVLT alongside a number of Americans, including Kaleb Merritt, a 26-year-old from Texas who used the online nickname “eTerror”.

In March Merritt, a convicted rapist, confessed to producing child sexual abuse material, including images of self-harm for around 50 members who also called their CVLT circle “764”.



Following a trial in Los Angeles, and an earlier one in Virginia, Merritt is currently serving a 33-year prison sentence in the USA.

John A. Eisenberg, America’s assistant attorney general for national security, said: “This guilty plea exposes the depravity of CVLT, a criminal enterprise that systematically targeted vulnerable children, coerced them into producing abuse material, and threatened to destroy their lives if they resisted.

“Merritt was one of the online administrators who made CVLT’s monstrous machinery of child exploitation run.”



It was thanks to technical work by groups such as the FBI (Federal Bureau of Investigation) in the States, that members of CVLT were tracked down.

French law and order officials considered Rane to be every bit as dangerous as Merritt, and have kept him on remand since his original arrest in 2021.

Another investigating source in Paris said: “The crimes that Rane is accused of are absolutely sickening.

“He expressed hatred of feminists, Jews, Muslims and black people, and considered the most vulnerable members of such groups to be easy targets.

“His strategy was to pose online as a friend, so as to win their confidence, and to get the girls to strip.



“He then said he would report their nude photos and videos to the authorities if they did not carry out a number of tasks”.

These included getting children to abuse themselves with knives and cactus plants.

Some teenagers were told to use a razor to carve Rane’s name on their skin, alongside a Swastika, and the CVLT community number, 764.

Up to 60 harrowing videos were due to be shown in court, and – according to a judge’s instruction – they contained “precise and cruel instructions for carrying out acts,” including “penetration with a blade.”



Images created and stored by Rane also show girls being forced to drink their own urine, and plunging their heads into toilet bowls.

Another court document reads: “The aim was absolute pain and humiliation – male members of CVLT would try and outdo each other with new ideas about how to torture girls.”

All of Rane’s offences between 2019 and 2021 are said to have been carried out from his bedroom on his college campus in Antibes.

He created multiple extortion videos, it is claimed, while controlling membership and access to the group using the nickname “Warlord”.



Even after his imprisonment in 2021, Rane continued to target minors from his prison cell, calling his victims “Slave children”.

Using illegally obtained burner phones, he would view videos of teenage girls self-harming, while logging onto Discord to lure minors into joining his “cult”.

The self-styled neo-Nazi scrawled messages on his cell walls glorifying Adolf Hitler and the far-right Norwegian terrorist Anders Breivik, who murdered 77 people and wounded 323 others in 2011.

Rane even wrote a “manipulation manual” outlining his online behaviour, and called it “How to Get a Girl”.

Admitting to testing his methods on at least 200 youngsters, he wrote: “Be a tyrant. Spot a vulnerability in the girl’s life. It could be anything—from daddy issues to body image struggles.”



During another earlier hearing, a 15-year-old told how CVLT members ordered her to cut off her hair and abuse herself with it.

She said Rane “held power over me”, and would send explicit images of her to her own aunt.

During the Paris trial, such videos were shown on screens inside the court.

Rane himself told investigating magistrates that all “western feminists have a rape fantasy”, and admitted he hated “black, Muslim, Arab, and Jewish women, as well as neo-feminists”.

In his recorded confessions, he said he got particular pleasure in tormenting a 12-year-old girl linked to a gay Black Lives Matter community, because of her race, branding her with a vile racist word.



He also said he liked to imagine a Jewish victim carving images of Israeli coins, Shekels, “into her own skin.”

Up to 12 victims – who cannot be named for legal reasons – were also giving evidence via video link, appearing from overseas, including the USA.

At least one was also expected to be in the Paris court, so enabling her to confront Rane for the first time, after only seeing his blurred face online.

Hippolyte Marquetty, a barrister representing five of the victims, said: “This trial will raise staggering questions.

“We need to understand how a teenage girl—sitting in her room, isolated perhaps, but in her own home thousands of kilo-meters away from the ringleaders of these fringe groups — can fall under such psychological control and stress that she is driven to commit acts of severe self-harm or contemplate taking her own life.”



Mr Marquetty added: “That was back in 2021, now we have AI [Artificial Intelligence]. It is crucial to raise awareness and educate both parents and teenagers about this.”

It is also hoped that the trial will shed light on the online spread of poisonous ideas, particularly those related to white supremacism and the hatred of women.

Despite being dark-skinned, and from a well-educated family in Mumbai, Rane was allied with American racists in the so-called Nihilistic Violent Extremism, or NVE, movement.

Since details of the Rane case were made public, complaints about cyberbullying and “sextortion” have multiplied in France, according to the county’s National Police.

A spokesman said a 21-year-old man was arrested in a Normandy town in August 2025 and, during a search of his home, detectives found thousands of child sexual abuse images.



They included pictures and videos of youngsters carving the suspect’s name into their skin, alongside the number 764.

Lawyers for Rane told the court that he suffered domestic abuse and bullying when he was at school, and this contributed to his conduct as an adult. They have declined to comment publicly.

Rane is the only person in France to have been charged in connection with the CVLT network so far, but more prosecutions are expected in the months ahead.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A judicial source in Paris said: “We are dealing with the activities of a large online community of male abusers.”

The Paris Assizes Special Court will hear evidence in the Rane case until today, before a verdict is handed down.

News.title: People smuggler, 38, who used ‘luxury’ yacht to charge migrants £13k to sneak into the UK is deported after being jailed
News.content:
COSTLY CROSSING People smuggler, 38, who used ‘luxury’ yacht to charge migrants £13k to sneak into the UK is deported after being jailed







Next

A PEOPLE smuggler who used a yacht to provide a premium service for migrants sneaking into the UK has been deported.

Vladyslav Cherniavskyi, 38, made at least eight crossings from northern France with his accomplice Oleksandr ­Yavtushenko, 43.



The Sun can reveal he was removed from the UK in September after serving part of a six-year prison sentence for three counts of assisting unlawful immigration.

Their scheme was uncovered after their yacht, Uforia, was intercepted four miles off the coast at Chichester, West Sussex, in July.



On board were five Albanian men and a young Vietnamese girl.

They were believed to have paid £13,000 each for the trip to the small harbour of Itchenor.

Prosecutor Robin Leach told Portsmouth crown court: “Both defendants ferried migrants across the English Channel from northern France to the English coast, in particular to Itchenor in Chichester Harbour and they ferried the migrants across the Channel in a yacht called Uforia.

“It was established some of the migrants paid up to 15,000 euros – this was a premium bespoke service and any one trip would involve three to six migrants being taken across the Channel.”



Since the election, over 80,000 immigration offenders and individuals illegally in the UK have been returned, an increase of 52 per cent on the previous two years, with levels of removals at their highest since 2016.

Nearly 12,000 of these were foreign criminals, an increase of 41 per cent.

Minister of State for Border Security and Asylum, Anna Turley, said: “This vile criminal played a key role in a people-smuggling operation that sought to undermine the integrity of our border, profit from illegal migration, and endangered the lives of vulnerable people.

“His deportation sends a clear message: foreign criminals who break our laws will be removed.

“We will continue to work across government and with international partners to remove these bad actors.”



Julian Harriman, NCA senior investigating officer, said at the time of their conviction: “These men ran what can only be described as a kind of ferry service, moving small numbers of people over the Channel each time, but charging them a premium price for the service.

“They stood to make tens of thousands of pounds for each trip but we were able to work with our French partners to stop this enterprise in its tracks

“Targeting people smugglers like this remains a priority for the NCA, and we’re doing all we can to disrupt and dismantle the gangs involved, wherever they operate.”

News.title: Mum & grandma charged after boy, 5, found naked in street after escaping ‘room barricaded with wooden boards & zip ties’
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

‘ABUSE’ HELL Mum & grandma charged after boy, 5, found naked in street after escaping ‘room barricaded with wooden boards & zip ties’







Next

A MUM and grandmother accused of locking a boy in a room allegedly barricaded with wooden boards and zip ties have been charged.

The five-year-old was found naked wandering the streets after escaping the real-life “house of horrors”, leading to the arrest of the two family members.



The alleged victim’s mother Jade Shuey, 21, her boyfriend Tucker Heagy, also 21, and grandmother Stephan Schaffner, 42, all were charged.

Investigators claim the youngster was trapped inside a dirty bedroom against his will at a property in Township near Philadelphia.



The room’s doorway was blocked with a baby gate held together with zip ties and duct tape, topped with wooden boards drilled into the frame to prevent escape, police allege.

Food and rubbish were allegedly strewn across the floor, with the walls and window stained with what appeared to be human faeces.



The remainder of the house appeared in “hoarder conditions”, according to Pennsylvania State Police.

Cops noted “trash throughout”, “hundreds of flies” and “limited room for manoeuvring the house” due to the “clutter”.

Lebanon County district attorney Pier Hess Graf said the child “lived in hell” behind caged bars.

“Every second of every minute of every day, that child deserved a better life and maternal love,” he added.



The list of alleged offences includes child endangerment, aggravated assault against a child under 13, unlawful restraint of a minor and conspiracy to endanger a child.

Shuey also faces a new charge of conspiracy to obstruct a child abuse investigation.

The victim’s grandmother Stephan Schaffner, 42, also faces the new charge, plus a previous allegation of endangering the welfare of a child.



Two additional suspects with an unknown relationship to the household have also been detained.

Scott Schaffner, 59, and Cathy Schaffner, 62, voluntarily surrendered themselves to authorities on September 29, according to reports.

The pair were charged with criminal conspiracy to commit child endangerment and criminal conspiracy to commit obstruction in a child abuse case.

They were both released on bail, with a preliminary hearing scheduled for October 22.

The other three defendants will face a jury trial on November 16.

News.title: Putin ‘stuck on plane’ over Moscow as Ukraine blitz on Russian capital traps tyrant & war chiefs
News.content:
STRANDED VLAD Putin ‘stuck on plane’ over Moscow as Ukraine blitz on Russian capital traps tyrant & war chiefs







Next

VLADIMIR Putin and his war chiefs have reportedly been left stranded in the sky after Ukraine blitzed Moscow.

The Russian tyrant was left red-faced after being unable to touch down in his beloved capital following a trip to Turkmenistan, according to Flightradar data.



Ukranian drones and “small balloons” massively disrupted airspace over Moscow in scenes of chaos.

Flight tracking data shows the tyrant’s fleet haplessly circling after much of the city’s skyline was on lockdown before at least three approached to land.



One government plane is believed to have flown to St Petersburg.

Other civilian planes were diverted and at one point all four major Moscow airports—Vnukovo, Sheremetyevo, Domodedovo and Zhukovsky—were closed.

Putin was expected to return to Vnukovo airport from a summit of former Soviet leaders in Turkmenistan, where he also attended talks on the Caspian Sea’s environmental crisis.

As his fleet of planes approached, Moscow mayor Sergei Sobyanin reported 15 drones had been shot down as the war came to the Russian capital.



Transponders of the four Special Flight Detachment aircraft were regularly turned off and on, as the “Flying Kremlin” fleet zig-zagged around Moscow amid the alert.

One of the planes – the aircraft Putin had used on the outward journey to the summit in Caspian Sea port Turkmenbashi – is believed to have instead eventually landed in St Petersburg rather than Moscow.

It is not known if Putin, 74, was on this aircraft for the return journey.

The other planes in the Putin entourage landed safely in Moscow, reports say.

No other civilian aircraft were in the sky over the Russian capital during the dramatic approach.



Moscow airspace was hit with a vengeance today, with at least 370 flights delayed and some 62 cancellations amid major disruption.

Crowds were crammed into the terminals in the city’s airports.

It follows intense drone swarms over the city and sightings of mysterious balloons.

Authorities in the Yaroslavl region reported the destruction of small reconnaissance balloons launched from Ukrainian territory.

It comes after a Russian war chief has warned the Kremlin plans to “drown Kyiv in sewage” by hitting power plants and striking water facilities.



Not satisfied with killing almost 80 civilians in two days, Putin is now scheming to make the Ukrainian capital completely unlivable.

Kyiv was one of 30 Ukrainian cities that was hammered in overnight drone strikes.

The barrage of attacks led to the metro shutting down in parts of Kyiv.

A guided aerial bomb killed one in Zaporizhzhia and another struck one dead in Ivano-Frankivsk.

In the last two days, Putin’s brutal war machine has killed at least 78 people and wounded 215.



The bombing of two packed passenger buses and a block of flats has been slammed as a “war crime” after the vehicles were engulfed in flames.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Horrific images showed the depravity of the strikes as the burnt out wreckages of the buses were seen on the streets.

Bodies could be seen strewn across the street surrounded by debris.

News.title: Polanski vows to stay on as Green leader as he faces criticism after by-election defeat
News.content:
Zack Polanski has vowed to stay on as Green Party leader after his by-election defeat, as he faced pressure from within his own party to resign.

The leader of the Jewish Greens, Vivien Lichtenstein, said on Friday he should resign, adding it was a "big mistake" for him to have dodged a debate about a party conference motion that declared Zionism a form of racism.

Lichtenstein's comments come after two former Green leaders accused Polanski of failing to show leadership over the Zionism row.

Polanski, who came second to Labour overnight in the Holborn and St Pancras by-election, told BBC Breakfast he would "absolutely" stay on as leader and "of course" had not questioned that.

The Greens had hoped to take the seat, previously held by former Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer, after a by-election success earlier this year.

Polanski lost out in Thursday's contest in London to Labour candidate Sagal Abdi-Wali, who secured 45% of the vote to his 33% - but the Green vote share was up by 22 percentage points on the 2024 general election.

In her comments calling on Polanski to resign, Lichtenstein told Times Radio: "I don't know which Jewish members of the party he's been working with â it certainly hasn't been with the Jewish Greens committee."

Her criticisms were similar to those of former Green Party leader Caroline Lucas who said Polanski should have attended the vote on the conference motion on Sunday.

The motion, which was passed by rank-and-file members to become official party policy, defined Zionism as an ideology supporting "an ethnonationalist Jewish state" and backed a "single democratic Palestinian state in all of historic Palestine", which includes modern-day Israel.

Adrian Ramsay, a Green MP and former co-leader, declined to back Polanski when asked on the BBC's Politics East on Friday.

"A lot depends on what happens in the days and weeks to come," he replied when asked if Polanski should still lead the party.

"[He] did not show leadership I would have been looking for," said Ramsay, who said he was now working to reverse the motion.

News.title: King pays Andrew's £1.5m repair bill on Royal Lodge
News.content:
Mountbatten-Windsor left his Royal Lodge home in February, in the middle of a storm of revelations about his connections to the US sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

He has consistently denied any wrongdoing in relation to Epstein.

The former Prince Andrew was moved to Sandringham, with his brother the King using his own money to provide his upkeep and accommodation.

Mountbatten-Windsor was arrested later that month on suspicion of misconduct in public office - and a court ruling on Thursday found fault with the search warrants used by the police.

But despite moving to Sandringham, Mountbatten-Windsor's lease on Royal Lodge had remained until October - and as that officially ends, the Crown Estate is revealing the terms on which it concluded.

When Andrew had taken on the 75 year lease in 2003, he had made considerable up-front payments, including about Â£7.5m for repairs, which meant that he did not have to pay a monthly rent.

It also meant that if he gave up the lease within the first 25 years he would be legally entitled to some compensation - with that amount reducing each year.

Leaving in October 2026 would have meant that the Crown Estate would have had to pay him back about Â£302,000.

However that amount has been overshadowed by what he owes to the landlord for the state of the building - and so the Crown Estate says it has now received a net amount of Â£1.5m.

It's understood that the payment of that money by the King is to avoid leaving the Crown Estate out of pocket.

Whether Mountbatten-Windsor will repay his brother is said to be a private matter - and there are no further details of what this might say about Andrew's personal finances.

There was also no comment on how the King feels about this arrangement - and there is said to be no connection between this payment and the King making clear this week that his financial support should not go to cover Andrew's legal costs in his battle over search warrants.

It has so far not been decided how the 30-room mansion in Windsor will be used in future, but it is expected to be used to deliver a commercial return - and at present there are no plans for another royal occupant.

"The lease for Royal Lodge has ended and our focus now is firmly on its future use and the opportunities to generate additional financial value for the nation from its early return," said a Crown Estate spokesperson.

A report by the National Audit Office had revealed earlier this year that Mountbatten-Windsor had been sub-letting buildings at Royal Lodge, although the amount was never revealed.

That report from the public spending watchdog also showed that Andrew's daughters, Princess Beatrice and Eugenie, had accommodation inside royal palaces which they did not pay for, with the cost being covered privately by the King.

News.title: JD Vance casts doubt on firing squad execution and says he will not watch it
News.content:
The Pentagon announced earlier this week it would execute Hasan by firing squad, the first of its kind since the end of World War Two. Then on Thursday US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth said the execution would be livestreamed for the public.

"People need to understand that there's serious consequences for these types of things," said Hegseth.

The BBC has asked the White House whether Trump supported the plans.

Speaking to reporters on Friday, Vance said: "I see these announcements. I don't know that that's actually going to happen."

The vice-president said that Hasan was meant to treat soldiers for mental illness and other problems and "took them at their most vulnerable and gunned down these people where they lived".

The announcement over the livestream plans has been met with criticism from both political parties.

Republican Senator John Curtis pointed to Rome's history of a "bloody spectacle" corrupting people who watched them, warning that public executions erode civilisations "when it cultivates an appetite for executions as a form of entertainment".

Curtis said that Hegseth's plan "risks feeding that appetite" and urged him to reconsider.

"The victims deserve justice administered with solemnity. Broadcasting a death diminishes us and is not an effective deterrent," he said.

Democratic Senator Chris Murphy told CNN that the idea was "disgusting" and reminiscent of executions carried out by the Islamic State group.

The US Conference of Catholic Bishops condemned the decision to publicly livestream Hasan's execution, expressing "shock and great sorrow" in a statement.

The UN human rights office told AFP that livestreaming it would be "tantamount to a public execution and would breach the absolute prohibition of torture".

News.title: Widdecombe suspect had 'particular hostility to Reform', court told
News.content:
The man accused of murdering Ann Widdecombe had a "particular hostility to Reform", prosecutors alleged on Friday.

They said Joshua Kerry, 28, "had an extreme left wing and/or anti-establishment mindset".

The prosecution also told the Old Bailey Widdecombe's murder had a "terrorist connection" as it was "politically and ideologically motivated".

Last week, Kerry, who had already been charged with Widdecombe's murder in July, was charged with a second offence of preparing terrorist acts.

He is accused of "online reconnaissance" of prominent people and institutions, travelling to Nigel Farage's home in South London on 19 April 2025, and trying to break into it 15 months before Widdecombe was killed.

Mrs Justice Cheema-Grubb agreed to the prosecution request to join the two charges into one case.

The prosecution argued they were "inextricably linked".

Kerry appeared in court by video link from Belmarsh prison wearing a prison-issue grey sweatshirt.

The judge set a date for a five-week trial on 8 June next year.

The next hearing will be on 29 January.

Nicholas Lumley KC, defending, told the court that Kerry was likely to contest all the charges against him.

Kerry was charged in July with the murder of 78-year-old Widdecombe, a former Conservative minister and Reform spokeswoman.

Widdecombe was found dead on 9 July at her home in Haytor, Devon, having sustained serious injuries.

The former Tory MP was hit on the head with a hammer 21 times at her home as she ate lunch, prosecutors said during a hearing at Westminster Magistrates' Court in July.

She served as Conservative MP for Maidstone and the Weald in Kent for 23 years and was appointed to ministerial roles in Sir John Major's government in the 1990s.

She became a member of Reform in 2019.

Following her departure from the Commons, Widdecombe appeared on the BBC's Strictly Come Dancing in 2010 and was a runner-up on Celebrity Big Brother eight years later.

News.title: Lib Dem MP quits frontbench job over Ed Davey's leadership
News.content:
Liberal Democrat MP Charlie Maynard has resigned from the party's frontbench and wants to see Sir Ed Davey replaced as leader.

As first reported by the Financial Times, external, the Witney MP left his role as Treasury spokesman on Friday.

Those close to Sir Ed privately acknowledge that there is what they see as a "small group" of Liberal Democrat MPs who are not happy with his leadership, of which Maynard is one.

Daisy Cooper, the deputy leader of the party, said: "The vast majority of our MPs support Ed, want him to lead the party into the next election, and are furious at this distraction." The BBC has approached Maynard for comment.

Lib Dem MP and former leader Tim Farron also defended Sir Ed, saying under his leadership the party was in a position to match or even beat the "record numbers of MPs" the party won at the last election.

"To think we're helped by this kind of rubbish, you'd need to be smoking the kind of stuff even we aren't in favour of legalising," he quipped.

Several other Lib Dem MPs, including some frontbenchers, also gave Davey their backing in social media posts on Friday evening.

Julian Brazil, a Liberal Democrat council leader who has previously been critical of Sir Ed, said Maynard had "put his head above the parapet - we'll see if other people follow".

Speaking to BBC Radio 5Live's Matt Chorley, he said: "I would have thought that in the next few days, we will see if there's a groundswell behind him."

Brazil added that Sir Ed had been a "fantastic leader" but added: "For whatever reasons people aren't listening to Ed, they don't take notice of him, so we need to have a fresh start and be able to articulate what our vision of the country is.

"I think that's best done by someone else."

Maynard was first elected to his Oxfordshire constituency in 2024, winning the traditionally Conservative seat, formerly held by David Cameron, with a majority of more than 4,000.

Before becoming an MP, he ran an international mergers and acquisitions advisory firm.

He is the second Lib Dem to leave the frontbench this week, following Alison Bennett's decision to resign her post of spokesperson for care and carers.

Bennett would not confirmed why she stepped down but it is understood it was not for personal reasons.

Under Liberal Democrat rules, a leadership contest can be triggered if a vote of no confidence in the leader is passed by the majority of all the party's MPs.

To enter a leadership contest, a Lib Dem MP must have nominations from at least 10% of the parliamentary party, not including the candidate themselves, and have the backing of 200 members across at least 20 local parties.

Sir Ed has been leader for six years and in the 2024 general election led the party to its biggest election success, winning 72 seats.

However, the party has found it difficult to build on that success, with polling numbers remaining at relatively low levels.

More recently, some Liberal Democrats have publicly attacked the leader for his stance on the triple lock - the mechanism which guarantees the state pension goes up each year in line with either inflation, wage increases, or 2.5% whichever is highest.

Last week, Sir Ed criticised Andy Burnham's announcement that he would adjust the triple lock, arguing it would "put more pensioners into poverty".

"This would mean people who are working hard now - the millennials - when they retire would have a very poor pension," he said.

One Lib Dem MP described Sir Ed's argument as "nonsense", while another said: "Most millennials don't think there will be a state pension when they retire so this isn't being done with them in mind."

News.title: Commentator Katie Zacharia offered job of new White House press secretary
News.content:
Conservative commentator Katie Zacharia has been offered the job of White House press secretary, a White House official confirmed to the BBC.

Zacharia, who currently works as a communication's adviser for Trump Media & Technology Group would become the president's sixth chief spokesperson across his two administrations. She previously had a brief stint as a spokesperson at the Department of Homeland Security.

Former White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt, who left the White House in August, has reportedly taken a job with Fox News.

The BBC has contacted Zacharia for comment.

News.title: Watch: Who is Nobel Peace Prize winner Navi Pillay?
News.content:
Navi Pillay, a former International Criminal Court judge and United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights, has won the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize.

In a statement announcing the award, the Nobel Committee praised Pillay's "efforts to promote peace and international law".

BBC correspondent Joe Inwood explains how Pillay's childhood in South Africa led her to become a driving force in international law and human rights, from Rwanda to Gaza.

Read more about this story.

News.title: Bank cashier outed by holiday photos after stealing £13k is ordered to pay back money
News.content:
A building society cashier who stole thousands of pounds from customers to pay for "lavish" holidays has been ordered to repay more than Â£12,000.

Kelly Kershaw, 54, stole Â£13,333 including from vulnerable and elderly customers at Nationwide in Caernarfon, Gwynedd, even forging the signature of a man with learning disabilities.

Kershaw admitted five counts of fraud after colleagues spotted Facebook posts of her on safari in Africa, and on trips to Paris, Tuscany and Dubai.

She was jailed for 16 months in May but returned to Caernarfon Crown Court for a Proceeds of Crime Act, external hearing, and told to pay back Â£12,630.

Judge Jones ordered Kershaw to repay the sum within three months or face a further five months in prison.

The mother-of-two posted pictures of skiing trips, safaris and romantic European getaways on her Facebook page and boasted she was "living and loving life one adventure at a time."

Kershaw's victims included an 85-year-old man who had lost some "cognitive abilities" after suffering a stroke - and she stole Â£6,300 from him.

On one occasion, he came to the branch asking to withdraw Â£200, but Kershaw logged the withdrawal as Â£500 and pocketed Â£300 herself.

Another victim was a 49-year-old man with learning difficulties who lost Â£1,400 to Kershaw - he had his bank card kept in the branch as he was a previous victim of fraud.

News.title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England
News.content:
A second head teachers' union has called for a halt to graded Ofsted inspections in England, saying it is "increasingly concerned about the welfare and morale" of its members.

The Association of School and College Leaders (ASCL) also raised the prospect of potential strike action, saying a new grading system had become an "overbearing mess".

On Friday, Ofsted's chief inspector Sir Martyn Oliver said an independent survey of education providers showed it was "on the right track" with inspections.

The Department for Education (DfE) said ministers were "working with Ofsted and school leaders to ensure accountability is fair, proportionate and focused on helping every school get better".

ASCL's announcement comes after another union, the National Association of Head Teachers (NAHT), said changes Ofsted made to inspections just under a year ago had been severely harmful to school leaders' welfare.

ASCL said it had passed a motion of no confidence in "the ability of Ofsted's leadership to address the damage being done by the new inspection system", adding that it was "increasingly concerned about the welfare and morale of members".

Pepe Di'Iasio, general secretary, said the union did not take the step "lightly", but added Ofsted's "warm words about recognising wellbeing pressures... have not been matched by the action necessary" and that "negotiation [had] hit a brick wall".

"The current system is not fit for purpose. It is an overbearing mess and urgently needs to be reviewed," he said.

News.title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know
News.content:
No time should be wasted in tackling these challenges, the review says.

On long waits, it says everyone on a waiting list should be reassessed so that those most in need are prioritised for help. There should no longer be a first-come, first-served approach.

Some of those waiting may benefit from non-medical support, advice about sleeping better or getting more physical exercise, for example. That may even lead to some being removed from the waiting list.

There should also be better assessments before people are placed on waiting lists too. Not every problem needs a medical solution, the experts make clear.

Quality and consistency of autism and ADHD assessments must be improved, with the review highlighting concerns about those done by the private sector on behalf of the NHS. Half of ADHD and a third of autism assessments are done by non-NHS providers, such as charities and private firms.

But they are not subject to the same regulation as NHS providers â and this must change.

The experts also said it wanted to see a ban on direct-to-public advertising of assessments.

The review has said it wants to see action over the next 12 to 24 months. The government has promised to act â and is expected to set out more details in its forthcoming mental health strategy which is expected by the end of the year.

News.title: Woman found dead in burning van was pregnant, police say
News.content:
Bell appeared via video link and spoke only to confirm his name.

Judge Geraint Walters confirmed that Samantha died as a result of the fire.

He said: "At the time of ignition the person was alive. Someone set the van alight and the person was alive and was killed as a result of the fire."

Emergency services were called to reports of a vehicle fire at 23:30 BST on Sunday close to an industrial estate and retail park in the centre of the town.

In a tribute issued on Friday, Samantha's family described her as a "much-loved mum, daughter, sister, auntie and friend".

Known to everyone as Sammi, they said she would be "remembered for the special place she held in the hearts of everyone who knew and loved her".

They said: "No family should ever have to endure the pain of losing a loved one in such circumstances.

"She will forever be cherished by those who loved her, and she will be deeply missed."

News.title: Teen's life transformed by gene editing
News.content:
A teenager has revealed how her life has been transformed thanks to pioneering gene editing, which reversed symptoms of a crippling blood disorder.

Vian, 16, was born with thalassemia, a condition that affects haemoglobin - used by red blood cells to transport oxygen around the body. It left her short of breath and with no appetite.

Her own stem cells were edited and she no longer needs the monthly blood transfusions she endured for most of her life.

"My whole life's different now. It's changed so much," she said.

The treatment, for patients with thalassaemia or sickle cell disease, is offered to young people at three children's hospitals in the country.

Vian, from Coventry, was one of the first to have it.

News.title: Abusive ex admits murdering woman after she began new relationship
News.content:
A man with a history of domestic abuse has admitted murdering his former partner a day after learning she had begun another relationship.

Lee Inglis pled guilty at the High Court in Edinburgh to stabbing Stacey Hogg to death in her home in Hawick earlier this year.

BBC Scotland News has learned that the 39-year-old had twice avoided prison for previous knife attacks on the mother of three.

He was still serving a home curfew and an unpaid work order when he killed the 35-year-old in June.

He waited until his curfew ended at 07:00 before making the three-minute journey from his parents' home to Stacey's house.

Warning: This article contains details readers may find upsetting

The court heard that he slipped in through the back door and attacked Stacey as she came down the stairs.

She suffered "catastrophic wounds" to her neck and head. Police found her in a pool of blood on a downstairs bathroom floor.

The court heard that when he was arrested by police he told them: "I intended to cut off her head."

"If I couldn't have her, nobody would," he added.

Inglis will be sentenced at the High Court in Edinburgh on 5 November.

News.title: New evidence gives family hope after death in Spain
News.content:
Four years after watching his brother die in his arms, Maximilian White believes new evidence could help him get answers.

Tobias White-Sansom, a father-of-two from Nottingham, died in a Spanish hospital in July 2022, five days after a night out in Magaluf, and his family believes the way security and police officers handled him that night led to his death.

A blood spatter report and a court order received by the family this month have reignited their hopes that criminal proceedings could commence in the Spanish courts.

White told the BBC: "I won't stop until we get justice for Toby."

The 46-year-old medical cannabis entrepreneur said he found it difficult to talk about the way he lost his younger sibling, who was on a family holiday at the time.

White-Sansom was pinned down at a nightclub following a row over him removing his T-shirt because he was too hot, his family said.

They told the BBC the Spanish Civil Guard - the Guardia Civil - was called and he was handcuffed, Tasered and injected with tranquilisers before going into cardiac arrest.

News.title: Burnham promises to curb non-compete rules in job contracts
News.content:
Andy Burnham has promised to curb companies' ability to restrict what their workers can do after leaving their job.

In a speech, the prime minister said the use of non-compete clauses in employment contracts had "gone too far" and was holding innovative UK companies back.

He added the clauses had forced workers to go without pay after leaving a role, as well as making it harder for growing firms to hire new staff.

Ahead of the Budget later this month, he also said there was "more to do" on tax to encourage promising firms to stay in the UK.

Sir Keir Starmer's government had been exploring possible restrictions on non-compete clauses since late last year, including a total ban, banning them above a certain salary threshold, or limiting how long they can last.

Although commonly associated with the financial services and technology sectors, research cited by the government has estimated around 5 million jobs in Britain are covered by the clauses, typically lasting around six months.

Speaking at a business summit in Manchester, Burnham confirmed his government would press ahead with new legislation to ensure the clauses can "no longer be a barrier" to hiring new staff.

He added that their use had stopped workers leaving to join other companies, or founding their own firms instead, adding: "I think that's a drag on innovation."

Referencing a landmark 1995 court ruling that is credited with revolutionising the football transfer market in Europe, he said he hoped reining in non-compete clauses could prove the "Bosman ruling for the innovation sector".

News.title: Dad and son remain critical after masked men attack
News.content:
A father and son are in hospital in a life-threatening condition after an attack in their family home which appeared "completely unprovoked", police have said.

Officers were called to reports of a disturbance at a house in Station Road, Thurnby, shortly before 00:30 BST on Thursday.

Leicestershire Police said a man in his 50s was stabbed multiple times, while a boy, 15, was also stabbed by two masked men who entered the property. The force gave an update on Friday to say both remained critical in hospital.

Officers added that the man's wife - who is in her 40s - suffered minor injuries to her hand and shoulder during the attack. Three other children who were in the address were not injured.

In the interest of public and police safety, police said armed officers were deployed but the men had left the house prior to them arriving.

The force added an investigation, led by the East Midlands Special Operations Unit (EMSOU), to understand the circumstances and motive would continue over the weekend.

News.title: Powerful 7.6 magnitude earthquake hits Panama coast as nine countries issued tsunami warnings
News.content:

A powerful magnitude 7.6 earthquake has struck off the coast of Panama.

There were no immediate reports of damage in Panama, though television footage showed people evacuating buildings.

The quake was felt in the capital of Panama City, as well as the capital of neighbouring Costa Rica, according to witnesses.

Following the quake, the US Tsunami Warning System alerted nine countries to possible coastal tsunami waves.

Panama, Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Peru, Nicaragua, Guatemala, El Salvador and Mexico have all been warned over the threat of tsunami waves within the next three hours.

News.title: FlyDubai co-pilot intended to crash plane into Tel Aviv airport, UAE prosecutor says
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The axe-wielding co-pilot who attacked the captain of a FlyDubai flight to Tel Aviv last month intended to seize control of the airplane and fly it into the passenger terminal at Israel’s main international airport, authorities in the United Arab Emirates said Friday.

The suspect, an Omani national, did so “with the intention of causing the greatest possible number of human casualties,” the UAE’s top prosecutor said in a statement carried by the state news agency WAM. Most of the 174 passengers on the flight were from Israel.

The statement said the co-pilot “drew inspiration” from the Sept. 11, 2001 attacks in the United States and used two previous flights from Dubai to Tel Aviv to “familiarize himself with the flight route and the airport.”

It said none of FlyDubai's security or professional checks had indicated that the pilot, who was identitifed by The Associated Press as 29-year-old Hamam al-Hammami, harbored extremist views or plans to carry out an attack.

Hammami “admitted that he had acted alone, without the involvement of others,” the statement said, adding that he “provided a detailed confession outlining his motives and the stages of planning and execution” in the presence of his lawyer. It also suggested he was radicalized at a mosque in Australia while attending the Royal Melbourne Institute of Technology in 2017.

The update from the public prosecutor Friday was the most comprehensive since the UAE took over the investigation shortly after the incident on Sept. 30. FlyDubai is a government-owned airline.

The crisis unfolded suddenly in the skies above Jordan and Saudi Arabia, when Hammami attacked the captain, Smit Machchhar, with a crash axe in the cockpit. Bloodied and beaten, Machchhar managed to open the cockpit door, alerting passengers and crew to the assault.

Passengers detained Hammami and helped steady the aircraft, which had plunged roughly 14,000 to 16,000 feet in less than a minute. Two reserve pilots then guided the plane to an emergency landing at Tabuk airport in Saudi Arabia.

News.title: Zack Polanski facing calls to quit as Green Party leader after by-election defeat
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Zack Polanski is facing calls to stand down as leader of the Green Party after he failed to win a seat in parliament at the Holborn and St Pancras by-election.

The leader of the Jewish Greens, Vivien Lichtenstein, has called for Mr Polanski to resign and said he made a “big mistake” by missing a debate about a party conference motion that declared Zionism to be a form of racism.

She is among a number of senior Green figures to have criticised Mr Polanski and raised concerns about whether he should continue to lead the party, with former leader Caroline Lucas accusing him of a failure in leadership and another long-term senior figure telling The Independent that the situation is “untenable”.

Meanwhile YouGov polling conducted on Friday in the wake of Mr Polanski’s by-election defeat found a third of voters (34 per cent) think he should quit as leader, compared with just one in five (20 per cent) who think he should remain in post.

While campaigning in the by-election, Mr Polanski missed the crucial conference vote which endorsed a policy effectively calling for Israel to be abolished and replaced with a single Palestinian state, a motion which brought condemnation from other political parties and Jewish groups. Mr Polanski was barred from entering Israel as a result.

open image in gallery Zack Polanski is under growing pressure after the by-election ( Reuters )

Ms Lucas said he “should have been there and he should have voted”. Meanwhile, Ms Lichtenstein, the chair of the Jewish Greens committee, issued a damning verdict on the Green leader, telling Times Radio: “I think he should resign.”

“It was a big mistake for Zack not to find a place, a quiet place, where he could have gone online for the motions debate, where he could have spoken to the two amendments that he supported. He should have done it,” she said.

Mr Polanski’s position came under further scrutiny after he was defeated in the race to replace Sir Keir Starmer as the MP for Holborn and St Pancras by Labour’s Sagal Abdi-Wali.

She secured 45 per cent of the vote to the Greens’ 33 per cent, a majority of 3,364 but with a 13 per cent swing to the Greens, whose vote share was up by 22.4 per cent.

Insisting that “of course I can carry on” as party leader in the wake of the defeat, Mr Polanski acknowledged that ultimately Green members would decide his fate, with a scheduled leadership vote due next year.

One senior party source told The Independent that there is “growing frustration” with Mr Polanski for missing the vote, accusing him of attempting to “sweep the issue under the carpet”.

“Most senior Greens recognise the situation is not tenable and the question will be whether Zack engages with this and shows leadership on finding a way forward for the party,” the source added.

open image in gallery Sagal Abdi-Wali grins after being declared the winner of the Holborn and St Pancras by-election ( PA Wire )

Speaking after Mr Polanski admitted that he does not agree with the Zionism motion, the source added: “The question is, what is he going to do about it?”, warning that the leader now risks alienating both sides of his party.

Green MP Sian Berry also piled in on the morning after the by-election, saying she is “full of regret” about the Zionism motion.

She said she is “very glad” Mr Polanski has now said he would have voted against the motion, adding: “We are not where we want to be today, but I know we can build from this starting point if we work together in a new spirit.”

Asked how confident he was about being re-elected as leader, Mr Polanski told Sky News: “That’s going to be up to the members and that’s going to be up to the leadership election that happens next summer.

“What I’m experiencing, though, is an immense amount of people who are saying actually they’ve never been prouder to be a Green Party member.”

He said it was “difficult being leader of any party, particularly the Green Party”, adding: “But I signed up for that difficult job and I’m more than ready to continue.”

He also defended his decision to miss the conference vote on the anti-Zionism motion because he was campaigning in the by-election.

Asked if he supported the motion, he said: “I would have supported the motion as amended. It wasn’t amended, so no.”

But he added: “Ultimately, I agree with the substance of the motion. Where I disagree is the idea the Green Party should be deciding what the future of the region looks like.”

open image in gallery Caroline Lucas was critical of Polanski’s position ( Getty )

Ms Lucas, who was the Green Party’s first MP, said people should “see what happens in the coming days and weeks” when asked about Mr Polanski’s future on Thursday’s BBC Newsnight.

She pointed to Mr Polanski’s failure to take part in the controversial anti-Zionism motion on Sunday, saying he “should have been there and he should have voted”.

Holborn and St Pancras has been a Labour stronghold since its formation in 1983, held by Frank Dobson for 32 years and Sir Keir for 11.

Despite the mounting criticism of Mr Polanski, polling guru Sir John Curtice insisted the Greens can take “some comfort” in Friday’s by-election result, insisting that the defeat alone “should not raise questions about Polanski’s position as leader”.

“Their tally was still their second-best performance in a parliamentary by-election, behind only their success in Gorton and Denton earlier this year,” he said.

“It represented a four-point increase on the joint vote for the Greens and the Independent pro-Palestinian candidate, Andrew Feinstein, in 2024, despite facing competition from George Galloway for the Muslim vote.

“All in all, this was about as good a performance as the party could have expected given its fall in the national polls and the divisions at its party conference over its attitude towards Zionism.

“On its own at least, this defeat should not raise questions about Polanski’s position as leader. However, he will want to ask himself why the party’s rise in the polls to 16 per cent earlier this year has fallen away so precipitously.”

Meanwhile, the party’s first ever member in the House of Lords, Jenny Jones, said Polanski still has another year of his two-year term to serve, and claimed that the Greens “don’t depose leaders by gossip and criticism”.

“We’ve had some huge blips in the past. We’ve managed to get through them and come out the other side,” she told Times Radio. “So he’s there for another year. And I’m sure he is going to work incredibly hard to make sure that the party goes on the track that we would all like.”

News.title: Zack Polanski has been crushed by the Burnham Bounce
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in
