Whether it's investigating the financials of Elon Musk's pro-Trump PAC or producing our latest documentary, 'The A Word', which shines a light on the American women fighting for reproductive rights, we know how important it is to parse out the facts from the messaging. At such a critical moment in US history, we need reporters on the ground. Your donation allows us to keep sending journalists to speak to both sides of the story. The Independent is trusted by Americans across the entire political spectrum. And unlike many other quality news outlets, we choose not to lock Americans out of our reporting and analysis with paywalls. We believe quality journalism should be available to everyone, paid for by those who can afford it. Your support makes all the difference. Read more

There is some irony in the way that further “proof of concept” for Andy Burnham’s leadership of the Labour Party came in Sir Keir Starmer’s former seat of Holborn and St Pancras.

It has been proved that Labour under Mr Burnham could take on and defeat Reform UK. Now it has been shown that the new Labour leader can also see off his Green rival.

Indeed, Mr Burnham has brushed aside a by-election challenge from a Green candidate who happens to be that party’s leader, and was standing in a constituency tailor-made for the classic Green demographic – young, cosmopolitan, lots of students and renters, many passionate about the sufferings of the Palestinian people and still disillusioned with Labour’s response. Much of the campaign was conducted in a heatwave – a tangible warning about climate change. In short: ideal conditions, electorally.

A few months ago Mr Polanski would have walked such a contest, but the Burnham Bounce has squashed another victim. Yet Mr Polanski and his party have created enough problems for themselves, not least over their attitude to Zionism.

The Greens have many questions to answer about the nature of their party and its uneasy coalition of nimby environmentalists in places such as Suffolk and Herefordshire, and the more radical pro-Palestine socialist wing that makes up their core support in urban bases in the North West, the Midlands and London.

A cultish belief in the hypnotic Mr Polanski held them together for a time, but his leadership is clearly now in question. His best hope of survival is that there is no one obviously ready to succeed him. He’s the best they’ve got and, like Nigel Farage, he is a polarising personality.

For Labour there are no longer, or at least for the time being, such distractions. By the end of his time in office, Sir Keir, however history chooses to judge him, could neither take on the Greens or Reform, nor the SNP and Plaid Cymru for that matter. Mr Burnham has thus managed to achieve something that few others have – to renew a party with a change of leadership while it is still in office.

It is not just a matter of “positioning”, though the tilt leftwards has obviously yielded a useful political dividend. It has also become clear that Mr Burnham is simply a better, more instinctive politician than was Sir Keir – much more natural in debate and at the podium, a clearer communicator, and less likely to delegate and more liable to intervene when he sniffs trouble and opportunity alike.

In taking the initiative on Europe, on water, on social care and on cost-of-living issues he has enjoyed drawing useful dividing lines with rival parties, and thus discomfiting Kemi Badenoch and Mr Farage. The Liberal Democrats, meanwhile, have been left confused at Mr Burnham’s habit of agreeing with them. At the end of this political conference season, it is the right of British politics that is the more fragmented, and the “progressive” wing that is the more consolidated around the larger player, Labour.

All that said, Mr Burnham should not fall into the same trap that Mr Polanski waltzed into and start to believe his party’s own hype. The Greens invited their own downfall when they went around claiming that, under Mr Polanski, they had already replaced the Labour Party. Something of the same might also be said about Mr Farage’s attempt to pose as the “real” leader of the opposition and next prime minister.

Mr Burnham, therefore, is in a relatively strong position. Some recent local by-elections also support the polling picture of a Labour recovery. But it would be folly for him to go for an early election on such a flimsy basis, and the voters would neither thank him for the timing nor oblige any assumptions of an easy Labour win.

Labour’s comeback story still has a long way to go. Even now the party has not recovered the strength it enjoyed at the last general election – and in terms of the popular vote, that was not exactly overwhelming. The Greens and Reform remain formidable foes in many areas of the country Labour has to win in order to govern. As Sir John Curtice asked recently in conversation with The Independent: why would Mr Burnham sacrifice three whole years in government with a landslide majority for an extra two in office with little or no Commons majority at all? How will that help him get things done?

Whenever Mr Burnham does decide to seek his own personal mandate, he must do so with real achievements to his name – not just hopes. He enjoys the huge advantages of incumbency, which should not be lightly given up. In the coming months, the prime minister and his colleagues will have many opportunities to move beyond the honeymoon phase and win the respect of the electorate. There will be another difficult Budget, what he terms his Ten Year Plan, and renewed moves to reform welfare, fund defence and control migration. The Burnham Bounce cannot defy political gravity forever.

News.title: Israel's scorn of Nobel Peace Prize laureate highlights its combative relationship with UN bodies
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The decision to award this year's Nobel Peace Prize to veteran jurist Navi Pillay has exposed the vast gulf between Israel and global institutions charged with upholding international law, a rift that has widened over the war in Gaza.

Over a decades-long career, Pillay served at the highest levels of international organizations created in the wake of World War II to prevent a recurrence of its horrors. As a young lawyer in her native South Africa she campaigned against apartheid and for the release of Nelson Mandela, and as an international jurist she helped sentence dozens of people convicted of taking part in the 1994 Rwandan genocide.

But her leadership of a U.N.-backed panel that determined Israel committed genocide in Gaza — allegations it vehemently denies — has led many in Israel to see the Nobel nod as a high-profile rebuke of the country just days after the anniversary of the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas attack that triggered the war.

Allegations of genocide are particularly explosive in Israel, which was founded in part as a refuge for survivors of the Nazi Holocaust.

“Awarding Pillay the Nobel Peace Prize isn’t a recognition of justice. It’s the grotesque weaponization of an award to legitimize anti-Israel hatred and prejudice,” Israel's Foreign Ministry said on X. “Joseph Goebbels is certainly applauding from hell,” it added, referring to the Nazi propagandist.

The vitriol comes from the widespread perception in Israel that the United Nations and other international bodies are biased against it. The United States has echoed that criticism and announced a raft of sanctions aimed at dismantling the International Criminal Court hours after the Nobel Prize announcement.

But Pillay's findings over the years were largely consistent with those of major human rights groups and other international bodies, and the facts she cited in reaching her conclusions had been widely reported.

Pillay led a panel that accused Israel of genocide in Gaza

Pillay led a three-member expert panel commissioned by the U.N. Human Rights Council that concluded last year that Israel had committed genocide in Gaza.

Their 22-page report cited the death toll; Israeli restrictions on humanitarian aid that led to widespread hunger; a policy of “systematically destroying” the healthcare system; the direct targeting of children and “explicit statements” of intent by Israeli civilian and military authorities.

Human rights groups and many experts on genocide have reached similar conclusions.

The commission has also issued reports accusing Hamas of war crimes during its Oct. 7, 2023, attack, when militants killed some 1,200 people and abducted 251 others. Israel’s retaliatory offensive has killed over 74,000 Palestinians, according to Gaza’s Health Ministry. The ministry, part of the Hamas-run government, maintains detailed records seen as generally reliable by U.N. agencies and many independent experts.

Israel has vehemently denied the allegations, casting them as an antisemitic blood libel. The Israeli military says it takes extraordinary measures to prevent harm to civilians and blames their deaths on Hamas because it operates in densely populated areas.

The International Court of Justice, the U.N.'s top court, is investigating genocide allegations brought by South Africa, and the International Criminal Court has issued an arrest warrant for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, for war crimes and crimes against humanity.

Pillay currently serves as an ad hoc judge in the ICJ's ongoing genocide case against Myanmar and served as an ICC judge from 2003-2008.

Israel has rejected the commission since its inception

The commission was created after the 2021 Israel-Hamas war and is the first to have an open-ended mandate. Critics say such permanent scrutiny shows anti-Israel bias, while supporters say it's needed to keep tabs on injustices faced by Palestinians under decades of Israeli rule.

Israel has refused to cooperate with the commission or other U.N.-endorsed investigations. It has pointed to the presence of notoriously repressive countries on the 47-member Human Rights Council and accused it of relentlessly singling out Israel while ignoring violations elsewhere.

A member of the commission, Indian jurist Miloon Kothari, sparked controversy in 2022 when he referred to a “Jewish lobby” in a media interview and questioned Israel's U.N. membership, citing its alleged violations of member state obligations.

Pillay issued a letter at the time saying Kothari had been misquoted and that the commission does not question Israel's status or U.N. membership.

She addressed the wider criticism in an interview with The Associated Press last year after she and the other commission members resigned, citing personal reasons and the need for change. They have since been replaced.

“We’re an independent panel,” she said. “People who accuse us of being antisemitic ... they twist the facts, they invent facts, falsify facts. I would like to see them challenge the report: Which of the facts that we have set out are incorrect?” she said.

Pillay also investigated Israel's decades-long occupation of the West Bank

Even before the latest Israel-Hamas war, Pillay had repeatedly taken Israel to task over its open-ended military rule over millions of Palestinians.

In a report released more than a year before the Oct. 7 attack, the commission accused Israel of de facto annexation of the West Bank, which it captured alongside Gaza and east Jerusalem in the 1967 Mideast war. The Palestinians want an independent state encompassing all three territories.

The International Court of Justice later issued a landmark ruling that Israel's occupation of the territories was unlawful.

The commission had said Israel's continuous expansion of Jewish settlements, its demolition of Palestinian homes and its fragmentation of Palestinian life were aimed at securing permanent rule over the territory, which is home to some 3 million Palestinians and 500,000 Israeli settlers.

Palestinians in the West Bank live under Israeli military rule, with the Palestinian Authority administering population centers. The settlers have Israeli citizenship, including freedom of movement and the right to vote.

Israel's U.N. mission rejected the report at the time of its release, calling it part of an “anti-Israel agenda” at the international body.

But Israel's current government and most of its political class is opposed to Palestinian statehood, and Netanyahu has repeatedly said Israel will maintain permanent control over the territories.

Israel views the West Bank as the biblical and historical cradle of Judaism, and says its withdrawal would pave the way for a Hamas-run state that would threaten its existence. The last substantive Israeli-Palestinian peace talks broke down in 2009, after Netanyahu returned to office.

Pillay's commission had also raised concerns about Israel's potential annexation of Gaza, saying its efforts to carve out buffer zones and military corridors were “vastly disproportionate to any reasonable military objective.”

It said calls by Israeli officials for the “voluntary migration” of much of Gaza's population from the war-ravaged territory, if implemented, would amount to forcible transfer, a crime against humanity.

News.title: Britain says it ‘strongly disagrees’ with US sanctions on ICC in joint statement with G7 allies
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The UK and fellow G7 partners have reiterated their "continued and unwavering support" for the International Criminal Court (ICC) following the introduction of sanctions against the tribunal by the US.

In a joint declaration, the UK, Canada, France, Germany, Italy and Japan – along with Denmark and the Netherlands – stated that they "regret and strongly disagree with" the sanctions.

The coalition acknowledged that while the tribunal has taken action to ensure ongoing functionality, the measures will "have a significant impact on the court’s work".

They also praised the dedication of tribunal personnel and their relatives, noting that they "work every day to bring those accused of the most serious international crimes to justice and to support their victims".

The statement comes after US secretary of state Marco Rubio announced sweeping sanctions on the ICC, calling it a “rogue court”.

The US announcement of sanctions coincided with one of the court’s former judges, Navi Pillay, being awarded the Nobel Peace Prize.

It also appears to be a rebuke to Mr Rubio, who had demanded that America’s allies “rein in” the court, threatening that otherwise the US would “continue its campaign” to “end the ICC”.

The US administration has been fiercely critical of the ICC over its investigation into the actions of US troops in Afghanistan and rejected it issuing an arrest warrant for Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

US secretary of state Marco Rubio demanded that America’s allies ‘rein in’ the court ( PA )

Neither the US nor Israel are signed up to the ICC – established in 2002 to prosecute war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide – and reject its jurisdiction over their citizens.

Mr Rubio said the sanctions would “ban transactions” with the ICC, “cutting off their resources and crippling its ability to operate”.

In a statement, the court itself said the sanctions were “an attempt to obstruct the course of justice” and “an assault on the rule of law and on the very foundations of the international legal order”.

Warning the court “cannot stand alone”, it added: “Its fate now rests also in the hands of the states that created it.”

The statement went on: “The court calls upon states to continue taking concrete actions, including to ensure that the court continues to have the necessary means to continue its work.

“This is not just about defending a single institution, but about safeguarding the international order grounded upon the rule of law.

“No one should be punished for serving the cause of justice. History will judge this moment. Future generations, and above all the victims of mass atrocities, will ask how we responded when an institution created to protect them came under attack.”

The International Federation for Human Rights also criticised the sanctions, with its president Alexis Deswaef saying the ICC’s 125 member states “cannot establish a court to hold the powerful accountable and then stand by while it is being dismantled”.

“They must act collectively to protect the court, civil society, and the victims and survivors who depend on them,” he added.

News.title: What is the XFG Covid strain? Symptoms and what to know as the variant hits the UK
News.content:
Cases of Covid-19 have risen sharply across the UK this month, driven largely by a variant of the virus known as ‘XFG’.

Sometimes referred to as ‘Stratus’ and the ‘American strain’, owing to the fact that it is now the most common strain in North America, it was first identified in January 2025 and has since spread worldwide.

Between August and September, Covid cases in Britain jumped 230 per cent, from 1,374 to 4,589 new infections, half of which were caused by the XFG strain.

Hospitalisation rates have also increased by 15 per cent in the same period, according to the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA).

The true number of cases is likely to be much higher, as most people who contract Covid-19 experience a milder illness and will not visit hospital or receive an official diagnosis via their GP.

What are the symptoms, and how is it different from other variants?

Symptoms of XFG are similar to other variants of Covid-19 like Delta and Omicron, and typically begin with a sore throat, before developing into a cough and fever.

However, experts have noted that patients diagnosed with XFG tend to present with a characteristic hoarse, croaky voice, which is distinctive from older strains.

More than 30 other symptoms have been known to be associated with XFG and other Covid strains, including diarrhoea, vomiting, loss of taste and smell, shortness of breath, headache, and muscle aches.

Why are cases rising?

Current data does not suggest that XFG leads to more severe illness than any other variant in circulation, according to the UKHSA.

As the UK moves into winter, colder and wetter weather naturally influences the rise in respiratory illnesses like Covid-19 and the flu, given people spend more time indoors and in closer proximity to each other, where viruses can more easily transmit between them.

It has also been roughly a year since the last significant wave of Covid-19 cases, meaning that the population-wide immunity has somewhat waned, making people more susceptible to the disease, the UKHSA said.

Can you be vaccinated against XFG?

The current Covid-19 vaccine is designed to protect against XFG and related strains specifically, after modelling suggested it would become the dominant variant this season.

Those eligible for a Covid-19 autumn booster include adults over the age of 75, residents in care homes, and anyone over six months old with a weakened immune system, due to a health condition or treatment.

Covid vaccines are also available to buy privately for those who are not eligible for a free jab, and typically cost around £98 per dose.

What should you do if you suspect you have XFG?

The NHS no longer advises that people with symptoms of Covid-19 take a test, unless they want to do so.

If you feel unwell or have a high temperature, health authorities advise you to try and stay home and avoid contact with people until you feel better.

They also recommend avoiding contact with vulnerable people, like those undergoing chemotherapy or the elderly, for at least 10 days.

Protect yourself and your family by learning more about Global Health Security

News.title: Harry’s Invictus Games challenge in Kenya is helping veterans battle physical and mental scars
News.content:
Wounded veterans from 10 countries have gathered in Kenya’s Great Rift Valley for a week of endurance challenges, organised by the charity behind Prince Harry’s Invictus Games.

Twenty-five serving and former personnel, among them a Ukrainian who survived a direct bomb hit in Donetsk and a Danish combat engineer who cleared roadside bombs in Afghanistan, will run, hike or cycle up to 120km across the area on Saturday October 10, World Mental Health Day.

The Invictus Games Foundation, the charity the Duke of Sussex founded in 2014 for wounded, injured and sick service personnel, has organised the event.

For Vasyl, a Ukrainian soldier, it will be his first time in Africa and his first long-distance challenge.

After three weeks of military training in the UK, the 34-year-old joined a brigade in Donetsk as a reconnaissance squad commander, spending more than 19 months on the front line. He was wounded when a drone dropped a grenade three metres from him, and the shrapnel still causes frequent pain in his leg which can sometimes make walking difficult.

But he said the physical injury was easier to bear than the loss of the friends he made in the trenches.

“There is a level of kindness between comrades in a trench that you will never find in civilian life,” he said. “If someone made a mistake or said something wrong, we immediately forgave them and thought nothing more of it.

“For me, the pain of loss is the hardest thing the war has left behind.”

News.title: From Yale to the Congo: The mathematician who became one of Africa’s most intrepid reporters
News.content:
Sundaram has a lot of experience with the Rwandan methods of control. After spending 17 months in DRC, he moved to Kigali and he is eloquent about the convoluted effects of dictatorship. “Living in Rwanda taught me so much about how dictatorships function internally and how counter-intuitive they can be. A friend of mine who was working in public health told me ‘When we ask people in India to wash their hands we get a 30 per cent success rate from a campaign, but when we need people in Rwanda to wash their hands, we just need to slip a line in one of Kagame’s speeches and we get a 90 per cent success rate. That’s fantastic isn’t it?’

“And I said, ‘well is it? It’s great for short term health outcomes but what does that say about society? Isn’t democracy about people choosing freely? What if the government tells them to do something bad – like what happened in the genocide when people were told to kill all the Tutsis?’

“Kagame and his army stopped the genocide, and he has restored peace, but he governs using the same system that was used to perpetrate the genocide.”

In Bad News: Last Journalists in a Dictatorship, the book Sundaram went on to write about his time in Rwanda teaching journalists, he describes a more extreme version of this phenomenon, recalling how Kagame once commented that thatched roofs on huts were primitive. “And the local authorities took that as a sign that he didn’t like thatched roofs, and that they should get rid of them. And without replacements being built, people climbed up and dismantled their own thatched roofs. And I saw these villages with houses which just had mud walls without roofs, and the families were sitting outside with their children and their goats, the thatch strewn on the ground. In the rain, quite often. The children would get sick, and it was like a war zone.

“At the end of my time in Congo, I was at a UN base and they were digging latrines, when they found some human bones. They stopped digging and alerted the press, and I happened to be in Goma nearby.” He subsequently found out that it was one of a series of mass graves containing the bodies of Congolese killed by forces controlled by Kagame. “And so when I arrived I had a sense of what Rwanda had done in Congo, but I didn’t fully appreciate the extent to which it was totalitarian. I’d heard that the country was a shining example of progress – aid programs were successful, and poverty reduction programs. The streets were clean, public services functioned. I was living in a nice house with a big garden provided by the journalism programme I was working in.”

Many European governments, including Britain, are enamoured with Rwanda, because, says Sundaram, “dictatorships can be very efficient”. But it is a “mirage of a country”, he says.

The teaching programme he was running was briefed not to challenge the government on any level, and an embassy official told him that if any of the journalists mentioned repression they would be expelled.

“Layer by layer, as I began to talk to the journalists I was training, the true story unravelled. The first instance was when one of them left the programme, and I heard him on the radio one day praising the president, but with a degree of flattery that was completely exaggerated, and I didn’t understand why. The rest of the class were reluctant to talk about it but eventually I learned that another student had been beaten to a coma on the day he criticised the president.

“I started to realise that my class contained some of the most courageous journalists in the country.” As a foreigner, if he transgressed, Sundaram could have his visa cancelled or get kicked out, or even locked up for a couple of days, but for the Rwandan journalists, everything was at stake. They could be killed or their families threatened.

“But still they persisted, and they took me around the country and showed me all the things the government didn’t want anyone to see – things they couldn’t report on because it was too dangerous, so they wanted to show me because they wanted somebody to speak up. It’s really a book about them – they’ve been my greatest teachers in journalism.”

News.title: I tried Amazon’s new iPad rival – and there’s one standout feature
News.content:
Amazon says that this tablet has three times the computing power and nine times the graphics power of any previous Amazon tablet, so this is a significant boost in performance to previous models.

That will make light tasks, such as crunching through emails, browser-based activity like online shopping and document work. With a keyboard factored in, it could work as a laptop alternative for some. The same could be said of the iPad Air, although with recent price increases from Apple and the matte screen, for my money, this is a better proposition.

The premium makeover that comes with the Alexa Tablet Pro includes a slim aluminium design, with flattened edges, so it looks like an iPad or Samsung tablet, only 6.5mm thick. The Pro version only comes in the Graphite colour seen here. All models in the new line-up feel more grown-up and less like kid’s tablets than the Fire range. Plus the switch to proper Android over Fire OS is welcome and will result in better app compatibility (although I noticed that these tablets were running Android 16, which is now an old version).

It has a battery that’s good for 16 hours of video playback and supports 27W charging. There are cameras front and rear although like any tablet, these won’t be as good as your phone, while there’s support for Dolby Atmos from the speakers, so your movies will sound decent.

The AI capabilities are a step up

As the name suggests, Amazon is keen to promote the AI element here. It has customised the interface slightly with access to Alexa+ meaning you can utilise Amazon’s AI at any time to ask about what’s on the screen, to control smart home devices or search for content. If you are a keen Alexa user, then that will be a plus, but for me it’s not the headline news.

News.title: Kenyan authorities scramble to find passengers on Ebola flight
News.content:
Authorities are racing to track down passengers who boarded a flight from Uganda to Kenya on Saturday alongside a man infected with Ebola.

The man travelled by bus from the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), the epicentre of an Ebola outbreak that has killed 4,000 people, to Kampala, Uganda. He then boarded a flight to Nairobi on Saturday, October 3, which was operated by the African airline Jambojet.

The patient went to a hospital in Nairobi and died just 48 hours later, meaning the journey took place in the final days of infection, the stage at which patients who die of the disease are most contagious. By October 6 authorities had tracked down 28 contacts, including family members of the deceased, but said they urgently needed to track down 23 passengers and crew who had travelled on the same flight.

The man is Kenya’s first ever case of the disease. Ebola does not typically spread through the air like Covid-19 or measles, requiring close contact with the bodily fluids of an infected person to spread. However, an aeroplane cabin significantly intensifies these risks because passengers share cramped spaces for prolonged periods and touch the same surfaces, such as a cabin toilet.

“We are working closely with the Ministry of Health, Port Health Services and other relevant authorities to support the ongoing public health response, including the identification and management of the other guests and crew who may have been in contact with the individual,” a spokesperson for Jambojet said on Tuesday.

After landing in Kenya, airport staff screened the patient, standard protocol for people travelling from at-risk countries during the current Ebola outbreak, but allowed him to continue his journey into Nairobi.

Kenya’s health ministry director-general, Patrick Amoth, said the patient may have passed through airport screening because medication had masked his symptoms.

News.title: Africa embraces ‘Go to Work on an Egg’ to boost maternal health and nutrition
News.content:
The sun is barely up when villagers start queuing for eggs at the metal gate of Shamim Haried’s home.

By noon, all that day’s supply is usually sold out, but people keep coming and asking if there are any left.

Demand is so high that arguments can break out in the queue, says the mother-of-two who lives outside Malawi’s capital, Lilongwe.

Her eggs are cheaper and fresher than those sold in the market.

“The people almost fight for eggs: it’s hard to watch,” she explains.

“Eggs are the cheapest healthy protein that they can get and it’s better for them to buy here than anywhere else.”

Her flock of 1,400 chickens lay around 1,000 eggs each day, but she reckons she could sell three times that.

Sports.title: Four ways Arsenal could line up for Leeds as Arteta faces major dilemma after Kai Havertz injury
Sports.content:
Next

MIKEL ARTETA is still sweating on the fitness of a number of top stars ahead of Arsenal’s clash with Leeds tomorrow.

The Gunners host Leeds at the Emirates in the early kick-off, looking to bounce back form their shock 3-0 defeat to Brighton last time out.



The extended three-week international break has thrown some curveballs at Arteta, who now faces a selection dilemma as a result of injuries and in-form squad players.

Arteta admitted that Christos Tzolis is set to face “weeks” out of action after he suffered a hamstring injury while away with Greece.



Meanwhile Ezri Konsa and Kai Havertz are major doubts for Saturday’s battle against Leeds after the pair withdrew from the England and Germany squads respectively.

Arteta said: “With Kai, because he had a muscular injury, I spoke to Jurgen [Klopp] and immediately they sent the player back as is normal.

“Ezri, has been carrying some issues as well, and we had good communication with the England camp about that.

“Tzolis because he had a muscle injury and he’s going to be out for a few weeks.”

Havertz’s potential absence opens the door for Arteta to use one of Mikel Merino and Viktor Gyokeres as his centre-forward.

Arteta has opted for Havertz from the start in every league game so far this season and always trusts the German in the big moments.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

But Merino and Gyokeres have both excelled during the international break and will be desperate to step into his role and try and nail down a starting spot after spending much of the season on the bench this term .

Arteta is also boosted by the return of Piero Hincapie, Cristhian Mosquera and Ben White, who should all be available for selection against Leeds.

Max Dowman also took part in first-team training on Thursday despite withdrawing from the England U19s squad with a contact injury.

Declan Rice is also expected to be available to Arteta after sitting out the international break due to load management.



Here, SunSport Arsenal reporter Joshua Hall breaks down four potential starting XI’s that Mikel Arteta could use as he looks to navigate his selection headache.

GYOK AND LOADED

Viktor Gyokeres scored four goals in four games for Sweden during the international break and became the first player in Nations League history to net in seven consecutive games.

The powerhouse striker has struggled for minutes and is yet to start a league game this term.

But given his red hot form, now could be the time for Arteta to trust the his £63.5m striker to do the business.

Gyokeres netteed three times in two games against Leeds last season and will be coinfident of doing it again, give the chance.



MER THAN A MIDFIELDER

Mikel Merino has become one of the best finishes at Arsenal since his arrival at the club.

His makeshift role as a No.9 against Leicester two seasons ago made him become a genuine deputy in the centre-forward position.

If Havertz is not fit, Merino is a far more technically sound replacement than Gyokeres and it allows Arteta to try and play in the same way.



Couple that with the fact that Merino scored three goals and registered one assist for Spain during the break and you can see why Arteta would be temptef to start him up top.

The Arsneal boss will have to be careful not to knock Gyokeres’ confidence even further, though.

TWICE AS NICE

When you have two players in such incredible form, perhaps the best thing to do is find a way to get them both in the squad.



Arteta could opt to play both Merino and Gyokeres in the same team, using them both in their natural positions and sacrificing a midfielder instead.

Merino’s technical ability and late runs into the box would not be lost, while Gyokeres can keep his momentum going and stretch the Leeds defence.

However, Arteta have to choose to drop one of Declan Rice, Martin Odegaard, Myles Lewis-Skelly or Bruno Guimaraes to pull this off.



HAV IT MY WAY

Sports.title: Roberto De Zerbi backed by ex-Brighton star to stop the rot and transform Tottenham’s season after £300m splurge
Sports.content:
Next

ROBERTO DE ZERBI has had to watch his megabucks Tottenham side get beaten up so far this season as they sit rock bottom of the table.

But one of his former favourite sons says there is good reason to believe Spurs will be fighting back soon enough.



Solly March played the best football of his career under De Zerbi while the pair were together at Brighton in the 2022-23 season.

Yet it was not a case of instant success, with March recalling how the Seagulls were “bullied” during a winless first five games of the Italian’s tenure.



Fortunes turned in his sixth game though, with a 4-1 victory over Graham Potter’s Chelsea sparking a fantastic run that took Albion to Europe for the first time.

De Zerbi will hope history can repeat itself on Saturday when Spurs, who have failed to win any of their first five league fixtures this term, go to Manchester United.



March has faith the current Tottenham side will start clicking once they get used to De Zerbi’s perfectionist methods, just as he and his team-mates did at Brighton.

The free agent, who netted seven Prem goals during that 22-23 campaign, told SunSport: “I remember the detail of his training sessions, where everything was so particular.

“If you weren’t doing it right, he wouldn’t have it and you’d do it again until you did it as he wanted.

“I enjoyed it. You had to be almost perfect. You had to get the pass to the right foot, your movement had to be right and if not he would show you how it was done.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“I remember those first five games and Brentford away particularly, which was his third game.

“We got in at half-time and it was just like, ‘We don’t know what we’re doing’. It was mental. Players were just not sure what to do.

“We weren’t in the right places, we weren’t in the right positions. We were just getting bullied all over the pitch.

“We just kept working on his methods over and over and then something clicked.

“We knew exactly what he wanted. Everyone would be in the right positions. You would have the ball, you would have three options, every option would be there.



“We ended up playing great, free-flowing football. It worked really well and just took a bit longer.

“Maybe that’s the same thing at Tottenham. Hopefully that changes round quickly.”

Spurs have splashed more than £300million on the likes of Sandro Tonali, Savio, Omar Marmoush and Jan Paul van Hecke.

De Zerbi’s side have played well in patches but results have been disastrous, with two points from the opening five games leaving Spurs bottom of the table.

And this is in the phase of the Italian’s reign where we are supposed to be seeing the real De Zerbi Tottenham.



As opposed to the final seven games of last term, when De Zerbi arrived with the only focus on saving the club from relegation rather than introducing any kind of tactical revolution.

It has led to some questioning the ex-Marseille chief’s credentials but March is in no doubt of his former gaffer’s quality.

The winger, who left Brighton after 13 years this summer, added: “He was incredible.

“I remember the first day he came in. He said, ‘Can you come to my office and can we talk’.

“He said, ‘You’re going to be a big player for me, you’re going to be scoring goals, getting assists. I don’t know how you’ve not played in Europe and the Champions League, I want to get you there’.



“Something just clicked when he said that. It was that belief that I had never felt before.

“I’m surprised with the season that Tottenham have had. I really thought they would have a great season and maybe they still can.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I know how good De Zerbi is and I know how much the players think of him, his sessions and his ways of managing.

“I really hope they turn it around and I really think they can. They’ve got the manager and players to do so.”

Sports.title: ‘All hell will break loose’ – Neville reveals worst thing Man City can do and why he’s certain they’d fail owners’ test
Sports.content:
Next

GARY NEVILLE has claimed “all hell would break loose” if Manchester City won the title this season amid their guilty verdict case.

City are facing a period of uncertainty after being found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the Prem’s financial rules over a nine-season period, and the majority of charges in relation to its failure to co-operate with the league’s investigation.



The club were accused of “systematically breaking Premier League Rules for nearly a decade”.

In an explosive report into City’s 130 charges, it was also found they had hid £900million in “sham” commercial deals.



City have always denied wrongdoing and have vowed to prove their innocence after lodging an appeal.

There have been suggestions the club could receive a hefty points deduction or massive fine, but City’s desire to fight the case could complicate matters.

But Neville believes the situation must be finalised by February or March to avoid the risk of City lifting the league title.

He told Overlap Daily, via SkyBet: “It’ll be very difficult to watch Manchester City win the league this year.

“If Manchester City are holding that Premier League title up in May, I think all hell will break loose. I think this will have to be dealt with by February, March.”

Neville also claimed City would fail the Prem’s Owners and Directors’ Test thanks to his knowledge of the requirements through owning Salford City.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

He added: “Because I’m an owner and a director, and I know the actual criteria for that test.

“If it’s the same test that I have to follow to be a director and owner, they’re going to fail it. Simple as that.”

City travel to Liverpool on Sunday in their first game since their bombshell guilty verdicts.

And co-host Mark Goldbridge – a diehard United fan – wants bitter rivals Liverpool to beat them because it will be a “win for football”.

He said: “Liverpool on Sunday. I can’t believe I’m saying this, but I want Liverpool to win.



“I want Liverpool to win because I think it’s a win for football.”

City boss Enzo Maresca was defiant in his pre-match press conference this week and claimed the club would win their appeal against the Prem.

He added: “There is an ongoing process and in this moment I completely trust the club.

Sports.title: Granit Xhaka in angry altercation with fan at market who shouts ‘COVID’ at him after conviction for fake certificate
Sports.content:
Next

GRANIT XHAKA was left fuming after a fan appeared to heckle him in a market following his fake Covid certificate conviction.

The Sunderland midfielder, 34, was slapped with a suspended fine by Swiss authorities after he was found to have obtained a fake coronavirus vaccination certificate while still an Arsenal player in 2022.



Xhaka had pulled out of his nation’s recent Nations League clashes amid the criminal investigation by the public prosecutor’s office in the Swiss city of Lucerne, though he avoided jail time and apologised for what he called an error of judgement due to concerns over the vaccine.

However, while authorities deemed to only fine him with a relatively light £136,000 for the forged certificate, one apparent Newcastle fan didn’t let him get away with it as easily.



A video on social media went viral which appeared to show the Black Cats captain being approached while he was in a shopping centre.

The person recording the video was seen making an explicit gesture at the start of the clip, before someone is heard saying: “Of course Geordies are going to shout at you.”



Another voice is then heard shouting: “Covid,” towards Xhaka, as he is led away by someone he was out with, presumably his wife of almost a decade, Leonita.

The person recording continued to heckle Xhaka by saying “Covid”, with the midfielder seen trying to then approach them.

He seemed to cool down when another man spoke to him and shook his hand, before Xhaka walked off.

The heckling did continue but this time moved on to saying: “Bruno,” referencing former Newcastle star Bruno Guimaraes‘ winner against Sunderland in the League Cup for Arsenal last month.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Xhaka released a statement on his suspended fine on social media, saying: “A few weeks ago, I spoke personally here and said that I would take responsibility for my decision. I stand by that.

“After I gave a full statement to the public prosecutor’s office, the public prosecutor’s decision has now been issued.

“I was sentenced by summary judgment for obtaining a false certification to a suspended fine of 50 daily rates of CHF 3,000 each, with a probationary period of two years.

“This means: The sentence will not be carried out if I do not commit any offenses during this period. I have already paid the court costs.

“I accept the decision and take responsibility for my actions. Thank you for the many messages of support over the past few weeks. They mean a lot to me.”



Xhaka is set to be available for Sunderland’s clash against Brighton on Saturday at 3pm.

Sports.title: Daughter of PSG manager Luis Enrique is passenger in car crash that killed motorcyclist – as cops probe Brit driver
Sports.content:
SMASH TRAGEDY Daughter of PSG manager Luis Enrique is passenger in car crash that killed motorcyclist – as cops probe Brit driver







Next

A FOOTBALL manager’s daughter and British horse rider have been involved in a car crash that killed a motorcyclist.

A motorcyclist, 20, has tragically died after colliding with a car containing Sira Martinez – the 26-year-old daughter of Paris Saint-Germain manager Luis Enrique – and a unnamed British Olympic equestrian, 41.



The fatal accident occurred on Thursday evening on the N-332 near Oliva, an hour south of Valencia, Spain on Thursday evening.

Paramedics rushed to the scene but were unable to save the victim’s life, whilst Martinez and the horse rider were unharmed.



Police have launched an investigation into the tragic crash.

According to local reports, the unnamed Brit was driving the car and passed drug and alcohol tests at the scene.



The Guardia Civil suspect an illegal driving manoeuvre, and the equestrian has been placed under investigation for causing death by negligence, says Todo Alicante.

A Civil Guard spokesman said this afternoon he had no information he could make available to the press.

Martinez is Luis Enrique’s first and only daughter, after his youngest daughter, Xana, passed away in August 2019.

She sadly died aged nine after battling a rare type of bone cancer.



Enrique also has a 28-year-old son, Pacho.

Martinez is a Spanish model and professional show jumper who used to date Spanish international and former Barcelona frontman Ferran Torres, who signed for PSG after he became a World Cup winner this summer.

She started a long-distance relationship with Torres while he was still playing for Manchester City and they continued dating after he moved to Barcelona.



The couple broke up in May 2023 after more than a year and a half together, allegedly due to Sira wanting to “focus on her sporting career.”

In April 2024 Sira, who has more than 400,000 followers on Instagram, was said to have been spotted in the arms of Atletico Madrid player Robin Le Normand, who despite being born in France chose to play for the Spain national team.

Sports.title: Rio Ferdinand jokily tries to STEAL Carlos Tevez’s Premier League medal as they reunite after Man City guilty verdict

RIO FERDINAND took matters into his own hands after demanding the Premier League to strip Manchester City of their titles – by attempting to snatch Carlos Tevez’s winner’s medal.

An independent commission sent shockwaves through football when they found the Sky Blues guilty of breaching financial rules.



And Ferdinand, 47, wants City to have their Premier League crowns erased from history.

It would allow the legendary defender to bag another medal after Manchester United finished just behind their fierce foes in the 2011/12 season.



Following the guilty verdict, Ferdinand took to social media and wrote: “Another Premier League medal to be added to the cabinet.”

And the England icon was involved in a comical stand-off when he reunited with pal Tevez.



Ferdinand jokingly tried to STEAL the ex-striker’s top-flight winner’s medal.

The six-time Premier League title winner shared a snap of Tevez, 42, clinging onto his prized possession on X.

Alongside the photo – and another showing them going up against each other in a fiery derby – Ferdinand wrote: “It’s mine… give me that! What a player… what a guy! We missed you!”

The pair were Old Trafford team-mates between 2007 and 2009 – before Tevez made the shock move from United to City.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

And the marksman notched four goals in 13 appearances as City were crowned the Premier League champions in 2012.

The Argentine also clinched the FA Cup and Community Shield during his spell at the Etihad.

But Tevez is in danger of the trophy wins being voided following City’s guilty verdict.

Sky Blues chiefs have launched a desperate appeal and are adamant they will clear their name.



There is an awareness they are on course to be slapped with huge sanctions if that falls through and the initial verdict stands.

But boss Enzo Maresca defiantly vowed the serial winners will have the charges overturned.

Sports.title: Premier League executives name one Man City punishment they're 'not expecting'
Sports.content:
Premier League executives name one Man City punishment they're 'not expecting'

There is a lot of talk over potential punishments for Man City after they were found guilty of 114 breaches of Premier League financial rules

View 2 Images City are appealing against the guilty verdict on 114 breaches of financial rules. (Image: Molly Darlington - WSL/WSL Football via Getty Images)

Premier League club chiefs are not expecting Manchester City to be directly thrown out of the league if the guilty verdict against breaches of financial rules is upheld. City are appealing the verdict, which rules them as guilty of 114 breaches over a nine-year period.

‌



‌



The three-person panel ruled that City artificially inflated their revenue through ‘sham’ sponsorship deals that were funded by the club owners, something that is now allowed under the financial regulations. It’s something that City strongly deny.

‌



There has been a lot of talk over what sort of punishment could be handed to City should their appeal against the verdict be unsuccessful. The sanction will be decided by the same three-person panel that delivered the initial verdict, with the Premier League able to give their recommendation.

‌



The Premier League handbook states that punishments can range from fines to points deductions and even expulsion from the league. But latest reports suggest that the latter is not expected.

Liverpool dealt double injury blow ahead of Man City clash as Andoni Iraola offers update READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

The Athletic reports that several executives from Premier League clubs are not expecting the sanction to be direct expulsion, due to relying on the backing of clubs. For City to be thrown out of the Premier League, 14 of the clubs would have to vote in favour of the sanction.

‌



That would not be the case with other punishments, including fines or points deductions. Another option for the commission could be to recommend a deduction that would effectively guarantee relegation from the division and into the Championship, rather than kicking City out directly.

There is, however, a fear that a huge points deduction would undermine the league’s competitive integrity and reduce the television product on offer. It could leave City effectively playing games that won’t have an impact on their future, as they could already be relegated via the deduction.

View 2 Images Man City boss Enzo Maresca. (Image: Tom Flathers/Manchester City FC via Getty Images)

‌



There is also a worry in the Championship that a relegation for City would allow them to spend just one season outside of the Premier League before earning promotion back. That would therefore take up one of the promotion spots on offer to other clubs competing for a place in the top division.

Speaking about the possibility of managing City in the Championship, or League one, Enzo Maresca said: “I won the Championship with Leicester.

"So in case of League One, we’re going to see. We are thinking about something that we don’t know.”

Article continues below

There are some arguments from a Premier League club executive that City should receive a punishment that would see them handed points deductions over multiple seasons. That would therefore hamper the club’s chances of qualifying for European competitions over a few seasons, with financial implications.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo 'suspended' by Portugal after storming out of Nations League camp
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo 'suspended' by Portugal after storming out of Nations League camp

Cristiano Ronaldo penned a lengthy statement just days after his stunning walkout on the Portuguese national team and it appears that the veteran forward is set to be hit with a lengthy ban

View 2 Images Ronaldo is set to be hit with a ban by the Portuguese Football Federation (Image: Getty Images)

Cristiano Ronaldo has been slapped with a suspension by the Portuguese FA for his angry walkout. The veteran forward decided to leave the national team camp following a row with boss Jorge Jesus.

‌



‌



Their argument seemingly revolved around the amount of minutes Ronaldo played during the international break. Despite having apologised in a lengthy statement, in which he suggested that he should be punished by the Portuguese FA, it appears that Ronaldo has already met the consequences.

‌



Portuguese Football Federation rules have automatically triggered a suspension and a disciplinary council will now decide on the length of ban that Ronaldo will have to serve, which could be anything between one and six months.

‌



Anything longer than a month would see Ronaldo ruled out of his nation’s Nations League fixtures against Denmark and Wales next month. The disciplinary council will now consider all aspects including Ronaldo’s apology when assessing a potential ban, albeit ESPN have suggested that a shorter ban is more likely.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Speaking on Tuesday, Ronaldo said: “I also owe an apology to my national team teammates for having left the camp. Despite the absolute breach of trust in the coach’s word, as those who witnessed these conversations can attest, I should not have done it.

"The responsibility is exclusively mine. I apologise to the Portuguese people once again, but the breaking of one’s word has, for me, a defining impact. I felt that, from that point on, my remaining would only harm the working group, and I did what I have always said I would do if I did not feel useful: I packed my bags and left.

"The consequence of this act of mine must be assessed and punished by the Portuguese Football Federation. I understand that the punishment should have no mitigating factors. I am not just any player; I am team captain, and that constitutes an aggravating factor.

‌



View 2 Images Ronaldo walked out on the Portuguese national team (Image: Getty Images)

"I have already apologised, but I know that attitudes must have consequences. Anyone who is in football as I am knows that, regardless of each person’s status, the rules are the same for everyone.”

Boss Jesus responded in the aftermath and said: “I read the statement and now I do (like I do) every day. I’m going to the federation to work, think about the team.”

Article continues below

In all, Ronaldo has made 234 appearances for Portugal since making his debut back in 2014. In that time, he has scored a record 146 goals.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi set for reunion as former team-mate asks them to play TOGETHER
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi set for reunion as former team-mate asks them to play TOGETHER

Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi could line up together in the twilight of their respective careers thanks to a former team-mate

View 2 Images Former rivals Messi and Ronaldo could take to the field as team-mates (Image: Josep LAGO / AFP via Getty Images)

For years, Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi did battle on opposite sides of the Real Madrid and Barcelona rivalry. This year, though, the pair could take the unusual step of playing on the same team.

‌



‌



It's all down to one of the men who played with both icons at the highest level. Carlos Tevez spent two seasons with Ronaldo at Manchester United in between two World Cups in the same Argentina side as Messi.

‌



The former Boca Juniors star, 42, is set for a farewell match at the Buenos Aires club's home of the Bombonera later this year, having never received a proper goodbye at the end of his playing career. A date just before Christmas has been floated and Tevez wants Messi and Ronaldo to take to the field as team-mates.

‌



According to Infobae, December 20 is a possible date for the match. The publication reports that Juan Roman Riquelme, another member of Argentina's 2006 World Cup squad, has already signed off on the use of the stadium in his capacity as Boca president.

TyC Sports reports that the hope is for the match to be played between one team comprising Tevez and his friends from the football world and his old neighbourhood, and another representing the 'Rest of the World'. Despite hailing from Argentina, Messi would join Ronaldo on the Rest of the World team.

‌



In April 2025, Tevez outlined his hopes for getting Messi and Ronaldo on board. "I'll go get them myself." he said. "We'll play this game, but we'll have to see when.

"It's not easy. It would be beautiful to close the cycle with a tribute game. It would be beautiful at the end of the year." At the time he had yet to speak to Riquelme but now has the permission of the former midfield maestro.

He has also mentioned other potential participants, though none have been confirmed. Edwin Van der Sar, Gianluigi Buffon, Leonardo Bonucci, Rio Ferdinand, Patrice Evra, Andrea Pirlo and Paul Scholes are among the former Manchester United and Juventus colleagues who he was hopeful of convincing to play.

‌



View 2 Images Tevez played with Messi for Argentina and Ronaldo for Manchester United (Image: Chris McGrath/Getty Images)

The exact date of the match could hinge on what happens with Boca in the remainder of the 2026 season. Rodolfo Arruabarrena's team are still fighting on three fronts and if they top the clausura league table they would take part in the Trofeo de Campeones on December 19.

Tevez had three separate spells with boyhood club Boca Juniors during his playing career. He made his senior debut for the club as a teenager and played more than 250 times for the team overall.

Article continues below

The ex-striker has twice returned to the Bombonera as a manager since retiring in 2022. He earned a 0-0 draw with Rosario Central in August 2022 and lost 2-0 with Talleres in November 2025.
