Sports.title: Michael Carrick takes Man City charges 'personally' as Man Utd boss makes appeal demand
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick takes Man City charges 'personally' as Man Utd boss makes appeal demand

Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick has opened up on how Manchester City's charges has impacted him, after they were found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules

View 3 Images Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick speaking in a press conference (Image: Getty Images)

Michael Carrick has admitted Manchester City's guilty verdict has impacted him "personally" and has called for the situation to be resolved as soon as possible.

‌



‌



On September 30, the Premier League confirmed that City had been found guilty on all charges relating to breaches of its financial regulations between 2009/10 and 2017/18. It was revealed that City had artificially inflated revenue by more than £900million through so-called 'sham' sponsorship deals.

‌



City, however, have strongly denied any wrongdoing and lodged an appeal against the ruling on October 1. In an official statement, the club insisted they are "innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League" and say they have "a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence" to back their position.

‌



£65m Man City signing hints at return to old club days after 114 charges verdict READ MORE :

With the Premier League back in full swing following the extended international break, Manchester United head coach Carrick has spoken in public for the first time since City were found guilty.

Carrick was part of the United squad that finished second to City in 2011/12 and then again in 2017/18, and could be in line for another Premier League medal if the Blues are stripped of all their titles.

Speaking in his pre-Tottenham press conference, Carrick said: "Difficult to say in many ways. It's thrown up a lot of questions," Carrick said. "It's ongoing, and there's only so much I can say. I have my own questions about it because it has affected me personally. We'll have to see how it goes. The sooner it gets sorted for everyone, the better.

‌



"There's no getting that back [winning moments] in any direction. The feeling we all crave is coming out on top. That sums it up. Whatever is done in the past, is done in the past.

"Speed is essential, as I just said. That's obvious for me to sit here and say that. There are so many angles, but speed is essential for everybody to be clear, to deal with it, and move on. It's unprecedented to be in this situation at this level. We all need to know what is going to happen."

View 3 Images Michael Carrick has fumed at Manchester City's guilty verdict (Image: Getty)

‌



When asked if he would want to receive an additional Premier League medal, Carrick added: "I think at the moment, as it's still not finalised, I think I'll hold that one until later on.

"I think regardless of anything, a medal anyway, in any sport in history, I think the later on you get the medal [it doesn't mean as much]. It's the moment that you strive for to win and achieve in that moment, so the medal here or there, not getting blasé about it, but that doesn't bring the feeling of when you initially win or you don't win. That's essentially what we're all in it for."

Arsenal head coach Mikel Arteta, meanwhile, delivered a more toned-down response to a question asked about his former club. "I fully understand the question but I think it's really important that we respect the process, the timelines and it's still an ongoing process that's not resolved as it's been appealed," the Spaniard said.

‌



View 3 Images Mikel Arteta and Pep Guardiola (Image: Getty)

Asked if the situation will inspire City, Arteta added: "I don't know, it's something that's not in our hands, we're preparing to play Leeds and be in the best condition and that's what we'll do tomorrow."

Arteta was appointed as Pep Guardiola's assistant head coach at City in July 2016 and spent three years there before returning to Arsenal in December 2019. During his time at the Etihad Stadium, Arteta helped the club win the Premier League twice, the Carabao Cup on two occasions and the FA Cup.

‌



Liverpool are City's next opponents on Sunday and Reds head coach Andoni Iraola was asked about the situation in his press conference. "I think uncertainty is not good for anyone involved but the process is ongoing so we have to be patient," Iraola said.

Xabi Alonso, the Chelsea head coach, was another Premier League manager asked about City in his press conference, as his side prepare to host Bournemouth this weekend.

"For sure, it's a decision but we need to be patient," Alonso said. "We need to wait until the final sanctions from the panel. They are independent enough to assess all of the situations. I am not an expert. We need to respect the decisions and be patient."

Sports.title: Arne Slot takes first job since Liverpool sacking after hitting back at speculation
Sports.content:
Arne Slot takes first job since Liverpool sacking after hitting back at speculation

Arne Slot has made it clear where he sees his future after a whirlwind two-year spell at Anfield

View 3 Images Arne Slot is back in work (Image: Newhouse Media/MB Media, Getty Images)

Arne Slot has landed his first role since being dismissed as Liverpool manager. The Dutchman was relieved of his duties at the end of last season after a hugely underwhelming title defence, which saw the Reds finish fifth and only just qualify for the Champions League.

‌



‌



He was touted for the Netherlands national team job, only to rubbish that speculation and insist he was focused on club management. The Netherlands had been searching for a new manager after Ronald Koeman stepped down following their last-32 defeat by Morocco at the World Cup.

‌



While he awaits his next opportunity in the dugout, Slot has been added to UEFA's Technical Observer Group. Joining numerous well-known figures in the game, he will analyse the Champions League, Europa League and Conference League.

‌



UEFA says the group will use "stats and video assistance, enabling them to deliver detailed reports on the latest developments in coaching, which are shared among the footballing community to give a dynamic account of the state of the game."

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Regarding Slot's appointment to the group, European football's governing body added: "Slot made his name at Feyenoord, reaching the UEFA Conference League final in 2022 and winning an Eredivisie title and Dutch Cup in the following two campaigns.

‌



Milos Kerkez gives Andoni Iraola verdict as Arne Slot's issues at Liverpool become clearer READ MORE :

Arne Slot immediately lined up for new job after Eddie Howe's bombshell Newcastle exit READ MORE :

"He joined Liverpool in 2024 and immediately guided the club to their second Premier League trophy in five years before departing Anfield this summer."

Also among the group are former Liverpool bosses Rafa Benitez and Roy Hodgson. They are joined by Gareth Southgate, Sean Dyche, former Manchester United managers Erik ten Hag and Ole Gunnar Solskjaer and ex-Tottenham bosses Thomas Frank and Ange Postecoglou.

View 3 Images Rafa Benitez is part of the UEFA panel (Image: Nick Potts/PA Wire)

‌



Slot has made no secret of his desire to return to club management eventually. Distancing himself from reports linking him with the Netherlands vacancy, he told Voetbal International: "That speculation is incorrect. We simply never got to that stage of the talks.

"At this stage of my career, I prefer to see myself on the training field with my players every day, something that is simply not possible in the same way with a national team.

View 3 Images Roy Hodgson brings his decades of experience to the group (Image: Getty Images)

Article continues below

"I have a lot of respect for the national team and for the KNVB [Dutch Football Association] and can only be positive about the professional way in which the talks went that week. For now, I believe that club football still has a lot to offer me."

The Dutch role subsequently went to Spanish football icon Xavi, who put pen to paper on a four-year deal running through to the end of the 2030 World Cup.

Sports.title: Sir Harry Redknapp to make film debut in movie about day he pulled 'mouthy' West Ham fan from stands to play
Sports.content:
Sir Harry Redknapp to make film debut in movie about day he pulled 'mouthy' West Ham fan from stands to play

The legendary West Ham boss, 79, appears in a cameo in the new move Halftime Hero - playing a stall seller flogging traditional jellied eels and cockles to fans

View 6 Images Harry Redknapp making his big screen debut (Image: CLICK NEWS AND MEDIA)

Harry Redknapp is set to make his big screen debut in a film about the time he plucked a mouthy fan from the crowd and put him on the pitch.

‌



‌



The legendary West Ham boss, 79, appears in a cameo in the new move Halftime Hero - playing a stall seller flogging traditional jellied eels and cockles to fans. Harry was pictured on set outside Leyton Orient Football Club, which has been transformed by movie bosses to double as the Hammers old Upton Park home.

‌



The movie tells the incredible true story of the day he famously picked supporter Steve ‘Pringle’ Davies from the stands and put him on the football pitch during a 1994 pre-season friendly. Steve incredibly went on to score as West Ham won 4-0.

‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 6 Images Former West Ham boss Harry was pictured on set outside Leyton Orient Football Club (Image: CLICK NEWS AND MEDIA)

Man City intervene in rare Erling Haaland interview as questions on 114 charges 'refused' READ MORE :

Everton put up for sale as owners The Friedkin Group set condition for takeover READ MORE :

Eddie Marsan plays a younger Harry in the movie, with MobLand star Anson Boon taking the role of Steve and Ellie Bamber playing his girlfriend Penny. In interviews about the day Steve, who grew up in Rushden, near Northampton, told how he started supporting West Ham after watching them beat Fulham in the 1975 FA Cup final.

‌



He used to make a 182 mile round trip to watch the team, saying: “I wore the shirt with pride and would travel to see the games as often as I could. Trevor Brooking was my hero. I had hundreds of photos of Brooking.”

View 6 Images West Ham fan Steve Davies playing after Harry Redknapp pulled him from the stands

Recalling the pre-season match at Oxford - he told how he received a call from his pal, Chuck, asking should they go to the game. He told The Guardian: “Chunk called me up one day and said, ‘We got a pre-season game over at Oxford – fancy it?’ We liked to get a couple of games in early. We get withdrawal symptoms when the season finishes in May. I very rarely missed a game, and I fancied a little away trip to Oxford anyways.”

‌



He told how he was with his friends, and partner, sitting by a fence with the travelling West Ham fans when Harry, then assistant manager, emerged from the dressing room and greeted them. Steve said: “Harry being Harry, he talks to people. He said hello and all that. A few fans exchanged pleasantries. But there’s no airs and graces with Harry.”

View 6 Images West Ham fan Steve Davies who had been hurling insults at Hammers Lee Chapman got called into action

Once the game kicked off he was shouting at their centre forward, he said: “Lee Chapman was up front for us, on the edge of the area, and he went up against a little guy from Oxford. Lee towered over him, but came down on his a**e.”

‌



He said: “If you’re watching your team and someone does something really daft, you won’t leave them alone for a couple of minutes. I think Chapman lost the ball again, he got tackled and got a cut on his shin. He went down, and I was shouting, ‘Come on! Get up, you donkey’.”

View 6 Images Harry on set in his jellied eels van (Image: CLICK NEWS AND MEDIA)

Harry told the TV show A League of Their Own: “There’s a guy next to the dug-out, and he’s got West Ham tattooed all over his arms and neck, he’s got the earrings. After two minutes, he started on me.” He said Steve was shouting: “We ain’t got that Lee Chapman up front do we – I ain’t coming every week if he’s playing.”

‌



Harry said: “Half-time I made five substitutions, and we only had the bare 11 out – I was running out of players. Then we got another injury, so I said to this guy in the crowd, ‘Oi, can you play as good as you talk?’”

The rest of the tale is football folklore which is told in the film. Steve said: “I slung a leg over the barrier and Harry walked me down the tunnel. I couldn’t believe it. Inside the dressing room, the players were sat down resting at half-time.”

View 6 Images Harry has a cameo in football movie Halftime Hero (Image: CLICK NEWS AND MEDIA)

‌



He told how Harry substituted Lee Chapman off and him on: “We come on up the tunnel and I still thought Harry was having a laugh with me. I didn’t think I was actually gonna get on, or I thought I might get a minute or two as a joke. I didn’t come out of Oxford’s half I was playing up front with Trevor Morley, goal-hanging! It was quick football. This was a step up from Sunday league, to say the least. Oxford play Saturday football – I played Sunday football, pub football.”

While admitting he was massively out of his depth, Steve tells the story of his goal: “Suddenly, we were on the attack. The ball went out wide – I’m sure it was Matty Holmes on the wing – and we pushed forward. I had two defenders in front of me and I was just sprinting forward, I think. I just hit it. I hit it like nothing else. Know what I mean? I belted it. It was like time stopped still – it was the greatest moment of my life.”

West Ham ended up winning the game 4-0 - but the kit manager wouldn’t let him keep his Number 3 shirt as they needed it of the next match against Newcastle.

Article continues below

The film is being produced by Sir Ridley Scott's Scott Free, alongside Live Nation Studios and The Saga Company, with Ole Sanders writing and directing. Harry’s cameo marks his first film role - more than three decades after the extraordinary football moment that inspired the movie.

Sports.title: Keely Hodgkinson defends 'sexy' outfit she'll be banned from wearing for Team GB
Sports.content:
Keely Hodgkinson defends 'sexy' outfit she'll be banned from wearing for Team GB

Keely Hodgkinson has hintered she could wear something similar at the next Olympics - but she may not be allowed

View 3 Images Keely Hodgkinson's black catsuit set pulses racing (Image: Shaun Botterill/Getty Images)

Keely Hodgkinson and her coaching team have defended her "sexy" catsuit that she'll be banned from wearing on Team GB duty. Hodgkinson unveiled the all-black Nike Speedsuit as she stormed to victory in the 800 metres at the all-female Athlos meet in London last month.

‌



‌



The Catwoman-esque outfit sparked a flurry of debate across the sporting world, with many questioning whether it was within the rules. Nothing has emerged to indicate it falls foul of regulations, and Hodgkinson has hinted she could wear something similar at the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles.

‌



However, as it stands, she would not be allowed to wear the same Nike suit when representing her country at events like the World Championships and the Olympics. While athletes can wear shoes and spikes from different brands, that doesn't extend to attire.

‌



Team GB is currently supplied by Nike's rival Adidas as part of a deal that runs until the 2032 Olympics in Brisbane. A Team GB spokesperson said: "Supported by our partners and in tandem with our sports, we have always worked to provide athlete-centred and innovative kit that supports our teams to perform at their best at both the Summer and Winter Games.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

"We're confident and excited about what's ahead and the developments we're working towards for future Games, including Los Angeles 2028.

‌



A UK Athletics spokesperson added: "The speed suit Keely Hodgkinson wore at Athlos was a bespoke Nike design created specifically for her. We are in regular dialogue with Nike regarding all aspects of performance apparel and will continue to assess any innovations that could benefit our athletes in future championship environments."

Keely Hodgkinson banned from wearing 'sexy' outfit after causing a stir READ MORE :

Addressing the outfit, Hodgkinson said it made her feel "sexy" and as if she were wearing nothing. She said: "I wanted to be comfortable but I wanted to feel a little bit sexy. The back's open and that makes it feel really cool. It feels like I'm wearing nothing to be honest."

Crucially, Hodgkinson has the full backing of her coaches, Ron and Jenny Meadows. She told Athletics Weekly: "Keely is an innovator, she's always wanted to do things differently, and she's a big lover of fashion.

‌



View 3 Images She wouldn't be allowed to wear the outfit when representing her country (Image: Shaun Botterill/Getty Images)

"Nike were so respectful of us as coaches because they obviously wanted us to be really, really comfortable with it. Because at the end of the day, we think about performance, and it's not just what you look like.

"You've got to think: Is it faster or is it just a gimmick? You've actually got to walk out in front of an audience the first time and you've got to win in that thing. It's a statement piece."

Article continues below

View 3 Images Hodgkinson in her Team GB attire (Image: Martin Rickett/PA Wire)

Hodgkinson is confident the suit complies with legal requirements, and while aerodynamics were paramount, she did secure one crucial concession.

She said: "The science was like technically with the air drag you're slower with your hair out, but I was like, 'That's a non-negotiable. My hair is staying out.' I'm very much, 'Look good, feel good.'"

Sports.title: Five Premier League things NOT including Man City charges to follow this weekend
Sports.content:
After three weeks away, the Premier League is back this weekend!

In case you hadn't heard, everything has changed after Manchester City were found guilty of breaking the league's financial rules over a nine-year period. City maintain their innocence and have appealed against the verdict, but are facing serious consequences which include relegation.

The fallout to the bombshell news will dominate proceedings this weekend, with City heading to Anfield to play Liverpool on Sunday. But what if you're already sick of the debate around City's cheating and just want to get stuck into some untainted top-flight action?!

Well, thankfully, there is plenty of that too. Here Mirror Football picks out five of the best storylines to keep an eye on.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Can Arsenal bounce back vs Leeds?

It may feel like years ago, but Arsenal were actually played off the pitch in their last competitive football match. Brighton produced one of the best performances in their history to smash the Gunners 3-0 on - it says here - September 19.

"There were certain basics you need to accomplish in football, especially in the Premier League that we were very far from," Mikel Arteta fumed post-match. He's had ages to ponder his approach to Saturday's early kick-off against Leeds, so expect a reaction.

‌



Kai Havertz was injured on Germany duty, so Arteta could be forced into starting Viktor Gyokeres up front. Leeds are unbeaten in the Premier League this season and it should be a real spectacle packed to the brim with high pressing and intensity - the perfect match to welcome back club football.

View 5 Images Arsenal were played off the pitch by Brighton three weeks ago (Image: Luke Hastings/Wired Photos/Shutterstock)

Battle of under-pressure bosses

We haven't yet had a Premier League managerial sacking this season, but - as ever - one isn't far off. Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa is still without a win, but the pressure is highest at Manchester United and Tottenham, who meet on Saturday evening at Old Trafford.

Spurs have been woeful this season, which is merely a continuation of the past two seasons when they've finished 17th, but the problem for Roberto De Zerbi is that expectations have skyrocketed after over £320million was spent on new players. Their 3-2 defeat against previously winless Aston Villa before the break was utterly miserable and not many fans were there to see their first two league goals of the season, which came late as scant consolation for their ineptitude.

‌



They face a United side who scraped a draw at Fulham before the break. Michael Carrick has transitioned from happy-go-lucky interim boss to gloomy full-time manager and while he still has some credit in the bank, Sir Jim's axe is always looming. Old Trafford expects.

View 5 Images Roberto De Zerbi and Michael Carrick are under huge pressure (Image: Getty Images)

Are Brighton the real deal?

The Seagulls are the top scorers in the Premier League this season with 16 goals in five games and are always an entertaining watch. Fabian Hurzeler is doing a wonderful job, with their brand of ultra-aggressive, high-pressing, position-rotation football seeing them punch above their weight.

Brighton, who will begin their Conference League campaign next week against Lithuanian side FK Kauno Zalgiris, head to Sunderland in third place on Saturday. How long can they keep up this brand of football when playing twice per week? Surely it's unsustainable. We're about to find out. Whatever happens, it should be fun.

‌



View 5 Images Pascal Gross has been a standout performer for Brighton this season (Image: (Photo by Molly Darlington/Getty Images))

The Premier League's newest rivalry

Fans of beef away from the pitch should enjoy Crystal Palace vs Nottingham Forest on Sunday. Oliver Glasner is expecting a frosty reaction on his return to Selhurst Park. "I have to accept the booing," he told the Guardian in the build-up to the fixture.

That provides a nice context to what is essentially a mid-table match. Then there's the fact that Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis is suing Palace for defamation relating to a banner unfurled by the club's supporters which showed him holding a gun to Morgan Gibbs-White's head.

“I know I will be, but I don’t want to be in the middle of all the comments and the stories about this game," Glasner pleaded. I personally think that would make for a much more interesting occasion.

‌



View 5 Images Oliver Glasner returns to Selhurst Park (Image: Jon Hobley/MI News/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Moyes soldiering on

David Moyes is working miracles at Everton, where he survived a farcical summer transfer window, which left his squad threadbare, and somehow managed to oversee an unbeaten start to the season. The veteran manager is the perfect man for the backs-against-the-wall siege mentality role - and Friday brought yet more distractions for him.

The Friedkin Group have put Everton up for sale after just two years. While they claim to be happy to wait patiently for the right buyer, the announcement will undoubtedly cause even more uncertainty for the team, who face Hull on Sunday. Moyes will relish the challenge.

Sports.title: Musical Times stays unbeaten in Fillies' Mile at Newmarket
Sports.content:
Musical Times overcame traffic problems to maintain her unbeaten record in the bet365 Fillies' Mile at Newmarket.

Charlie Appleby's youngster had looked a top-class prospect in winning her first two starts on the July Course and at Yarmouth, and completed her hat-trick with facile victory in the May Hill Stakes at Doncaster last month.

Subsequent 1000 Guineas heroine Desert Flower completed the May Hill-Fillies' Mile double two years ago for Appleby and William Buick and Musical Times was the 4/9 favourite to follow suit.

It was not entirely straightforward for odds-on backers, with Buick struggling to find a gap, but once the split did come she quickly went through the gears to beat Aidan O'Brien's Haven by a length.

Appleby said: "I'm delighted and I have to say after two furlongs we just had to hold our breath a little bit and see what was happening, but William was on the class filly in the race and he knew it himself. He was just trying to find those gaps and when he did she quickened up smartly.

"The rest were riding to beat one filly - ours, but credit to her and William they toughed it out and when she found the gaps she did what was needed.

"When she got the run upsides the eventual second she was always going to attack the hill well and the one thing we've seen is she always gallops out strongly.

"She had to work a bit hard there but she will have learned plenty and what I liked about her today was she went to post well and is still learning.

"The fillies division is strong this year and there's some lovely fillies around but they look to be all sprinting fillies while this girl sees out the mile well.

"She was seeing the dip for the first time and probably wanted easier ground and it is nice if they can see the dip.

"But there was no chance of her seeing it when she was rolling down and you could see that rounded action looking a bit enhanced here with the ground being tighter than Doncaster and not being able to see that dip bless her. But I think it's a performance you can mark up a little bit."

Musical Times was made 5/2 from 4/1 with BOYLE Sports for next year's 1000 Guineas and Appleby will take a tried and tested route to the opening fillies' Classic of the year via his usual Craven meeting racecourse gallop.

Appleby added: "There's no doubt about it she needed her class to get her home today but from what we saw I think she is entitled to be one of the favourites for the Guineas. She's done it over the mile and sees it out well.

"We'll put her away now and we'll probably just come here for a racecourse gallop and then on to the Guineas hopefully.

"I would say she is a miler through and through at the minute and she has a lot of natural pace and quickens.

"She could maybe get further and you don't always need to be a proper mile-and-a-half horse at Epsom sometimes and if you are miler who can get a mile and a quarter you might be able to get the job done."

While Appleby holds some reservations about middle-distance possibilities for Musical Times, it is those distances O'Brien feels Haven will thrive over next season after the Dundalk maiden winner took the leap into Group company firmly in her stride when second.

O'Brien said: "She's only a baby, is progressing lovely and I'm delighted with her run.

"We have always thought she was a nice filly and she's going to be lovely next season.

"She's progressing and the other filly is a big mature filly, so we couldn't be happier.

"I think she's probably an Oaks filly, a mile and a quarter and a mile and a half. She's going to be a middle-distance filly."

Sports.title: Antonelli casts further doubt over performance of Mercedes upgrades
Sports.content:
World Championship leader Kimi Antonelli cast further doubt over the performance of Mercedes' recent upgrade package as he explained his car was "very difficult" to drive during Sprint Qualifying in Singapore.

After the long-awaited upgrades failed to deliver improved performance when they debuted at last weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, Mercedes decided to compare different specifications of the car in Singapore.

Antonelli is running the latest version, which included an additional front wing that had not been available in Malaysia, while George Russell is running the pre-Malaysia version of the car that he won the Azerbaijan Grand Prix in last month.

The early evidence was concerning for Mercedes as Russell finished second to Max Verstappen in the shortened qualifying session, with Antonelli more than half a second down on his team-mate in seventh.

Asked whether he was surprised by the performance, Antonelli said: "Yes and no, to be fair. Already in FP1 I was struggling.

"Still a lot to understand about this package. The car is very difficult, very unpredictable, and very difficult to put a lap together.

"It's a shame because I was coming with high hopes, but so far it's been very difficult."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from Sprint Qualifying at the 2026 Singapore Grand Prix

While both Antonelli and Mercedes have built extremely commanding leads in the drivers' and constructors' standings and are near certainties for this year's titles, a lack of clarity in future development direction could have consequences for next season.

"I think it's going to be a difficult weekend unless we can pull something out," Antonelli continued.

"But other than that it's going to be very tricky. I don't really see where we can find seven tenths.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News' Craig Slater explains the FIA 'human error' which caused a power disparity between the cars during Sprint Qualifying at the Singapore Grand Prix

"But you never know. Maybe (Antonelli's engineer) Bono (Peter Bonnington) and the engineers are going to find something in the car.

"And for sure, I'm going to try to improve a little bit the driving, and then we'll see where we'll end up."

Singapore GP Sprint Starting Grid: Top 10 1) Max Verstappen, Red Bull



2) George Russell, Mercedes



3) Charles Leclerc, Ferrari



4) Oscar Piastri, McLaren



5) Lando Norris, McLaren



6) Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari



7) Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes



8) Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls



9) Isack Hadjar, Red Bull



10) Pierre Gasly, Alpine

Wolff suggests Mercedes may rethink upgrade strategy

Mercedes' major Malaysia upgrade was their first significant new package since May's Canadian Grand Prix and team principal Toto Wolff suggested the Silver Arrows may bring upgrades in smaller steps in the future.

"We felt that the right strategic decision was to work towards a bigger one and then introduce it. Obviously, with the risk of if it doesn't work as you've anticipated, it's just quite difficult to dial yourself out and understand why it hasn't worked," he said.

"So, it's something which we will look at in the future of saying maybe we'll do smaller steps, and then if there is a warning light saying, 'OK', it's easier to undo. But there is no clear way at that stage because so far it has worked.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Toto Wolff hits back at accusations that Mercedes favour Antonelli over Russell

"I remember 2022. We thought we had one-and-a-half seconds we're putting on the car at the beginning of the season, and that backfired.

"But since then, this year particularly, every upgrade we brought on the car, remember Montreal was a big hit, a big hit in terms of it worked very well. So, if that didn't, why? That's the most important question. And if we come to conclusions that say this is what wasn't as expected, then we have to obviously think for the future."

Russell, who starts on the front row in Saturday's Sprint in Singapore behind pole-sitter Verstappen, says Mercedes will see how Antonelli fares over the remainder of the weekend.

"We can definitely confirm the old one is not bad. Let's see what Saturday brings with Kimi on the upgrade," he said.

"As a team, there's still nothing telling us it isn't working. But it's a sport driven by the stopwatch and the stopwatch has not been great for the upgrade yet. Let's see. Maybe tomorrow (Saturday) is a different day."

Sports.title: FIA admits 'human error' created power disparity in Singapore Sprint Qualifying
Sports.content:
The FIA has admitted "human error" caused a power disparity during Sprint Qualifying in Singapore.

Following a red flag for debris in SQ1 caused by Cadillac's Sergio Perez, the FIA did not activate Overtake Mode - an extra power boost that is normally active throughout qualifying and used in races to aid overtaking.

The FIA reactivated Overtake Mode for 27 seconds before deactivating it again, thus causing an unfair advantage in the first part of Sprint Qualifying.

Sky Sports F1 understands the brief re-activation of Overtake Mode happened in the last minute of SQ1 when several drivers were on flying laps before being turned off.

It is also understood Williams petitioned for all teams to progress to SQ2, which was declined, and no protests are expected.

Williams' Carlos Sainz was one of the six drivers to miss out on SQ2 and says the drivers who had Overtake Mode for those 27 seconds gained around half a second.

There was also a timing issue during Sprint Qualifying, which the FIA says was "unrelated" to the "human error".

What is Overtake Mode in F1? Overtake Mode provides a car an extra half a megajoule of electrical energy at high speed.



On a normal lap, when the car reaches 180mph, it has to, by regulation, ramp down its electric motor power. With Overtake Mode active, that speed tolerance raises to 209mph.



In races, a driver within one second of another at a track’s detection zone can use Overtake Mode over the next lap to aid an overtake.

"This issue in question meant Overtake Mode was not available after the red flag period during SQ1," read an FIA statement.

"When it became apparent that Overtake Mode was not active after the restart, it was then activated for a period of 27 seconds before being deactivated again.

"The FIA acknowledges that this unfortunate human error had an impact on the performance of certain cars based on the timing of their run and their position around the lap. The second and third periods of Sprint Qualifying were not affected."

Which drivers were eliminated in SQ1 in Singapore? 17) Arvid Lindblad, Racing Bulls

18) Lance Stroll, Aston Martin

19) Alex Albon, Williams

20) Sergio Perez, Cadillac

21) Valtteri Bottas, Cadillac

22) Carlos Sainz, Williams

The human error comes just five days after an "unprecedented" software glitch at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia caused several cars to grind to a crawl or a halt.

Sainz, who qualified last for Saturday's Singapore Sprint at 10am (build-up from 9am), live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event, claimed half of the field had an advantage in SQ1.

"Half of the cars did their laps with half a second quicker engine than the others," said Sainz.

"There was another software issue with the cars this time around, and we were on the bad end of it.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Carlos Sainz was left fustrated at the FIA after they admitted 'human error' caused a power disparity during Sprint Qualifying in Singapore

"For whatever reason the FIA, like in Malaysia, at the end decide to do sporting equity and were happy to do half of the cars in qualy with higher power than the other half of the cars.

"A bit confused why the sport keeps doing different things depending on who is out in Q1 or who is out in lap one."

All of the main contenders progressed to SQ2 although Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad and Aston Martin's Lance Stroll would have fancied their chances of getting through.

Max Verstappen went on to take Sprint pole from Mercedes' George Russell and Ferrari's Charles Leclerc.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sergio Perez brings out an early red flag in Sprint Qualifying at the Singapore Grand Prix

Teams keen to understand what happened in SQ1

Sky Sports F1's Ted Kravitz:

"Unfortunate human error from the FIA, not the first time we've heard that.

"As far as Aston Martin are confirmed, their sporting director Andy Stephenson is still up with race control. They just want to understand what happened here today.

"They don't believe that anyone was doing their qualifying lap and then didn't have the extra half a megajoule available, what it's concerned about is the tyre preparation on the out-lap.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from Sprint Qualifying at the 2026 Singapore Grand Prix

"Most of the drivers were on the radio saying they didn't have power, so they couldn't do the out-lap they wanted to do. That skews everything else, the rest of the computations they've done.

"While Aston Martin aren't making a protest, they do want to understand what's going on.

"They say the easiest thing would have been to stop the session and do it all again, but you've used your tyres by that time and that's not going to be possible."

Sports.title: 'I only found out this morning' - Moyes surprised Everton are up for sale
Sports.content:
David Moyes has admitted his surprise at Everton being put up for sale by owners The Friedkin Group - even claiming he only found out on Friday morning when the statement was released to the supporters.

The Friedkin Group (TFG) announced they are open to new investment into the club - including the "potential sale of a controlling interest".

The group, led by American billionaire Dan Friedkin, only completed their full takeover of Everton in December 2024 - ending Farhad Moshiri's long spell at the helm.

"Yeah I was surprised, they'd only came in a year and a half ago," Moyes said in a press conference - before claiming he first felt signs of the owners not being committed during the most recent transfer window.

"Most owners come in for a lot longer than that. We were all expecting them to be here for 20 to 30 years, however long it may be.

"But maybe the way things worked out over the transfer window, I probably had seen through it a little bit before that. It's probably all there for Evertonians to see now.

"I truly believed that with new ownership who were in for it completely with us all, my ambition coming back was to get Everton back to the levels they'd been at in the past - challenging for Europe more often, being around it.

"And probably you could tell with how I've been a lot over the summer that that's the way it's been. It's been a difficult summer for us.

"I only found out this morning myself along with everybody else. I'm a little bit surprised, but maybe not really that surprised."

Moyes also admitted he feels sympathy for the Everton fans who have to go through another period of uncertainty.

The last three years alone have seen Moshiri try to sell the club to 777 Partners and John Textor, only for both of their takeover bids to fall through. TFG also saw talks collapse before finally breaking through in late 2024.

Everton also had two rounds of points deductions for breaching the Premier League's Profit and Sustainability Rules (PSR), which came in a period that nearly saw the club relegated from the Premier League for the first time.

Moyes, who returned to the club in early 2025, admitted the last year was one of stability for the club. But that has now changed.

Asked if he feels let down for being mis-sold a dream, Moyes said: "No. Because I love this club so much and they could have sold me anything and I'd have still taken it.

"But it's for Evertonians I feel sorry for the most. They've been through so many difficult periods, they really have. The last thing they wanted to hear was this.

"Last year we went through a season where there wasn't much drama. There wasn't any relegation problems, we had a bit of drama of money that we had to pay to Burnley.

"Apart from that, in the main we've done pretty well over the year and were just starting to get back at the right footing - and challenging at the right end of the table rather than the wrong end.

"I'm more disappointed for Evertonians who have to go through another period of: 'who's going to be the new owner?'"

Image: Everton are potentially up for sale

Asked if he's concerned about his own future, with potential new owners set to arrive at the club, Moyes said: "I've not really thought about it yet from that point of view. The players have been great so far and we'll keep them focused on what we can do which is win the games.

"I always think that Evertonians galvanise even more so when it comes to a situation where the team needs help, the manager needs help - we'll stick together. We'll certainly be in that camp.

"I'm just reading the things that I've seen this morning. They're looking forward to getting the right people in to bring the club further forward.

"It's a great club if anybody is out there who wants to buy it. If they want to speak to me, I'll be the first person to tell them that it's certainly worth buying."

Everton owners' statement in full

An Everton statement on Friday morning said: "When TFG became custodians of Everton, the club faced significant financial uncertainty and challenges both on and off the pitch.

"The immediate priority was to provide the stability, investment and support needed to secure the club's future, including helping to bring the long-promised stadium to completion for its deserving supporters.

"With that foundation now safely in place, the time is right to consider the next chapter for Everton. We will only entertain interest from parties who we strongly believe will be the right stewards to take the club forward and build on the momentum that has been established.

"Throughout this process, TFG's focus will remain unchanged. We will support the club in all ways necessary to achieve success on the pitch and will continue efforts to make a positive difference in the communities the club serves.

"TFG and the club will not be commenting further while this work is under way."

Why is club up for sale so quickly?

Alan Myers on Sky Sports News:

"It's not come as a big surprise to hear this news. When The Friedkin Group said a few months ago that they were looking for investors, the feeling and talk around Everton and the financial side of things that the club was actually up for sale. It was a sale they were looking for, rather than investors.

"One of the real reasons for this is TFG have probably come to a point where they have seen what it's going to cost to put Everton back at the top table of English football, which is where the club want to be and where they were a long number of years ago.

"That figure and cost implication is probably too much for them and they don't want to do that.

"From day one, there were rumours and mumblings that TFG weren't going to be at Everton for long. What they've been trying to do recently is put the club into a good financial situation, with a sale in mind.

"A lot of this also comes from the situation with Roma. They own Roma as well, they are building a new stadium there which will cost £1bn. In the end, it's all too much for them.

"I believe The Friedkin Group are looking for between £800m and £1bn to sell the club which will give them a tidy little profit, as they bought the club for cheaper than they should have done.

"It was interesting when you read the statement from The Friedkin Group saying: 'We will be fully committed to supporting the team on the pitch'. Well it didn't look that way in the summer transfer window, that's for sure. It was a bit of a disaster in the end.

"Although you have to remember the squad they had is a good squad, but a weak squad. If David Moyes was to get injuries with his players, then that squad would be tested. There's no two ways about that.

"The first squad he has at the moment is a very good, strong squad. But you could see that they were willing to sell Harrison Armstrong to Nottingham Forest. That said a lot about the investment and what they were doing.

"The only reason he didn't go was because the crowd made their feelings known. That pressure forced The Friedkin Group to reconsider selling him as he's one of the young bright talents of Everton."

Sports.content:

2h ago 12.18 EDT Matt Hughes The Women’s Super League will face major disruption next season due to the Club World Cup, with Arsenal and Chelsea likely to be absent from domestic competition for up to a month. The Guardian revealed last week that the inaugural Women’s Club World Cup is set to be awarded to the US, with transatlantic travel to cause additional problems for European sides, whwhile the proposed dates of 5-30 January will clash directly with the WSL. Fifa has yet to confirm the qualification criteria for the Club World Cup but the Guardian has learned Arsenal are guaranteed to be involved as 2025 Champions League winners and Chelsea are likely to join them, although they would lose their place if Manchester City win this season’s Champions League. Based on this season’s schedule, an extended run in the Club World Cup would mean the two English clubs missing up to four WSL match weeks plus the fourth round of the FA Cup, playing havoc with the fixture list and causing major congestion at the end of the season. Arsenal and Chelsea set to miss a month of next WSL season due to Club World Cup Read more Share

3h ago 11.17 EDT The last time England failed to qualify for the World Cup was in 2003. They had the misfortune to be drawn in the same group as Germany, the Netherlands and Portugal, with only the top team going through – no playoffs, no second chances. Germany won all six games in qualification – and all six at the actual tournament in the United States. They became world champions for the first time and retained the trophy in 2007. Share Updated at 11.18 EDT

3h ago 11.03 EDT Tom Garry Sarina Wiegman heaped praise on Ella Toone for her positive reaction to being left out of England’s initial squad for their Women’s World Cup playoff against Greece, after recalling the Manchester United midfielder for Friday’s first leg in Heraklion, Crete. An injury sustained by Lucy Bronze, described by Wiegman as “really small”, prompted the England right-back to return to Chelsea and Wiegman called up Toone, who travelled to Greece from Spain, where she had organised a training routine during the international window. Toone has 69 caps and has scored 24 goals, including in the Euro 2022 final and 2023 World Cup semi-final, but Wiegman said when naming her squad that she had left out Toone and Chloe Kelly because “the levels weren’t what I expect from them on the pitch”. On Saturday, after starting Manchester United’s victory over Liverpool, Toone took ownership of things, telling the BBC: “It’s about me now. I’ve got to keep working hard and use it as fuel to come back even better.” Wiegman, asked whether she had been impressed with Toone’s response, said: “Yes, very much. I think when I gave her the call, of course that was a hard call. But she took that straight away. Of course [she was] very disappointed, but the first thing she did [was say]: ‘OK, I’m going to get back, I’m going to do that.’ She has the support around her too.” Wiegman praises Toone’s attitude after late Lionesses recall for Greece playoff Read more Share

Sports.title: Maresca maintains almost total control as he follows Manchester City owners’ line | Jamie Jackson
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca’s first public display since Manchester City were found guilty on virtually all counts of breaching Premier League financial rules was controlled – apart from the sole, and telling, slip-up of his very first answer.

In Thursday’s pre-emptive PR move, the club had Maresca tell their channels that he was aware of the “noise” around City. Fast forward 24 hours, and to a packed media conference of 45 attendees – around a threefold increase on the norm – at the Etihad Campus, the Italian was asked if this was dismissive of the anger felt towards the club’s cheating. “I understand the reason why most of you are here but the only thing I can say is that there is a process ongoing and in this moment I completely trust the club,” he replied.

This correspondent’s radar bleeped at the use of “in this moment” and, when the microphone was passed, Maresca was quizzed if this meant he may change his mind. “Sorry, that was the wrong answer. I completely trust the club in this moment, in the future, always.” But there was no denying the initial response and how this points to these shaky times for all at City.

Maresca, clearly coached by the club’s media department, maintained a strict party line of “trust” in the veracity of a hierarchy headed by Khaldoon al-Mubarak and Ferran Soriano. And a mention of City’s chair and chief executive, respectively, caused the only intervention from the media officer. When Maresca was asked if al-Mubarak and/or Soriano should have fronted up instead of him, an interjection came that made clear that this was a briefing to preview Sunday’s trip to Anfield. “Don’t forget, it is a Liverpool press conference,” Maresca said.

After being found guilty of the vast majority of more than 100 charges related to breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules by an independent commission, the Premier League’s subsequent statement featured the word “sham” five times to describe City’s malfeasance. This has provoked various derisive memes – “Shamchester City” among them – and heading into Friday’s press conference, the club were concerned such emotive adjectives would be used in the framing of questions to Maresca. That did not occur during a 16-minute briefing, with the lack of the regular embargoed section for a Sunday game understandable given the circumstances.

View image in fullscreen Ferran Soriano’s absence from media duties to answer questions on City’s plight was raised at the press conference. Photograph: Tom Little/Reuters

Maresca, dapper in a bottle-green polo shirt, was smooth and serene when asked about Soriano’s explosive – and arguably desperate – assertion that “surprisingly for us and our lawyers after nearly two years the commission has issued an opinion that supports the Premier League’s conspiracy theory”. Maresca said: “I understand the reason why most of you are here but the only thing I can say is what I said already. The reason why I joined this club is because I completely trust 100% the owner, the CEO, the sport director, and all the organisation. So, I don’t have any doubt about that.”

Maresca also showed a lighter side when quizzed about the wellbeing of Erling Haaland, who had demanded to be replaced during Norway’s last game of the international break. Here, in a reminder of the simpler times before the news broke a fortnight ago, was a straight football question. “Finally,” the Italian said. “He’s good. He went to Marbella, two or three days off, played golf, recovered and prepared for Anfield. He’s good. Thank you. It was good. Also because, again, the players are thinking again. International team, some day off and go again.”

City won at Anfield last season thanks to Haaland’s late penalty. Maresca’s men, who are leaders with a maximum 15 points from the opening five games, can expect a febrile welcome on Sunday. “We need to be ready,” Maresca said. “Not only does the focus have to be about the game, but also we know that the environment in Anfield is nice. It will be even worse because of the situation. But again, it will be our duty to try to do our best and win the game. This is the situation. This is the noise.

“What do we need in Anfield? It’s also the passion from our fans and their voice. And hopefully at the end we can celebrate a good win. I’m always concerned. Not just Liverpool, I would be concerned also about Ipswich. I know that Anfield is a nice pitch, probably will be even more warm in terms of environment but the reason why I decided to be manager is for this kind of game.

“I’m not worried at all. The environment from the players is nice, in this moment we are top of the league, so the players have all the reasons to be happy and excited.”

Sports.title: Managers react to Manchester City’s guilty verdict: ‘Uncertainty is not good for anyone’
Sports.content:
1. Carrick ‘personally’ affected by verdict Michael Carrick has said retrospectively receiving a winner’s medal would not make up for being robbed of emotional moments of glory by Manchester City’s breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules. Manchester United’s manager was part of the squad that lost out on the Premier League title to City on the final day of the 2011-12 season when Sergio Agüero scored a last-minute winner to secure top spot on goal difference. Carrick and his United teammates were left solemn on the touchline at Sunderland while City, who have been found guilty of breaking financial rules during a nine-year-period between 2009 and 2018, celebrated. “The emotion, the feeling about winning, a lot of it is in the moment,” Carrick said. “Whether you’re successful, whether you lose, whether it goes against you, that initial [feeling], the beauty of sport and the beauty of football and the beauty of trying to win trophies here, is a little bit on the journey towards it and then the finale, and does it go for you, does it go against you. “Once that’s done, there’s no getting that back in any direction. The feeling we all crave is coming out on top – that kind of sums it up. Whatever’s done in the past tense is in the past, but in that moment is how you feel in that moment. Certainly as a participant, as a performer, and I’m sure the supporters feel the same, that’s why we love it so much because of the emotion in the moment.” Carrick was also part of United’s staff under Ole Gunnar Solskjær when they finished second, 22 points behind City, in 2021. City continue to plead their innocence and have appealed against the verdict. If they fail to overturn the independent commission’s ruling, they will probably face a serious punishment. “It’s affected me personally in different ways,” Carrick said. “But as the case is ongoing now I don’t know where that stands and how it’s going to end up, so we’ll just have to wait and see. What I will say, the sooner it gets sorted I think for everyone’s benefit is essential.” Will Unwin

2. Liverpool players ‘thinking about next game’ - Iraola Liverpool’s manager, Andoni Iraola, has called for the Manchester City case to be dealt with swiftly. “I think uncertainty is not good for anyone involved but there is the process ongoing and we have to be patient like everyone else and see what happens at the end,” he said. “No one knows what’s going to happen. We have to focus on Liverpool and being the best club we can be, the best team we can be. That’s my challenge. My opinion is not valid because I haven’t spent that time and I haven’t read as much as they’ve [the commission] done. “The challenge of the game is so high that I don’t think players think too much outside of this. They are thinking: ‘I have to mark this player’ or ‘I have to go and deal with this one’ or ‘I have be at this level because the level of the game is so high.’ They will be focused on those things. “Obviously they will have their own opinions, but I think they will be fully focused on what happens on the pitch.” Press Association

3. Kompany ‘really proud’ of City medals Vincent Kompany, the former Manchester City captain, insists he is still “really proud” of his success with the club after it was found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules. The Bayern Munich manager won four Premier League titles and multiple domestic cups during his spell at City from 2008 to 2019. The former Belgium international was a key figure in City’s dominant era under their Abu Dhabi-based owners and is honoured with a statue outside the Etihad Stadium. “I played 11 years for the club. I’ve loved all of the years I played for the club and everything we achieved and [did] on the pitch – that’s something I’m really proud of,” Kompany said. View image in fullscreen A statue of the former Manchester City player Vincent Kompany’s stands outside the Etihad: ‘I’m really proud of everything we achieved.’ Photograph: Dave Thompson/AP Kompany signed for City from Hamburg just weeks before Sheikh Mansour completed a takeover that turned the club from also-rans to serial winners. Asked about the off-pitch issues at his former club, he said: “Everything else, as a player you’re not a part of that and right now as a coach of Bayern Munich I’m not too much occupied with that topic. I’m preparing the game next week and preparing the game we have tomorrow and everything I have as a coach.” Agence France-Presse

4. Arteta will ‘respect process’ before judgment Mikel Arteta has insisted the Premier League remains the best in the world despite the ongoing uncertainty surrounding Manchester City’s guilty verdict. The Arsenal manager, who was an assistant to Pep Guardiola at City for more than three years before taking over at the Emirates in December 2019, was unsurprisingly bombarded with questions about his former club on Friday before Saturday’s lunchtime fixture against Leeds and responded “100%” when asked whether he thought the Premier League remains the best. “It’s very important that we respect the process,” he said. “I think the timelines and it’s still an ongoing process that is not resolved because it’s been appealed. And my position, I think the club’s position, is not to make any further comments.” Asked whether he thought the Premier League’s reputation has been damaged, Arteta added: “There is a process there again that is not resolved. It’s ongoing and we can have a much clearer opinion when it’s been resolved. I’m not prepared to make any comments.” Arteta did confirm that Christos Tzolis is out for a few weeks with a hamstring issue but said he will make a decision on whether Kai Havertz and Ezri Konsa will feature against Leeds. Ed Aarons

Sports.title: Rui Pinto to remain under witness protection after U-turn by Portuguese authorities
Sports.content:
Rui Pinto will remain under witness protection for the time being after Portuguese authorities suspended the decision to end it. The special security programmes commission (CPES) acknowledged he should have been given an opportunity to present his case before the decision was taken. The Manchester City whistleblower can now challenge the withdrawal of his protection, with the commission expected to reconsider the matter.

In a statement signed by the Ministry of Justice, the CPES was said to have recognised that Pinto had not been adequately informed of the grounds for terminating the programme or given the opportunity to exercise his right to challenge the decision.

The protection was due to end on Saturday. The commission will provide Pinto with the risk assessment reports that it says indicated a low threat to his safety. The relevant meeting took place on 9 July. On 30 September, the day Pinto was informed his protected-witness status was coming to an end, an independent commission’s guilty verdict against City, which had been confirmed 24 hours earlier, was dominating headlines around the world.

He has 10 working days to review the documentation underpinning the decision and respond to its reasoning and conclusions. The prospect of losing his protection had prompted Pinto to launch a fundraising campaign to help secure his financial future. He has voiced fears for his safety after receiving credible death threats and being assaulted in Lisbon last April.

Pinto’s protected-witness status dates to April 2020, when Portugal’s judicial police (PJ) placed him under protection after he agreed to give investigators access to millions of files obtained from football clubs, companies linked to the Angolan businesswoman Isabel dos Santos and other entities suspected of criminal activity. Dos Santos denies corruption allegations.

His disclosures have informed investigations by judicial, tax and sporting authorities across Europe, including the Premier League’s inquiry into City. Pinto’s lawyers argue the authorities must consider his cooperation with the justice system and the risks associated with his revelations before withdrawing his protection.

Growing scrutiny appears to have prompted the authorities to reconsider their position. Pinto remains willing to cooperate with British authorities investigating City and other matters arising from his disclosures. He also handed millions of documents to investigators in France, which can now be shared with other countries, including the UK.

Sports.title: Manchester United’s early wobble makes Tottenham visit a must-win for Carrick
Sports.content:
The noise in the Premier League was focused elsewhere for the last two weeks of the international break, allowing a glorious silence to drift across Manchester United. Without Manchester City’s woes, Michael Carrick may have faced a more difficult time, with plenty to review in regards to the first five games of the season.

United sit solemnly in 12th with only one league win, and misery needs company. The hosts will find just that at Old Trafford on Saturday evening. Tottenham, bottom of the Premier League, visit, with both sides hoping to kickstart their season. Spurs have secured a measly two points after a summer where £300m was spent on Roberto De Zerbi’s rebuild but the architect’s drawings are already at risk of being set alight. For Carrick and United, beating the worst team in the league is close to a necessity as they enter a very difficult run of fixtures.

October is theoretically and practically problematic for United, who have six fixtures this month, with away games against Leeds, Atlético Madrid, Como and Chelsea, who play a variety of styles that need preparing for, making a home game against Spurs a must-win. On paper, the second easiest game of the month is Bournemouth at home. Carrick has plenty of credit in the bank from his work in the second half of last season, and will be afforded as much time as possible to get things right because no one is eager for another mid-season change of manager. United need to be in a better position by the end of October than they started it, which will require significant improvement on the pitch.

For Carrick there are plenty of small margins he can point to. The opening-day defeat at Hull was a grisly performance and worthy of criticism; Ipswich were eventually dispatched, while the derby was a tight and controversial loss, coming between two draws. The truth of the matter is United know they need to be better in both boxes. United have conceded fewer opposition touches in their box than any other team in the league but, on the other hand, they are the only side yet to keep a clean sheet. They can also boast the most touches in opposition boxes but are largely incapable of killing matches off.

United, like Tottenham, are very good at dominating possession, averaging 60% per match, but cannot translate that to goals and points. Even in the victory against Ipswich, United were unable to put a full 90 minutes of composure together, relying on Bruno Fernandes to drag them through against a promoted side. The forwards are yet to synchronise, with Matheus Cunha, the man tasked with leading the line, having only one goal to his name, and even that took a heavy deflection.

No one has more than one assist so far, while only Fernandes and Bryan Mbeumo have scored twice or more, the Portuguese getting a hat-trick against Ipswich. Marcus Rashford has shown glimpses of promise on the left but has no goal involvements, giving the impression of a man who requires a confidence boost after returning to the club where he was not wanted for 18 months. Nor is there the option of Benjamin Sesko playing as a more traditional central striker given he is sidelined with injury, while Joshua Zirkzee cannot even class himself as a plan B. But United are prolific compared with Tottenham, whose only league goals came in a 3-2 defeat by Aston Villa just before the international break.

View image in fullscreen Michael Carrick has had lots to ponder this season, with only one league win so far. Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PA

Losing to 10-man Manchester City was the most worrying of United’s defeats, showing how far off they look against a Champions League side. Phil Foden’s red card gave United plenty of space but they were unable to take advantage, instead plodding around, short of ideas, barely threatening. United are expert at dominating possession but not games, traits that create hope and frustration in equal measure.

The summer signings of a goalkeeper who cost nothing and three central midfielders is coming under as much scrutiny as Carrick’s tactics. At least Carlos Baleba is poised to finally make his debut after joining from Brighton for £65m in August and Carrick desperately needs him to provide the energy lacking in central areas thus far. Having recovered from an ankle injury, the Cameroonian has what it takes to snuff out the danger that has been leading to the concession of goals.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Sesko is not the sole injury concern; Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford were ruled out of playing for England, while Patrick Dorgu and Noussair Mazraoui’s international breaks ended prematurely. Meanwhile, Matthijs de Ligt has not played competitively for 10 months and Amad Diallo is yet to feature this season.

The run of 12 wins in 17 games after Carrick took interim charge in January showed plenty of individual and collective improvements, but whether certain players can crash through their current ceiling requires clear evidence sooner rather than later. With finances tight, it is imperative that United improve from within. More academy players have spent time with the squad in recent weeks, with Noah Ajayi impressing the coaches Steve Holland and Jonathan Woodgate. It is thought a number of youngsters could make first-team debuts before the season concludes, which would be a display of Carrick’s long-term vision. Results, however, will decide if he gets a chance to implement it in the first place.

United are desperate for a catalyst and if it does not come against Tottenham at the weekend, Carrick will become fearful of Halloween.

Sports.title: Everton owner The Friedkin Group exploring sale of club after two years
Sports.content:
Everton’s owner, The Friedkin Group, is looking to sell the club less than two years after taking over from Farhad Moshiri.

The Houston-based company confirmed in a statement on Friday that it was seeking fresh investment in Everton but was also open to relinquishing control should a suitable buyer be found. No timescale has been placed on a sale but TFG is confident of attracting a buyer quickly and potentially concluding a deal this season.

“The Friedkin Group is exploring new investment options for Everton Football Club, including the potential sale of a controlling interest,” it said. Moelis & Company, an investment bank, will handle any sale.

Quick Guide How do I 

TFG’s announcement follows a calamitous end to the summer ­transfer window that raised scrutiny over its long-term commitment to the ­Premier League club. The group’s decision is understood to be based on the amount of funding needed to further Everton’s ambitions and restrictions surrounding multi-club ownership. Roma, another high-profile asset requiring serious investment, and Cannes are also in TFG’s stable. The company is preparing to launch an NHL franchise in Houston worth about $3.5bn (£2.6bn).

TFG’s move is also an opportunity to make a quick profit on a club it bought as a distressed asset from Moshiri in December 2024. TFG spent about £400m to take over Everton and the club’s considerable debt – Moshiri walked away with an initial £25m – and has stabilised the finances while securing funding for Hill Dickinson Stadium on more favourable terms. An asking price of about £800m, including long-term debt of about £380m, would represent a healthy return in the event of a full sale, although all levels of investment are being considered.

The statement read: “When TFG became custodians of Everton, the club faced significant financial uncertainty and challenges both on and off the pitch. The immediate priority was to provide the stability, investment and support needed to secure the club’s future, including helping to bring the long-promised stadium to completion for its deserving supporters.

“With that foundation now safely in place, the time is right to ­consider the next chapter for Everton. We will only entertain interest from parties who we strongly believe will be the right stewards to take the club ­forward and build on the momentum that has been established.

“Throughout this process, TFG’s focus will remain unchanged. We will support the club in all ways necessary to achieve success on the pitch and will continue efforts to make a ­positive difference in the communities the club serves.”

TFG’s financial and personal commitment to Everton has been ­questioned in recent months. The club’s transfer strategy changed midway through the summer window to a sell-to-buy policy, with the owner’s decision to accept a £40m offer from Nottingham Forest for Harrison ­Armstrong the first sign of that shift.

Armstrong’s sale was halted after a backlash among Evertonians but the team’s most creative asset, ­Iliman Ndiaye, was then sold to ­Manchester City for £65m. David Moyes, whose long-term future at Everton is also uncertain, then revealed he had never spoken to Dan Friedkin, TFG’s founder and the club’s chair, since returning as manager in January 2025.

Moyes’s squad was left short on numbers and a centre-forward on deadline day after Beto’s sale to Fiorentina and the collapse of ­Folarin Balogun’s mooted £40m move from Monaco. Everton have plans to address those weaknesses in January but they could be affected by a potential takeover.

TFG believed it could work around Uefa regulations on multi-club ownership should Everton and Roma qualify for the same European competition. That is not the case and, with Uefa enforcing rules on such ownership structures strictly, TFG faces having to put one club in a blind trust to avoid any sanctions.

With the stadium move complete and finances stabilised, Everton are a more attractive proposition than when TFG bought the club.

Sports.title: European FAs pushing for three-week international break to be abandoned
Sports.content:
Europe’s football associations have raised serious concerns about the impact of the extended international break and will ask Uefa to push for a reversion to the previous scheduling.

The new three-week break left European countries tasked with four Nations League games, which typically took place within 11 days. It has brought deep misgivings about player workload, injuries and financial viability, with one FA president telling the Guardian it was “a disaster” and numerous others saying the schedule is unworkable.

Opposition to the break was virtually unanimous when it was discussed at a meeting of European FAs in Berlin on Thursday, the subject understood to have prompted a series of passionate interventions. The Football Association chair, Debbie Hewitt, and chief executive, Mark Bullingham, were among those to speak out highlighting the drawbacks of a calendar change approved by the Fifa council in 2023. Many expressed clear preference for the set of five two-week breaks that preceded this season.

The break, which truncates the previous September and October windows into one longer spell, was intended in part to improve player welfare and reduce travel commitments. But an overwhelming number of FAs are unhappy with how a bruising run of Nations League fixtures, generally played at a higher intensity to friendlies and with fewer substitutions available, worked out in practice.

Kylian Mbappé, Alex Scott, Cody Gakpo, Alexander Isak and Brian Brobbey are among a lengthy list to have picked up injury issues. It is a worry that unites Uefa’s members, with smaller countries additionally concerned that their reduced player pools offer less scope for players to be rested. There is also a sense that countries with bigger resources have a competitive advantage when playing a large chunk of their Nations League fixtures at once, a potentially significant consequence given Euro 2028 seeding will be determined by performance in this competition.

Some federations also expressed dissatisfaction about the break’s commercial implications, reporting the challenges of marketing and selling tickets for two home matches in close proximity. International games are usually valuable ways for football associations to raise funds.

Another FA president suggested the window should be adapted according to the needs of each continent, although the logistics of such a plan would be unclear. A counterpoint was raised by a different FA chief, who said his federation would conduct an analysis of the break’s merits and pointed out the benefits of extended time for his national team’s manager to work with players.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Although there is a strong appetite that Uefa lobby Fifa to scrap the format, the prospects of their efforts bearing fruit are slim. Relations between the governing bodies have plummeted to an all-time low since the Fifa Forward Enterprise scandal and, just as relevantly, the international match calendar is locked in until 2030. Any success may hinge on a change of leadership at Fifa, whose under-fire president Gianni Infantino is looking to win a fourth term in March.

Sports.title: Riyad Mahrez risks infuriating wife Taylor Ward on Dele Alli's live stream with indiscreet comment about 'the birds in Dubai'
Sports.content:
Riyad Mahrez risks infuriating wife Taylor Ward on Dele Alli's live stream with indiscreet comment about 'the birds in Dubai'

Riyad Mahrez has risked infuriating his wife Taylor Ward with a comment he made to Dele Alli during the former Tottenham star's live stream.

Alli, 30, was speaking to various footballer friends on his new Twitch channel and Mahrez did not appear to appreciate that he was being broadcast live to thousands of fans watching on.

Mahrez picked up the call and struggled to hear Alli when he said: 'I'm in London, streaming, I was just calling people, they can hear you, they can hear you live on stream bro.'

The 35-year-old replied: 'I'm in Dubai bro. There are some f***ing birds in here bro, honestly.'

Upon realising what Mahrez had said, Alli swiftly pushed his chair away from the microphone before moving out of shot briefly and looked sheepish upon his return to the stream.

Mahrez has been married to his British model and influencer wife since 2023 and the couple share two children. He also has two children with his first wife, British model Rita Johal.

Riyad Mahrez made an indiscreet comment to Dele Alli while speaking on his live stream

Ward and Mahrez have lived in Saudi Arabia since his move to Al-Ahli three years ago.

His indiscreet remark on Alli's stream risks embarrassing his other half, who co-founded jewellery line Astalia and has almost three million followers on social media.

Her relationship with Mahrez has been well documented. They starred in Amazon series Married to the Game, which gave viewers a deep dive into the lives of footballers' wives and girlfriends.

Ward opened up on her life during that programme, including the moment when Mahrez revealed he would be leaving City for Saudi Arabia in a clip that went viral.

Ward said she was 'overwhelmed' when Mahrez informed her they would be leaving Manchester and moving to Jeddah at short notice, with the star telling her: 'It's part of the game, innit,' after she had expressed concern that she would be 'sat at home on my own'.

Speaking to Daily Mail Sport last year, Ward admitted Mahrez's response to her 'still haunts me', but said the Algerian player was 'straight-talking' and 'to the point'.

'That whole week was just an emotional rollercoaster really,' she said. 'It was a huge shock and I had absolutely no idea. One day we were planning for Riyad to go back to pre-season with City and then overnight we were moving to Saudi and I was planning this whole move.

'I think it was just very overwhelming at the time and a massive shock because I just didn't see it coming at all. That scene with Riyad - that is just him to a tee.

Mahrez and wife Taylor Ward are pictured celebrating after his victory with Al-Ahli last season

Ward is a social media sensation with nearly 3million followers on Instagram

'He is just straight talking and to the point. He is very much just like, "it is what it is, you've got to get over it now", whereas I'm more emotional. That's why we work because I'm a bit of a flapper in those situations and he's very on the ball and just gets on with it.

'One day he rang me while I was sat on the beach and said "we're moving and I'm going tomorrow, that's it".

'He put me on the phone to one of the girls at the club and I burst into tears - I was like "I can't believe this is happening". It happened so quick, you don't get a minute to say bye to everyone. One minute he was starting pre-season, the next he was saying goodbye.'

Mahrez has scored twice in four games this season for Al-Ahli and the Algerian is regarded as one of the best African footballers of all time.

Alli, meanwhile, remains without a club and appears to be transitioning into raising his media profile, though he says he remains intent on returning to the sport.
