In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: The £13,128 ticket: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua is sport's most expensive standard seat EVER as fans complain they are half a million places back in online queues
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua tickets have reached £13,128 at the top end of the scale, as more than half a million fans joined an online queue for one of the most eagerly anticipated fights in boxing history.

The most expensive seats for the December 11 showdown in Cardiff cost more than those for some of the world's biggest sporting events, eclipsing the top face-value price of £6,300 for the 2026 Super Bowl and World Cup ticket prices of £8,333.

Tickets for Fury vs Joshua went on sale at midday on Friday, with Saudi Arabia's Turki Alalshikh keen to ensure fans had an accessible entry point, reflected in the starting price of £88.50 including fees.

The top-tier tickets, priced at £13,128, sold out within just 45 minutes, underlining the extraordinary demand for the December 11 showdown.

The figures do not include VIP packages, hotel and travel packages, group bookings or concession prices, and all tickets remain subject to availability.

Demand for the fight was immediately apparent, with more than half a million people waiting in the online queue as fans raced to secure seats for the long-awaited clash.

Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua tickets have been priced from £88.50 to a staggering £13,128, as fans prepare to snap up seats for the long-awaited heavyweight showdown

Fury and Joshua's fight is due to take place on December 11 in Cardiff with the showdown set to begin at 1am so Netflix subscribers can stream it at peak time in America

The fight will take place at Cardiff's Principality Stadium on December 11, bringing an end to years of speculation over a meeting between the two former world heavyweight champions.

Fury and Joshua have been linked with a blockbuster contest for more than a decade, with negotiations repeatedly failing to produce the long-awaited clash.

Now, the British rivals are finally set to share a professional ring in a contest that could prove defining for both men's careers.

Fury, 38, returned to the ring in April after another retirement announcement, beating Arslanbek Makhmudov on points. The former WBC heavyweight champion has won 36 of his 39 professional contests, with two defeats and one draw.

Joshua, 36, won Olympic gold at London 2012 before becoming a two-time unified heavyweight world champion. He has recorded 30 victories, including 27 knockouts, alongside four defeats.

Joshua's most recent high-profile outing came in December 2025, when he stopped Jake Paul, before returning to the ring in July 2026 to defeat Kristian Prenga by second-round knockout.

The December showdown will give both men the chance to settle their long-running rivalry and claim a defining victory in front of a huge crowd.

The Principality Stadium can accommodate up to 80,000 spectators for major events, while Netflix is set to stream the contest globally.

The December showdown will give both men the chance to settle their long-running rivalry and claim a defining victory in front of a huge crowd

Fury against Joshua was almost the fight that got away, with the heavyweights now set to sort out differences that should have been settled a decade ago

Main-event ring walks are expected at approximately 1am local time on Saturday, December 12, although the final schedule remains subject to confirmation.

As for those in attendance, Turki Alalshikh had been keen to ensure there was an accessible entry point for fans, with tickets starting at £88.50 including fees.

At the top end of the scale, tickets cost a staggering £13,128, putting them among the most expensive publicly listed prices for a major boxing event.

The figure is not without precedent in a sport where premium seats can command eye-watering sums.

When Floyd Mayweather and Manny Pacquiao met in 2015, official tickets cost up to $10,000 (£6,700), while resale listings subsequently reached around £94,000 after the initial allocation sold out in less than a minute.

Meanwhile, a premium hospitality package for Mike Tyson's 2024 bout with Jake Paul was advertised at $2million (£1.57m) for 10 tickets and an exclusive ringside experience.

Some individual ringside seats were also listed on the secondary market at $50,000 (£39,000).

The highest-priced ticket previously listed for a British boxing event was a VIP ringside seat for Anthony Joshua's 2017 showdown with Wladimir Klitschko at Wembley, which was advertised for £202,400 on resale platform Viagogo.

However, that figure was an asking price rather than a confirmed sale. Around 90,000 fans attended the fight, which saw Joshua stop Klitschko in the 11th round.

Meanwhile, face-value prices for inner-ringside seats at Tyson Fury's 2022 fight against Dillian Whyte at Wembley reached £2,250.

Sports.title: Mike Tyson says he delivered letter to Trump from Diddy from behind bars in bombshell claim as he opens up on friendship with disgraced rapper
Sports.content:
Boxing legend Mike Tyson revealed that he hand delivered a letter from his friend Sean 'Diddy' Combs to President Donald Trump in a recent meeting.

In an appearance on SiriusXM radio show 'Andy Cohen Live,' the former fighter spoke at length about his friendship with the disgraced music mogul who is serving a 50-month prison sentence for a sex-crimes conviction.

Tyson said he is 'friendly with Puff' – using one of Combs' many stage names – before Cohen asked him if the boxer was 'surprised by what happened with him?'

'Listen, I was surprised that they went through so many lengths to get him,' the athlete replied.

'They used a 110-year-old rule to get him – that case 110 years ago, but they used it to get him. Can you imagine that?'

After being convicted on this charge, Tyson said that he spoke with Combs from jail – where he asked 'Iron Mike' to deliver a message to the President.

Mike Tyson says he was asked to deliver a letter from Diddy to President Donald Trump

Diddy - born Sean Combs - wrote Trump a letter from jail asking the President for a pardon

'And did you give a letter to the president from him?' Cohen inquired, to which Tyson replied: 'I did what he told me to do, yeah.'

In January, President Trump confirmed that he received a letter from Combs asking for a pardon. Trump did not reveal how he received the letter, but said that he wouldn't grant the request.

The '110-year-old' rule Tyson referred to was the 1910 Mann Act, a law that criminalizes the transporting of 'any woman or girl for the purpose of prostitution or debauchery, or for any other immoral purpose.'

Combs faced accusations of leading a criminal enterprise where he allegedly coerced victims to participate in debaucherous sex parties – nicknamed 'freak offs' – which occasionally involved travel across state lines and international borders.

After a two month trial, Combs was acquitted of trafficking and racketeering, a jury cited the Mann Act when finding him guilty of two counts of transportation to engage in prostitution.

Combs has denied all allegations of sexual misconduct and has attempted to appeal his conviction.

He is currently being held at FCI Fort Dix in New Jersey and still faces upwards of 70 civil lawsuits throughout the country.

In January, Trump said he got a letter from Combs but said he wouldn't pardon him

Combs is serving 50 months in prison on two counts of transportation to engage in prostitution

Join the discussion Should celebrities be able to use their connections to seek pardons for serious crimes?

Combs' release date has moved multiple times since his incarceration due to his alleged misdeeds behind bars.

An NBC News report revealed it was pushed back from January 21, 2028 to March 2, 2028 after he allegedly made fellow inmates cook and clean for him, give him massages and received access to outside alcohol and a cellphone.

In an August 2025 interview, Trump addressed Combs' conviction in an interview with Newsmax.

'I was very friendly with him. I got along with him great,' the President said at the time.

'[He] seemed like a nice guy,' Trump continued. 'I didn't know him well, but when I ran for office he was very hostile.'

Sports.title: 'He's not a p***y President': Mike Tyson launches wild defense of Trump and says president has overcome problems only 'black' people face
Sports.content:
'He's not a p***y President': Mike Tyson launches wild defense of Trump and says president has overcome problems only 'black' people face

Donald Trump is 'not a p***y President,' according to his longtime friend and boxing legend Mike Tyson.

Speaking on the latest episode of Piers Morgan Uncensored, Tyson discussed his history with Trump, whom he first met as a young heavyweight in the 1980s as the future President was making a name for himself in New York and Atlantic City real estate.

'I voted for him,' the 60-year-old Tyson told Morgan. 'I ran the streets for him. You know, me getting votes… I'm very proud of him. He's somebody that everybody should be proud of.'

Tyson doesn't have many remaining personal ties to his early days in the ring. The boxing legend's famed trainer, Cus D'Amato, died in 1985, his turbulent marriage to actress Robin Givens ended four years later and Tyson's fragile business relationship with promoter Don King finally ruptured in the late 1990s.

But for all of the turnover surrounding Tyson, Trump has been a constant for the former heavyweight champion. Not only did Tyson fight at Trump's hotels and casinos, later adding the real estate mogul to his unofficial entourage, but the two remained friends throughout the ups and downs of their later lives.

And it's those obstacles that make Trump an admirable figure in the eyes of Tyson: 'Listen, if you didn't know who Donald Trump was and you didn't know his name, you would think he's Black.'

Speaking on the latest episode of Piers Morgan Uncensored, Mike Tyson discussed his history with President Trump, whom he first met as a young heavyweight in the 1980s

Trump and Tyson attend the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) 287 in April of 2023

Donald Trump and Mike Tyson attend March of Dimes Gourmet Gala Benefit in 1989

According to Tyson, it's Trump's perseverance in the face of multiple bankruptcies and sexual misconduct allegations that have made him a formidable figure.

'When he went for President, he was bankrupt... He owed taxes, he owed so much money,' Tyson said, somewhat erroneously.

While Trump's businesses did declare bankruptcy six times, the last filing came in 2009, well before his successful 2016 White House run.

But it's not just the financial problems that give Trump credibility in Tyson's eyes. Tyson was also impressed with the way Trump survived multiple waves of sexual misconduct claims.

'All this sex abuse and all that stuff that he went through,' Tyson continued. 'People don't normally go that well. They normally have a nervous breakdown. He handled it. And that's why everyone has to respect him. Just from the way he handled his court procedures… I don't care if you hate his guts… you have to respect that. Just off the bat.'

Trump has never been convicted of any sexual misconduct, although in May of 2023, a federal jury found him liable in a civil trial for sexually abusing and defaming writer E. Jean Carroll. A later trial resulted in a federal jury ordering Trump to pay an additional $83.3 million on top of the initial $5 million penalty he was ordered to pay Carroll.

Previously, Trump supported Tyson in the face of sexual misconduct claims. When Tyson was convicted of rape in Indiana in 1992, the future President told NBC the boxer was 'railroaded in the case' and questioned the victim's story.

While heavyweight champ Mike Tyson steals a kiss from his wife Robin Givens (R), real estate developer Donald Trump and Givens' mother Ruth Roper (L), talk to the media in 1988

Tyson chats with an attorney during a court hearing aimed at ending his contract with manager Bill Cayton. Sitting with Tyson's wife Robin Givens and her mother Ruth is Donald Trump

Donald Trump, Mike Tyson and Fred Trump attend a press conference at the Plaza Hotel

Donald Trump, Mike Tyson and Don King attend Gourmet Gala Benefit for March of Dimes on November 21, 1989 at the Plaza Hotel. King and Tyson later broke their business ties

Trump went so far as to publicly suggest Tyson should be allowed to dodge prison by giving 'millions and millions' of dollars to the victim.

'What has happened to him, the conviction, is already punitive,' Trump told the New York Post in 1992. 'The victim has had the satisfaction of humbling him and being vindicated.'

Speaking with Morgan, Tyson did not address the support he received from Trump in 1992.

He did, however, discuss the assassination attempt Trump survived in Pennsylvania on the campaign trail in 2024 by explaining he is 'not a p**** President.'

As for his immediate future, Tyson's planned exhibition with Floyd Mayweather Jr. is currently on hold after the former heavyweight broke his hand in May. Another complicating factor is a lawsuit against Mayweather by the promoter, CSI Sports.

In his previous return to the ring in 2024, Tyson was easily defeated by cruiserweight Jake Paul, who scored a unanimous decision victory that was watched by an estimated 60 million households on Netflix.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua braced for dramatic 1am start time under new proposal to Cardiff Council - and the Gypsy King wants to walk out flanked by Donald Trump!
Sports.content:
The highly-anticipated bout between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua could be set for a 1am start time at the Principality Stadium, Cardiff, in December.

That's after Cardiff Council received an application stating the ring walks are planned to start gone midnight, with proposals for the stadium to stay open until 3.30am.

According to the BBC, Millennium Stadium Plc has applied to change its premises licence to allow the fight to take place late 'on a very limited one-off occasion'.

Fury has suggested he will try to persuade United States president Donald Trump to join him for his ringwalk. 'I'll definitely make that offer to my old buddy, old pal, and we'll see if he's available. Probably unlikely because of the situation he's in at the moment, being the President of the United States.'

There is also a request to play live music until 3am on the same date, with a live performance expected before the ring walks.

It is proposed that the stadium roof is closed for the duration of the event, with enhanced security in place.

Other authorities and members of the public can make an objection until November 3, and a council hearing will be held to consider them. It is understood the permission will be granted if there are no objections.

There is a proposal for the ring walks for Tyson Fury (left) vs Anthony Joshua (right) to take place at 1am

There was initially doubt over whether the fight would take place in the United Kingdom or New York City.

It is understood Eddie Hearn pushed hard for the fight to be in Cardiff, with broadcaster Netflix keen to host it later so it can be shown at a reasonable time in the States.

Fury is currently favourite to take victory in the bout, with the Gypsy King claiming he has battled back from 28st – as heavy as an adult mountain gorilla – to chisel down to the shape he's in today.

Fury's physique has fluctuated heavily down the years – in January he described himself as a 'fat, binge-drinking junk-food addict' as he returned from retirement for a fifth time – but he is not messing around on this occasion.

Each fighter will pocket £75million from the face-off. As Daily Mail Sport revealed in September, the two fighters would have been taxed around 30 per cent of their purses in America, compared to 20 per cent in the UK, with Joshua particularly unhappy about the prospect of an extra £7.5million being added to his bill.

The two-time world champion instead demanded that his contract be honoured, which stipulated a British-based fight.

Hearn initially pushed for Wembley Stadium, but the combination of a roof over the Principality Stadium and the Welsh government’s willingness to bend their late-night curfew swung the fight towards Cardiff.

Sports.title: Dana White labels Eddie Hearn a NEPO BABY as war of words escalates between the promoters over Tyson Fury-Anthony Joshua showdown
Sports.content:
Dana White's war of words with Eddie Hearn has taken another turn after the UFC and Zuffa Boxing chief essentially branded his rival a nepo baby.

The duo have been at each other's throats over various topics this year, from Conor Benn's future to the £150million blockbuster fight between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua.

Things have escalated over the last month. White, who runs Zuffa Boxing alongside Saudi Arabia's boxing supremo Turki Al-Sheikh, has been billed as the main promoter for the heavyweight showdown and fought for the contest to take place in New York City.

Hearn, who successfully wrestled the fight back to Cardiff, has claimed that the contract Joshua signed stipulates that White cannot be involved in the contest and threatened crunch talks with broadcaster Netflix over White's attendance at Fury and Joshua's press conference on Wednesday in London.

And now, White has taken aim. He said on the Diary of a CEO podcast: 'Eddie's not the guy, Eddie's dad is the guy.

'And I'm not saying this to s*** on Eddie - I'm just being honest. I don't dislike Eddie. But he's not the guy; his dad's the guy.'

Dana White (left) has taken aim at Eddie Hearn (right) as their war of words continues - source: X - @danawhite

White branded Hearn a nep baby due to the sporting success of his father Barry (second left)

Barry Hearn, Eddie's father, has been a sports promoter since the 1970s and has had a huge influence on the likes of boxing, darts and snooker.

Eddie, though, now works in his own right though, according to White, is in his dad's shadow.

White continued: 'Frank Warren's the real guy. I just saw this interview with him; I was like, 'F***ing love it… all this f***ing talking and all this f***ing bulls***, let's f***ing fight.''

There had been doubt over whether the December 11 fight would in fact go ahead due to the involvement of White.

White, whose involvement has been criticised by sections of the British boxing public, was grilled by the media in a cagey press conference, where he labelled the bout a 's***show' while conceding he has 'no idea' if the contest will take place.

'I don't know. The guy who is supposed to be helping the fight has been hurting the fight the entire time,' he said. 'He hasn't done the fight any favours. I don't know anybody who is more full of s*** than Eddie Hearn.'

When asked whether he would step aside to allow the fight to go ahead, White said: 'That's not up to me. I'm involved in the f***ing fight.

'If Eddie Hearn really cared about this f***ing fight — first of all the fight would've happened a f***ing long time ago, one. Number two, he could finance the thing himself.

'Listen, this whole thing's a s***show right now. We'll all know a lot more in the next three, four days, see how this thing plays out.'

The duo have been at a battle over who will promote the fight between Tyson Fury (left) and Anthony Joshua (right)

White had initially raised eyebrows when Benn left Hearn's Matchroom to join Zuffa.

It remains to be seen whether White will have any involvement.

Hearn said this weekend: 'At this point, (White's) completely cooked. What he actually said was, "We're doing the TV production". Which, again, in the contract, is prohibited.

'After that video (of White saying he was producing the fight), I spoke to Sela (the Saudi entertainment company listed as promoters of the event). I said, "Have you seen this video?" They said, in writing, "Yes, and it's completely untrue".

'(White) cannot do that under the contract. They want me to meet them in LA next week, which I probably will.'

Sports.title: From beauty to beast! Former 'Miss Germany' targets a BOXING career and is set for her professional debut
Sports.content:
A former winner of Miss Germany has announced a surprise career switch - and will swap the catwalk for the boxing ring at the age of 33.

Tatjana Genrich was voted Germany's most beautiful woman in 2022 and has now announced she will make her professional boxing debut next month in Magdeburg, rekindling her childhood love of the sport.

Genrich was the Saxony-Anhalt state champion in the flyweight division for amateur boxers between 2007 and 2009. And she recently opened up on why she originally went into the sport, saying: 'At school I was often bullied and I wanted to find a way to defend myself. That's how it all started.'

This then led to her attending a sports school in Halle, Germany where she was picked up by boxing promoter Ulf Steinforth. Years later he reconnected with the model after her fame and stature had grown and suggested the former amateur champion try her hand in the professional ranks.

When asked about their talks, Genrich said: 'Since I sponsor the ring girls at his boxing events, he approached me one day and asked if I wouldn't like to get back in the ring. I finally agreed and am now about to make my professional debut.'

Only four years ago she was Miss Germany... now Tatjana Genrich has her sights set on a career in boxing

The supermodel turned boxer still posts regularly to her 44,500 Instagram followers and owns her own modelling agency

Genrich will be hoping to her journey will inspire a new generation of young women into different sports

Promoter SES Boxing are backing Genrich to become the country's next big superstar, saying: 'Tatjana can follow in Regina Halmich's footsteps. She has all the necessary qualities, an incredible presence, and is extremely ambitious.'

Halmich won 54 of her 56 fights during a storied career between 1994 and 2017 which saw her become one of the most successful female boxers of all time, and also modelled for German magazines.

To prepare for her first fight on November 14, Genrich - who also runs her own modelling agency with 80 models under contract - has begun a rigorous training routine that sees her spending five full days a week in the gym.

In her corner she will have coach Dirk Dzemski, who guided Robert Stieglitz to world champion status in the 2010s.

Genrich also detailed another motivation to succeed in her new career, saying:' I want to be a role model for young women and show them that you can be successful in both your career and sports.

'I train in areas like posture, running and choreography. This prepares me for competitions as well as events like fashion shows.'

Sports.title: Tyson Fury plans to invite 'old buddy' Donald Trump to be part of his ringwalk for £150m mega-fight with Anthony Joshua: 'I'll definitely make the offer!'
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury plans to invite 'old buddy' Donald Trump to be part of his ringwalk for £150m mega-fight with Anthony Joshua: 'I'll definitely make the offer!'

Tyson Fury has suggested he will try and persuade United States president Donald Trump to join him for his ringwalk when he takes on Anthony Joshua in December.

Fury met the president at the UFC Freedom 250 event at the White House in June, joining Trump, First Lady Melania Trump and a host of MAGA royalty on the South Lawn.

He raised eyebrows with a cap, which featured a particularly bold message of support for Trump. 'Donald Trump for Prime Minister', it read alongside an embroidered British flag.

The slogan was a nod to Trump's signature red 'Make America Great Again' caps, which he sported throughout his election campaigns.

It was there Fury said he was keen to take on Joshua in the near future – and that fight has come to fruition, and will take place on December 11 at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff.

And Fury is keen to have his friend there. He said: 'I'll definitely make that offer to my old buddy, old pal, and we'll see if he's available.

'Probably unlikely because of the situation he's in at the moment, being the President of the United States.'

Tyson Fury (centre) has said he will ask Donald Trump (right) to join his ringwalk when he faces Anthony Joshua

Though Fury may want Trump in his corner, Joshua will literally have a Fury in his, with Tyson's uncle, Peter, part of Joshua's group of trainers.

Tyson shrugged off suggestions that Joshua would have the inside track claiming that he hadn't spoken to him in years, but his father John was even more emphatic in discussion with Playbook Boxing, hinting at a betrayal from his brother which meant that he will 'never speak to him as long as (he) lives'.

'If he was to do that (talk to Joshua) in any way, shape or form, that would make him the lowest form of human being,' John stressed. 'Even thinking about doing it, that makes him the biggest dog, the biggest untrustworthy dog of all time.

'If he's going to start giving phone calls and advice, meeting in secret, giving him secret sessions, he's a f***ing cockroach.

'The only advice he could have wanted is on Tyson, isn't it? There is no smoke without fire.'

As if speaking directly to Peter, he finished: 'Son, give your head a wobble. Don't sell your soul to the devil for a fiver.'

Peter shared on social media that he had spoken to AJ 'two months ago' about 'advice on his skill set', calling the Londoner 'a really nice guy'.

'After his fight anything he needs from me (would) be a pleasure. He has a great team around him (including) Team Usyk.'

Sports.title: John Fury hits out at brother Peter, calling him a 'cockroach' for joining Anthony Joshua's camp ahead of Cardiff showdown
Sports.content:
John Fury called out his brother Peter for being a 'cockroach' after his estranged brother joined Anthony Joshua's camp ahead of the Briton's showdown with his son Tyson in December.

The long-awaited Battle of Britain is set to take place in Cardiff after months of back-and-forth between the Fury and Joshua camps, but neither John nor Peter will be in the corner of the Gypsy King, after Joshua announced this week that Fury's uncle had helped with his preparations.

Eyebrows were raised due to Peter's family ties, but Fury shrugged off suggestions that Joshua would have the inside track claiming that he hadn't spoken to him in years.

His father John was even more emphatic in discussion with Playbook Boxing, hinting at a betrayal from his brother which meant that he will 'never speak to him as long as (he) lives.'

'If he was to do that (talk to Joshua) in any way, shape or form, that would make him the lowest form of human being,' John stressed. 'Even thinking about doing it, that makes him the biggest dog, the biggest untrustworthy dog of all time.

'If he's going to start giving phone calls and advice, meeting in secret, giving him secret sessions, he's a f***ing cockroach.

John Fury called out his brother Peter (left) for potentially helping Tyson's rival Anthony Joshua ahead of their Cardiff showdown (pictured in 2015)

'The only advice he could have wanted is on Tyson, isn't it? There is no smoke without fire.'

As if speaking directly to Peter, he finished: 'Son, give your head a wobble. Don't sell your soul to the devil for a fiver.'

Peter shared on social media that he had spoken to AJ 'two months ago' about 'advice on his skill set', calling the Londoner 'a really nice guy'.

'After his fight anything he needs from me (would) be a pleasure. He has a great team around him (including) Team Usyk.'

John may have been staunchly defensive of Fury in the context of Peter doing anything to sabotage him in the ring, but relations between father and son remain minimal after having been, in John's words, 'completely destroyed'.

The duo are at loggerheads over Fury Junior's career, with his father adamant that he should prioritise his health and wellbeing by retiring for good after two failed attempts.

Peter previously trained Fury between 2011 and 2017, but left the camp amid a schism with father and son.

The Gypsy King had previously sought to set the record straight on Peter's involvement with his rival on social media, deeming Joshua's comments 'categorically untrue'.

'Even if Peter Fury hated me, he’s still my family,' he said. 'That would mean he would be a Fredo, scorpion, snake, rat, b****** piece of s*** if he did that.'

Sports.title: Singapore sprint qualifying chaos leaves F1 teams furious
Sports.content:
A race control error that left cars down on power in sprint qualifying at Formula 1's Singapore Grand Prix has left several teams frustrated - with Aston Martin still considering its options.

The first segment of sprint qualifying at Marina Bay was red-flagged to clear up debris from Sergio Perez's front wing.

Once the session resumed, a human error in race control meant that overtake mode - the power boost normally active throughout qualifying - wasn't reactivated. Several drivers reported they were curiously down on power, which was the result of the lack of additional electric boost.

Realising the error, a race control official reactivated the mode for 27 seconds before deactivating it again.

As a result of the human error, the result of SQ1 was severely affected because some cars had set their best lap during the first part, using Overtake Mode as normal, while after the stoppage other cars were either unable to improve without the extra power or were left outside the top 16 cut-off.

While the majority of cars were affected to some degree, the human error particularly affected the likes of Arvid Lindblad, Lance Stroll and the two Williams cars, who were all eliminated in SQ1.

Autosport understands Williams made a request to race control after SQ1 to allow all 22 cars to participate in SQ2, effectively starting with a clean slate. But it is understood the race stewards denied that request, because they were unsure if they had the regulatory capacity to do so. Another request to re-run SQ1 also couldn't be granted due to a lack of available tyre sets.

Carlos Sainz, Williams Photo by: Andy Hone/ LAT Images via Getty Images

As the FIA's single-seater director Nikolas Tombazis met with the affected teams and drivers, Williams and Racing Bulls are understood to be extremely frustrated by the events, but both teams have indicated they are not planning to protest the results of sprint qualifying.

Aston Martin was indicating it still wanted to leave its options open, depending on any further action by the FIA to make any rectifications. Aston Martin is keen for the starting grid for Saturday morning's sprint to reflect a fair and equal playing field. However, it is understood there will be no further changes to the sprint qualifying result, and equally the result of SQ1 is not subject to protest at this point. In any case, it is hard to see how the governing body could have pulled any levers to untangle the mess without causing further angst up and down the grid.

The issue is the second significant hiccup in two consecutive weekends after the start of last week's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia was delayed because of a software glitch in the power unit control systems.

The FIA race control issue was independent of a separate timing issue, controlled by F1 management, which failed to register several lap times throughout SQ1. But the lack of reliable lap times did leave several drivers confused about whether or not they had done enough to progress to SQ2, further adding to the chaos.

An apology issued by the FIA after the SQ1 error read: "During the first period of Sprint Qualifying there was a human error in Race Control unrelated to the timing issue also encountered in SQ1.

"This issue in question meant Overtake Mode was not available after the red flag period during SQ1. When it became apparent that Overtake Mode was not active after the restart, it was then activated for a period of 27 seconds before being deactivated again.

"The FIA acknowledges that this unfortunate human error had an impact on the performance of certain cars based on the timing of their run and their position around the lap. The second and third periods of sprint qualifying were not affected."

Sports.title: FIA reveals "human error" caused latest software glitch in Singapore sprint qualifying
Sports.content:
The FIA has confirmed the existence of a second error during sprint qualifying for the Singapore GP, on top of a glitch in the timing and scoring system which caused some drivers' times to not be displayed.

SQ1 was halted by a red flag when Sergio Perez hit the barrier at Turn 5, then extracted his car and made his way back to the pits, losing his damaged front wing in the process. This forced race control to pause proceedings while the debris was cleared.

Once the session got back under way, two peculiarities manifested themselves: some lap times not being registered on the system, and several drivers complaining that they had less power than expected. Many of these were informed that the latter issue was the responsibility of the FIA, leading them to conclude that it was related to the software bug which affected last weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

"We only got one lap. We had some brake issues," said Carlos Sainz, who was eliminated in SQ1.

"But on top of that, half the cars did the lap with an engine half a second quicker than the others. There was another software issue this time around and we were on the bad end of it.

"For whatever reason, the FIA, like Malaysia, didn't decide to sort it quickly and were happy to do half of the cars in quali with higher power than the other half of the cars.

"So a bit confused why the sport keeps doing different things depending on who is out in Q1 and who is out in lap one."

Sergio Perez, Cadillac Racing Photo by: Clive Rose / Formula 1 via Getty Images

But the governing body has clarified that this was not a software issue but a case of human error regarding the enabling of Overtake Mode, the system which gives drivers access to an extra half-megajoule of energy. This can have far-reaching effects since it can not only have an input into outright laptime on a push lap, but also affect tyre preparation on out-laps.

"During the first period of sprint qualifying there was a human error in Race Control unrelated to the timing issue also encountered in SQ1," said an FIA spokesperson.

"This issue in question meant overtake mode was not available after the red flag period during SQ1. When it became apparent that overtake mode was not active after the restart, it was then activated for a period of 27 seconds before being deactivated again.

"The FIA acknowledges that this unfortunate human error had an impact on the performance of certain cars based on the timing of their run and their position around the lap. The second and third periods of sprint qualifying were not affected."

Although not software-related, this is another high-profile slip-up after the farcical scenes which caused last weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix to be paused after a single formation lap in which the cars lost electrical power in the wet conditions.

It is understood that as well as Sainz, Kimi Antonelli, Charles Leclerc and both Aston Martin drivers were affected.

Sports.title: F1 Singapore GP: Verstappen storms to sprint pole with Antonelli only seventh
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen topped sprint qualifying for Formula 1’s Singapore Grand Prix, where he will be joined on the front row by George Russell.

This is the first time Verstappen has come first in a qualifying session of any sort at Marina Bay Street Circuit.

Meanwhile, championship leader Kimi Antonelli will start Saturday’s sprint race from seventh, having been outpaced by the Ferraris and McLarens.

SQ1 - Verstappen fastest, Lindblad misses out

Arvid Lindblad, Racing Bulls Photo by: Rudy Carezzevoli / Getty Images

Nobody had even set a time in SQ1 when Sergio Perez caused a yellow flag as he crashed into the Tecpro at Turn 5. The Cadillac driver damaged his front wing and eventually lost it on the racing line, with the red flag waved to clear the debris.

There were just six minutes remaining with few actual competitive lap times. As a consequence, the final moments were a rush to get a decent mark on the board, with cars out in the pitlane several minutes before the light even went green.

Verstappen eventually went fastest in 1m33.477s, nearly half a second slower than his own FP1 benchmark on the same medium tyre. The Red Bull racer led Charles Leclerc by 0.018s and George Russell by 0.096s, with Lewis Hamilton 0.271s down.

Everyone else was at least six tenths adrift, starting with an impressive Nico Hulkenberg for Audi, closely followed by Isack Hadjar, Lando Norris, Oscar Piastri and Antonelli.

Further down the classification, Carlos Sainz was slowest of all. “I had a lot of front locking and no rear, combined,” he complained on the radio. He was eliminated after SQ1, like Williams team-mate Alex Albon, Cadillac duo Perez and Valtteri Bottas, Aston Martin’s Lance Stroll and, more surprisingly, Arvid Lindblad. Racing Bulls’ rookie was missing one tenth to make the cut, albeit after confusion caused by an FIA software glitch

SQ2 – Russell narrowly survives after lock-up

George Russell, Mercedes Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

Verstappen went 0.75s quicker than the SQ1 fastest time as early as his first attempt in the second segment of sprint qualifying, setting a 1m32.724s.

However, the Dutchman’s reference was swiftly surpassed by Leclerc, Hamilton and Norris, with the Monegasque adding a 1m32.457s to the board. Antonelli and Russell were six and nine tenths adrift respectively.

Meanwhile, Hadjar, Gabriel Bortoleto, Fernando Alonso, Franco Colapinto, Esteban Ocon and Oliver Bearman were at risk of elimination. Even Hadjar was missing nearly half a second compared to 10th-placed Hulkenberg.

Russell’s second attempt was no better, with a lock-up into Turn 13. Hadjar’s and Colapinto’s respective improvements knocked the eight-time grand prix winner out of the top 10, but last-ditch progress saw him jump to safety in fourth.

Colapinto was therefore eliminated with a 0.094s deficit on Alpine team-mate Pierre Gasly, along with Hulkenberg, who failed to improve late on.

SQ3 – Verstappen outpaces Leclerc

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari Photo by: Clive Mason / Getty Images

Switching from medium to soft rubber as per the regulations, drivers had few actual chances to make an impact in the eight-minute SQ3 phase.

The McLarens and Mercedes were first out, with Norris setting the pace in 1m31.587s, leading Piastri by 0.189s, Russell by 0.250s and Antonelli by 0.518s.

Then it was the Ferraris in action, and Leclerc went quickest in 1m31.568s, narrowly edging Norris out. Hamilton was nearly two tenths faster than his team-mate in the first sector but lost even more in the final part and ended up 0.134s adrift.

Leclerc actually improved late on with a 1m31.399s, but couldn’t hold off a much faster Verstappen, who set a 1m31.156s on his sole attempt – not an actual pole position given this was sprint qualifying, but still unprecedented from the four-time world champion.

Russell clinched a front-row spot in the final instants of the session, leading Leclerc, Piastri, Norris and Hamilton.

Antonelli ended up seventh, 0.693s down on Verstappen, while Hadjar and Gasly exceeded track limits and have no lap time to their names. They will share the fifth row of the grid on Saturday afternoon.

Sports.title: Is Antonelli favoured by Mercedes? Wolff responds to latest claims
Sports.content:
Mercedes Formula 1 team principal Toto Wolff says people who suggest Kimi Antonelli is being favoured over George Russell are “brainless” and should stick to ‘watching Teletubbies’.

Conspiracy theories stemmed from Russell’s engine failure in Malaysia, which forced the Briton into an early power unit change and grid penalty, as it was previously hoped he would benefit from the ADUO upgrade later this month.

Because he is taking a penalty anyway, Russell is running Mercedes’ older aerodynamic package at the Singapore Grand Prix. The 28-year-old himself suggested it might be worth reverting to the previous version, which he won with in Baku before revised floor and sidepods were introduced at Sepang, where Red Bull prevailed for the first time this season. Antonelli is keeping those new parts this weekend.

On top of this, Wolff’s unblinking facial expression during his brief appearance on screen as Russell retired from the Malaysian race only fuelled the theories further.

However, when the topic was brought up to the Austrian in Friday’s press conference in Singapore and he was asked what to say to those who speculate, he retorted: “They're brainless, whoever thinks that. I mean, it's completely nonsensical. We've had it in the past with Lewis [Hamilton] fans.

“I don't know what's going on! Do they think I have a button and that says ‘George engine failure now’? Or disadvantaging one driver against the other when we're fighting for a constructors’ championship. We've always had the mindset of providing everybody equal material.

George Russell, Mercedes Photo by: Liam Fabre

“But I guess this is maybe where social media goes today. People hide behind their screens, and then they lash out. There's a lot of polarisation going on and sometimes I read what people write. I find it hilarious. These people really contribute to my own entertainment when they're abusing the team or myself. I'm Satan, I've heard. So yeah, overall, funny.”

Wolff added: “Really, zero understanding and respect for people who come up with these things. Rather than watching Formula 1, they should do Teletubbies or, I don't know, some Mickey Mouses.”

Still, Antonelli’s advantage in the lead of the championship is larger than ever before, with Russell’s 84 points in arrears, and one reporter remarked teams are thought to naturally gravitate towards the driver delivering results. Wolff was therefore asked how much he has strived to nurse Russell’s morale in that context.

“I've always tried, since I came into Formula 1, even in my Williams days, to be the most balanced and most transparent with the drivers,” he replied.

“I have told this story before, I remember being a complete rookie and running into Alain Prost on the grid of a race, and I said, ‘Just out of interest, why did it go so wrong between you and Senna?’ And he said, ‘Because we never knew what the team was about’. You felt that you were the flavour of the month at one time, and then two months later, you thought the politics were going against you. There were different situations where you had the feeling that you’re really not wanted.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, George Russell, Mercedes, Toto Wolff, Mercedes Photo by: Andy Hone/ LAT Images via Getty Images

“So I took it as my challenge to keep it always balanced. And it was not easy with Lewis and Nico [Rosberg] back in the day. And that’s why people can think what they want, but the integrity in that respect is something that's important for me, and the drivers know it.”

Wolff also pointed out both his drivers are products from Mercedes’ young-driver programme, which each of them joined nearly a decade ago.

“We have had Kimi since he was 11,” he continued. “He's an integral part of the team. It is very nice to see him grow, be in a position now that he's fighting for a championship at such a young age, the talent he has.

“And then on the other side, George, who's been with us since he was 17 – someone that I feel a lot of emotions for, and compassion. We are very close. We're spending time with [Russell’s fiancee] Carmen and [Wolff’s wife] Susie off the track with each other.

“If people would see that we're travelling together, we're having coffee in the same coffee shop, we're going to the gym… That's why it's pretty annoying to have some lunatics that have no understanding really about how relationships work, coming up with this kind of accusations.

“So I don't pay any attention to this. Most important is that George knows how the team is, and Kimi knows, and we will always try to give them equal opportunity.

“And when it comes to the upgrade, it's a good example. We don't know which one is going to be quicker. And so you take a decision and say, ‘Let's try to find out’, and there is no political thinking behind it.

“Even if now it's more realistic for Kimi to win a championship in sheer mathematical probability, we would still give George the same opportunities. And that's important, that's the ethos and the integrity on which the team has operated since 2013, since I came. And we are going to stick to that. And then people can think what they want.”

Sports.title: "It should be banned" - F1 drivers still divided over cooling vests
Sports.content:
F1 drivers are split over the use and importance of cooling vests as the series is set for its fourth "heat hazard" race of 2026.

Driver comfort in hot climates has been a point of conversation since the 2023 Qatar Grand Prix, when several drivers experienced heat exhaustion symptoms. In response, the FIA and all F1 teams commissioned extensive research, ending up with a standard cooling vest that circulates water through a tube system. When temperatures are expected to exceed 31C, the FIA declared a "heat hazard" forcing drivers to either use the vest or add 0.5kg of corresponding ballast to the car.

With the original design not particularly popular with drivers because of its limited effectiveness beyond a handful of laps and a lack of comfort inside the cockpit, the FIA has provided a cost cap allowance for teams wishing to improve the design. They were offered a 50,000 USD cost cap exemption if they could come up with a cooling system that was proven to work for the entire race duration, as well as a 75,000 USD allowance for improving the comfort and effectiveness of the cooling vest itself.

Mercedes driver George Russell triggered debate with an interview in The Times, calling on the governing body to step in and do more to improve the regulatory framework. Mercedes is one of the teams that decided not to pursue a bespoke system because it felt the cost cap allowance wasn't sufficient and because it would rather spend the engineering resources on making its car quicker than devote them to a comfort issue.

As Russell mentioned in his explanation, any extra human resources poured into sporadically used vests would not be spent on improving the performance of his W17 car.

So, as Mercedes battles to stay ahead of the pack against advances from McLaren, Red Bull and Ferrari, and the issue revolves around comfort rather than outright safety concerns at this stage, it is clear where the priority is.

Few drivers appear to agree with Russell, with some feeling the current systems are good enough to cover the most extreme cases and others outright declaring the system shouldn't exist in the first place, like Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar.

Isack Hadjar, Red Bull Racing Photo by: James Sutton / Formula 1 / Formula Motorsport Ltd via Getty Images

"I think it should be banned, because it's supposed to be tough," Hadjar said in Singapore, the fourth heat hazard event of 2026.

Verstappen added: "For me it's not needed. Yes it's hot, but it's not a sauna, and with this cooling vest you have these stupid cables in your car, so it's just limiting your movement as well. Even if it would work for one and a half hours, like cool cool, I don't need it. But it doesn't work anyway for one and a half hours."

Alpine driver Franco Colapinto was equally dismissive. "Yes, I think it's hot, but it's been hot for the history of the sport. It's good to have it as an option. Personally, I don't like it. I don't feel it's comfortable."

Russell's teammate Kimi Antonelli said he didn't use the standard system because of "two very bad experiences" in his debut campaign last year. And while he would welcome an improved solution, he is happy to just focus on work he can do while training to aid his heat acclimatisation.

"When I wore it last year, I had two very bad experiences," Antonelli said. "The first time it didn't work as long as we hoped for. The second time, the pump system failed and I did the whole session with the system pumping the water at 50 degrees. I suffered a heat stroke after the session, so it wasn't very pleasant.

"Ever since, I was like: 'You know what, I'm going to train hard so I don't have to use it for the weekends. If we get to a point where it's developed and we have the confidence that it's going to work every time and for the time that we need to, I think it's very nice because it definitely keeps you cool. But now there's so much uncertainty."

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Photo by: Mark Sutton / Formula 1 via Getty Images

Ferrari's Charles Leclerc said he would take an imperfect system over one that doesn't exist, even if it only works for half an hour. "Ideally, if I can have an even better cooling vest, I will always take it," he said. "Let’s say that for 15, 20 laps it works pretty well. Then after, for the rest of the race you are quite warm, just like you are with other cooling vests. At least I’m getting 15, 20 laps, and I’m already grateful for that."

"Some drivers don't even want to hear about the cooling vest, but that's the preference of each single driver."

There are also some unequivocal proponents of the system, such as Williams driver Carlos Sainz. "If there's one thing as a team we've done well on development this year, it's the cooling vest, which has definitely given Alex and me a good time inside the car. We're very happy to have it. I see Mercedes' point. At the same time, we've prioritised it more than Mercedes, and that's why we have it going and working better."

Haas driver Esteban Ocon even felt the system helped his personal performance, even if just for a limited amount of time. "I think it's been a massive performance gain for the physical aspect of things," the Frenchman said.

"Of course, it hasn't worked the whole race since we introduced the system. It lasts for like 40 minutes, and then it's just hot fluid that keeps going on because it's so hot in the car. But it's already good that we have something, because I've raced my whole career before that without."

"I don't think everybody realises how much better it is for an athlete to be at the right temperature to perform."

Sports.title: F1 Singapore GP: Russell tops FP1 with Verstappen also impressing
Sports.content:
George Russell came fastest in the only free practice outing of Formula 1’s Singapore Grand Prix, but Max Verstappen was half a second quicker than anyone on medium tyres.

This was the only non-competitive running on the sprint Singapore weekend, albeit held in unrepresentative conditions – 53C track temperature – with regards to both upcoming qualifying sessions and the main race, which will be held at night.

Everyone therefore rushed out on track when the light went green at the end of the pitlane, with all cars but the Cadillacs on hard tyres, and started chasing the limits.

With the white-walled compound, Kimi Antonelli set the pace in 1m33.830s, outpacing Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc by 0.034s and Mercedes team-mate George Russell by 0.056s.

Isack Hadjar was fourth, having complained that his Red Bull bottomed too much, especially in braking zones, and his throttle pedal was slippery. Oscar Piastri, Lando Norris and Lewis Hamilton followed within 0.6s of the benchmark.

Everyone else was more than a second down, starting with midfield leader Nico Hulkenberg for Audi. Verstappen was down in ninth, followed by Pierre Gasly and Fernando Alonso; Liam Lawson and Esteban Ocon were another couple of tenths adrift.

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: James Sutton / LAT Images via Getty Images

Hulkenberg however stopped on the main straight with 20 minutes remaining, indicating on the radio: “Something bad happened on the gearbox.” He was pulled into the pitlane while the virtual safety car neutralised the session.

Cars kept lapping on hard tyres, with Lawson jumping to ninth ahead of Verstappen, until softer rubber was fitted on for the last 15 minutes.

Despite running the older Mercedes specification, Russell was fastest by far on soft tyres, setting a 1m32.274s. This was two tenths faster than Leclerc and Norris, while Hamilton and Piastri were half a second adrift. They were the only five drivers to run the soft compound, except the Cadillac racers, who propped up the order.

Verstappen led the medium-tyre running in sixth with a 1m33.006s, half a second faster than championship leader Antonelli, who ran into the Turn 16 escape road on his final flying lap. Hadjar was seven tenths slower than his Red Bull team-mate.

Also on medium tyres, Gasly led the midfield for Alpine on a 1m34.038s, with Racing Bulls’ Lawson one tenth down and Haas’ Oliver Bearman three tenths adrift. Aston Martin, Williams and Audi were closely matched, albeit further down the order – but the green car’s progress was entirely down to Alonso, given Lance Stroll reported problems with his brakes.

Sports.title: McLaren targets Norris’ costly fuel system issue with Singapore F1 power unit fixes
Sports.content:
The McLaren F1 team has made a number of peripheral changes to Lando Norris' Mercedes power unit in a bid to eradicate a persistent fuel system problem.

McLaren was left significantly off the pace on Baku's long straights two weeks ago compared to Mercedes, with which it shares engines. But while some of its deficit was explained by intrinsic car weaknesses and by how it ran the Mercedes unit, Norris' car was particularly down on top speed in qualifying with what McLaren identified as a fuel injection issue. The issue returned intermittently in the race, also on Oscar Piastri's car to a lesser extent, and then hampered the team in last weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

It's understood McLaren has now decided to make a number of changes to auxiliary components related to the power unit, including the fuel system, which is on the team side rather than Mercedes, ahead of Singapore FP1 in a bid to resolve the issue.

"[I am] hopeful. We need to get on track first and see how much better it is," Norris said on Thursday.

"'It's been a frustrating two weekends trying to figure out what the issue has been and why there's just been a constant lack of straight-line speed and performance. And especially in this kind of battle we've been in, the last two qualifying [sessions] it's been two or three positions. So, it's cost me quite a lot."

Photo by: Liam Fabre

Singapore is one of the least power-sensitive circuits on the F1 calendar, but with a close battle between the top four expected, McLaren can't leave any performance on the table, and FP1 is a good opportunity to see if its fuel system issues are a thing of the past.

"It's obviously also a circuit where straights are not the highest priority and not as detrimental as the last few weekends," the reigning world champion said. "But nevertheless, you always want to go down the straights as quick as you should be able to and it's always tough when you come out of corners better and end up going slower.

"At the same time, there's obviously things I can do better as well. But confident that the team has done a good job. They put a lot of work into trying to figure out things and I'm hopeful that it'll be better this weekend. But honestly, I have to get out on track and see first."

More generally, Singapore is an important test for McLaren to verify whether its puzzling lack of performance in Malaysia was a one-off. The Sepang circuit was expected to suit the MCL40's strengths, but instead McLaren was only the fourth-fastest team on the circuit, potentially linked to how the car's aerodynamics interacted with the extremely rough track surface.

Sports.title: Audi F1 drivers reveal biggest engine limitation – and why they’re not worried
Sports.content:
In theory, the Marina Bay Street Circuit in Singapore should suit Audi well. The team led by Allan McNish would normally benefit from tracks on the Formula 1 calendar that are slightly less power-sensitive, but that rule of thumb does not necessarily apply in Asia.

Yes, in terms of outright power, the gap to the leading engine manufacturers should be smaller, but according to the drivers, another factor is causing Audi problems in the extreme conditions of Malaysia and Singapore.

“I think we have to be cautious and careful”, Nico Hulkenberg said during his Thursday media session.

“I think Malaysia brought some new things to light and these climatic conditions are not so favourable for our PU at the moment. We definitely had some struggles on that side and obviously here it's more of the same.”

Just as in Malaysia, the FIA has issued a so-called heat hazard declaration for the Singapore Grand Prix, indicating that temperatures of 31 degrees Celsius or higher are forecast. Hulkenberg therefore expects another challenging weekend.

“It is a less power-sensitive circuit on paper, for sure, but my personal expectations are not too high for the moment”, the German said.

Asked whether this is mainly related to cooling – with Audi having to open up more of the bodywork and consequently losing aerodynamic performance – Hulkenberg clarified that this is not the case.

Nico Hulkenberg, Audi Photo by: Srinivasa Krishnan

“No, I think we suffer from power.”

This means that Audi is losing outright engine power in the extreme heat, an assessment shared by team-mate Gabriel Bortoleto.

“Yes, I would say that right now, especially in the last races, it’s our biggest limitation”, Bortoleto said when asked about the heat by Autosport.

“I think what we already have for our first season is something decent. We just need to make some more steps to improve drivability, the situations of the climatisation that you were mentioning, and yeah, that's it.”

However, Bortoleto is fully confident that Audi will take those steps and eventually become the benchmark in terms of engine performance in F1. The Brazilian draws that confidence partly from Audi's successes in DTM and the 24 Hours of Le Mans.

“If I trust them? Absolutely. I think they can fix it. These people in Neuburg have built the best engines in other series that they have taken part in in the past, and I have no doubts they're going to do the same in Formula 1.

“We just need to give them time. We cannot believe that we would arrive in Formula 1 in the first year and build the best thing ever made. It would make the others look like... I would swear right now, but you understood what I was going to say!

“So we need to have patience. I believe in the people that are there in Neuburg, and I believe they're going to make something great.”

Audi finds answers about its major upgrade package

Gabriel Bortoleto, Audi Photo by: Srinivasa Krishnan

While there are still areas for improvement on the power unit side, the German-Swiss team has now found answers regarding the major upgrade package it introduced in Baku.

The Baku City Circuit predominantly featured 90-degree corners and therefore did not provide a representative picture, but after back-to-back tests in Malaysia, it is clear that the upgrade has indeed been a step forward.

“Well, we concluded that it worked. It worked pretty OK, like we expected”, Bortoleto said.

“Entry, mid, exit of all the corners, I think we made a good step everywhere. There were a lot of doubts after Baku, because we had a tough weekend, about the package and if it worked or not. But I think now we can finally put a dot on this and say that we are sure that it worked as expected and that things are working in the right way.”

It also underlines that F1 teams often need some time to fully understand major upgrade packages and extract the maximum performance from them. In Audi's case, that has now happened, as Hulkenberg also confirmed when asked by Autosport.

“Yes, we are for sure closer [to understanding it]. The understanding obviously grows and builds with every session you do. You do different setup variations, you scan the delta to map, and in general you build your correlation between the track, the wind tunnel and CFD, so it's good.

“I think there's probably still some bits and bobs to explore and to discover, but it's not like we're going to get another second out of it or something.”

Sports.title: Verstappen keeps sprint race pole position after passing Hamilton under yellow flags | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen has kept his pole position for Saturday’s sprint race at the Marina Bay circuit in Singapore.

They determined the Red Bull driver was already approaching Hamilton’s car at speed when the yellow flags were displayed. They accepted Verstappen’s explanation that he would have had to slow sharply to avoid passing Hamilton.

As car three [Verstappen] was exiting turn seven on a push lap, a single yellow flag was displayed. Car 44 [Hamilton] was ahead of car three and had been warned of car three’s approach. The driver of car 44 said that after exiting turn seven, he slowed and moved to the right to ensure he was off the racing line. Car three overtook car 44 prior to turn eight while both cars were still in the yellow flag sector. Car three then abandoned the push lap.

The driver of car three explained that he was on throttle exiting turn seven and then saw the yellow flag and lifted. This was confirmed by telemetry. Within approximately 40 metres of entering the yellow flag sector, the driver of car three had lifted fully off throttle. The driver of car 44 was braking and had reduced speed to less than 60km/h at the point car three overtook. Because car three was on a push lap and was on throttle out of turn seven and car 44 had slowed, the speed differential at the point of the overlap was significant despite the fact that the driver of car three had also started braking.

The stewards were satisfied that the driver of car three reacted appropriately to the yellow flag by lifting off throttle and reducing speed. The speed of car three at the overtake point was some 70km/h less than car three’s speed on another push lap in the same session. The driver of car three explained that to have avoided the overtake would have required him to have braked very heavily and he considered to have done so would have potentially created an unsafe situation.

The stewards determined that the driver of car three breached the yellow flag regulation by overtaking car 44. However, the stewards were satisfied that the overtake was an unfortunate consequence of the significant closing speed differential and, in these circumstances, determined not to impose a penalty.

Sports.title: Sainz slates FIA for qualifying blunder which left some drivers down on power | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Carlos Sainz Jnr says the FIA showed no regard for “sporting equity” after an error left some drivers down on power in qualifying.

Sainz was one of the six drivers who were eliminated in SQ1. He set the 15th-fastest time in first practice but ended qualifying 22nd and last.

He said a number of problem affects his lap, one of which was the reduction in power due to Overtake Mode being disabled.

“We did the whole lap with half a second less power than any other lap of the weekend, so that’s never going to help,” said Sainz. “But with all the issues that we had on the brakes and tyres in that quali, we would have always struggled to get through.”

“We only got one lap and we had some issues with the brakes in FP1,” he explained. “We had to change them for [sprint race qualifying] and we were having some brakes issues still. I had a few lock-ups and was struggling a lot with that and with the tyres.

“But on top of that half of the cars did the lap with half a second quicker engine than the others. There was another software issue with the cars at this time around and we on the bad end of it.”

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Overtake Mode is only available at certain times during a race but is supposed to be enabled by default in qualifying. It allows drivers to recharged their batteries by 9MJ per lap instead of 8.5MJ, giving them more power.

The latest technical fault to affect a competitive F1 session comes just five days after the start of the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia was delayed for almost an hour due to an FIA software fault. On that occasion several drivers complained that those who stopped on-track were allowed to regain their original starting positions.

“For whatever reason, the FIA, like in Malaysia, didn’t decide to do sporting equity, and were happy to do half of the cars in quali with a higher power than the other half of their cars,” said Sainz. “So I’m a bit confused why the sport keeps doing different things depending on who is out in Q1 or who is in lap one.”

Williams team principal James Vowles said the fault “A very frustrating evening. After the red flag in the first session of Sprint qualifying there was an issue with the way overtake mode was activated which definitely had an impact on our lap times. We are confident this will be fully investigated by the FIA.

Lance Stroll also confirmed he was affected by the same problem. “I didn’t have overtake mode available on my second push lap so missed out on any chances [of] fighting to get through to Q2,” said the Aston Martin driver.

Sports.title: FIA confirms some drivers lost power in qualifying due to Overtake Mode error | Formula 1
Sports.content:
The FIA has confirmed a problem with Formula 1’s Overtake Mode system affected the performance of some cars in qualifying for the sprint race.

The messages ‘overtake enabled’ and ‘overtake disabled’ appeared on the timing screens during SQ1.

The session was interrupted by a red flag after Sergio Perez crashed. The FIA confirmed that, after the session restarted, Overtake Mode was unavailable for a period.

The FIA also experienced a problem with its timing systems which delayed the beginning of SQ2. It said the two faults were not connected.

“During the first period of Sprint Qualifying there was a human error in Race Control unrelated to the timing issue also encountered in SQ1,” the FIA said in a statement.

“This issue in question meant Overtake Mode was not available after the red flag period during SQ1. When it became apparent that Overtake Mode was not active after the restart, it was then activated for a period of 27 seconds before being deactivated again.

“The FIA acknowledges that this unfortunate human error had an impact on the performance of certain cars based on the timing of their run and their position around the lap. The second and third periods of Sprint Qualifying were not affected.”

Sports.title: Verstappen beats Russell to pole but faces investigation for yellow flag incident | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen scorched to pole position for the sprint race in Singapore ahead of George Russell.

However the Red Bull driver is under investigation for overtaking Lewis Hamilton under yellow flags during the first round of qualifying.

Verstappen took provisional pole position off Charles Leclerc with his sole lap of SQ3. Russell then pulled out a rapid lap in his Mercedes to join Verstappen on the front row of the grid.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, who started the weekend running Mercedes’ upgrade package, could only manage seventh on the grid. The Ferrari and McLaren drivers separated him from his team mate.

Lewis Hamilton began his final lap strongly but lost time with a few snaps of oversteer in the middle sector. Both McLaren drivers beat his time, leaving him sixth.

Liam Lawson took a strong eighth on the grid after his team mate Arvid Lindblad was eliminated in the first round. The Racing Bulls driver benefited from Isack Hadjar going wide in the final corner, exceeding track limits and losing his lap time as a result.

The session was disrupted by a timing fault which struck at the end of SQ1. The problem developed at the end of the first round of qualifying when several drivers’ lap times failed to appear on the screen. A number of “overtake enabled” and “overtake disabled” messages also appeared incorrectly.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

The FIA initially advised they were “investigating whether we can proceed with the rest of the session”. Some drivers who were eliminated in SQ1 were unsure where they qualified when the session ended. However SQ2 commenced soon afterwards.

Franco Colapinto was unable to join his team mate in SQ3, but will start immediately behind him. The Audi and Haas drivers also dropped out at this stage, as did Fernando Alonso, who left his team mate behind in SQ1.

The first round of qualifying was interrupted after Sergio Perez crashed at turn five. He was able to extract his Cadillac from the barrier but its front wing was hanging off and eventually part of it came loose, leaving a lump of debris approaching turn eight.

Verstappen slipped past Hamilton’s Ferrari as they reached the yellow flag. The Red Bull driver immediately suspected he had broken the rules and got on the radio to his team. The stewards will investigate the incident after the session but confirmed they would take no action against Perez.

All 22 drivers participated in the restart. The Cadillac drivers went no further but both of them beat Carlos Sainz Jnr, who will start last in his Williams.

Sports.title: Claims Mercedes favour Antonelli over Russell are ‘brainless’ and ‘nonsensical’ – Wolff | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff sharply criticised those who suggest his team is favouring one of its drivers over the other.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli has out-scored George Russell by 320 points to 236 so far this season. Russell’s fading championship hopes suffered a fresh blow in Malaysia when he suffered an engine failure. He was running behind his team mate at the time.

Both drivers have retired from races due to technical problems this year, though Russell has suffered more. He will start this weekend’s grand prix from the back of the grid as Mercedes had to replace his power unit again due to his retirement in Malaysia.

Wolff made it clear he has no time for those who claim the team has prioritised Antonelli. “Really [I have] zero understanding and respect for people who come up with these things,” Wolff remarked. “Rather than watching Formula 1, they should do Teletubbies or some Mickey Mouse.”

“They’re brainless, whoever thinks that,” he said.

“I mean, it’s completely nonsensical. We’ve had it in the past with Lewis [Hamilton] fans. I mean, literally, I don’t know what’s going on. Do they think I have a button that says, ‘George engine failure now’, or disadvantaging one driver against the other when we are fighting for a constructors’ championship, when we have always had the mindset of providing everybody equal material?”

He suggested the claims largely come from people posting anonymously online. “I guess this is maybe where social media goes today,” he said. “People hide behind their screens and then they lash out.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“There’s a lot of polarisation going on, and sometimes I read what people write, I find it hilarious. These people really contribute to my own entertainment when they are abusing the team or myself. I’m Satan, I’ve heard. So, yeah, overall it’s funny.”

Neither of Mercedes’ drivers believe there is favouritism within the team, Wolff emphasised.

“We have had Kimi since he was 11. He is an integral part of the team. It is very nice to see him grow, be in a position now that he is fighting for a championship at such a young age, the talent he has.

“Then on the other side, George, who has been with us since he was 17, someone that I feel a lot of, how can I say, emotions for and compassion. We are very close.

“We are spending time with Carmen and Susie off the track with each other. If people would see that we’re travelling together, we’re having coffee in the same coffee shop, we’re going to the gym, that’s why it’s pretty annoying to have some lunatics that have no understanding really about how relationships work coming up with these kinds of accusations. So, I don’t pay any attention to this.

“Most important is that George knows how the team is and Kimi knows, and we will always try to give them equal opportunity.”

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

The team is in an unusual situation this weekend as only one driver, Antonelli, is running their latest upgrade while Russell has reverted to the old car specification.

“When it comes to the upgrade, it’s a good example,” said Wolff. “We don’t know which one is going to be quicker.

“So you take a decision and say, ‘Let’s try to find out.’ And there is no great political thinking behind it.

“When it comes to racing, like [McLaren’s] ‘Papaya Rules’, we have always been very clear that we’re not standing in each other’s way. We don’t like the yo-yo racing that could cost a position if someone is close to us, and the quicker car, if it’s behind, is always going to have an advantage. And that could go either direction, it doesn’t matter.

“Even if it is now that it’s more realistic for Kimi to win a championship in sheer mathematical probability, we would still give George the same opportunities. And that’s important. That’s the ethos and the integrity on which the team has operated since 2013, since I came, and we are going to stick to that. And then people can think what they want.”

Sports.title: Russell quickest in old-spec Mercedes as Antonelli and Red Bull pair save tyres | Formula 1
Sports.content:
George Russell was quickest in the sole practice session for the Singapore Grand Prix after returning to Mercedes’ pre-Sepang car specification.

However his team mate Andrea Kimi Antonelli, running the latest parts plus the team’s new front wing, did not set a flying lap on the soft tyres, as he chose to save fresh sets for qualifying. Nor did Max Verstappen or Isack Hadjar of Red Bull.

The Mercedes drivers are pursuing different strategies as Russell has a grid penalty for this weekend’s race. Mercedes fitted a complete new power unit to his car following his retirement in Malaysia, meaning he will have to start from the back of the ghrid.

Russell therefore led the Ferrari and McLaren drivers on soft rubber. Charles Leclerc got within two-tenths of a second of the Mercedes, having backed out of his first tyre run claiming Lance Stroll held him up at turn four.

Lando Norris looked quick from the off in his McLaren. Lewis Hamilton and Oscar Piastri backed up their team mates in the next two positions.

Antonelli locked up at turn 16 during one of his late runs on the medium rubber. That left him seventh behind Verstappen, who was immediately quick on the hard tyre when the track was at its dirtiest early in the session, and fastest of those who set times on mediums.

Hadjar was next in eighth albeit seven-tenths of a second slower than Verstappen. He was unhappy with his car’s balance early in the session, telling his team: “the grounding is a disaster on the brakes, I have zero confidence to push.”

Pierre Gasly put his Alpine in ninth place and Liam Lawson completed the top 10 for Racing Bulls. Nico Hulkenberg came to a stop at the pit lane exit just after the halfway point in the session due to an unspecified problem in his Audi.

Sports.title: Williams ‘completely missed this set of regulations and got it really wrong’ – Sainz | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Williams’ poor 2026 campaign “has nothing to do with” team principal James Vowles’ recent criticism of Formula 1’s cost cap, says Carlos Sainz Jnr.

Vowles recently claimed the team faces a “cost cap trap” where it cannot pay for the improvements its infrastructure needs without taking money away from car development. Sainz, who is a director of the Grand Prix Drivers’ Association, agrees this is a problem which F1 should tackle.

“When James says something as clear as that, it’s not a political battle, it is something that, for sure, 20 years’ under-investment you cannot recover quickly within a budget cap,” said Sainz. “Because you’re basically attributing [part] of the budget cap, that is not being attributed to car development, in improving your infrastructure.

“It is definitely the case for us and for other teams that are in the same trajectory and same path as us.”

However Sainz does not believe that is the reason why the team has suffered a much less competitive season than last year. “I think the underperformance of this year has nothing to do with that,” he said.

“We completely missed the new set of regulations and we got it really wrong with this year’s concept of the car and aerodynamics and the timing of it,” he explained.

“But if you want Williams to catch up quicker, or Williams or other teams with under-investment for many years to catch up quicker, we need allowance from the budget cap to be able to invest on it. So it’s simple.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“I don’t see it’s very complicated, it’s whether the sport is ready or not to change up the regulation in order for that to happen.”

Williams has scored 12 points so far this season. At the same point last year it had 86.

The team introduced a significant upgrade package in Baku, where Sainz scored their first point for nine rounds, but he said it has not transformed their season.

“Definitely we made a step forward thanks to it,” he said. “I think you saw it in Baku.

“I think in Malaysia, it was a track that we were never going to be competitive on, but relatively, if we wouldn’t have had the update, we would have definitely been slower for sure. So the package is working, but as predicted, it’s not enough to really get us anywhere near safe, points-scoring positions.

“So we know that until the end of the year, we’re going to be scrapping to get into Q2 and potentially get a few points.”
