Sports.title: Tony Bellew Doubts Moses Itauma’s Love for Boxing
Sports.content:
Tony Bellew wonders if Moses Itauma even likes boxing, arguing that natural ability might outstrip genuine passion. Still, that loss to Filip Hrgovic revealed technical flaws passion by itself cannot fix.

“I don’t think the kid’s a student of the game,” Bellew said on Fight Your Corner via the Stomping Ground. “I don’t think he actually likes boxing. I think it’s something he’s good at. And that’s a worry.”

A fighter can train constantly yet still unravel during prolonged exchanges. Facing Hrgovic, Itauma grew visibly unsettled whenever punches came back his way. He leaped backward to clear distance, then burned massive energy leaping back inside to hunt a knockout.

Think of it like an inefficient take on Shakur Stevenson stepping back. Itauma kept hauling his heavy build completely out of range before lunging forward again. Chasing an early stoppage with that footwork burned up his gas tank fast.

The real problem was his reaction to getting tagged. Taking shots only made him rush harder for a finish. With every round Hrgovic absorbed, Itauma entered the next exchange on empty.

Bellew stood up for trainer Ben Davison, pointing out the corner told Itauma to ease off.

“He should have known after four rounds or five rounds of hitting Filip Hrgovic with the kitchen sink, I need to just put this fella on a jab for five or six rounds here,” Bellew said.

Pumping a jab makes sense, but Itauma really needed tighter defense to stay composed when leather started flying. That comes down to craft, not how much he enjoys his job.

He is only 21, so there is plenty of runway. Still, youth will not magically iron out bad habits. Fragile opponents who melt under early power let him win without fixing anything. A rugged veteran ready to drag him into deep water will exploit the exact same gaps. Bellew questioning his love for the gym grabs headlines, but how Itauma handles incoming fire is what really matters.

Sports.title: Conah Walker Faces Alexis Rocha in WBA Eliminator
Sports.content:
Conah Walker will put his world title push on the line against Alexis Rocha in a WBA welterweight eliminator on December 5 at The Halls in Wolverhampton, Matchroom announced. DAZN will broadcast the fight worldwide.

Ranked No. 3 by the WBA, Walker returns home with five consecutive victories, four inside the distance. His tenth-round stoppage of Sam Eggington in May continued a run that includes wins over Pat McCormack, Liam Taylor, Harry Scarff and Lewis Ritson.

Rocha offers a different test for the Jamie Moore-trained contender. The American southpaw defeated former world champions Joseph Diaz and José Ramírez by unanimous decision in March and September, respectively. He arrives with recent wins that give Walker reason to be careful about charging into exchanges.

“I’m back headlining in Wolverhampton in front my people. They aren’t fans, they are friends and family, and I’ll give them another night to remember,” Walker said in Matchroom’s announcement. “From the first bell you know what I bring, and this fight won’t be any different. I want to do a right job on Rocha.”

Walker’s pressure is the attraction, but how he applies it could decide this fight. Coming forward gives Rocha a target. Walker needs to close the distance behind his punches and keep working once he gets inside, rather than leave the southpaw room to catch him approaching.

“I don’t know too much about Conah Walker yet, but I’ve watched some videos of him, and he looks like a strong fighter who likes to come forward,” Rocha said.

That assessment gets to the tactical question. Walker will have the crowd encouraging him to attack, while Rocha has an opportunity to use that eagerness against him. Sustained pressure could make the visitor uncomfortable; rushed attacks could give him cleaner punching opportunities.

Matchroom describes the bout as a WBA eliminator, without identifying it as a final eliminator or guaranteeing an immediate title shot. Walker has a chance to strengthen his claim at 147 pounds, but Rocha is pursuing the same opportunity and comes to Wolverhampton with momentum of his own.

Sports.title: Jack Catterall Pushes Teofimo Lopez for Cardiff Fight
Sports.content:
Jack Catterall wants his ordered fight with Teofimo Lopez on the December 11 Tyson Fury–Anthony Joshua card in Cardiff, posting on X that he is ready to go. His willingness to fight elsewhere puts the emphasis on securing Teofimo rather than securing a home advantage.

“There’s no reason why me and Lopez don’t get it on on the Fury AJ card December 11th in Cardiff. I’m raring to go and mark my words I’ll beat Teo,” Catterall said on X.

Dan Rafael responded, “You’re in dreamland,” prompting Catterall to explain that Cardiff was a preference rather than a condition.

“I’ve boxed on the last couple of Ring cards. I don’t see why that’s dreamland? I just want to fight Teo and take his belt. I couldn’t care less where it is.”

That second response strengthens Catterall’s position. Teofimo cannot take it as a demand to travel to Britain when Catterall is publicly leaving the location open. He has proposed a date and a high-profile event while making clear that another venue would work.

The WBA ordered its two welterweight champions to meet on September 22, giving their camps until October 22 to negotiate. If talks fail, the championship committee may order a purse bid with the WBA president’s approval. The deadline does not automatically trigger a stripping.

Teofimo’s interest in Ryan Garcia creates the complication. The Ring reported that he was pursuing that bigger fight for the first half of 2027 before the Catterall order intervened. Taking Catterall first would introduce the possibility of a defeat before that payday, which helps explain why an attractive Cardiff platform alone might not get the bout made.

Catterall’s confidence adds another layer. He wants the opportunity to beat Teofimo himself, rather than watch the title become available without that fight.

Cardiff remains a proposal. The more immediate test comes on October 22, when the negotiation period ends, and the WBA must decide how to proceed if the camps have no agreement.

Sports.title: Bill Haney’s November 28 Target Creates Zuffa Problem
Sports.content:
Bill Haney wants Devin Haney to fight Shakur Stevenson on November 28 in Atlanta, but his disclosure that an offer comes through DAZN creates an awkward possibility for Zuffa: its fighter taking a difficult matchup while another platform gets the event.

“The offer is on the table for him to fight in November,” Bill told the Tru Media Podcast. Later, when asked about DAZN, he added: “The offer is presented from DAZN as well.”

November 28 remains Bill’s target rather than an announced fight date. The broadcast arrangement also needs confirmation. If DAZN funds and shows the bout, however, Zuffa would miss the opportunity to use Shakur’s appearance to attract viewers to Paramount+.

A win over Devin would increase Shakur’s value. Getting there could be difficult against a bigger fighter whose long jab and control of distance offer a demanding test for someone who relies on timing and accuracy rather than knockout power.

The proposed date leaves seven weeks from October 9. Further negotiations would shorten that window, although neither fighter’s current preparation is publicly clear.

Zuffa’s problem has developed during Shakur’s inactivity. After beating Teofimo Lopez in January, he passed on Jose “Rayo” Valenzuela while pursuing other opponents. His attention went toward Lamont Roach before Roach lost to William Zepeda, then Gary Antuanne Russell and Devin. Raymond Muratalla has attracted little interest from him.

Rayo offered a possible earlier return in an in-house Zuffa fight. The likely smaller payday could have bought something useful: activity, another appearance for Zuffa’s audience, and a chance to build on the Teofimo victory.

Waiting has costs. By November 28, nearly ten months will have passed since that win. Audience attention moves elsewhere, while a fighter can lose the timing and judgment that competition helps maintain. Sparring provides work, but the extent of any lost sharpness becomes apparent under fight-night pressure.

For Shakur, whose technical style appeals most strongly to a narrower boxing audience, regular meaningful fights are especially useful. Zuffa now needs to get him moving again. Approving Devin on DAZN could solve the inactivity while exposing its investment to a difficult opponent on someone else’s platform.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua Sells Out in One Hour
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua sold out Cardiff’s Principality Stadium in just one hour on Friday, according to BBC Sport, showing how much drawing power the two former champions retain despite their decline in the ring.

Around 80,000 tickets went on sale, with more than 500,000 people joining the online queue within minutes. That demand came despite ringwalks being expected around 1 a.m. on December 12 and organizers having yet to confirm any undercard fights.

Fans are buying Fury and Joshua’s names. Neither man needs a strong supporting card or a convenient start time to move tickets for a fight that has spent years being discussed.

The uncomfortable part is how far this event has drifted from the sporting contest it once promised to be. Fury, 38, and Joshua, 36, are faded versions of the fighters who built this rivalry. Neither occupies the position he once held in the heavyweight division, and their recent work has done little to justify treating their meeting as a fight for supremacy.

Their reputations were built in an earlier heavyweight era that, in my view, offered less depth than today’s division. Those reputations have proved more durable than their performances. Beating either man would still bring enormous attention, but that is different from beating the best heavyweight available.

The sellout gives the promoters little reason to worry about that difference. There is still a huge audience willing to pay to settle an argument that began when both fighters were closer to their peaks.

Original ticket prices ranged from £88.50 to £13,128, including booking fees. Resale listings quickly appeared, with upper-tier seats advertised at £425 and ringside VIP seats at £73,645. Those figures are asking prices rather than confirmed sales.

Netflix will broadcast the fight globally, while spectators in Cardiff face a night stretching well into Saturday morning. The stadium is scheduled to remain open until 3:30 a.m.

An hour was enough to fill it. Fury and Joshua may have lost much of what made them dangerous at their best, but the public’s willingness to pay for their overdue meeting remains intact.

The undercard could be an even bigger factor for viewers outside Britain, particularly in the U.S., where Fury–Joshua does not have the same national appeal. Two faded former champions finally settling an old rivalry may fill Cardiff, but overseas viewers will need more reason to spend their evening watching. Loading the supporting bill with competitive, meaningful fights would make the event worth tuning in for, even for those who have little enthusiasm for the main event.

Sports.title: Bektemir Melikuziev Calls for WBA to Strip Munguia Over Mandatory Snub
Sports.content:
Bektemir Melikuziev accused Jaime Munguia of refusing their ordered WBA super middleweight title fight, writing on Instagram Thursday morning that he had accepted concessions on preparation, drug testing, and pay to secure his mandatory shot.

His complaint came before news of Munguia’s proposed October 31 fight against Nikita Zon on the Canelo Alvarez–Christian Mbilli card in Riyadh. Melikuziev’s account raises a question for the champion’s team: what is preventing the mandatory defense if the challenger has accepted everything asked of him?

“I agreed to fight Jaime Munguia on short notice, without a proper training camp. I agreed to fight without VADA testing, even though we have always insisted on it. I even agreed to accept the lowest possible purse or no purse at all,” Melikuziev wrote on Instagram. “We made every concession possible to make this fight happen. And yet, my team has now informed me that Munguia is still refusing to fight me.”

Those are Melikuziev’s claims about the negotiations. His willingness to accept those terms does not establish that an agreement was completed, but it puts pressure on Munguia’s team to explain why another opponent is being pursued.

“So I have one simple question: Why hasn’t a purse bid been ordered? And if the champion refuses to fulfill his mandatory obligation, why hasn’t he been stripped of his title?” Melikuziev wrote.

The WBA gave the teams until October 21 to negotiate, so that deadline has not yet expired. However, Melikuziev is asking the organization to act if Munguia is refusing the ordered defense while pursuing another opponent.

“Stop acting as if there is no mandatory and no rules,” Melikuziev wrote.

Later Thursday, the WBA announced that it had not approved Munguia–Zon and reaffirmed Melikuziev’s status as the official challenger.

Melikuziev further alleged that Munguia wanted more money to face him and offered to stage the fight in Uzbekistan with additional funding. That financial account remains his version of events.

For Munguia, scheduling Zon does not resolve the mandatory. Melikuziev says he has removed every obstacle on his side. Munguia’s team now faces the question of what remains on theirs.

Sports.title: WBA Has Not Approved Jaime Munguia–Nikita Zon Fight
Sports.content:
Jaime Munguia’s proposed October 31 fight against Nikita Zon has not received WBA approval, the sanctioning body announced Thursday night, reminding his team that Bektemir Melikuziev remains the mandatory challenger for his super middleweight title.

The statement puts an obstacle in front of the planned Riyadh appearance. Munguia has been named to face Zon, but the WBA has already ordered him to negotiate a defense against Melikuziev.

“The WBA has not approved the Jaime Munguia vs. Nikita Zon bout. Bektemir Melikuziev is the official contender in the super middleweight division,” the organization posted on its official X account on October 8. “The WBA will review the situation.”

That leaves Munguia’s team needing a ruling before it can present the Zon matchup as an approved WBA title defense. The announcement of an opponent has not settled the championship obligation.

The WBA ordered Munguia–Melikuziev on September 21, giving the teams until October 21 to reach an agreement. Its published order stated that Munguia’s 120-day mandatory defense period expired on August 30. If negotiations fail, or either side refuses to negotiate, the championship committee may call a purse bid.

That deadline falls just ten days before the proposed Zon fight. Unless the WBA grants an exception or approves another arrangement, the mandatory order remains an obstacle to Munguia defending his belt against someone else.

Munguia could risk losing his WBA title if he goes ahead with Zon without approval. The organization has already ordered him to negotiate with Melikuziev, and announcing another opponent does not suspend that obligation or stop the October 21 deadline.

Melikuziev should not have to wait indefinitely while Munguia pursues a different fight. He is the mandatory challenger, negotiations have been ordered, and the WBA has publicly confirmed that the proposed Zon defense has not been approved.

The WBA has not announced a stripping decision. However, if Munguia proceeds without an exception, he risks entering the Zon fight with his championship on the line outside the ring.

Sports.title: Iglesias Drops Oliver Zaren Twice, Scores 7th round stoppage
Sports.content:
IBF and IBO super middleweight champion Osleys “El Tornado” Iglesias broke down Oliver “The Great Dane” Zaren, scoring two sixth-round knockdowns before stopping the Danish challenger in the seventh on Thursday at Capitole de Quebec in Quebec City, Canada.

The Cuban southpaw’s first IBF title defense headlined Camille Estephan’s Eye of the Tiger card, streamed on DAZN. Iglesias gradually wore down his larger opponent before turning a one-sided contest into a decisive finish.

Zaren’s size and toughness kept him in the fight, but he could not land enough punches to slow the champion’s attack. Iglesias continued finding him with clean shots, increasing the punishment as the rounds passed.

The sixth was particularly damaging for Zaren. Iglesias put him down twice and left him with a cut over his left eyebrow. The challenger continued into the seventh, but his trainer, former super middleweight champion Mikkel Kessler, threw in the towel to prevent further punishment. The stoppage came at 1:31, with Eddie Claudio refereeing the scheduled 12-round contest.

Iglesias, who is based in Berlin, followed his title-winning victory over Pavel Silyagin with another stoppage. Zaren, from Roskilde, Denmark, showed determination in his first world title challenge, but the fight exposed how much more he needed offensively to compete with the champion.

Wilkens Mathieu Takes Split Decision Over Vladimir Shishkin

In the co-feature, Montreal’s Wilkens Mathieu retained his NABF super middleweight title with a split-decision victory over Vladimir Shishkin in a 10-round contest.

Two judges scored the fight 98-92 for Mathieu, while the third favored Shishkin 97-93. The divided scoring reflected a fight in which Shishkin’s boxing skills gave Mathieu considerably more to deal with than Iglesias faced in the main event.

Mathieu looked for heavy punches but did not always follow them with enough regular work, allowing Shishkin to compete through his more measured boxing. Steve St-Germain was the referee.

Dzmitry Asanau Outpoints Luis Santana

Dzmitry “The Wasp” Asanau defeated Montreal’s Luis Santana by unanimous decision over 10 rounds at lightweight, adding Santana’s NABF title to his IBF Intercontinental and WBC Continental Americas belts.

Asanau dropped Santana with a left jab to the chin in the third round. The judges scored the bout 98-91 twice and 97-92. Junior Padulo Jr. refereed.

Imam Khataev Knocks Out Padraig McCrory

NABF light heavyweight champion Imam Khataev needed just 69 seconds to knock out Belfast’s Padraig “The Hammer” McCrory in their scheduled 10-round bout.

Khataev landed a left hook to the head that dropped McCrory, who could not beat the count. Junior Padulo Jr. was the referee.

Leila Beaudoin Wins Every Round On The Cards

Leila Beaudoin, of Lévis, Quebec, defeated Argentina’s Brisa “La China” Alfonzo by unanimous decision in their 10-round super featherweight contest.

Beaudoin dropped Alfonzo with a body shot in the sixth round, with the challenger taking an eight-count before continuing. All three judges scored the fight 100-89. Alain Villeneuve refereed.

Daylen Pepin Stops Matias Pinilla

Quebec’s Daylen Pepin stopped Chile’s Matias Pinilla at 2:59 of the fourth round in their lightweight contest.

A flurry from Pepin brought the finish in the round’s final seconds. Jeff Topping was the referee.

Jacob Blais Defeats Yoan Trottier

Montreal welterweight Jacob Blais earned a unanimous decision over Quebec City’s Yoan Trottier in a four-round bout.

Trottier suffered a cut over his right eyebrow in the second round. All three judges scored the contest 40-36 for Blais, with Jeff Topping refereeing.

Ghana News.title: Fire destroys mattress showroom at Sokoban in Kumasi
Ghana News.content:
A devastating fire has broken out at Sokoban-Ampayoo in the Ashanti Region.

This has destroyed several mattresses at a showroom near Kumasi Hospital.

The circumstances leading to the fire remain unclear.

The blaze has consumed a large portion of the showroom, as residents race to save vehicles parked in a commercial garage adjacent to the facility.

Fire tenders arrived at the scene after residents attempt to bring the blaze under control.

Ghana News.title: ECOM-SMS Ghana launches ‘Agriculture Our Future Clubs’ to address threat of ageing farmer population
Ghana News.content:
As part of efforts to inspire the next generation to embrace agriculture and secure the future of the sector, the Sustainable Management Services (SMS) under the auspices of ECOM Ghana has launched the Agriculture Our Future Clubs initiative in basic schools within its operational areas.

The clubs are designed to go beyond classroom learning, exposing pupils to opportunities in agribusiness, science, technology, processing, marketing and entrepreneurship.

So far, the initiative has been rolled out in 40 basic schools across 12 districts within ECOM Ghana’s operational areas. All the clubs have already secured farmlands and commenced cultivation of various crops and rearing livestock.

At the official launch at Old Edubiase in the Adansi North District, the Acting General Manager of Sustainable Management Services (SMS) at ECOM Ghana, Emmanuel Baffoe-Bonnie, explained that the initiative stems from a growing concern in agriculture is the issue of the ageing farmer population in the country.

Citing data from the Ministry of Food and Agriculture, he said the average Ghanaian farmer is 55 years old, but the situation is even worse in cocoa-growing communities, where most farmers are over 50 and young people are increasingly gravitating towards non-agricultural careers, making the future of agriculture uncertain.

According to him, although agriculture remains the backbone of Ghana's economy and many global communities, contributing over 20% of Ghana's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) and employing more than half of its workforce, most young people still do not see it as a profitable and exciting career path.

He said the Agriculture Our Future Clubs initiative is aimed at changing that perception.

"Agriculture remains the backbone of many of our communities and continues to support livelihoods, food security, and national development. Yet, many young people do not see agriculture as an attractive career path," he said.

"If we do not inspire the next generation to develop an interest in agriculture, who will produce the food we eat and sustain the crops that support our economy in the future?" he asked.

Mr. Baffoe-Bonnie said the vision of the clubs is to raise a generation that understands agriculture, appreciates its value and recognises the opportunities it offers.

Through the clubs, children will gain knowledge in good agricultural practices, environmental conservation, climate awareness, nutrition, savings and entrepreneurship, as well as leadership, teamwork, creativity and problem-solving skills.

The Acting General Manager stressed that child protection remains central to the initiative, explaining that there is a clear distinction between introducing children to agriculture in a safe, educational manner and exposing them to child labour.

"Every child deserves the opportunity to learn, grow, and pursue their dreams without being subjected to hazardous work, abuse, or exploitation," he emphasized.

He said club members are being sensitised on children's rights, child labour prevention, personal safety and responsible participation in agriculture, while the clubs serve as safe spaces for children to express their views and build confidence.

He added that teachers serving as Club Coordinators have been trained in effective club management and child protection to serve as mentors.

Call for Partnership

Mr. Baffoe-Bonnie stated that ECOM Ghana cannot achieve the vision alone and called for sustained partnership from the Ghana Education Service, Ministry of Food and Agriculture, District Assemblies, traditional authorities, school leaders, teachers, parents and community members.

"Together, we can create an environment that encourages children to learn, innovate, and thrive while ensuring their rights, safety, and wellbeing are protected," he said.

He encouraged club members to be curious and explore the opportunities in agriculture, noting that agriculture is not a last resort but a field of opportunity, innovation and prosperity.

"Today, as we inaugurate these clubs, we are planting much more than trees. We are planting curiosity, knowledge, confidence, leadership, and opportunity. Above all, we are investing in the future of our children and the future of agriculture," he said.

"Agriculture is not a profession of the past. It is the foundation of our future. Agriculture is our future, and our children are an important part of that future," he added.

Farm Work as Punishment

Speaking on the role of education in nurturing children's interest in agriculture, the Adansi North District Director of Education, Alhaji Ibrahim Abubakar Amankwah, urged teachers to desist from using farm work as a form of punishment.

He said teachers have a critical role to play in making agriculture attractive to pupils, adding that using weeding, land clearing and other farm-related activities as punishment discourages them from developing an interest in the sector.

"Teachers have a role to play in schools to make agriculture attractive to students. In the first place, teachers must stop using farm work, clearing of land or weeding as a punishment for breaking school rules. Such rules discourage young people from seeing farming as a normal, attractive and valuable activity," Alhaji Amankwah said.

He urged teachers and club coordinators to adopt confidence-building strategies and mentorship approaches to raise pupils' self-esteem and strengthen belief in their own agricultural abilities.

Alhaji Amankwah emphasized the need to combine classroom teaching with practical experience on school farms and gardens to sustain pupils' interest.

"When we keep teaching the importance of agriculture in the classroom and practically engage in agricultural activities in our school farms or school gardens, pupils will definitely develop interest in it," he said.

He further called on schools to bridge the gap between theory and practice by moving agriculture out of textbooks.

"Let us put together the theories and bridge the gap between theory and practice. Teachers should move agriculture out of the books by utilizing school gardens to plant, harvest and enjoy. By so doing, agriculture will look attractive to all pupils who engage in it," he added.

Removal of Agricultural Science as Standalone Subject

Meanwhile, the District Director of Food and Agriculture for Adansi North, Mr. Prince Asare expressed concern over the removal of Agricultural Science as a standalone subject from the basic education curriculum.

According to him, the merging and eventual abolition of Agricultural Science as a single subject weakens hands-on practical training and dampens youth interest in farming.

Mr. Asare noted that the implementation of new educational reforms in the 2012 academic year in Ghana led to the abolition of Agricultural Science as a core subject in basic schools.

He warned that without early exposure to agriculture, the country risks future food insecurity and rising youth unemployment.

He therefore appealed to policymakers to reinstate Agricultural Science as a core subject in basic schools, particularly at a time when the sector ministry has directed district agricultural directors to recognize and reward basic schools actively engaged in farming as part of the National Farmers' Day Awards.

Stakeholders in the agricultural sector who graced the inauguration welcomed the initiative, commending the management and staff of Sustainable Management Services and ECOM Ghana for the intervention.

They described the establishment of the clubs as timely and crucial for reigniting young people's interest in agriculture and ensuring the sustainability of the sector.

Ghana News.title: Cherif Sarr: Economic participation needs more pathways, not one prescribed route
Ghana News.content:
West Africa's economic future depends on how well we turn ambition into sustainable livelihoods. Yet for decades, we have tended to talk about economic opportunity in fairly narrow terms.

Study hard. Get qualifications. Find a good job. Build a career.

It remains a perfectly valid aspiration. But across West Africa, it cannot be the only route we prepare people for.

Our region is young, ambitious and increasingly connected. Every year, millions of young people enter working age with expectations that are fundamentally different from those of the generation before them. Women are seeking greater economic independence. Technology is lowering some barriers to participation while creating entirely new forms of work.

Yet the formal economy cannot absorb everyone who wants, or needs, to participate in it. In a July 2024 article, the World Bank reported that six million young people enter the labour force each year across Western and Central Africa, while only about half a million new jobs are created.

The question we therefore need to ask is not simply: How do we create more jobs?

It is also: How do we widen the number of legitimate, responsible pathways through which people can participate in the economy?

Economic participation is bigger than employment

A healthy economy needs salaried employees. It needs large companies and public institutions. It needs engineers, teachers, doctors, bankers and civil servants.

But it also needs small traders, independent professionals, farmers, creators, artisans, technology entrepreneurs, family businesses, consultants, distributors and people providing services within their communities.

Many West Africans already earn their livelihoods in these ways.

For some, these livelihoods are a deliberate choice; for others, they reflect limited alternatives. Our focus should be on helping people move from informal and vulnerable economic activity towards more productive, skilled and secure participation.

That requires a broader definition of entrepreneurship.

Not every entrepreneur will build a technology unicorn or raise millions of dollars in venture capital. Most never will.

Entrepreneurship can begin much more simply: identifying a need, providing a product or service, finding customers, managing income and expenses, and gradually building something sustainable.

For someone who has never had access to formal employment, even that first step can be significant. But starting a business is only the beginning. Access to customers, suitable finance and practical support helps determine whether it can become a sustainable livelihood. More predictable trade policies aligned with the African Continental Free Trade Area could also help smaller businesses reach wider markets, as the World Bank has highlighted.

Opportunity must be responsible

Expanding access to entrepreneurship cannot mean lowering the standards around it.

As more people search online for ways to earn additional income, the distinction between a genuine economic opportunity and an unrealistic promise becomes increasingly important.

No legitimate form of entrepreneurship guarantees success.

Income depends on many factors: effort, capability, demand, competition, experience and timing. Anyone entering an entrepreneurial activity deserves to understand clearly what is required, what it costs, where the risks lie and how income is generated.

Businesses also have a responsibility to address exaggerated income claims and misleading offers made by those representing them. Clear information and accessible complaints procedures should be part of every opportunity.

Entrepreneurship should expand people's choices, not exploit their aspirations.

Governments, businesses, civil society and law-enforcement agencies therefore have a shared interest in creating environments where legitimate opportunities can grow while fraudulent ones become harder to operate.

Skills may matter as much as capital

When entrepreneurship is discussed, the conversation often begins with access to finance.

Financing matters, but someone starting a small business also needs to understand customers, communicate effectively, manage cash flow, use digital tools, negotiate, solve problems and build trust.

These capabilities remain valuable even when a particular venture does not succeed.

Selling responsibly can strengthen communication. Managing customers develops service skills. Tracking income and expenses builds financial discipline and helps people distinguish revenue from profit. Building networks develops relationship skills. Using social platforms for business can build digital capability.

We should therefore think beyond simply creating entrepreneurs and focus on creating economically capable individuals.

People may move between employment, entrepreneurship and independent work several times during their lives. The skills developed in one setting can travel with them into the next.

Women need pathways designed around reality

Across our region, women participate extensively in commerce and informal enterprise, yet their economic potential remains constrained by unequal access to finance, networks, technology, training and, in many cases, time. The need to widen participation is particularly evident among young women. ILOSTAT's May 2026 analysis, using 2022 data, found that the employment-to-population ratio for women aged 15 to 29 in Senegal was just 22.5 per cent.

Economic models that offer greater flexibility can help widen participation. But flexibility alone is not empowerment.

Women also need skills, financial literacy, digital tools, mentoring and credible business networks. Training schedules and delivery should recognise care responsibilities. The opportunities available to them must also be transparent and financially viable.

If entrepreneurship is to contribute meaningfully to women's economic participation, we should look beyond how many women start businesses and ask whether those businesses strengthen their skills, income security and economic independence.

Digital access changes the possibilities

Technology is lowering some barriers to economic activity. BCEAO, the Central Bank of West African States, reports that merchant acceptance points for electronic money in the West African Economic and Monetary Union increased from approximately 1.75 million in 2023 to 3.71 million in 2024. This growth in payment acceptance locations shows the expansion of infrastructure for digital commerce, although a single business may account for more than one acceptance point.

A smartphone can now provide access to customers, payments, education, logistics, financial services and markets that were difficult for small entrepreneurs to reach a generation ago. Artificial intelligence could extend these possibilities further.

A small business owner can increasingly access tools for translation, marketing, design, customer service, bookkeeping and research. Their usefulness depends on affordability, relevant skills and checking the accuracy of what they produce.

But connectivity alone is not enough. People also need the skills to use technology productively. Entrepreneurship programmes should therefore teach not only how to start a business, but how to operate in an increasingly digital marketplace.

We need an ecosystem, not a single solution

There is no single model that will solve West Africa's employment challenge.

Formal employment, vocational training, small-business development, agriculture, technology startups, creative industries, independent professional work, social enterprise and responsible direct selling can all contribute.

The real objective should be to build an ecosystem in which people have more credible choices.

Governments can create enabling regulation and infrastructure. Educational institutions can equip young people with adaptable skills. Financial institutions can improve access to responsible capital. Businesses can create platforms for participation and invest in training. Civil society and the media can help people distinguish genuine opportunities from fraudulent ones.

Those of us in the private sector must also accept that inclusion comes with responsibility. At QNET, our FinGreen programme focuses on financial literacy through education and training, particularly for young adults and communities with limited access to resources. Its purpose reflects the broader need to help people make informed financial decisions. Training, however, must never be presented as a guarantee of income.

Opening a door is not enough. We must be clear about what lies behind it.

West Africa does not lack ambition. Spend time in Dakar, Accra, Abidjan, Lagos or Lomé and you encounter it everywhere — in markets, small businesses, technology hubs, university campuses and digital platforms.

Our challenge is to turn more of that ambition into sustainable economic participation. That begins by moving beyond the assumption that everyone must follow the same economic path, while continuing to invest in good jobs.

A resilient economy is one in which people have several legitimate opportunities, the skills to make them productive and the knowledge to choose among them. That is how West Africa can turn more of its ambition into lasting economic progress.

About the Author

Cherif Sarr is Regional General Manager for Central and West Africa at QNET, an international direct selling company specialising in wellness and lifestyle products. He oversees the company’s growth across the region, with a focus on social commerce and expanding responsible microentrepreneurship opportunities in emerging economies.

Ghana News.title: Cyber Security Authority: Ghana led Operation Blackout, not FBI
Ghana News.content:
The Cyber Security Authority (CSA) has rejected claims by the United States Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) that the cybercrime operation carried out in Ghana this week was conceived, commanded or executed by the bureau.

In a press release issued on Thursday, October 8, 2026, the authority said the operation, also referred to as Operation Cyber Hunt, was led and coordinated by Ghana's Cyber Security Authority.

It said the operation was conducted with support from Ghana's National Security Council, the Criminal Investigations Department of the Ghana Police Service, the National Crime Agency of the United Kingdom, the FBI, the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission of Nigeria, the Joint Case Team on Cybercrime, the Ghana Immigration Service and the Office of the Attorney-General.

The authority said Ghanaian authorities planned, coordinated and executed the operation within Ghana's legal and institutional frameworks. It said the operation could not be said to have been conceived as part of an FBI-led global programme, nor was it conducted under a foreign operational command.

It stated that Ghana is a sovereign republic governed by its Constitution and laws, and that foreign law enforcement agencies have no independent authority to exercise police powers or conduct arrests within Ghana. It said their participation must take place through lawful cooperation, with the authorisation and involvement of relevant Ghanaian authorities.

The authority acknowledged the intelligence contributions of the FBI and the National Crime Agency, saying the partnerships remain important to effective investigations and operations. It, however, said the contribution of international partners must be described accurately.

It called on the FBI to clarify its public account of the Ghana-led operation and to acknowledge the contributions of the Ghanaian institutions and other international partners responsible for its execution. The authority said it remained available for constructive engagement to ensure the public record reflects the respective roles of all participating agencies.

The authority said the operation uncovered suspected cybercrime centres in parts of the Greater Accra Region. Eight suspects were arrested, and one hundred and twenty others suspected to have been trafficked and exploited for online fraud activities were rescued.

It said the operation followed intelligence received on August 26, 2026, indicating that several apartments at Ubuntu Haven Estate in Kpone Katamanso, Franko Estate in Ga North and other locations in Ga West were being used as bases for organised cybercrime, including romance scams.

Items seized included 136 mobile phones, 130 laptops, internet connection devices, four motor vehicles, one of which was stolen from Canada, and other digital equipment. The search team also recovered jewellery and ten Nigerian passports.

The authority said it was working to repatriate the rescued victims, identified largely as Nigerians, while investigations into the suspects and the seized devices are ongoing.

It reaffirmed Ghana's commitment to dismantling cybercriminal networks and protecting the public from online fraud. It said it would continue to strengthen intelligence-led investigations, inter-agency coordination, digital forensic capabilities and international cooperation.

Ghana News.title: GH¢800,000 goods destroyed as fire engulfs Kia Rhino truck on Apedwa-Kibi Road
Ghana News.content:
A Kia Rhino truck loaded with refrigerators, generators, gas burners and chairs has been gutted by fire at Amanfrom on the Apedwa-Kibi road in the early hours of Thursday, October 8, with the estimated loss put at GH¢800,000.

According to a Facebook post by the Ghana National Fire Service, the Kibi Fire Station received the distress call at 0314 hours and dispatched a crew led by ADO II Michael Kwakye.

The crew arrived at 0332 hours to find the truck, registered GE 4273-26, fully engulfed in flames. Firefighters deployed two hose lines with foam, bringing the blaze under control at 0400 hours before extinguishing it completely at 0428 hours.

The driver reportedly said he and two other occupants were travelling from Tema towards Kumasi when they stopped to rest and fell asleep. They were awakened by passers-by who alerted them to the fire and managed to escape through the windscreen.

Fortunately, no casualties were recorded.

The cause of the fire remains under investigation, while the estimated financial loss stands at GH¢800,000.

Ghana News.title: Chief Justice calls for supportive workplaces to address mental health stigma
Ghana News.content:
Chief Justice, Paul Baffoe-Bonnie

Chief Justice Paul Baffoe-Bonnie has urged employers to promote inclusive and supportive working environments to help combat stigma associated with mental health conditions.

He made the call in a speech read on his behalf by Supreme Court Judge Sophia Rosetta Bernasko-Essah at this year’s World Mental Health Day celebration at the Court Complex in Accra on Friday, October 9.

The event was jointly organised by the Greater Accra Regional Health Service and the Judicial Service of Ghana under the theme, “Lived Experiences Heard: Real Voices, Real Change.”

In his address, the Chief Justice called for compassionate and accessible healthcare services, alongside institutional policies that prioritise mental well-being.

He observed that stigma and the fear of judgement or exclusion often prevent people from speaking openly about their mental health challenges, urging the public to listen to their experiences with empathy and without prejudice.

“We must listen with empathy; most importantly, we must let those experiences inform how we design policies, provide support, and respond to people going through difficult periods in their lives,” he said.

He stressed the need for institutions to prioritise mental well-being and foster a workplace culture where employees feel comfortable seeking support without fear of being judged.

“It is therefore important we recognise that mental well-being is not a peripheral matter; it is an essential part of a healthy, effective and human workplace. We must therefore create an institutional culture in which seeking help is not regarded as a weakness,” he said.

Justice Baffoe-Bonnie said the mental well-being of judicial officers and staff was fundamental to an effective justice system, enabling them to perform their duties with clarity, integrity and compassion.

The Chief Justice further highlighted the importance of mental health screening and assessments in preventing potential problems, identifying concerns at an early stage and ensuring timely intervention.

“As a society we must move from merely sympathising with people experiencing mental health challenges to creating systems of support,” he said.

He encouraged employers to sustain conversations about mental health in the workplace, promote mutual support among colleagues and create an environment in which staff feel comfortable seeking professional assistance when necessary.

The World Mental Health Day celebration also featured screening for chronic medical conditions and mental health assessments for participants.

Ghana News.title: NVI CEO defends GH¢13m spending on training, workshops and conferences
Ghana News.content:
The Chief Executive Officer of the National Vaccine Institute, Dr. Sodzi Sodzi-Tettey, has defended the Institute’s GH¢13 million expenditure on training, workshops and conferences in 2025, insisting the activities are critical to its mandate and capital-intensive.

This follows concerns raised by the Public Accounts Committee after the Auditor-General reported a financial downturn, with the Institute moving from a profit of 36 million Ghana cedis to a loss of 21 million cedis within the financial year.

Appearing before the Committee, Dr Sodzi-Tettey defended the expenditure, explaining that much of the Institute’s work involves building the capacity of researchers, manufacturers and regulators to support the development of Ghana’s vaccine industry.

He said the Institute’s mandate required significant investment in training and knowledge-sharing activities because the country’s vaccine ecosystem lacked the technical capacity needed to support local vaccine manufacturing.

Dr Sodzi-Tettey explained that the Institute’s activities extended beyond conventional training programmes to include efforts to develop expertise across the various stages of vaccine research, production and regulation.

He said the Institute worked with researchers at universities across the country, manufacturers whose production capabilities needed improvement, and regulators who required specialised knowledge to perform their duties effectively.

He added that manufacturers and regulatory institutions also needed support to develop the technical expertise required to establish a sustainable domestic vaccine industry.

According to him, activities involving these groups could be classified under training, seminars and conferences in the Institute’s financial records, contributing to the substantial amount recorded under those expenditure headings.

Institute cites limited technical capacity

Dr Sodzi-Tettey argued that developing vaccine manufacturing capacity was a complex and expensive undertaking that could not be achieved within a short period.

He described vaccine manufacturing as one of the weakest areas of Ghana’s vaccine ecosystem, saying the country lacked the technical expertise and infrastructure required to undertake several specialised processes independently.

“Vaccine manufacturing is not something that you would get up and then suddenly realise that you have the capacity to do it. It is our weakest area in the vaccine ecosystem,” he said.

To illustrate the skills gap, he cited the production of snake venom antiserum, explaining that the Institute had to bring in experts from India to conduct some of the required tests.

He said foreign specialists were also needed to support certain animal studies undertaken as part of the process of developing manufacturing capabilities.

“In the course of manufacturing the snake venom antiserum, we have to bring in experts from India to be able to do some of the tests that are required,” he told the Committee.

“In some of the animal studies that we have to do to be able to manufacture the vaccines, experts have to be brought in from outside of the country to support us,” he added.

The CEO said Ghana had several young scientists whose skills could be developed to meet the country’s future vaccine research and manufacturing needs.

However, he maintained that formal education alone was insufficient to provide all the specialised expertise required for vaccine production, making continuous training and capacity development necessary.

“We have some young scientists for sure, but their capacities will have to be built now and going into the future, to be able to do what we want them to do,” he said.

He stressed that the sector required substantial investment because the technical skills and facilities needed to manufacture vaccines were not readily available locally.

“The thing about these areas is that they are all capital-intensive. They are really capital-intensive, and the capacity is not there. So you do have to train people to be able to do it, and that’s where a lot of the budget is going into,” Dr Sodzi-Tettey said.

Community engagement forms part of the mandate

Beyond scientific research and manufacturing, the CEO said the Institute also engaged communities to assess public understanding of, and willingness to accept, vaccines manufactured locally.

He explained that such engagements were necessary to understand public attitudes towards locally produced vaccines and support efforts to build confidence in domestic vaccine development.

The activities, he suggested, formed part of the broader work required to establish a functional vaccine ecosystem in Ghana, alongside building the capabilities of researchers, manufacturers and regulators.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Drone strike kills 30 people in Sudan’s Blue Nile region
World.content:
At least 30 displaced people, including women and children, have been killed and dozens of others have been wounded following a drone attack in southeastern Sudan.

The governor of Wad al-Mahi province told Al Jazeera on Friday that a drone belonging to the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) targeted the centre of the province, killing 26 women and four children.

Governor Mahjoub Al-Sheikh described the attack as “cowardly”. He said the drone was launched from “inside Ethiopia”, according to the AFP news agency.

Al Jazeera Arabic’s Sudan correspondent, Wadah Al-Tahir, explained that the attack was the latest in a wave of drone strikes targeting the Blue Nile region and this time Wad al-Mahi province near the city of Damazin was struck.

Friday’s attack was just outside a displacement camp, near an informal gold mining site, where women earn a daily wage using chemicals and their bare hands to clear gold nuggets from the earth extracted by men.

The latest frontline in the war between the Sudanese army and the RSF is the border region with Ethiopia, which is facing its own internal conflict that threatens to escalate.

Sudan has repeatedly accused Ethiopia of harbouring RSF fighters and bases – Ethiopia has denied the allegations.

Local sources say the porous border between the two countries is a key supply line for the paramilitary and its allies, AFP reported.

The RSF launched its offensive towards Damazin but the advance could put the army in a bind, forcing it to defend territory on both the Blue Nile front and in the Kordofan region, where a year of deadly drone strikes has left the two sides deadlocked.



Aid workers estimate that Sudan’s civil war has killed more than 200,000 people since it started in April 2023, creating one of the world’s largest hunger and displacement crises.

Nearly 100,000 people have been displaced in Blue Nile state this year alone, according to United Nations figures.

World.title: DHS defends ICE shooting in NYC, says officers believed they were in danger
World.content:
The shooting prompted protests in New York City as officials defended ICE and Mayor Zohran Mamdani condemned the incident.

Share DHS defends ICE shooting in NYC, says officers believed they were in danger on social media

The United States Department of Homeland Security has defended Immigration and Customs Enforcement’s (ICE) shooting of a man in New York City while his child was present. Federal officials used the incident to criticise sanctuary-city policies that limit cooperation with federal immigration authorities.

New York officials have condemned the shooting and have called for ICE to end its operations in the city.

The shooting took place on Thursday afternoon when ICE officers attempted to arrest a man identified by New York City police as Oscar Belgal.

Homeland Security officials gave their account of the incident on Friday during a news conference, saying that Belgal refused to exit his car when approached by officers and then accelerated, striking two ICE vehicles.

They said officers then opened fire, grazing Belgal’s neck while his five-year-old child was in the back seat.

According to Homeland Security officials, Belgal received first aid and was taken to hospital before being transferred to a secure detention facility outside New York state. They did not disclose where Belgal is being held.

Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Markwayne Mullin said that the agents did not know the child was inside the vehicle when they fired.

ICE senior official Marcos Charles said agents had attempted to arrest Belgal as part of an investigation into suspected gang involvement in an earlier shooting of a US Customs and Border Protection officer.

According to US officials, Belgal is an undocumented migrant from the Dominican Republic who had previously evaded arrest and received a five-year sentence for grand larceny in April 2025.



“[Belgal] was a thug,” Mullin said at the Friday news conference. “The absolute worst of the worst.”

Mullin confirmed that officers were wearing body cameras but the footage has not been made public. New York City police released bodycam footage on Friday of police officers on the scene who had responded to a 911 call about the incident.

In other violent incidents involving federal immigration officers, video evidence has contradicted initial accounts from ICE and Homeland Security officials, including in Minneapolis, where footage of the fatal shootings of Alex Pretti and Renee Good challenged federal officials’ descriptions of the encounters.

The latest shooting prompted protests on Thursday night in the Bronx, where the shooting took place, with demonstrators condemning ICE and calling for the agency to be abolished. Tensions rose after NYPD officers clashed with some of the protesters.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani condemned the shooting and said he had called US President Donald Trump to demand an end to ICE enforcement in the city.

Speaking to reporters late on Thursday at the scene of the shooting, Mamdani said he had tried unsuccessfully to secure Belgal’s release in phone calls with Trump and Mullin.

“These actions are making the city less safe,” Mamdani said. “ICE is rotten to its core.”

Mullin accused Mamdani of prioritising politics over public safety and said Trump had offered to transfer Belgal to New York police custody if they pursued charges. Mullin said Mamdani refused this offer.

World.title: ‘A Ceuta-style surge is possible’: Border tensions on NATO’s eastern flank
World.content:
Masked and armed men attempted to cross into Latvia from Belarus alongside 20 undocumented migrants on Monday.

“The (masked) escorts of the illegal migrants, who were located on the Belarusian side, were armed, issued threats to … soldiers, and also actively urged and drove the migrant group toward Latvia,” Janis Dombrava, Latvia’s interior minister, said on Tuesday.

The group was stopped by the military.

Later, masked men managed to enter Latvia, destroying an electrical box and stealing surveillance cameras before returning to Belarus – an act of sabotage orchestrated by the country, according to Latvian officials. It was not clear if the second incident involved the same masked men as the first.

“Unlike many previous incidents, this time the provocation was particularly demonstrative and aggressive,” said Dombrava.

Since 2021, Belarus, Russia’s ally, has used migration as a tool to destabilise NATO’s eastern flank. It shares borders with Russia, Ukraine, Poland, Lithuania and Latvia – the latter considered Europe’s weakest link.

“The crisis at the EU [European Union] border with Belarus has been ongoing for five years. The situation in Latvia has been deteriorating since May of this year,” Bartosz Chmielewski, Baltics expert from the Poland-based Centre for Eastern Studies told Al Jazeera. “There has been a steady rise in border violations and the number of people crossing.”

In September and October, “the number of border violations has already reached 12,000, a level equal to the total for the entire previous year”, he said.



According to Olevs Nikers, the Latvian president of the Baltic Security Foundation, “A Ceuta-style surge is physically possible, and we should plan for it.”

He was referring to the recent crossing of tens of thousands of people from Morocco to Spain.

“But sustained low-level pressure may be the more effective strategy. It creates exhaustion, budget pressure and friction between allies. Poland’s renewed controls on its border with Lithuania are already an example of this.”

He noted that Lithuania’s border with Belarus is four times longer than Latvia’s 173km (107 miles), yet pressure has been concentrated in Latvia.

“This looks less like spontaneous migration than a deliberate instrument, adjusted to test the neighbour perceived as most vulnerable,” Nikers said.

Any migration pressure from Belarus may cause bureaucratic chaos. Latvia, with a population of 1.8 million, would struggle with the reception, processing and providing medical aid to potential asylum seekers, he said.

According to the Polish Border Guard, in 2021, almost 40,000 people tried to cross the border from Belarus. Thousands more crossings of undocumented people were never recorded.

Before Russia’s war in Ukraine began in 2022, Belarus built a system – including travel agencies, plane connections and visa programmes – encouraging migrants seeking a better life to cross into the European Union from the east. The scheme targeted people from the Global South, or Latin America, Africa and much of Asia.

According to experts, the system has since been dismantled, but Belarus is still pressing migration when it can.

“A sudden influx of several thousand people into Latgale in winter would become a humanitarian and political problem before it became a border-security problem,” Nikers added.

Out of all of NATO’s eastern flank countries, Latvia seems the least prepared for provocations coming from the east.

“Until now, Latvia remained on the sidelines, as the pressure was primarily focused on Poland and Lithuania. Now it finds itself in the spotlight, partly because it is unprepared, its border infrastructure is inadequate, and the resources of the border guard – even with military support – are dwindling,” Chmielewski said.

“Latvia struggles to execute major infrastructure projects … It shares the shortest border with Belarus, but has been unable to complete the necessary infrastructure there; this is due both to the challenging terrain and the state’s limited operational capacity.”

Other experts said the migration pressure from Belarus might be a response to recent political developments in Latvia.



“The elections in Latvia were won by a coalition led by [Prime Minister] Andris Kulbergs, which seeks to maintain sanctions against Belarus. So Belarus uses both carrots and sticks to show it can destabilise the situation in the Baltics,” said Marta Jaroszewicz, assistant professor at the University of Warsaw’s Centre of Migration Research.

“For the past year, there have been periodic releases of Belarusian political prisoners, a process supported by the US administration. Belarus’s goal is the lifting of sanctions and the ability to transport its raw materials via Baltic ports, including through Poland. The objective is, in fact, the normalisation of trade.”

Russian and Belarusian pressure on the EU has also changed over the years as migration pressure is only one of the tactics employed. Others include disinformation, arson, the recruitment of local citizens and GPS jamming, according to Nikers.

He said that “2026 is increasingly about airspace and infrastructure. The most important change is that Russia has moved from targeting what we believe to targeting what we depend on: cables, grids, navigation and airspace. It is also increasingly operating below the Article 5 threshold.”

Established in the aftermath of World War II, NATO’s collective defence commitment, Article 5, was designed to ensure mutual protection among member states in response to the perceived threat of Soviet expansion, particularly in Eastern Europe during the early stages of the Cold War.

“This is an attempt at intimidation by Russia. And what deters Russia from aggressive actions on the eastern flank is the solidarity of European nations,” Chmielewski said. “That is what Russia fears most: that should it stage a more brazen provocation, solidarity will stretch from Lisbon to Stockholm, and the European Union will act as a united front.”

World.title: Thousands rally for anti-austerity protest in Brussels amid clashes
World.content:
