Belgian police respond to ‘troublemakers’ on sidelines of main rally with tear gas, water cannon and baton charges.

Clashes have erupted near Brussels Central station on the sidelines of a demonstration organised by the country’s socialist trade union against the federal government’s austerity plans.

As thousands of protesters gathered at the station on Friday, a smaller group clashed with the police and threw wooden beams, glass bottles and rubbish bins, The Belgian Times reported.

Police were deployed in large numbers around the stations as officers checked groups of young people not wearing trade union colours.

Police said the main trade union rally went ahead peacefully but “groups of troublemakers were responsible for serious incidents before and after the march.”

Riot police responded to those protesters with tear gas, water cannon and baton charges. Police said those who “cause the problems of public order are not linked” to the rally.

Reporting from Brussels, Al Jazeera’s Rosie Birchard said damage was caused during Friday morning’s protests with an “acrid smell of burning in the air”, due to fires that were set and the tear gas.

“Police [and] emergency services have been arriving, starting to disperse or clean up and then the protests flare up again. So the day is still early; often these things get worse in the evening in terms of the street violence,” Birchard explained.

“There were some young people who came out, they say they were inspired by what they had seen in France in terms of school protests, and they also wanted to talk about the education environment they’re learning in,” she said, adding that the students felt that they were “not being listened to”.

The clashes came after a week of tension in the city of Liege after authorities banned gatherings as students clashed with police and vandalised shops. More than 200 people were arrested in Liege, and dozens of police were injured.



The ABVV trade union and the Christian ACV, the country’s two biggest unions, organised protests on Friday morning, with protesters marching from Brussels Central station to Brussels South Station under the slogan “stay out of our pockets”.

Police said about 30,000 people attended the demonstrations, while ABVV had earlier estimated attendance at 50,000.

The anger stems from the government’s austerity measures, as officials consider a new budget that opposes potential measures that affect purchasing power, the wage indexation system and value-added tax (VAT), as well as plans to introduce annualised working time.

At the same time, the ACV organised a separate protest involving hundreds of activists at the capital’s headquarters of the governing coalition parties.

World.title: Trump launches probe into Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook
World.content:
Trump began efforts to remove Cook as one of the governors on the US Fed Reserve Board in 2025 and litigation on the matter is still on.

United States President Donald Trump has announced a committee to investigate Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook and whether alleged false statements on mortgage documents constitute grounds for her removal under federal law.

The White House announced the new committee on Wednesday, but published the notice on its website on Friday.

The three-member committee, which will be tasked with reviewing evidence and reporting to the president on whether he has sufficient cause to remove her, will include the assistant to the president for economic policy, the chair of the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission and the director of the Office of Government Ethics.

The notice says there will be a hearing on November 5, where Cook will be required to appear and answer questions.

Political pressure

Trump began efforts to remove Cook as one of the governors on the US Federal Reserve Board in August 2025 after Federal Housing Finance Agency Director Bill Pulte accused her of misrepresenting two different properties on a 2021 mortgage application before she joined the central bank. She was appointed to the Fed Board in 2022 by then-President Joe Biden. Cook’s term runs until 2038.

Trump announced Cook’s removal amid the allegations, but Cook sued, and a federal judge blocked her firing in September 2025. Cook remained in office while the case continued.

In June, the Supreme Court declined to let Trump remove Cook while the litigation continues.

The case led to the US Supreme Court ruling earlier this year that the president could not remove a Fed governor without adequate cause and needed to follow a clear process to lay out the reasons and provide evidence.



The ruling left Cook in her position, but kicked the case against her back to a federal district court.

The case has been closely watched as Trump has put political pressure on the central bank to cut interest rates, including launching investigations into then-Federal Reserve Chairman Jerome Powell, whose term ended in May.

In December 2025, Trump said he would only appoint someone who agreed with him on cutting interest rates. He appointed Kevin Warsh as Powell’s replacement.

Amid ongoing tensions with Iran, pressure on the oil market and rising inflation, the Fed last month raised the benchmark interest rate by a quarter of a percentage point to 3.75–4 percent, the first hike in three years. With the final rate decision before the midterm elections later this month, CME FedWatch, which tracks the likelihood of monetary policy decisions, forecasts that rates will likely remain unchanged.

World.title: ‘Rogue court’: US sanctions ICC hours after ex-judge wins Nobel Prize
World.content:
NewsFeed ‘Rogue court’: US sanctions ICC hours after ex-judge wins Nobel Prize

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio announced sanctions against the International Criminal Court on Friday, hours after the Nobel Prize was awarded to the court’s former judge Navi Pillay. Rubio called the ICC a “rogue court” and threatened to “dismantle it piece by piece”.

World.title: US unveils sanctions on ICC in move court condemns as 'assault on rule of law'
World.content:
The UK joined Canada, Denmark, Germany, France, Italy, Japan and the Netherlands in reaffirming their "continued and unwavering support" for the ICC and said they "regret and strongly disagree with" the sanctions.

They also praised the court's staff for their work bringing "those accused of the most serious international crimes to justice", as well as supporting victims.

The ICC was founded in 2002 to prosecute war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide, and counts 125 countries as member states. Several major countries remain outside the ICC, including the US, Russia, China, India and Israel.

The Trump administration argues the ICC is run by what it calls globalists who threaten American sovereignty.

It is furious over a past investigation into actions of US soldiers in Afghanistan the court has since closed and by its arrest warrants for Israeli officials including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. The new sanctions, however, do not say that those warrants must be withdrawn before the measures can be lifted.

But Rubio said Trump would not allow the ICC to prosecute Americans, adding: "Either the ICC will end its threats, or we will end the ICC."

The US sanctions will stop US companies from providing goods or services to the ICC, such as banking or software.

Rubio said Washington had delayed imposing the sanctions in the hope that the ICC and its member countries would address US concerns. He said the measures had been structured to allow other countries to negotiate a possible solution.

He also called on US allies that were ICC signatories, including the UK, to "rein in" the institution.

The Netherlands, which hosts the court in The Hague and is also a Nato ally of the US, faces particular pressure. Dutch Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen has said the sanctions would seriously affect the court's ability to function.

Netanyahu welcomed the sanctions, saying the ICC was "not a court" but a political body that threatened law-abiding democracies and "the very idea of national sovereignty".

The ICC said that the sanctions were aimed at disrupting its work and intimidating those who co-operate with it - but that it "will not be deterred".

It called the measures "an assault on the rule of law" and said no one should be punished for serving the cause of justice, adding: "History will judge this moment."

This showdown potentially marks the gravest crisis in the court's 24-year history. Rather than targeting individual ICC judges and prosecutors, the US is now sanctioning the court itself.

World.title: Navi Pillay, former UN human rights chief, wins Nobel Peace Prize
World.content:
Frydnes said the committee had not been able to notify Pillay that she had won in advance, "so my message to her would be 'if you see a Norwegian number calling, please pick up'".

Shortly afterwards, Pillay reacted to the news from Nuremberg's Palace of Justice by saying "it must be a joke" and thanked those who had gathered to applaud her.

"If you clap a little bit more I may share this prize with Trump," she joked. Last year's winner, Venezuelan opposition leader MarÃ­a Corina Machado, gave her medal to the US president in January as "recognition for his unique commitment with our freedom".

Pillay dedicated her award to "all the survivors of international crimes" and the practitioners of international justice "whose compassion and courage continue to ensure that impunity will not be allowed to reign".

Navanethem "Navi" Pillay grew up in South Africa during apartheid as a bus driver's daughter in a poor Indian section of Durban.

She went on to become the first woman to establish a law practice in Natal Province in 1967, and later the first non-white woman to be appointed to the country's high court.

Pillay served as a judge on the UN-backed International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda - focused on the 1994 genocide in which 800,000 people were killed - including four years as its president. She was elected to the International Criminal Court (ICC) in 2003.

From 2021-25, she chaired the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory - a fact-finding body established by the UN Human Rights Council to investigate alleged violations of international law.

The commission concluded that Israel had committed genocidal acts in Gaza and that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, and his former defence minister Yoav Gallant, had "incited the commission of genocide" in their speeches and statements.

The three-member expert panel did not speak officially for the UN and had no legal authority. Israel rejected its findings and accused the three members of the commission of serving as "Hamas proxies".

The panel had previously concluded that Hamas and other Palestinian armed groups committed war crimes and other grave violations of international law on 7 October 2023, in which about 1,200 people were killed and another 251 taken hostage. The same report also accused Israel of war crimes.

Reacting to Pillay's award on Friday, Israel's Foreign Ministry said it represented a "grotesque weaponisation of an award to legitimise anti-Israel hatred and prejudice".

It said in a statement: "Her role in the relentless, politically motivated demonisation of Israel and promotion of the genoLIE speaks volumes."

World.title: Firing squad execution to be livestreamed, Pentagon says
World.content:
The public will be able to watch the execution of a former US Army major by firing squad, US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth has said.

A Defence Department official told the BBC the execution of Nidal Hasan, who fatally shot 13 unarmed US soldiers at the Fort Hood military base in 2009, would be livestreamed.

It is believed it would be the first public execution in the US in almost a century. The decision to livestream it was "unprecedented in the modern era" and "on uncertain legal terrain", said John Mills, a lawyer who works with inmates sentenced to death.

"People need to understand that there's serious consequences for these types of things," said Hegseth.

The UN human rights office told AFP that livestreaming it would be "tantamount to a public execution and would breach the absolute prohibition of torture".

Democratic Senator Chris Murphy told CNN that the idea was "disgusting" and reminiscent of executions carried out by the Islamic State group.

The Pentagon announced earlier this week it would execute Hasan in the first military execution in more than 60 years.

Hasan, a US Army psychiatrist from Virginia, admitted fatally shooting 13 unarmed soldiers in a crowded medical building at Fort Hood.

Alonzo Lunsford, a former US Army sergeant who was shot seven times in the attack, told the BBC's Today programme that he supported the execution by firing squad, as a method "befitting" for what he did.

But he said he did not believe everyone should be able to watch the livestream over concerns about the message it might send to younger people, but added that it was important that those affected by the shooting were given the opportunity.

"As far as the families of the fallen and the families of the survivors, and the survivors themselves, yes, I think we should be able to look at it uncensored."

Lunsford said he planned to attend the execution and before they pull the trigger he wants Hasan to look him in the eyes. "I want him to know he failed. I'm still here."

World.title: Russian search engine Yandex struggles after Ukrainian strikes on data centres
World.content:
Russian tech giant Yandex has said it was struggling to maintain services after two of its five data centres were struck by Ukrainian drones in the past two days.

Often dubbed "Russia's Google", the company runs the country's most popular search engine, as well as a food-ordering and taxi app used by tens of millions of people.

President Volodymyr Zelensky said the attacks were in response to weeks of Russian strikes on Ukrainian data centres.

Both sides have stepped up attacks on infrastructure in recent months as the war between the two drags on. Kyiv says its strikes are aimed at revenue streams for Moscow's war machine, and that the latest attacks could force Russia to divert resources to Yandex.

Yandex said that its data centre in Sasovo, in the Ryazan region, had been "seriously damaged as a result of a drone attack" overnight into Thursday, with its operations "completely suspended".

Another data centre in Kaluga, a region south-west of Moscow, had also been attacked on Friday morning, it said, with part of that site's infrastructure "taken out of service".

Yandex said on Friday that its data centres were "critical" for the normal operation of its services and that it was "very difficult to predict" when they would be back online.

It said teams were working "day and night" to keep services running, but "unfortunately it is not a simple task".

The tech giant said none of its employees had been injured in the strikes. The regional governor in Kaluga said nine people had been injured in a drone attack on the city's infrastructure.

The exact scope of the disruption to the company's services is unclear - though it told state news agency Tass that some of its AI chatbot functions were temporarily unavailable, while its smart home devices may also experience problems.

Yandex previously said its Kaluga data centre was one of Russia's largest - covering an area of 130,000 sqm (1,399,000 sq ft) and consuming as much electricity annually as 220,000 UK households.

Its data centre in Sasovo, meanwhile, houses two of three supercomputers used to develop the company's AI model. It is unclear whether the supercomputers survived the attack.

Ukraine's defence ministry confirmed the data centre attacks, saying they could "force Russia to divert resources to repair the damaged capacity".

Zelensky said Kyiv was responding to similar Russian attacks on Ukrainian data centres in a "mirror-like fashion".

Last month, a Russian drone hit a business centre in Kyiv, killing four people and damaging a data centre. Due to the strikes, about 100,000 households in Kyiv and the region suffered internet outages.

Some Ukrainian firms have already begun moving data from damaged servers to facilities abroad.

Moscow has justified the attacks by saying the data centres were used by Ukrainian military intelligence.

But Ukraine accuses it of deliberately targeting civilian infrastructure. Russia has stepped up strikes on energy infrastructure ahead of the winter, as it has done in previous years of the full-scale invasion, which began in 2022.

World.title: Thieves steal 30,000 bottles of wine worth €5m in Italy, reports say
World.content:
Thieves have stolen 30,000 bottles of wine collectively worth about â¬5m (Â£4.2m) from a prestigious Italian winery, Italian media report.

Marchesi Antinori, one of Italy's biggest family-owned wineries, said the theft at its storage facility in Tuscany took place on Saturday as the company was preparing to ship a consignment to customers abroad.

At least seven masked men are believed to have deactivated the alarms, disabled the cameras and used company forklifts to load two large trucks of the company's prized Tignanello, Solaia and Guado al Tasso Tuscan reds.

Renzo Cotarella, the chief executive, told Italian newspaper Corriere della Sera this was the largest theft of its kind in Italy.

"A theft of this scale and value has certainly never occurred in Italy," he said.

He added that he was hopeful the authorities would be able to trace the stolen wine.

"Two trucks full of merchandise can't just disappear into thin air. The Tuscan roads are full of cameras - perhaps with a bit of luck we'll be able to recover at least some of the bottles stolen from us."

He told the Financial Times: "These wines have a great value and I don't know how they can sell all this wine around the world without being seen."

The company believes the selection of bottles, which usually sell for between â¬150 and â¬500 each, suggests the thieves were wine connoisseurs and had inside knowledge.

The theft was only discovered on Monday morning as staff arrived on site. No arrests have been made.

Marchesi Antinori was founded in 1385 and exports to 170 countries. It had a revenue of â¬263m (Â£223m) last year.

There has been a spate of wine thefts in Italy this year, including two in the northern Piedmont region where hundreds of thousands of euros worth of bottles were reportedly taken.

World.title: Man named Hitler Mussolini elected mayor in Peru
World.content:
A man named Hitler Mussolini Simeon Flores has secured a narrow victory in Peru's local elections, exit polls show.

The candidate for the centre-left Ahora NaciÃ³n party was elected mayor of Queropalca, a remote district in the Peruvian Andes.

Some 229 residents voted for the 45-year-old, putting him ahead of the second-place candidate from right-wing RenovaciÃ³n Popular PerÃº by just 25 votes.

Despite being elected to represent fewer than 1,000 people, his forenames being those of two notorious fascist dictators has drawn outsized international attention to the small corner of the country.

Data from Peru's elections office showed a little over 700 people had participated in the election, with Simeon securing around 34% of the vote.

He was born in the district in the central department of HuÃ¡nuco, some 360km (224 miles) from the capital, Lima, according to his candidate profile.

That he shares his name with Adolf Hitler and Benito Mussolini - "two of the most well-known figures of 20th-Century European totalitarian regimes" - has made his candidacy a "striking event", local outlet Peru21 reported.

Despite the curiosity generated by his name, local media noted that Hitler Guesclin Alba SÃ¡nchez had been elected mayor of YÃºngar in 2018.

He reportedly beat rival candidate Lenin Vladimir RodrÃ­guez Valverde after campaigning on the slogan "I'm the good Hitler".

A politician named Adolf Hitler Uunona attracted similar attention in 2020 after winning local elections in Namibia - a former German colony where Adolf and other Germanic first names are not uncommon.

World.title: Ethiopia warns Eritrea it will defend itself after troops cross border
World.content:
Ethiopia has accused Eritrea of an "all-out invasion" of its northern Tigray region and warned it will defend itself, days after residents told the BBC Eritrean troops had crossed into the country.

In a letter sent to the UN Security Council and seen by the BBC, Ethiopia's foreign minister called it a "blatant act of aggression that engages Ethiopia's inherent right to self-defence".

Eritrean Information Minister Yemane Gebremeskel responded by saying it was facing "an unprovoked war of aggression" from its neighbour.

Fighting broke out two weeks ago between the government and the party that controls Tigray, the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF).

Both blame each other for violating a 2022 deal that ended a civil war.

Ethiopia says Eritrea is backing the TPLF, which it denies.

During the two-year civil war, Eritrea was a key ally of the Ethiopian government, having fought alongside them against the TPLF.

But relations between the two neighbours have since deteriorated - largely over the Ethiopian prime minister's ambition to take ownership of one of Eritrea's Red Sea ports - leading to the severing of diplomatic ties last week.

Accusing Eritrea of violating its sovereignty, Ethiopian Foreign Minister Gedion Timothewos said Eritrean forces had advanced up to 60km (37 miles) into Tigray.

Ethiopian drone strikes reportedly targeted Eritrean forces in the Tigrayan town of Adigrat on Wednesday and Thursday, amid fears of a wider regional war.

US-based conflict monitor Acled said "Eritrean troops and ammunition" in Adigrat were hit by "multiple drone strikes" overnight.

One resident told AFP news agency "there were many, many drone strikes", and that some Eritrean lorries had been destroyed.

Another witness said Eritrean forces appeared to be retreating north after the strikes, AFP reported.

There have so far been no verified reports of casualties. The BBC is unable to report from Tigray.

World.title: US immigration officials defend ICE agents who shot man in same car as child
World.content:
US immigration officials have defended the actions of officers who shot and wounded a man in his car in New York on Thursday while his five-year-old son was in the back seat.

Markwayne Mullin, the head of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), which runs the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), said officers fired their weapons while trying to arrest a man with a criminal history.

"We weren't aware the child was in the car," Mullin added at a news conference on Friday, arguing that it was the man, Oscar Belgal, who had put his child in danger. Belgal is now being held at a detention facility.

The legal organisation representing Belgal told the BBC that lawyers had not yet been able to speak to him.

The shooting happened in the residential neighbourhood of Marble Hill.

Marcos Charles, a top ICE official who was also at Friday's news conference, said agents used their vehicles to try and stop Belgal in his car but that he resisted orders to get out and instead accelerated, smashing into two ICE vehicles.

Charles said Belgal then "weaponised his vehicle and proceeded to accelerate going towards other officers", adding: "Our officers, using their training, and believing that their life and the life of their partners in the general public were in danger, used their training and fired weapons."

The number of officers who fired their weapons is being investigated.

Charles said Belgal "was struck by one of the bullets or fragments superficially in the neck".

New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani, who called what happened "unconscionable and incredibly serious", said ICE agents surrounded Belgal's car before opening fire.

"They wore construction vests and masks that concealed their faces. There is no reasonable way to identify them as ICE agents," Mamdani said. He confirmed that the child was unharmed.

Mullin said the officers identified themselves and were wearing body-worn cameras that were turned on during the incident.

Video of the shooting, including body camera footage, has not been made public but unverified videos on social media appear to align with Mamdani's comments.

Body-worn camera footage released by the New York Police Department (NYPD) on Friday shows its officers arriving on scene and attempting to help Belgal after he has been shot. One ICE officer appears to be wearing a neon construction vest and carrying a large gun.

The NYPD officers then call for an ambulance and putting him in a police car to take him to hospital. They are later seen pulling Belgal from the vehicle and carrying him into the hospital.

World.title: Ogun sustains palliative support for public servants, allocates N987m in nine months
World.content:
The Ogun State Government has allocated ₦987.185 million for palliative support for public servants between April and December 2026, including ₦327.31 million earmarked for the fourth quarter.

Disclosing this in a statement on Friday, the Head of Service, Olanrewaju Iskeel Saka, said the sustained intervention reflected the administration’s commitment to workers’ welfare and its efforts to cushion the effects of prevailing economic challenges.

The latest allocation of ₦327,310,000 covers October to December 2026, following ₦330,630,000 allocated for April to June and ₦329,245,000 for July to September, bringing the total provision for the three quarters to ₦987,185,000.

The continuation of the programme underscores the government’s determination to sustain support for public servants amid economic pressures, particularly the rising cost of transportation and other essential expenses.

The intervention also highlights the administration’s recognition of the importance of workers’ welfare to productivity, effective public service delivery and the implementation of its development agenda.

By extending the palliative support through December, the administration of Governor Dapo Abiodun is maintaining a welfare measure designed to ease the financial burden on workers while ensuring that the public service continues to deliver essential services to residents across the state.

World.title: NHRC, foreign embassies push for abolition of death penalty in Nigeria
World.content:
The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), Avocats Sans Frontieres, Australian High Commission, Embassy of the Federal Republic of Germany and the Spanish embassy in Nigeria on Friday called for the revocation of the death penalty in Nigeria.

They made the call at the NHRC’s head office in Abuja to commemorate the International Day Against the Death Penalty, observed annually on 10 October.

The NHRC’s Executive Secretary, Tony Ojukwu, represented by the Director of Legal Services and Enforcement, Rabir Anwar, called for “transition of Nigeria’s tenure clause into an official, effective moratorium on execution.”

“The commission urges the government to systematically revoke Section 312 of the Constitution and Section 122 of the Nigeria Correctional Service Act to commute death sentences to life imprisonment,” he said.

Mr Ojukwu, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria, said that by December, Nigeria would mark 10 consecutive years without a state execution, meeting the international standard for a de facto moratorium. However, over 3,000 persons are on prolonged death row detention.

The Australian High Commissioner to Nigeria, Leilani Bin-Juda, commended Nigeria for reaching the de facto moratorium on executions.

“Behind every death sentence are individuals, families and communities whose lives are profoundly affected by the decisions of the justice system,” she said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Ms Bin-Juda explained that Australia opposes the death penalty in all circumstances and for all people, because we believe it is a cruel, inhumane and degrading punishment that has no place in a modern justice system.

While she recognised Nigeria’s autonomy as an independent state, Ms Bin-Juda encouraged the nation to consider formalising its de facto moratorium on executions or narrow the range of offences over which the death penalty may be imposed.

Like Australia, the Ambassador of Spain to Nigeria, Felix Costales Arteida, said Spain opposes the death penalty because “life is an inalienable right, and no state should have the power to take it away.”

He said, “There is no evidence that capital punishment acts as a greater deterrent than other penalties involving the deprivation of liberty.

“Yet it is undoubtedly irreversible, eliminating any possibility of correcting judicial errors.”

Citing the US as an example, he said that since 1973, 130 people sentenced to death have been found innocent since 1973 and released from death row.

Mr Arteida said the strength and justice of a society are not “measured by the severity of its punishments, but by its capacity to protect the fundamental rights of all people, even in the most difficult times.”

He also encouraged the Nigerian government to review capital punishment. Doing this is not a sign of weakness but a demonstration of strength, he said.

Lorena Moore, who represented the German Ambassador, acknowledged the need for justice, but stressed that taking the life of another human being can never be the solution to the justified need for justice.

Commitment to advocacy and human rights

The Country Head, Avocats Sans Frontières France Angela Uzoma-Iwuchukwu, expressed commitment to advocating against the death penalty, describing it as a violation of the right to life.

“It is discriminatory because it targets the weakest in our society. It is used disproportionately against the poor.”

Guests who graced the commemoration of the World Day Against the Death Penalty at the NHRC included the Ambassador of Belgium, Patrick Englebert, the representative of the European Union, the representative of the President of the Nigerian Bar Association (NBA), Oghenero Okoro, and Italian Ambassador, Roberto Mengoni.

NCOS committed to professionalism

The Nigerian Correctional Service, Comptroller-General Sylvester Nwakuche, represented by Comptroller Olufemi Oluyemi, the men and women on death, whom, he said, prison officers often come in contact with, “are not merely case files or numbers.”

“We meet them every day, in the yard, in the workshop, in the classroom, in the chapel, in the mosque, all around us. We also hear the stories of the families who wait for them, and we remain conscious of the stories of victims and communities whose pain must never be forgotten,” he said.

He noted that whatever the direction of the national conversation on the death penalty, the NCOS will stand ready to play its part with professionalism, humanity, and integrity to the law.

‘Human cost of capital punishnent’

This year’s theme for the World Day Against the Death Penalty is Stories for Life: the human cost of capital punishment.

Amanda Arthur, a 21-year-old daughter of death row survivor Angel Arthur, gave a testimonial of his father to illustrate the theme of the day.

Mr Arthur was imprisoned when he was 21 years old and spent 16 years in prison. His name was later removed from the list of those to be executed. He insisted that he was wrongfully imprisoned.

His daughter on Friday said her father never forgot his awful experience and his story always resonated in the house. Ms Arthur said this has impacted their lives and view of society.

“It’s made me conscious, super conscious of things around me because I know at any point in time I could be a victim or I could be a perpetrator. The trauma has stuck with us,” she said.

“A very subconscious stigma: the moment you say your parent has been in prison, everybody starts looking at it differently.”

Speaking on the death penalty, she said that, guilty or not, no human should undergo such punishment. “It’s dehumanising.”

Commutation of death row inmates in Nigeria

Amnesty International reported that as of 2025, 145 countries have abolished the death penalty both in law and practice.

While Nigeria would become a de facto abolitionist state, by December, there are laws that allow for state pardon for those on death row.

Similarly, section 12(2)(c) of the Nigerian Correctional Service (NCoS) Act, 2019 allows the commutation of a death sentence to life imprisonment under specific conditions.

Some governors have pardoned some death-row inmates. For instance, on 1 October, the Governor of Plateau State, Caleb Muftwang, commuted the death sentences of four inmates to life imprisonment.

Enugu State Governor, Peter Mbah, also commuted the death sentences of 13 inmates, and the Governor of Adamawa State, Ahmadu Fintiri, commuted the death penalty of one person to lesser punishment.

In April 2025, the NHRC appealed to Mr Fintiri to spare the life of Sunday Jackson, a farmer who was sentenced to death in 2019 for killing a herder during a confrontation on his farmland.

In December 2025, Mr Fintiri granted a full pardon to Mr Jackson.

World.title: Train collides with car at Lagos crossing, driver escapes unhurt
World.content:
A motorist escaped unhurt after a train struck his Honda car at the PWD railway crossing in Ikeja, Lagos, on Friday, the Lagos State Traffic Management Authority (LASTMA) has said.

According to a statement posted on X by LASTMA, the train was travelling towards Agege when it collided with a Honda car, registration number EKY 902 JT.

A photograph from the scene shared by the agency shows a part of the car crushed by the train. But no injuries or deaths were reported.

The statement noted that LASTMA operatives and security personnel rescued the 55-year-old driver and cleared the wreckage from the tracks, allowing the train to continue its journey.

Traffic congestion persisted around the PWD axis after the incident, slowing movement along the affected route.

LASTMA said the damaged vehicle was handed over to security personnel as investigations into the cause of the collision were expected to follow.

The agency’s General Manager, Olalekan Bakare-Oki, commended the operatives and security personnel for their response.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He also urged motorists to obey railway safety rules and avoid crossing the tracks when a train is approaching or already in motion.

Fatal crashes at PWD crossing

Friday’s collision adds to a series of train accidents at the PWD railway crossing.

In October 2025, a dispatch rider died after his motorcycle collided with a moving train at the crossing.

The crossing was also the scene of a fatal accident on 9 March 2023, when a train collided with a Lagos State Government staff bus, killing six people and injuring dozens.

Following that crash, the Lagos State Ministry of Justice released a report alleging that the driver committed a prima facie case of manslaughter and grievous bodily harm.

The cause of Friday’s collision has not been established. However, the latest incident has again drawn attention to safety at a crossing where previous train accidents have claimed lives.

World.title: Banky W becomes ordained pastor in US
World.content:
Nigerian singer Olubankole “Banky W” Wellington has revealed that he is now an ordained pastor in the United States (US), two years after relocating there with his family.

The 45-year-old announced it in a statement he posted on his Instagram page on Thursday. He said he serves as Associate Pastor and Global Ambassador at Union Church, a non-denominational Christian church with multiple campuses across the US.

Pastors Stephen and Zai Chandler lead the church. Banky W also revealed that he works as a teacher and leader at Union College.

Reflecting on his new roles, the singer and entrepreneur recalled a joke he once made about whether the “P” in his nickname, P.Banks, stood for professor or pastor.

He said: “Somewhere along the way, I realised that I was asking God to choose between things He had never asked me to separate. It wasn’t either/or. It was all of the above. Turns out, God wasn’t trying to put me in a box. He was expanding my assignment. So yes, I’m still a filmmaker, musician, and entrepreneur. But somehow, by the grace of God, I’m also a Pastor and a Professor.

“Constantly travelling back and forth between Lagos and the DMV isn’t always easy. But has it been worth it? Absolutely. Because I now have the privilege of serving as an Associate Pastor and Global Ambassador at Union Church, and as a teacher and leader at Union College. And I get to do it under the extraordinary leadership of Stephen Chandler and Zai Chandler.”

Election

Banky W said he was thankful for the positive influence the Chandlers had on his personal life, spiritual growth, family and future.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“See, I never wanted to be put in a box. But little did I know that while I was busy trying to figure out what I wanted to do with my life, God was already writing a story I couldn’t have imagined”, he said.

Banky W also spoke about the personal impact of his defeat in the 2023 elections and how the experience eventually drew him towards pastoral ministry.

He contested the Eti-Osa Federal Constituency seat in the House of Representatives on the platform of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) but lost to the Labour Party’s Thaddeus Attah.

According to him, the loss left him emotionally shattered and pushed him to turn to God for direction. He added that after the election defeat, he struggled to determine whether to pursue a future in politics, ministry, entertainment or business.

He noted, “In 2023 I lost an election. And while the experience inspired me in many ways, it also broke my heart into a million little pieces. When the dust settled, I took those pieces back to God. And I surrendered.

“I asked Him, “What’s next? What’s Your will for my life? Is it leadership or ministry? Entertainment or business? Marketplace or ministry?”

“A continued journey’

Reflecting on his first year as a pastor, Banky W said that an apparent ending could instead be God’s way of beginning a new chapter in someone’s life.

Although the election result fell short of his expectations, the actor said he trusted God’s purpose for his life would be greater than anything he had envisioned.

“And the beautiful thing is, He’s still writing. There’s more to come on the business, film, and music fronts (stay tuned 99), but today, I want to pause and say thank you, Jesus.

“For the doors You open and the ones You close. For the people you bring into my life and the purpose you reveal, one piece of the puzzle at a time. One year down. A lifetime of purpose ahead. Please wish me a happy 1st Unionversary.”

World.title: Communications Ministry made ₦345.5 million duplicate payment for Abuja ICT Park project – Audit Report
World.content:
The Auditor-General of the Federation flagged an alleged ₦345.5 million duplicate payment by the Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation, and Digital Economy to a contractor handling the Abuja ICT Park project.

The finding was contained in the Auditor-General’s Annual Report on Non-Compliance and Internal Control Weaknesses in Ministries, Departments and Agencies of the Federal Government for the year ended 31 December 2024.

The special audit of the communication ministry covered the period from 1 January to 31 December 2021 and raised 14 issues concerning the planning, funding, procurement and implementation of the ICT Park project.

At the time the project was being implemented, Isa Ali Pantami, who was appointed by former President Muhammadu Buhari, served as Minister of Communications and Digital Economy from 2019 to 2023. He was succeeded by Bosun Tijani, who was appointed by President Bola Tinubu.

₦345.5 million duplicate payment

In Issue 13 of the findings, titled “Loss of Fund Due to Duplicated Payments to Contractor,” the Auditor-General said the ministry processed and approved two separate payments of ₦345,499,262.74 each as the third tranche of the 15 per cent mobilisation advance to the contractor.

The payment was intended to establish the Information and Communication Technology (ICT) Park, Abuja.

The Permanent Secretary approved the first payment on 19 January 2022 through payment voucher No. FMCDE/CAP/606/2021 dated 24 January 2022.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The same accounting officer approved the second payment on 17 January 2023 through payment voucher No. FMCDE/CAP/149/2022 dated 8 February 2023.

The report said the two paid vouchers had identical contract references, amounts, and narrative descriptions, which it said indicated duplicate payment.

It added that no record showed the first payment had been reversed, adjusted, or treated as an accounting error.

“There was also no journal entry, refund, or internal memo linking the 2023 approval to any prior transactions. These omissions demonstrate a failure of supervisory review, record reconciliation, and payment verification within the Ministry,” the findings stated.

The Finance and Accounts Department also failed to justify the repeated authorisation or the lack of reconciliation between the Cash Book and Vote Book, according to the report.

The findings said the contractor, while claiming it received only one payment in 2023, submitted a bank statement that excluded the critical period between 2 January 2022 and 8 February 2023, preventing independent verification of its claim.

The audit said the payments posed risks of fund diversion and loss of public funds, attributing this to weaknesses in the ministry’s internal control system.

The audit said the ministry’s management did not respond to the alleged duplicate payment under the contract.

The Auditor-General recommended that ₦345.499 million be recovered and remitted to the Treasury, and that evidence of remittance be forwarded to the Public Accounts Committee of the National Assembly.

₦447.67m from undisclosed funding sources

In Issue 11, the auditors questioned ₦447.67 million in payments to the ICT Park contractor, which they said could not be traced to the Government Integrated Financial Management Information System (GIFMIS).

The amount comprised ₦102,166,730 and ₦345,499,262.74 paid to the contractor, vide paid vouchers, Ref. No. FMCDE/CAP/061/2021 and FCMDE/606/2022 on 11 June 2021 and 19 February 2022, respectively.

According to the report, the payments appeared in the cash book. The contractor acknowledged them in the progress report and bank statement, but they did not appear in GIFMIS records, indicating they were processed off the system.

The audit said officials in the ministry’s Finance and Accounts Department could not explain the existence or authorisation of the alternative funding sources.

The report said the ministry also failed to provide documentation showing lawful appropriation, supplementary approval, or an external funding agreement for the payments.

The audit said the action posed a risk of misappropriation of funds and diversion of public property.

It said the ministry’s management did not respond to questions about the history of the payments in the GIFMIS records.

The Auditor-General recommended recovering and remitting ₦447.67 million to the Treasury, with sanctions under paragraphs 3106 and 3129 of the Financial Regulations (2009) if the ministry fails to comply.

₦396.65 million project funds used for unrelated items

In Issue 9, the findings showed that N396.65 million from the ICT Park project fund was used to pay for consultancy services, office consumables, furniture, and stationery printing.

The audit said approvals had been processed for consultancy services relating to the ICT Park. Still, payments were made to unrelated suppliers for consumables and office furniture that were not contained in the project’s Bill of Quantities.

The report said this reduced funds meant for the mobilisation and execution of the ICT Park project.

It also said the ministry failed to provide evidence of approval for the virement from the Minister of Finance, Budget and National Planning and the National Assembly.

It said the actions posed a risk of misappropriation of funds and undue delay in completion of the project, noting that the ministry failed to respond to the question on the use of the project funds for unrelated items.

The Auditor-General recommended recovering and remitting ₦396.655 million to the Treasury, with sanctions under paragraphs 3106 and 3129 of the Financial Regulations (2009) if the ministry fails to comply.

₦1.85bn paid without performance bond

In Issue 10, the auditors also found that N1.848 billion was paid to the contractor without securing a valid Performance Bond.

The report said the Bureau of Public Procurement had directed in December 2020 that a minimum 10 per cent Performance Bond be secured for major contracts before payment of mobilisation fees.

However, the ministry first released ₦1.348 billion in mobilisation payments between March 2021 and February 2023 without obtaining the required bond.

The report said that nearly three years after the contract award, the contractor submitted a commitment letter dated 29 December 2023, promising to furnish a Performance Bond upon receiving an additional N500 million. This amounts to ₦1.848 billion.

It said the actions exposed public funds to loss, noting that the ministry failed to respond to the question on the payment.

The Auditor-General recommended recovering and remitting ₦1.848 billion to the Treasury, and imposing sanctions under paragraphs 3106 and 3129 of the Financial Regulations (2009) if the ministry fails to comply.

₦500 million paid without interim performance certificate

In Issue 12, the Auditor-General said the ministry released an additional ₦500 million to the contractor on 29 December 2023 without an Interim Performance Certificate or verified progress report.

The report said the payment was made after the contractor received the 15 per cent mobilisation fee.

Instead of an Interim Performance Certificate, the ministry relied on a commitment letter from the contractor promising to provide project vehicles and undertake overseas technical trips upon receipt of the additional funds.

The audit said the actions posed a risk of diverting public funds and losing government funds. It said that the ministry failed to respond to the question on the payment.

The Auditor-General recommended recovering and remitting N500 million to the Treasury and imposing sanctions under paragraph 3106 of the Financial Regulations (2009) if the ministry fails to comply.

Premature foreign trips of ₦90 million

In Issue 8, the auditors questioned a ₦90 million provisional sum for foreign trips to inspect technical equipment for the ICT Park.

According to the findings, the sum of ₦90 million was included and described as “Allow a provisional sum of N90 million to cater for Client’s and Consultants’ representatives for foreign trips for the inspection of technical equipment to be deployed for the project,” in the priced Bill of Quantities (BOQ) for the contract for the ICT Park project, with a contract sum of ₦8.984 billion.

The report said the expenditure was being planned while the project was still at foundation level, before structural works, equipment procurement or installation had commenced.

It said no evidence was provided to justify the technical need, approved schedule, or cost-benefit assessment supporting the timing of the proposed trips.

The audit said the action demonstrated weak expenditure prioritisation and poor sequencing of project activities, noting that it posed a risk of undue delay in completion of the project and diversion of public funds.

Again, the ministry did not respond to questions about the premature foreign trip.

The Auditor-General recommended recovering and remitting the N90 million. It also recommended sanctions under paragraphs 3106 and 3115 of the Financial Regulations (2009) if the ministry fails to comply.

Denial of access to project documents

The audit also raised concerns about the ministry’s failure to give auditors access to project documents.

In Issue 14, the report said auditors were denied access to documents including needs assessment reports, bank mandates for ICT project payments, payment vouchers, due diligence reports on the contractor and the Environmental and Social Impact Assessment report.

The report said several requests for project-related documents made between March and June 2025 were not answered by the ministry.

It said the denial of access to procurement documents contravened the Constitution and risked concealing financial information, diverting government revenue, and the loss of public funds.

The Auditor-General asked the Permanent Secretary to justify the denial of access and produce all documents relating to the ICT Park project.

The report stated that the ministry did not respond to the issues raised in the audit and that the findings remained valid until the recommendations were implemented.

Other issues

Other issues included a ₦94.05 million cost overrun attributed to the failure to conduct feasibility studies and an Environmental Impact Assessment before the ICT Park project began.

The Auditor-General also flagged ₦19.47 million in costs linked to delayed site handover, while questioning the absence of resident technical supervision despite a ₦160 million provision for it.

The report further cited inadequate budgetary provisions that contributed to project delays and the ministry’s failure to conduct or document a needs assessment before procurement.

World.title: Kayefi headlines Tales & Tunes as ID Cabasa leads music direction in Sheffield
World.content:
Nigerian Afro-Soul musician Lawal “Kayefi” Olufunmilayo has brought Nigeria’s cultural heritage to the fore in Sheffield, combining music, fashion and other forms of artistic expression.

The Ogun-born artiste showcased the country’s rich traditions at the 2026 edition of Tales & Tunes, an event featuring live performances, African fashion, dance, DJ sets and food.

The programme began with a lively fashion show highlighting African-inspired designs and modern styles. Utana Stitches, Hope 4 Sheffield, All Things Kayefi, Grei Linage and Everything Coloured featured in the runway showcase.

Their collections featured eye-catching patterns, bold fashion statements, and sophisticated silhouettes that captivated attendees.

Performances

Music and dance added to the atmosphere of the night, with Kayefi delivering one of the event’s most emotional performances.

In a particularly moving moment, the singer played a voice note from her late father, leaving some attendees deeply touched.

She also read a letter her grandmother had written to her father in the early 1970s. The letter, which reflected on family, love, memories and legacy, became one of the evening’s defining moments.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Some guests described the playback of the voice note and the reading of the letter as the event’s most touching parts.

Kayefi shared the stage with Eyinju Eledumare, iPraiz, Mitchyx, Surayi Dancers and Ehi. Dancers Oyidamola Timothy Fagbamigbila, popularly known as Damodance, and Abigail Tonade, known as Dancewithabby, also performed.

DJs Àrònì, DJ Lorna T and DJ Pee provided the music, while Nigerian producer ID Cabasa directed the event.

Storytelling

Reflecting on the event, Kayefi Kafeyi told PREMIUM TIMES on Friday that Tales & Tunes was conceived as a platform to bring people together through shared cultural experiences.

She likened the initiative to a contemporary village square, where people gather to connect and celebrate their heritage. She said she had always envisioned a space that would bring together music, fashion, dance, food, storytelling and other aspects of African tradition.

Kayefi described this year’s edition as particularly memorable, noting that its personal significance came from her family’s story, which she said made the experience feel close to home.

“I have long wanted to create a space where music, fashion, dance, food, storytelling and the entire African Traditions would corroborate and stay in the minds of the people, where they will particularly enjoy themselves.

“Seeing that happen in Sheffield was incredibly beautiful. I’m deeply grateful to every artist, designer, musician, dancer, DJ, model, vendor, volunteer, partner and everyone who became part of our village.”

She explained that Tales & Tunes would remain a meeting point for African culture and modern British life, giving budding artists, designers, and other creatives a chance to showcase their work.

She added that the platform would encourage cultural exchange and strengthen connections among people from diverse communities and generations.

World.title: FAAN proposes 25-day closure of Owerri airport runway for repairs
World.content:
The Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN) has proposed closing the runway at Sam Mbakwe International Cargo Airport, Owerri, Imo State, for about 25 days to carry out repairs and resurfacing.

FAAN disclosed this on Thursday, saying the closure was tentatively scheduled to begin on 20 October 2026, subject to final confirmation.

The authority said sections of the runway had deteriorated, with potholes and extensive surface cracks worsened by recent heavy rainfall.

The planned works will include pavement repairs, crack treatment and resurfacing of affected sections to improve the runway’s condition and safety.

FAAN said the repairs were also intended to prepare the airport for an anticipated increase in passenger and flight traffic during the Christmas season.

Runway extension planned

Beyond the repairs, the project will extend the runway to accommodate wide-body aircraft as air traffic to the region grows.

The authority said the extension was expected to improve the airport’s capacity and passenger experience.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

However, FAAN did not provide details of the planned extension or specify how much additional runway length would be required.

The authority said the closure and reopening dates would be confirmed after consultations with relevant stakeholders.

READ ALSO: Mbah appoints Enugu Air chair as transport commissioner

Passengers advised to contact airlines

FAAN advised passengers planning to travel through Owerri during the proposed closure period to contact their airlines for updates on flight schedules and alternative arrangements.

It said the confirmed closure and reopening dates would be communicated once finalised.

The proposed closure comes ahead of the Christmas travel season, when passenger and flight traffic is expected to increase.

The airport serves Owerri and surrounding communities in Imo State and the wider South-east region, making its runway condition and capacity important for maintaining safe flight operations and accommodating growing air traffic.

World.title: Airtel Money commences conditional trading on London Stock Exchange
World.content:
Airtel Money, the mobile money subsidiary of telecom operator Airtel Africa Plc, has begun conditional trading of its shares on the main market for listed equities on the London Stock Exchange (LSE), effective from 9 October 2026, according to a regulatory filing on Friday.

“The commencement of unconditional dealings in the Airtel Money shares on the London Stock Exchange is expected to occur at 8.00 a.m. on 14 October 2026,” Airtel Africa stated.

It further noted that Airtel Money’s admission to the equity shares (commercial companies) category of the Official List of the FCA and to trading on the Main Market for listed securities of the London Stock Exchange will also occur on the same date.

Earlier this month, Airtel Money set its initial public offering (IPO) price at £1.96 per share, targeting a market capitalisation of $7 billion at admission.

It also announced a proposal to sell 270 million shares via a secondary share sale to raise around $703 million, making the IPO the biggest London listing since Fermi Inc, a Texas-based speciality energy infrastructure and real estate development company, listed its shares last September.

Airtel Africa, the parent, is retaining a majority stake of roughly 78 per cent. Institutional shareholders in the fintech include the Qatari Sovereign Wealth Fund, Mastercard, Chimetech and The Rise Fund II Aurora.

Airtel Africa noted in the Friday statement that it “is not selling existing Airtel Money shares in the offer and is expected to remain a long-term strategic shareholder and to support Airtel Money’s next phase of development as an independently listed business.”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Airtel Money is expected to have a free float – the portion of a company’s outstanding shares that is readily available for trade on the open market – of around 16.5 per cent following the listing.

Airtel Money shares fell below their IPO price on their LSE debut on Friday, easing to £1.93 per share in early trade after briefly climbing to £2.

The company provides fintech services, including transfers, digital banking, and bill payments across thirteen African countries, including Nigeria, Tanzania, and Kenya.

World.title: ‘I may share this prize with Trump’ — Nobel winner Pillay
World.content:
South African lawyer and champion of international law Navi Pillay addresses journalists after she was awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize, on October 9, 2026 at the historic Courtroom 600 of Nuremberg’s Palace of Justice, venue of the 1945-1946 Nuremberg Trials against leaders of defeated Nazi Germany, in Nuremberg, southern Germany, where she was attending the Nuremberg Forum 2026 conference of the International Nuremberg Principles Academy. The Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to South Africa’s Navi Pillay, the judge who headed the Rwanda genocide tribunal and who last year presided over a UN commission which accused Israel of genocide in Gaza. Pillay, currently a judge on the International Court of Justice in a case where Myanmar also stands accused of genocide, has been “instrumental in ensuring that war crimes, crimes against humanity, and genocide are prosecuted,” said Jorgen Watne Frydnes, the chair of the Norwegian Nobel Committee in Oslo. (Photo by Frank BOXLER / AFP)

South African champion of international law Navi Pillay, who was awarded this year’s Nobel peace prize, joked that she might “share the prize” with US President Donald Trump if people kept applauding her.

“If you clap a little bit more I may share this prize with Trump,” Pillay said in a video posted to X by the Secretary General of Amnesty International, which showed Pillay being applauded in Nuremberg after the announcement of the award.

She said that her first reaction to hearing the news was that it must be a joke.

“Being a lawyer and a judge, I still want to verify this,” the 85-year-old said, wanting to make sure it was true.

Pillay mentioned her work heading the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry (COI), which does not speak on behalf of the world body, and which last year found that genocide was occurring in Gaza.

“The last thing I did is the delivery of the report on Gaza, naming what’s happening there as genocide,” she said.

“One of the main reactions to that report is paying tribute to me for my courage. And you can imagine how surprised I was, why would you need courage to speak the truth?” she added.

The prize comes with a gold medal, a diploma and a prize sum of $1.2 million.

The award will be presented at a formal ceremony in Oslo on December 10, the anniversary of the 1896 death of the prizes’ creator, Swedish inventor and philanthropist Alfred Nobel.

World.title: 2027: Tinubu made life expensive; Atiku will make life affordable — ADC
World.content:
By Luminous Jannamike, Abuja

The African Democratic Congress (ADC) on Friday launched its 2027 presidential campaign with a pledge to reverse the economic hardship Nigerians face, declaring that President Bola Tinubu must be voted out and replaced with former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar.

The party, which unveiled its Presidential Campaign Council in Abuja, said soaring living costs, insecurity, unemployment and rising public debt had deepened Nigerians’ hardship, insisting that its Atiku Abubakar–Rotimi Amaechi ticket offered a credible alternative.

National Chairman, Senator David Mark, Campaign Council Chairman, Kashim Ibrahim-Imam, and Director-General, Senator Austin Akobundu, spoke at the inauguration, charging party members to mobilise nationwide around the promise of affordable living and better governance.

Akobundu said the campaign would focus on the daily struggles of families, workers, farmers and business owners, arguing that government policies had made basic necessities increasingly difficult to afford.

“Tinubu made life expensive. I will make life affordable again,” Akobundu quoted Atiku as saying.

He said Atiku would prioritise local refining through a targeted, budgeted production subsidy for fuel refined in Nigeria, alongside reforms in electricity, education, healthcare and agriculture. The proposed measures, he said, would ease production costs, improve access to essential services and create opportunities for young people and women.

Akobundu also pledged to review the Nigerian Education Loan Fund, pursue student debt forgiveness, improve security on farmlands and implement the Supreme Court judgment on local government autonomy.

On the political climate, he accused the administration of subjecting ADC members to intimidation and harassment through state agencies, vowing that the party would resist such actions while campaigning within the law.

“The ADC will resist every form of intimidation and harassment!” he declared.

He also condemned what he described as the continued incarceration of the council’s Deputy Chairman, former Kaduna State governor Nasir El-Rufai, calling it an affront to the rule of law.

Ibrahim-Imam delivered the sharpest political attack, declaring that the campaign was a mission to rescue Nigerians from economic hardship and insecurity.

“The palace feasts while the people fast!” he said, accusing the Tinubu administration of excessive spending while millions of Nigerians struggled to meet basic needs.

Citing figures presented in his address, Ibrahim-Imam said Nigeria’s public debt had risen from N87.38 trillion when Tinubu assumed office to N166.79 trillion by June 30, 2026. He also cited reports on killings and mass abductions to argue that the government had failed to protect lives and property.

He called on Nigerians to reject Tinubu’s re-election bid, presenting the 2027 contest as a choice between continued hardship and a change of direction.

“Tinubu priced you out of your own country. Atiku will bring you back in,” Ibrahim-Imam said.

Mark, meanwhile, charged the campaign council to take its message to every state, local government, ward and community, warning members against taking voters for granted.

“Our task is therefore bigger than winning an election. Our task is to present Nigerians with a credible alternative and give them the reason to believe and trust that the essence of governance is to protect them and make their lives better,” he said.

He urged the party to run an issue-based campaign, engage Nigerians across ethnic and religious lines and avoid violence, while calling on the Independent National Electoral Commission and other electoral institutions to remain impartial and transparent.

With the campaign council now inaugurated, the ADC faces the task of converting public frustration over economic hardship and insecurity into votes for the Atiku–Amaechi ticket in 2027.

World.title: 2027: 30 days can’t erase over three years of hardship, Atiku tells Tinubu
World.content:
By Luminous Jannamike

ABUJA — Presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, Atiku Abubakar, has dismissed President Bola Tinubu’s 30-day petrol discount as an inadequate response to years of economic hardship, saying Nigerians would hold the administration accountable in the 2027 general election.

Atiku argued that a temporary reduction in petrol prices could not reverse the rising cost of food, transportation, electricity and business operations, insisting that Nigerians needed lasting relief rather than what he described as an election-season palliative.

Speaking at the inauguration of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council in Abuja on Friday, the former Vice President accused Tinubu of adopting the principle behind his proposed production subsidy after previously dismissing it, but failing to implement the policy’s essential safeguards.

“Thirty days cannot erase three and a half years of hardship. Nigerians have heard your excuses and endured your failed promises. They are ready to judge your record,” Atiku said.

He challenged the President to explain what would happen after the discount expired and whether transport fares and the cost of moving agricultural produce and running businesses would actually fall.

“When I proposed targeted support to ease fuel costs, you called me ignorant of economic policy. Your government said it could not be done. Now, in a desperate and clumsy retreat, you have shamelessly embraced the principle you mocked. You owe me an apology,” he said.

Atiku said his proposal would support petroleum products refined in Nigeria and sold locally, with government assistance capped, budgeted and independently audited, while excluding imported products.

“My alternative is clear. Support petroleum products actually refined in Nigeria and sold to Nigerians. Cap the support. Put it in the budget. Audit it independently. Exclude imports. Show the public what it costs and what they save,” he said.

He also called for measures to make food affordable, restore reliable electricity, create jobs, expand business opportunities and secure roads and farms, arguing that economic recovery must translate into tangible improvements in household welfare.

Turning to the campaign council, Atiku charged members to take the ADC’s message to markets, motor parks, farms, campuses and communities, explain the party’s proposed policies and demonstrate how they would be funded.

He described the 2027 election as a contest over the welfare of Nigerian families and urged eligible voters to mobilise behind the opposition party.

“Another four years of Bola Tinubu means another four years of hunger, hardship and national decline,” he said.

Atiku also demanded electoral reforms to protect votes, including immediate public access to polling-unit results, live broadcasts of state and national collation centres, and independent audits of election technology before and after elections.

He called for an independent commission to investigate and prosecute electoral offences, as well as stronger penalties for vote suppression, result tampering and fraud.

The ADC candidate further accused APC-controlled governments of restricting opposition campaigns, citing an attempt to prevent an opposition candidate from campaigning in Benue State.

“There will be no ‘no-go’ areas in Nigeria. Opposition members are citizens with the constitutional right to move freely, express their views and campaign anywhere in the country,” he said.

He vowed that the ADC would campaign across the country and resist attempts to prevent its candidates from reaching voters, saying the party would defend its rights through lawful means.

In a challenge to Tinubu, Atiku urged the President to resign, arguing that the 30-day petrol discount could not erase the administration’s record on the economy.

“After this latest admission of failure, the honourable thing to do is step down. Nigerians deserve a government that will do the work and make life affordable again,” he said.

World.title: Outrage over plan to livestream US military firing squad execution
World.content:
Condemnation of the Pentagon’s plan to livestream the firing squad execution of a convicted military base mass shooter escalated Friday, with the UN saying it would amount to torture and US lawmakers from both parties slamming the move.

Nidal Hasan’s execution — which is scheduled for December 3 at Fort Hood, Texas, where he gunned down 13 people in 2009 — is set to be the first by US military firing squad since 1945.

Representative Austin Scott, a member of US President Donald Trump’s Republican Party, said he supported executing Hasan but that “livestreaming executions is what jihadists do. America is better than that.”

Senator Jack Reed, the top Democrat on the Senate Armed Services Committee, said broadcasting the execution would be “a barbaric spectacle” that would give Hasan “more attention and more control” and “a global platform to amplify his hateful, anti-American message.”

“This is a gift to anti-American terrorist recruiters,” Reed said.

Trump on Friday backed the execution — saying Hasan “deserves it” and branding him a “maniac” — but did not comment on the plan to publicize it.

A Pentagon official told AFP the previous day that the execution would be streamed live, after US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said “we’ll make sure that people are able to watch it, that it’s public.”

Later, Hegseth wrote “Correct” when retweeting a media report about the planned livestream.

The UN High Commissioner for Human Rights condemned the move, saying in a message sent to AFP on Friday that “the livestreaming of an execution is tantamount to a public execution and would breach the absolute prohibition of torture.”

Archbishop Paul Coakley, president of the US Conference of Catholic Bishops, said it was a “barbaric promotion of a culture of death and must be reconsidered.”

– ‘Compound the cruelty’ –

Hegseth said it would be the military’s first firing squad execution since World War II — a reference to the case of Eddie Slovik, who was put to death for desertion in 1945.

“People need to understand that… there’s serious consequence for these types of things,” Hegseth said in a video disseminated Thursday on official Pentagon X accounts.

“I kind of like the mentality we had in World War II, which was win, which was understand when the enemy attacks you, you need to stand your ground,” Hegseth said.

The last US military execution was carried out in 1961, when John Bennett was hanged for rape and attempted murder.

The Death Penalty Information Center says that 135 soldiers have been executed by the US military since 1916.

According to rights group Amnesty International, at least 17 public executions are known to have been carried out in 2025 — six in Afghanistan and 11 in Iran.

Amnesty’s Justin Mazzola said Friday that the death penalty is “a violation of human rights,” and that streaming Hasan’s execution “would only compound the cruelty.”

Twelve of the 13 people Hasan killed and 30 of those he wounded were soldiers.He was shot and partially paralyzed by a civilian police officer who responded to the attack.

Hasan chose to conduct his own defense during the trial but called no witnesses and gave no testimony, and made no attempt to deny the charges.

He was sentenced to death by a military jury in 2013.

Court-appointed defense attorneys expressed concern that he was seeking execution.

The court that convicted Hasan was told he was opposed to the US military’s occupations of Iraq and Afghanistan, and that he had spoken online with an alleged Al-Qaeda figure, radical cleric Anwar al-Awlaki, an American citizen subsequently killed in a US drone strike in Yemen.

While mass shootings in the United States are common, they are relatively rare at military facilities.

The furor over Hasan’s impending execution comes just days after convicted murderer Christa Pike survived a botched execution in the US state of Tennessee, fueling debate about the death penalty in the country.

World.title: 2027: Sanction Amaechi now; Wike urges INEC
World.content:
…Links FCT NLC chairman to ADC, says teachers’ strike is political blackmail

By Omeiza Ajayi, Abuja

The minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has demanded action from the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC against the African Democratic Congress ADC vice presidential candidate, Rotimi Amaechi, over his remarks about President Bola Tinubu and his supporters.

Wike spoke on Friday in Abuja, shortly after a closed-door meeting with the chairmen of the six Area Councils and security operatives.

He said he had not heard that INEC had drawn Amaechi’s attention to his utterances.

“Many Nigerians have called INEC to sanction political parties and candidates or some politicians who, in their campaigns, incite the public or raise matters that are not issue-based. We have been told to go on campaigns based on issues. What are you going to do about the people attacking personality or insulting individuals? Up till now, I have not heard that INEC has been able to call or draw the attention of the vice presidential candidate of the ADC, Rotimi Amaechi, to this,” the minister said.

He also challenged the media to press the opposition for accountability instead of staying neutral in the face of what he called unsubstantiated insults against the president and his supporters.

Wike raised questions about projects during Amaechi’s time as governor of Rivers State, including a multi-million-dollar hospital, the state monorail, the sale of a state-owned gas turbine and a state-wide fumigation contract.

“I challenge him. Ask him the $10 million you paid to a Cuban company to fumigate Rivers State so there will be no mosquito bite. Up till now, mosquitoes have been biting Rivers people, including myself. Ask him, ‘The ₦68 billion monorail – where is the monorail?’ Ask him, Where is the $308 million with which you sold our gas turbine?” he said.

He warned that continued attacks on the president and his supporters would meet resistance from supporters across the country, particularly in Rivers State, and added that thieves and lunatics will not preside over Nigeria.

“If he continues along this line, it may be difficult for him to campaign in Rivers. And I want somebody to go and write it down. Because we will not take that. We will not,” he said.

On the strike declared by the FCT Chapter of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC), Wike described it as a politically motivated attempt to blackmail the administration. He said the FCT Administration had met all its obligations to local government workers and teachers.

“We want to state categorically and let it be known to the public that this so-called strike declaration is political, and we will not accept it. We will not accept it because there’s no basis for anybody to call for a strike. We don’t have any issue with anybody, either be it the area council, local education, primary authority, or secondary schools; we have no issues,” he said.

He announced the immediate implementation of a “no work, no pay” policy across all Area Councils.

The minister said major education bodies, including the Universal Basic Education Board (UBEB), had explicitly dissociated themselves from the strike because existing agreements were already being carried out.

He said the FCT NLC Chairman, Hon. Stephen Knabayi, was a candidate of the ADC in the last Area Council elections and warned against using industrial action for political gain.

“And you can see his interest trying to see that FCT is in crisis, and then he wants to use it as a political tool that FCT teachers are at home, and nobody is teaching students; how can you now come and vote for a government when the pupils are at home? We cannot accept that blackmail. We won’t accept it.

“I have told everybody, and I have told Labour, ‘Look, if you want to involve yourself in politics, you are free to, but then excuse yourself from the leadership of the union so you don’t politicise it,'” he said.

Wike also ordered a crackdown on unapproved beer parlours along the Guzape-Asokoro axis, directing that they be dismantled before they become security liabilities.

World.title: 2027: ADC campaign dares APC, tells Nigerians to collect PVCs, defend votes
World.content:
By Luminous Jannamike

The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC) has urged Nigerians to collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs), vowing to resist attempts to manipulate the 2027 general election in favour of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC).

The council urged eligible voters not to be discouraged by claims that their votes would not count, insisting that staying away from the polls would only undermine their power to determine who governs them.

In a statement on Friday, the ADC-PCC’s Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, described the narrative of predetermined election results as a ploy to suppress voter turnout, alleging that it was being promoted by APC agents.

“Go and collect your PVC. Your voter’s card is your power and your guarantee that you will vote on January 16, 2027,” Ologbondiyan said.

He accused the APC of seeking to exploit public fears about electoral manipulation because of what he described as its poor performance in government, citing hunger, hardship and insecurity.

“The APC knows it cannot win a free, fair and credible election after plunging Nigerians into hunger, hardship and insecurity. That is why it wants Nigerians to believe that results will be written. It is a lie. The era of writing results in hotel rooms is gone forever,” he said.

Ologbondiyan said the amended Electoral Act, the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS), the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV) and increased political awareness among Nigerians provided safeguards against electoral fraud.

“Every polling unit will be protected. Every vote will be counted, and every vote will count. Nigerians are more determined than ever to take back their country through the ballot,” he said.

The council urged traditional rulers, religious leaders, youth groups, women’s organisations and civil society groups to mobilise eligible Nigerians to collect their PVCs and resist voter apathy.

It also pledged that the ADC, under its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, would deploy polling agents to every polling unit nationwide to monitor the process, protect ballots and challenge attempts to subvert the people’s mandate.

World.title: People Tinubu helped before abandoned him in 2023 – Yilwatda
World.content:
Prof. Nentawe Goshwe Yilwatda, the Minister of Humanitarian Affairs, Disaster Management and Social Development

By Omeiza Ajayi

National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress APC, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, has said that many of the people President Bola Tinubu supported over the years withdrew their backing when he declared his ambition to contest the presidency in 2023.

Yilwatda spoke on Friday at the party’s national secretariat while receiving defectors from opposition parties in Sokoto, Kaduna, Jigawa, Kano and Plateau states.

“People that he has supported all through from the North and South, when he said he wanted to contest, most of them pulled out their support,” he said.

He said Nigerians who had watched Tinubu’s record came out to vote him into office in 2023, notably for his role in the country’s unity and, in his words, for having “defended democracy with his life and his blood.”
