World.title: São Paulo Nightlife Tonight: Simoninha Sings Simonal — October 9, 2026
World.content:
São Paulo · Nightlife

Tonight, Friday 9 October 2026, São Paulo has a Spanish dub and electronic duo at the Cine Joia in Liberdade, Wilson Simoninha singing Simonal at the Sesc Belenzinho and a stand-up night in Cerqueira César. There is a 49 per cent chance of rain at 6 p.m., easing to 8 per cent by 10 p.m. Most paid tickets run from R$30 (about US$6) to R$160 (about US$32). All times are São Paulo time.

Tonight at a Glance — Date Friday, 9 October 2026. The start of the weekend in São Paulo. All times São Paulo time (UTC-3).

— Weather Showers early, drier later. Open-Meteo shows 21.3°C (70°F) to 22.4°C (72°F), with a 49 per cent chance of rain at 6 p.m., 23 per cent at 8 p.m. and 8 per cent from 10 p.m.

— Top pick Wilson Simoninha, “Alegria, Alegria”, at the Sesc Belenzinho at 8 p.m. A show of Wilson Simonal’s repertoire, with tickets from R$30 (about US$6).

— Neighborhood in focus Liberdade and Belenzinho. The Cine Joia sits on Praça Carlos Gomes in Liberdade, next to the Metro, and the Sesc Belenzinho is in the east zone.

— Entry prices R$30 half-price ticket (about US$6) to R$160 for a floor ticket (about US$32), plus service fees. Rate: US$1 = R$5.02 (RT, 9 October).

— Safety note Use rideshare or the Metro, keep phones out of sight near crowded exits and avoid walking alone late in Centro and Liberdade after the shows end.

Planning more nights? Read our São Paulo Nightlife Guide 2026, with neighborhoods, costs, safety and how the scene works.

If You Only Go to One Place Wilson Simoninha, “Alegria, Alegria”, Sesc Belenzinho A show of the repertoire of Wilson Simonal plus his own songs, at 8 p.m. It is the best-priced paid ticket of the night, a clear listing and a room built for music. The Sesc limits sales to two tickets per person.

Tonight’s Top 4

1. Wilson Simoninha, “Alegria, Alegria” The singer Wilson Simoninha, son of Wilson Simonal, revisits his father’s hits and his own career at the Sesc Belenzinho, in a show of about 80 minutes. Tonight 8 p.m. The show is for ages 14 and over.

Genre Samba, soul and MPB (Brazilian popular music).

Entry R$60 full price (about US$12), R$30 half price (about US$6) and R$18 for Sesc credential holders (about US$4). A limit of two tickets per person applies.

Address Rua Padre Adelino 1000, Belenzinho.

Verdict The most reliable night out. For foreigners: Sesc is a network of cultural centres with good sound, fair prices and a mixed local crowd.

2. MUCHO! Ciudad Sonora presents Iseo & Dodosound The Spanish duo Iseo & Dodosound bring dub, reggae, electronic music, trip hop and alternative pop to the Cine Joia, a converted cinema in Liberdade. Tonight Doors open at 8 p.m. and the show starts at 10 p.m., according to the Sympla listing. Other listings give different times, so check before you go.

Genre Dub, reggae, electronic and alt-pop.

Entry Full and half-price tickets are on sale on Sympla; the prices were not confirmed.

Address Praça Carlos Gomes 82, Liberdade.

Verdict The best choice for the late slot. For foreigners: Liberdade is São Paulo’s Japanese district and has plenty of restaurants open late, so you can eat before the show.

3. Criss Paiva, stand-up comedy The comedian Criss Paiva performs at the My F Comedy Club, a comedy venue near Avenida Paulista. Tonight Show at 8 p.m.

Genre Stand-up comedy, in Portuguese.

Entry Tickets are sold on Clube do Ingresso. The prices and sold-out status were not confirmed.

Address Alameda Santos 1518, Cerqueira César.

Verdict A good start before dinner on Paulista. For foreigners: the show is in Portuguese, so it suits those who speak the language well.

4. Anirap The rapper Anirap plays at the Carioca Club in Pinheiros. The show is for ages 16 and over (12 to 15 with a guardian). Tonight Doors at 3 p.m. The show time was not confirmed.

Genre Rap.

Entry Third-lot floor ticket R$160 (about US$32) plus a R$24 fee. The third-lot half-price ticket, the second lot and the VIP areas are sold out.

Address Rua Cardeal Arcoverde 2899, Pinheiros.

Verdict The sold-out lots show strong demand. For foreigners: if you want to go, buy the last floor tickets before you travel, and check the start time with the venue.

Also Tonight

— Baile Démodé, Blue Note São Paulo “O Melhor das Love Songs”, 8 p.m. Conjunto Nacional, Avenida Paulista 2073. Prices were not confirmed.

— Tren and Thiago Mendonça, Blue Note São Paulo A tribute to Legião Urbana, 30 years after the death of Renato Russo, 10:30 p.m. Avenida Paulista 2073. Prices were not confirmed.

— Cirque du Soleil, “Alegría”, Villa-Lobos Listed on 9 October by the BaresSP agenda. The time and prices were not confirmed.

The Night in Context

São Paulo’s Friday nights are spread across a very large city. Unlike Rio, where much of the music sits in one district, the choice here is between the Metro-linked centre, the Paulista corridor and the far zones, where the arrocha and pagode crowds go. Plan one area for the evening instead of crossing town.

Tonight’s list runs from a Sesc show at R$30 (about US$6) to a rap show at R$160 (about US$32). The Blue Note SP, the jazz and popular-music club in the Conjunto Nacional building, has two shows tonight, at 8 p.m. and 10:30 p.m. We could not see the clubs’ own agendas for the dance floors in Vila Madalena and Barra Funda, so this list leans towards concerts and shows.

Prices on this page come from ticket sellers on 9 October, and most add a service fee of 10 to 15 per cent. Rain is likeliest early in the evening, so a late start keeps you drier. Check Sympla, Clube do Ingresso or the Sesc site for last-minute changes.

Practical Notes

— Transport The Metro stops at Liberdade (Line 1-Blue) for the Cine Joia and at Faria Lima and Fradique Coutinho (Line 4-Yellow), about 600 metres from the Carioca Club. Late at night, use Uber or 99 and wait inside the venue for the car. Plan the ride home before the show ends, as prices rise.

— Tickets Buy online in advance. Sesc shows sell out and limit tickets per person. Meia (half-price) tickets are for students, seniors and some other groups, and you may need to show proof at the door.

— Safety Keep phones out of sight near the Metro and bus stops, avoid walking alone late in Centro and Liberdade, and use rideshare after midnight.

World.title: Rio de Janeiro Nightlife Tonight: Free Xande de Pilares Samba — October 9, 2026
World.content:
Rio de Janeiro · Nightlife

Tonight, Friday 9 October 2026, Rio de Janeiro has a free Xande de Pilares samba show in Centro, the Zig Festival with Slayyyter in Lapa and the official closing party of the Festival do Rio on Praça Mauá. The weather is dry, around 23°C (73°F), with no rain expected. Tom Zé’s show at the Circo Voador is sold out. All times are Rio de Janeiro time.

Tonight at a Glance — Date Friday, 9 October 2026. The start of the weekend in Rio, with the Festival do Rio film festival in its final days (it runs to 11 October) and several music festivals under way. All times Rio de Janeiro time (UTC-3).

— Weather Dry evening. Open-Meteo shows 22.8°C (73°F) to 23.9°C (75°F) with a 0 per cent chance of rain in every hour from 6 p.m. to 11 p.m.

— Top pick Xande de Pilares at the Palácio Gustavo Capanema in Centro, free, from 8 p.m., part of the Festival Próxima Parada Samba.

— Neighborhood in focus Centro and Lapa. The Capanema palace in Centro, the Fundição Progresso and the Casa Com a Música in Lapa sit within a short ride of each other.

— Entry prices Xande de Pilares is free. Paid tickets tonight run from R$30 (about US$6) to R$350 (about US$70). Rate: US$1 = R$5.02 (RT, 9 October).

— Safety note Centro is busy until the shows end and quiet afterwards. Use a licensed taxi or rideshare for the ride home, keep phones out of sight in crowds and avoid empty side streets after midnight.

Planning more nights? Read our Rio de Janeiro Nightlife Guide 2026, with neighborhoods, costs, safety and how the scene works.

If You Only Go to One Place Xande de Pilares, Palácio Gustavo Capanema, Centro A free samba show at 8 p.m. in one of Rio’s landmark modernist buildings. It is the easiest ticket of the night: no payment, a central location and a famous name in samba. Expect a queue, so arrive early.

Tonight’s Top 5

1. Xande de Pilares (Festival Próxima Parada Samba) Xande de Pilares is one of Rio’s best-known samba singers and a former member of the group Revelação. Tonight he plays a free show in a landmark of modern architecture. Tonight 8 p.m.

Genre Samba.

Entry Free.

Address Rua da Imprensa 16, Centro, Palácio Gustavo Capanema.

Verdict The best-value night in town. For foreigners: free shows draw large local crowds, so arrive well before 8 p.m. and expect to stand.

2. Zig Festival Rio, with Slayyyter The Zig Festival moved from The Home to the Fundição Progresso because of demand. Doors open at 8 p.m. and the programme starts at 9 p.m., with Tom Mauza, INJI, Haute & Freddy and Only Fire. The headliner Slayyyter is due on stage around 2:30 a.m. on Saturday. Tonight Doors 8 p.m., music from 9 p.m. into the early hours

Genre Pop, club and electronic music.

Entry R$350 in the 7th lot (about US$70), according to a local agenda. The organiser’s price was not confirmed.

Address Rua dos Arcos 24, Lapa, Fundição Progresso.

Verdict A long night for dance-music fans. For foreigners: Slayyyter, an American pop artist, plays very late, so plan your ride home for the early hours.

3. Festa BOMA, closing party of the Festival do Rio Elderbrook plays a DJ set with AMÉMÉ, Halfcab, Jackson, Lysia, Escola de Mistérios and OSGÊMEOS at the official closing party of the 28th Festival do Rio, which runs until 11 October. Tonight 10 p.m.

Genre House and electronic.

Entry R$229.50 in the 5th lot (about US$46), according to a local agenda. Sold-out status was not confirmed.

Address Acervo Bar, Edifício Touring, Avenida Rodrigues Alves 10, Praça Mauá.

Verdict The late option in the port area. For foreigners: Praça Mauá is quiet late at night, so book a rideshare home rather than walking.

4. Dorina & Paulão 7 Cordas The singer Dorina and the seven-string guitarist Paulão 7 Cordas play samba and choro at the Palácio da Música in Flamengo. Listed by the La Cumbuca agenda; we could not confirm it with the venue. Tonight 8 p.m.

Genre Samba and choro.

Entry R$60 in advance (about US$12) and R$70 at the door (about US$14), according to the agenda.

Address Rua Buarque de Macedo 87, Flamengo.

Verdict A seated, listening night. For foreigners: choro is Rio’s instrumental chamber music from the 19th century and a good way to hear the roots of samba.

5. Robertinho Silva & Nivaldo Ornellas The drummer Robertinho Silva and the saxophonist Nivaldo Ornellas play together at Casa Com a Música in Lapa. Listed by the La Cumbuca agenda; we could not confirm it with the venue. Tonight 8 p.m.

Genre Instrumental music and jazz.

Entry R$50 (about US$10), according to the agenda.

Address Rua Joaquim Silva 67, Lapa.

Verdict The pick for serious listeners. For foreigners: Lapa is the nightlife district, but this is a quiet room away from the street crowds.

Also Tonight

— Wanda Sá, Cave Music Lounge Bossa nova, 7 p.m., R$70 (about US$14). Subsolo do Quiosque Deseo, Avenida Atlântica, Leme.

— Júlia Borges, Teatro Café Pequeno Bossa nova (Festival Bossa Nova Sessions), 8 p.m., R$50 half-price ticket (about US$10). Avenida Ataulfo de Paiva 269, Leblon.

— Linda Ramalho, Acaso Cultural Live music, 8 p.m., R$60 half-price ticket in sector 1 (about US$12). Rua Vicente de Sousa 16, Botafogo.

— Késia, Dolores Club Live music, 7 p.m., R$30 half-price ticket (about US$6). Rua do Lavradio 10, Centro.

The Night in Context

Fridays in Rio start early. Many of the best shows begin at 7 or 8 p.m. in theatres, cultural centres and small music houses, and the free ones fill up first. The big names sell out in advance: Tom Zé’s “90 anos” show at the Circo Voador in Lapa, at 8 p.m., is sold out.

Tonight’s list shows the range of the scene. Free samba in a modernist palace, a pop festival in Lapa, choro and instrumental jazz in small rooms, bossa nova in the South Zone and a house-music party in the port area all fall on the same evening, for prices from nothing to about US$70. Several festivals overlap this week, among them the Festival do Rio, the Festival Próxima Parada Samba and the Festival Bossa Nova Sessions, which is why Centro is busier than usual.

For a visitor from the United States, the cheapest way to see Rio’s music is the free circuit: the Capanema palace tonight, and the weekly Friday roda de samba at Pedra do Sal in Saúde, which we could not confirm for this date. Prices on this page are from ticket sellers and agendas on 9 October and can change at the door. We could not confirm sold-out status for most paid shows, so check Sympla, Eventim or the venue before you go.

Practical Notes

— Transport The Metro (Line 1) serves Cinelândia and Carioca in Centro, and Catete in the South Zone. Lapa and the Fundição Progresso are a short walk from Cinelândia. Late at night, use Uber or 99 and wait inside the venue for the car. Lapa and Praça Mauá are best reached by rideshare after 11 p.m.

— Tickets Check the Capanema palace’s rules for the free show before you go. For paid shows, buy online through the venue’s ticket seller and bring an ID. Many venues give half-price (meia) tickets only to students and seniors.

— Safety Keep phones out of sight at crowded exits, avoid empty streets in Centro and the port area late, and use the venue’s rideshare pick-up point.

World.title: Hungry burglars break into Kings Korner for 12 whole chickens, microwave, rice cooker, pressure cooker, containers and seasonings
World.content:
Hungry burglars break into Kings Korner for 12 whole chickens, microwave, rice cooker, pressure cooker, containers and seasonings

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Some apparently hungry burglars targeted Kings Korner, a business located at the corner of Central American Boulevard and Nargusta Street in Belize City, making off with just about everything needed to cook a slew of nice meals, including containers to store the leftovers. The thieves stole kitchen appliances, food supplies and other items valued at almost $1,000.

The 45-year-old store owner reported that she secured the establishment around 1:30 p.m. on Monday, October 5, before leaving for work elsewhere.

When she returned the following morning, she discovered that a wooden door and burglar-bar lock had been damaged.

The stolen items included a microwave, rice cooker, Instant Pot, storage container, 12 whole chickens and assorted seasonings.

The total estimated value of the stolen property is $977. Police are investigating the burglary.

World.title: Cabinet approves Belize’s participation in Global Initiative on International Humanitarian Law
World.content:
Cabinet approves Belize’s participation in Global Initiative on International Humanitarian Law

By Zoila Palma: Cabinet has approved Belize’s participation in the Global Initiative to Galvanize Political Commitment to International Humanitarian Law, reaffirming the country’s commitment to international law and humanitarian principles. The decision reflects Belize’s stated foreign policy objectives and priorities, according to the Cabinet’s announcement.

Belize’s participation aligns with its position on international law and the principles outlined in the United Nations Charter.

Cabinet noted that joining the initiative will further demonstrate Belize’s commitment to upholding international legal standards and strengthen its credibility as a supporter of international law.

World.title: Cabinet endorses $4.7 million financing mechanism for Rural Electrification in Southern Belize
World.content:
Cabinet endorses $4.7 million financing mechanism for Rural Electrification in Southern Belize

By Zoila Palma: Cabinet has endorsed the use of retroactive financing through the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB) to support a rural electrification programme aimed at expanding access to electricity in underserved communities in Southern Belize.

The decision was made during Cabinet’s meeting on October 6, 2026. Under the mechanism, the Government of Belize can self-finance up to US$4.7 million in project costs, which would subsequently be reimbursed under the loan.

The programme aims to provide sustainable, reliable and modern electricity to unserved and underserved rural and Indigenous communities, improving access to essential services and supporting development in Southern Belize.

World.title: $25,000 Lincoln MKX stolen from outside Belize City home
World.content:
$25,000 Lincoln MKX stolen from outside Belize City home

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police are investigating the theft of a luxury SUV valued at $25,000 that disappeared from outside a residence on Spain Avenue in Belize City.

A 54-year-old businessman reported that his black 2014 Lincoln MKX was stolen on Wednesday, October 7.

According to police, the vehicle owner’s 21-year-old son left home around 4:10 p.m. and discovered the vehicle missing when he returned at approximately 5:20 p.m.

The SUV, bearing Belize City licence plate BCC-75918, had been parked directly in front of the family residence.

Police have reviewed surveillance footage and issued an alert to police formations as investigations continue.

World.title: American boat owner in Hopkins reports two 40HP engines valued at $8,320 stolen
World.content:
American boat owner in Hopkins reports two 40HP engines valued at $8,320 stolen

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police are investigating the theft of two boat engines valued at $8,320 from a vessel docked along the beachfront in southern Hopkins Village.

An American national reported that two 40-horsepower engines were stolen from his 26-foot vessel named Mr. Precision, which had been docked on the southern side of the village.

The boat owner told investigators that the engines had been installed in March 2026 and that he was informed of their disappearance on August 20. Damage was also reportedly caused to the vessel.

Police have processed the scene, obtained purchasing documents and interviewed several people as part of the investigation.

Several persons of interest have been identified, but no charges are indicated in the report.

World.title: Ministry of Public Service extends National Day greetings to Taiwan
World.content:
Ministry of Public Service extends National Day greetings to Taiwan

By Zoila Palma: The Ministry of the Public Service, Disaster Risk Management and Enterprise has extended best wishes to the people of Taiwan on the occasion of the country’s 115th National Day, celebrating the longstanding friendship and partnership between Belize and Taiwan.

In its message, the ministry expressed hopes for continued peace and progress for the Taiwanese people.

Belize and Taiwan maintain diplomatic relations built on cooperation and mutual support in areas including education, healthcare, agriculture, technology and sustainable development.

World.title: Department of Environment takes Enforcement action after Mangroves cleared along Belize River
World.content:
Department of Environment takes Enforcement action after Mangroves cleared along Belize River

By Zoila Palma: The Department of the Environment (DOE), under the Ministry of Sustainable Development and Climate Change, has taken enforcement action following land-clearing activities along the Belize River near Mile 6.5 on the Philip Goldson Highway. The action followed a complaint that prompted a joint inspection by the DOE, Forest Department and Lands and Surveys Department.

The inspection confirmed that approximately 3.78 acres of vegetation had been cleared, including about a quarter-acre of red mangroves removed without the required permit.

The Forest Department has since charged the landowner under the Mangrove Regulations.

The DOE has directed the landowner to undertake immediate riverbank stabilization and restoration measures, construct a properly designed seawall subject to the necessary permits and approvals, and restore mangroves along the affected riverbank in coordination with the Forest Department.

The landowner has also been ordered to cease all further development activities on the property and obtain environmental clearance before undertaking any future development.

World.title: Belize Police Officer awarded Commonwealth scholarship for studies in Scotland
World.content:
Belize Police Officer awarded Commonwealth scholarship for studies in Scotland

By Zoila Palma: The Belize Police Department has congratulated Assistant Superintendent of Police (ASP) Elroy E. Awardo on receiving a Commonwealth Scholarship to pursue a Master of Science (MSc) in International Conflict and Cooperation at the University of Stirling in Scotland.

Awardo currently serves as a Policy, Research and Innovation Analyst in the department’s Standards and Accountability Branch. He also holds a Master’s degree in Defence Analysis and a Postgraduate Diploma in Disaster Risk Management.

Awardo’s research will examine the transition from historical tensions to security cooperation between Belize and Guatemala, particularly following an International Court of Justice (ICJ) ruling on the countries’ border dispute.

His work aims to develop strategies for confidence-building and joint threat management, with a focus on narcotrafficking, cross-border crime and climate change-induced migration.

A key objective of the research is to develop a framework for cooperation among Belize’s national security institutions, including the Belize Police Department, Belize Defence Force, Belize Coast Guard and Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

The Belize Police Department said the academic achievement represents a valuable investment in national and regional security and expressed confidence that Awardo’s studies will contribute to strengthening security cooperation.

World.title: Hope, Rutherford fire West Indies to record T20 chase of 250
World.content:
West Indies Romario Shepherd (left) and captain Shai Hope celebrate after winning the second T20 international cricket match between India and West Indies at the JSCA International Stadium Complex in Ranchi on October 9, 2026. (Photo: AFP)

RANCHI, India (AFP) — Skipper Shai Hope and Sherfane Rutherford struck blazing knocks as the West Indies recorded the second-highest T20 chase of all time on Friday to beat India by six wickets.

After India posted 249-5 batting first, the West Indies rode on a 120-run fourth-wicket partnership between Hope, who hit an unbeaten 102, and Rutherford (84) to achieve the target with nine balls to spare in Ranchi.

Hope completed the win with the ninth six of his innings and one that brought up his century off 45 balls, as the West Indies bounced back to level the five-match series at 1-1.

“When you chase here in India, you always give yourself a chance,” said Hope.

“You always think you’re in the game, regardless of what score is on the board. But (from) 5-2 was always going to be challenging.”

South Africa hold the record for the highest successful run chase in men’s T20 cricket, scoring 259-4 against the West Indies in Centurion in 2023.

West Indies’ previous best chase was when they overhauled 231 by South Africa in Johannesburg in 2015.

Hope and the left-handed Rutherford led an aggressive counter-attack after joining forces with the West Indies 58-3.

Rutherford reached his fifty off 24 balls and kept up the charge before falling to left-arm wrist-spinner Kuldeep Yadav.

He hit seven fours and seven sixes in his 37-ball blitz.

Hope, who struck his second T20 ton, stood firm and put on an unbeaten stand of 74 with Romario Shepherd, who hit 34.

Rutherford later called Hope a “phenomenal player” and one who “inspires” him.

Indian speedster Mayank Yadav struck in the opening over with two successive wickets, including removing Shimron Hetmyer for a first-ball duck.

Yadav also bowled Rovman Powell for 24 with a delivery that clocked 150 km/h (93 mph), but Hope and Rutherford turned the match in the West Indies’ favour.

Earlier, Sanju Samson made 82 off 41 balls before skipper Shreyas Iyer and Tilak Varma powered India to an imposing total after being asked to bat first.

Iyer said dew played a major part in the West Indies chase.

“The margin of error on this wicket was very minor. Any minor error was going into the stands,” he said.

Samson and Ishan Kishan (43) put on 97 runs for the second wicket after swashbuckling opener Abhishek Sharma departed for 20.

Spinner Roston Chase struck the first blow and then delivered two more — bowling Kishan and Shivam Dube — to check India’s surge.

Pace bowler Shamar Springer dismissed Samson but Iyer and Varma bludgeoned 83 runs off 33 balls for the fifth wicket.

Iyer fell to the penultimate ball of the innings after a rapid 40 off 18 balls while Varma finished unbeaten with 44 in equally quick time.

The third match is on Sunday in Indore.

World.title: JPS says power restored after outage impacts several parishes
World.content:
A Jamaica Public Service (JPS) technician on the job. (File photo)

Jamaica Public Service Company (JPS) is advising that all customers have been restored with electricity following service disruption across several parishes on Friday morning.

The electricity provider said the outage was due to transient trips on the transmission network which also impacted generating units. Adverse weather conditions were being experienced at the time of the trips, JPS said in a release.

All customers were restored by 11:34am following the system disturbance at 10:14am. The cause of the event is being further investigated, JPS said.

Among the parishes impacted, based on reports reaching Observer Online, were Kingston, St Andrew, Manchester, Clarendon and St James.

World.title: WATCH: Tile City launches $290m showroom on Constant Spring Road
World.content:
Tile City and Home Centre launched its state-of-the-art Signature Showroom on Constant Spring Road in St Andrew on Thursday, bringing an immersive experience that the company says opens the door to a fresh approach to building, renovating and designing spaces.

The company invested approximately $290 million in the 10,000 square foot showroom, including $40 million in a 240 kilowatt solar energy system.

Among the guests at the launch were Minister of Industry, Investment and Commerce Senator Aubyn Hill, as well as Minister of State in the Ministry of Industry, Investment and Commerce, Delano Seiveright.

Seiveright praised Tile City’s growth and the impact the initiative will have on the Jamaican economy.

“I am very proud of Tile City and Home Centre, they have been around for 27 years, they started off with two containers and here there are now with this massive showroom,” Seiveright said. “We are excited about it, they have created jobs, they have created opportunities and their reach spreads throughout the entire Jamaican economy.”

According to the company, the grand opening celebrates more than a new space, noting that it represents a renewed commitment to inspiring creativity, making quality design more accessible and helping Jamaicans bring their visions for their homes and projects to life.

(Video by Llewellyn Wynter)

World.title: ‘Just know it wasn’t me’: Cardi B addresses cancelled BZR WKND performance
World.content:
Cardi B performs during halftime during Game Three of the 2026 NBA Finals between the San Antonio Spurs and the New York Knicks on June 8, 2026 at Madison Square Garden in New York, New York. (Photo: AFP)

American rapper Cardi B has broken her silence following the cancellation of her highly anticipated performance at BZR WKND in Jamaica, apologising to disappointed fans while insisting that the circumstances surrounding her withdrawal were beyond her control.

In a video message shared on Friday morning, the Bodak Yellow hitmaker said she had initially intended to let the official cancellation statement speak for itself but felt compelled to address the situation amid speculation about the reason for her withdrawal.

“Good morning, I wasn’t really gonna address this because I felt like the statement was enough, but clearly it wasn’t. First things first, I want to really, really apologise to Jamaica and to my Jamaican fans. The reason why I cancelled so late is because when I say I tried my best and I waited and I waited and I waited for things to get in place and together, but it didn’t,” she said.

The Grammy-winning artiste explained that she had been looking forward to visiting the island, particularly as the trip coincided with her birthday celebrations. She revealed that she had made arrangements to extend her stay in Jamaica for a vacation with friends and family following the performance.

“I’m actually sad that I’m not able to go to Jamaica because this weekend is my birthday weekend. So I made plans for next weekend cause after my performance, I was planning to vacation with my friends and my family members for a couple of more days after my performance, which clearly that’s not happening,” she continued.

Cardi B also dismissed speculation that poor ticket sales had prompted the cancellation, claiming that more than 18,000 tickets had been sold for the event.

“For the haters, not the Jamaicans, but for the haters talking about due to low ticket sales, it was never that because I heard there was over 18,000 tickets sold and not only that, but it’s like be for real I’m Cardi B. I’ve done sold out in Saudi Arabia, in Thailand, everywhere around the world and not only was Jamaica was going to pop out for Cardi B, you have people from different Caribbean islands that were going, from The Bahamas to the Dominican Republic to St Lucia…Everybody was going to come see me.”

While the rapper stopped short of revealing the specific issues that led to her withdrawal, she suggested that contractual restrictions prevented her from disclosing further details.

“However, I can’t talk. I can’t talk…contracts, but just know it wasn’t me. Just know. And I’m sorry. I tried my best. I waited this long because I was trying to give chances over and over and over and over and over and over and over again and things didn’t meet to the point that it’s like, it would have just, it’s just, oh, I don’t want to say much,” she said.

Despite the setback, Cardi B expressed hope that she would eventually get the opportunity to perform for her Jamaican fans.

“Just know that I’m sorry. And I really, really, really wish that I could come and perform in Jamaica one day because I really love you guys. I have an amazing fan base out there and I’m sorry. And I love you and sh*t is beyond my hands. I promise y’all,” she ended the video saying.

News of the American rapper’s withdrawal broke on Thursday afternoon, just over a week before her scheduled October 18 performance at the National Stadium in Kingston.

Cardi B had been announced as the headline act for BZR WKND, which is scheduled to run from October 16 to 18.
