World.title: CNN, MS Now, Politico urge judge to extend White House access
World.content:
Washington – CNN, MS NOW and Politico urged a federal judge on Thursday to extend White House access to the three media outlets which President Donald Trump is seeking to ban.

District Judge Timothy Kelly prolonged until Tuesday the temporary White House access he granted to the news organizations last month and said he expected to issue a ruling by then.

Trump barred CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House on September 18 for distributing what he called “fake news” and “fiction and lies.”

The three outlets filed a joint lawsuit asking for a temporary restraining order (TRO) against the ban on the grounds that it violates the First Amendment of the US Constitution, which upholds the right to a free press.

CNN, MS NOW and Politico appeared in a downtown Washington court on Thursday to ask that the judge transform his TRO into a preliminary injunction prohibiting Trump from barring them from the White House while the case proceeds.

Theodore Boutrous, a lawyer for the media outlets, said Trump issued the ban “because of what he perceives as negative, false, bad, not positive enough reporting.”

The Republican president, Boutrous said, apparently “got up on the wrong side of the bed and declared a ban on these news organizations.”

“He doesn’t like scrutiny of his policies. He doesn’t like the reporting. He wants more good press,” he said. “If your press pass is at risk because President Trump decides something you said is false, that’s a very, very dangerous, chilling doctrine.”

Justice Department attorney Michael Velchik, urging the judge to uphold the ban, accused CNN, MS NOW and Politico of violating “journalistic standards” and endangering national security by revealing classified information.

A skeptical Kelly asked Velchik whether it was a “a violation of minimum journalistic standards to portray the administration in a negative light?”

In his ruling last month temporarily restoring the White House credentials of CNN, MS NOW and Politico, the judge, who was appointed by Trump during his first term, said the ban “likely violated their constitutional due process rights.”

Trump has long attacked media that have aired critical coverage of him, repeatedly blasting the press as the “enemy of the people.”

Following the judge’s order, CNN, MS NOW and Politico were granted access to the White House grounds and the briefing room but have been kept out of the Oval Office and Air Force One.

In a rare move, the top five US broadcasters — ABC, CBS, CNN, Fox and NBC — halted pool coverage of the White House — where a broadcaster films on behalf of all television outlets for the day — in solidarity with CNN.

World.title: OpenAI says Iran, Russia influence ops busted
World.content:
Washington – OpenAI on Thursday said it shut down two influence operations — from Russia and Iran — that used ChatGPT to push fake journalist personas and run a “think-tank” to covertly peddle anti-Ukraine propaganda.

OpenAI’s report is the latest illustration of how state actors can easily exploit widely available AI tools to peddle sophisticated propaganda against adversaries on a mass scale.

The American AI giant said it banned a cluster of ChatGPT accounts that originated in Russia and Iran and were used to support “false front” entities for geopolitical and conflict-related messaging.

The Iranian operation involved seven “journalist” profiles, each purporting to be from Western countries including the United States, that were used to plant long-form articles in media outlets around the world.

“We identified almost 100 articles published or syndicated under the operation’s bylines across roughly a dozen online outlets around the world,” OpenAI said.

“These were small to medium outlets, generally focused on international affairs, geopolitics, and events in the Middle East.”

The earliest article identified by OpenAI was published in July 2025, and the latest in October 2026, with the frequency of reports increasing after the US-Iran war broke out earlier this year.

The operation also generated social media comments on topics related to the US-Iran war, it added.

One of the personas named Ervin B. Hoskins, whose bio claimed to be “an American freelance writer,” had social media accounts across tech platforms including Elon Musk’s X and Meta-owned Instagram.

X’s transparency information showed the account was connected via a “West Asia android app” and Instagram’s transparency information showed the account was based in Iran, according to screenshots provided by OpenAI.

Both accounts appeared to be suspended.

The Russian operation co-opted “unwitting people” in Latin America to run a “think-tank” — called the Social Research Center (SRC) — used for covert activities aimed at undermining Ukraine’s reputation in the region and to influence local politics, the company said.

“The available evidence indicates that the SRC’s employees in Latin America were not aware that they were working for a Russian group,” OpenAI said.

“The SRC appears to have produced a majority of original content via its co-opted staff. This stands out as the most complex attempt to run a front identity that we’ve disrupted over the past two and a half years.”

SpaceX CEO Elon Musk on Friday fired another salvo over the delay in the commercial rollout of Starlink in India, taking swipe at billionaire Mukesh Ambani once again.In a post on X, Musk addressed the Reliance Industries chairman as âPrime Minister Ambaniâ, alleging that he was the âreal boss of Indiaâ and questioning why Starlink was yet to receive the necessary clearances to begin commercial operations.âDear Prime Minister Ambani, Please accept my humble apologies for not realizing that you are the real boss of India. Naturally, you would prefer to maintain your monopolistic exploitation of the great people of India, but would you nonetheless consider allowing Starlink to compete?â Musk wrote.He argued that Starlink could improve access to the internet in underserved parts of the country, particularly for children seeking educational opportunities and small businesses looking to reach international markets.âThere are many areas of India, as there are in all countries, with no Internet access, which denies children the opportunity for education and for small businesses the opportunity to sell their goods to a global market. Starlink would change their lives for the better. Thank youâ he added.Musk's latest remarks come a day after he accused unnamed Indian business groups of obstructing Starlink's entry to protect their market positions.He had alleged that the company was being blocked by âcertain oligarchsâ seeking to maintain a âmonopolistic chokehold on the Indian peopleâ.The Indian government has rejected the allegations, maintaining that the delay stems from pending regulatory and security requirements rather than preferential treatment for domestic telecom companies.At the India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026 in New Delhi, Union communications minister Jyotiraditya Scindia said India would not permit a monopoly in any sector and that three satellite communication operators had received licences.These include Reliance Jio Satcom, Bharti Airtel-backed Eutelsat OneWeb and Starlink. Amazon's Project Kuiper has also expressed interest in entering the market and will undergo the standard evaluation process.Scindia said the government was finalising the satellite spectrum pricing framework, while security assessments by the Ministry of Home Affairs and other agencies were under way. Commercial operations can begin once the companies meet the prescribed requirements.The government has also said security clearances remain pending for all three licensed operators, rejecting the suggestion that Starlink alone is facing regulatory hurdles.

World.title: 'City can't be brought to a halt': Delhi Police's rationale for restrictions ahead of CJP stir
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

has justified its restrictions on a proposed protest by the Cockroach Janta Party at Jantar Mantar, citing past violence, alleged assaults on women constables and the need to maintain public safety.

The police said the organisers were proceeding without permission and stressed that the temporary curbs were necessary to prevent overcrowding and keep the capital functioning.

In a statement posted on X, the force said, "The right to protest must be protected, but so must the right of a city to function safely. Responsible policing is about balancing both."

The police cited violence during a protest in July to explain its concerns.

According to the statement, permission had been granted for a one-day demonstration, but it continued for a month. More than 200 police personnel were injured, while over 2,000 people with criminal antecedents joined the protest, contributing to the violence.

The police said the situation eventually spiralled out of control, leading to clashes in which students were also injured. It added that women constables had been molested and assaulted by protesters at Jantar Mantar in the past week.





Crowd management and public safety

The police also pointed to the limited capacity of Jantar Mantar, saying the site could accommodate only 1,000 people at a time. It said restrictions were needed to prevent overcrowding and protect protesters, residents, shopkeepers and others in the area.

The force said Delhi Police had to balance the right to protest with the safety of residents and the capital's economic interests. It added that the city could not be brought to a halt every time a demonstration took place.

According to the statement, seeking permission allows authorities to estimate crowd numbers and plan traffic diversions, emergency access and safe movement around the protest site. The police said this would help demonstrators raise their concerns while allowing residents, workers and businesses to continue with their daily activities.

Police cite legal position on unauthorised protests

The police said the Cockroach Janta Party was proceeding with its planned gathering without permission.

Citing the Supreme Court's position, the statement said a protest held without permission was unlawful and participants could face prosecution.

It added that organisers were responsible for explaining the legal position to those they invited to attend.

"The restrictions being put in place today are temporary. They are intended to regulate the flow of people, prevent overcrowding and keep protesters, residents, shopkeepers and others in the area safe," the statement read.

The police said the precautions were intended to ensure that people could raise their concerns peacefully without compromising public safety or disrupting the functioning of the city.

World.title: 'Unprecedented security': How Delhi is bracing for October 10 protests against CEC
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Delhi is gearing up for major portests on Saturday as the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) plans to march to Jantar Mantar demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in electoral rolls.

With police refusing permission for the demonstration, authorities have stepped up preventive measures across the national capital to stop protesters from assembling at unauthorised locations.

The security arrangements include the deployment of thousands of police and paramilitary personnel, the temporary suspension of mobile internet services within a four-kilometre radius of the Janpath-Kartavya Path crossing, and restrictions at 57 Delhi Metro stations.

Police have also intensified checks at the city's borders, railway stations, bus terminals, hotels and other sensitive locations amid expectations of a large mobilisation.

Delhi Police expects around 7,000 protesters to arrive in the capital, news agency ANI reported. More than 35,000 police and paramilitary personnel are expected to be deployed, according to sources cited by ANI. More than 120 companies of Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) are also expected to be involved in the security arrangements.





The Delhi Police commissioner has directed personnel to maintain restraint and professionalism, avoid reacting to provocation and prevent unauthorised gatherings. Officials have also been instructed to detain people attempting to stage demonstrations, regardless of their location.

Why Delhi Police denied permission

Joint Commissioner of Police Nupur Prasad said on Friday that permission had been denied for the October 10 demonstration, citing the short notice given for the event and concerns over compliance with directions during an earlier protest.

The application was submitted on October 7, just three days before the proposed gathering. Police said applications for such demonstrations must be submitted at least 10 days in advance. Authorities also cited concerns arising from the conduct of an earlier demonstration in July.

Despite the denial, CJP's Abhijeet Dipke reiterated that the organisation would proceed with its planned protest at Jantar Mantar.

Several student outfits and political groups are also expected to join the mobilisation.

AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal appealed to people across the country to participate, accusing the BJP-led government at the Centre of undermining democracy through alleged manipulation of electoral rolls.

"I appeal to all the people across the entire country that the way the BJP government at the Centre is playing with our democracy, people's votes are being deleted on a mass scale.

Those who don't vote for the BJP have their votes deleted, while fake votes are added. This was happening openly under Gyanesh Kumar,â Kejriwal told reporters.

Internet blackout, metro restrictions and border checks

The Union home secretary has authorised the temporary suspension of all mobile internet services within a four-kilometre radius of the Janpath-Kartavya Path crossing, from 10pm on October 9 to 10pm on October 10. The restriction covers all mobile internet technologies, while services elsewhere in Delhi are expected to remain unaffected.

Entry and exit gates at 57 metro stations will remain closed from 9pm on Friday until further notice. Interchange facilities will continue at affected stations, except New Delhi metro station. Among the stations affected are Rajiv Chowk, Central Secretariat, Patel Chowk, Kashmere Gate, Janpath, Mandi House, ITO and Supreme Court.

Several train services scheduled to arrive at or depart from New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin railway stations between 4am and 2pm on Saturday have also been reported cancelled.

Other preventive measures include:

Deployment across Central Delhi: The New Delhi district has been divided into 20 zones, each to be monitored by senior police officers. Additional women personnel from Uttar Pradesh and Haryana have also been called in.

Surveillance and monitoring: Police will use facial recognition systems, additional CCTV cameras, rooftop spotters and drones. More than 200 content creators are reportedly under scrutiny over online mobilisation linked to the protest.

Checks across the capital: Police have stepped up surveillance at borders, hotels, guest houses, railway stations, bus terminals and airport approach roads. Vehicle restrictions in New Delhi may also be imposed depending on the security assessment.

Detention arrangements: Six designated centres, including Chhatrasal Stadium, Rajiv Gandhi Stadium and Yamuna Sports Complex, have been identified to hold detained protesters.

Liquor shops across Delhi have also been ordered to remain closed on October 9 and 10 as a preventive measure.

Police told to exercise restraint

During a briefing, the police commissioner instructed personnel not to react to provocative behaviour or engage in unnecessary verbal confrontations. Officials were also warned against situations in which their interactions with protesters could be recorded and circulated online.

CAPF units have been instructed not to issue weapons for the deployment, with letters sent to the concerned directorates regarding the arrangements.

World.title: Nagaland explores long term partnership to boost learning in Government schools
World.content:
Nagaland is teaming up with both Indian and German philanthropic groups to improve the quality of education in its government schools.

Five-year roadmap to improve teaching standards

Focus on learning outcomes and fund utilisation

Wider support beyond financial assistance

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Corporate investment and local employment

Nagaland is exploring a long-term partnership with Indian and German philanthropic organisations to improve learning outcomes in government schools and ensure more effective utilisation of education funds, Advisor for School Education Kekhrielhoulie Yhome said.The planned project comes after talks between the state government and a team headed by Martin Kasper, president of the Childaid Network Foundation in Germany, and Nikunj Jhaveri, president of the Rotary Club of the Queen's Necklace, Mumbai, which held on October 5, Yhome told reporters.Kasper said the proposed collaboration could run for at least five years, with a roadmap to be developed to enhance teaching quality and student performance.The planned interventions would cover teacher training, digital infrastructure, early childhood education, vocational skills, and project-based learning, while strengthening existing government systems, Yhome said.Yhome said, Nagaland spends around 8.3 to 8.7 per cent of its budget on education but acknowledged that public resources could be utilised more effectively.The state government was examining gaps in the education system and would assess potential interventions over the coming months, he added.Highlighting the challenges, Kasper said fewer than half of the students in Nagaland's government school system passed the Class 10 examinations. He stressed the need to improve learning outcomes despite progress in school infrastructure and enrolment.Childaid Network spends around 2 million to 3 million euros annually on education and operates across approximately 1,500 project locations in the Northeast, Kasper said.The initiative would focus on government schools, with assistance extending beyond funding to knowledge-sharing, networking and monitoring, Jhaveri said.He added that the partnership would bring together Rotary, Childaid Network and local organisations, including Mantra for Change, ShikshaLokam and Elevate.The collaboration would also seek to connect Nagaland with corporate-sector networks and investment opportunities, Jhaveri said.Kasper said the long-term vision was to encourage companies to establish centres in Kohima and Dimapur, generating local employment and enabling young people from Nagaland to work in their home state instead of migrating elsewhere.According to news agency PTI, he clarified that Childaid Network was a private non-governmental organisation, although the German government also contributed funding to its programmes.The proposed initiative would complement existing government efforts rather than create parallel systems, he added.

World.title: Eggs an affordable source of nutrition, says MP on World Egg Day

World.title: Delhi braces for CJP protest: 45 metro stations shut, trains cancelled, 23,000 security personnel deployed
World.content:
Ahead of the massive protest by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) alongside student organisations, social activists and farmer organisations on Saturday (October 10, 2026), authorities have clamped down with strict security measures and traffic restrictions across New Delhi.

The CJP, led by founder Abhijeet Dipke, along with other student bodies such as All India Students Association (AISA) and AISF, announced a nationwide march to Jantar Mantar demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the complete rollback of Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

Protestors allege that the SIR exercise is being misused to tamper with voter lists by deleting genuine voters, misclassifying living citizens as deceased despite producing Aadhaar, PAN and other valid documents to establish that they were alive and altering key registration documents like Form 6 without consent.

45 metro stations closed

In response to the protests, several restrictions on transit have been implemented across the national capital. The Delhi Police have also proposed closing entry and exit gates at dozens of metro stations and reducing train frequency, citing the likelihood of “unruly crowd movement towards sensitive locations”.

Major transit hubs such as Janpath, Patel Chowk, Central Secretariat, Rajiv Chowk, Mandi House, Kashmere Gate, Hauz Khas, and Supreme Court are among the closed locations.

Trains cancelled and diverted

Similarly, railway zones across the country, including Western Railway, Central Railway, Northern Railway and North-Western Railway, have cancelled or rescheduled over 200 trains coming into or originating from Delhi citing severe road traffic congestion around New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin railway stations.

Western Railway rescheduled the Mumbai Central–New Delhi Rajdhani Express (12951) and August Kranti Rajdhani Express (12953) by five hours, while cancelling services like the Bandra Terminus–Hazrat Nizamuddin Express (12247), Dr. Ambedkar Nagar–New Delhi Express (20155), Indore–Hazrat Nizamuddin Express (09309), Indore–New Delhi Express (12415), and Sabarmati–New Delhi Express (12957). Central Railway cancelled the CSMT–Hazrat Nizamuddin Rajdhani Express (22221) and CSMT–New Delhi Rajdhani Express (22209. The North Western Railway on Friday (October 9) cancelled 13 train services scheduled to depart for the national capital on October 9 and 10, citing “operational reasons”. Meanwhile, the Jammu railway division on Friday announced the cancellation of four key trains heading to the national capital, including the superfast Rajdhani Express.

This includes 75 Mail/Express including Rajdhani, Tejas, Shatabdi, and 170 passenger trains.

Railways has set up dedicated helpdesks and officials clarified that passengers with valid, verified train tickets will be allowed access to stations.

23,000 security personnel deployed

The Ministry of Home Affairs has provided the Delhi Police with additional companies of Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) to strengthen security arrangements in view of the proposed protest and other potential gatherings in the national capital.

According to sources, around 23,000 security personnel are expected to be deployed across Delhi between October 8, 2026 and October 12, 2026.

The New Delhi area is expected to witness extensive security deployment on October 10, 2026, with multi-layered barricading, CCTV surveillance and Facial Recognition System (FRS)-enabled cameras being used to monitor movement.

Strict vigil will be maintained at Delhi’s borders, railway stations and bus terminals. Security agencies are also keeping a special watch to prevent criminal elements from entering protest gatherings by posing as protesters, sources said.

Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) is in force, and gatherings in violation of the restrictions will not be permitted.

Depending on the situation, police may also regulate access to metro stations and markets in the New Delhi area.

Security agencies are maintaining close coordination and monitoring developments ahead of October 10 to prevent any law-and-order situation in the national capital, sources said.

Other closures: schools, colleges, liquor shops shut

The Delhi government ordered all retail liquor vendors to remain closed on October 9, 2026 and October 10, 2026, citing the prevailing situation and the need to maintain public order. Multiple educational institutions including Sardar Patel Vidyalaya, shifted classes online and postponed scheduled events

Who are joining the CJP protest

Despite the Delhi Police denying permission for the protests, citing past rule violations and short application notice, several civil groups and prominent leaders have shown their interest in participating in the protests.

Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convenor Arvind Kejriwal has announced that his family and he will join the protest at Jantar Mantar. AISA national president and student activist Neha Bora urged participants across the country to hold local sit-ins wherever they are. The demonstration will continue along with the Left student groups, farmers associations and civil rights groups.

CJP leaders including Mr. Dipke, Sayrav Das and Ashutosh Ranka will be leading the agitation.

(With PTI inputs)

World.title: Ahead of CJP protests, Railway Ministry cancels over 200 trains to and from Delhi stations
World.content:
To avoid massive crowds near railway stations, Indian Railways has cancelled 245 trains terminating and originating from Delhi stations ahead of the CJP protest in the national capital. This includes 75 Mail/Express including Rajdhani, Tejas, Shatabdi, and 170 passenger trains.

All Mail and Express trains scheduled to arrive at New Delhi (NDLS) and Hazrat Nizamuddin (NZM) between 4:00 a.m. and 2:00 p.m. on Saturday (October 10, 2026) have been cancelled.

Keep track | CEC row key updates - October 9, 2026

The Railway Ministry, in a letter to all zones, said it ordered these cancellations because of expected severe road traffic congestion. The Railways has ordered the cancellation of trains in anticipation that massive crowds will surround the stations, tied to a nationwide political protest called by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) demanding the resignation of the Chief Election Commissioner.

The Railway Ministry has also said that more than 5,000 passengers missed their trains on October 8 due to severe traffic jams and road blockades caused by political protests in the national capital. Affected passengers missed trains like the Dibrugarh Rajdhani, Mumbai Rajdhani and Vande Bharat trains among others.

The decision covers major trains like the Sealdah–New Delhi Rajdhani Express, CSMT–Hazrat Nizamuddin Rajdhani Express, Ranchi-New Delhi Garibrath Express and Howrah Junction — New Delhi Rajdhani Express- departing from their original stations have been cancelled, according to a public statement issued by CPRO Northern Railways Himanshu Shekhar Upadhyay.

Important Update: Cancellation of Rajdhani Express services from Howrah and Sealdah today (09.10.2026). Please refer to the details below. #EasternRailway #TrainCancellation #RajdhaniExpress #PassengerUpdate https://t.co/6JNTY2ZBG7 — Eastern Railway (@EasternRailway) October 9, 2026

Cancellation of trains has led to inconvenience amongst passengers. For instance, the cancellation of the CSMT - Hazrat Nizammudin Rajdhani Express has impacted close to 1200 passengers. Railway Ministry has also stated that passengers will receive a 100% refund for the cancelled train ticket, and those who had booked tickets from physical counters will have to go back to counters to claim refunds or rebook their tickets.

Affected trains also include two Delhi-bound trains from Indore in Madhya Pradesh — the Indore-Hazrat Nizammudin Express and the Indore-New Delhi Express, and two trains plying from Lucknow to Delhi — Lucknow Mail and Lucknow - New Delhi AC SF Express.

Departures of two trains — Mumbai Central — New Delhi Tejas Rajdhani Express as well as Mumbai Central - Hazrat Nizammudin August Kranti Tejas Rajdhani have been delayed by five hours. These trains will now depart after 9 p.m. from Mumbai on October 9, Ministry of Railways has stated.

Among the trains that are cancelled are Udaipur City – Hazrat Nizamuddin and Shri Ganganagar – Tilak Bridge, which were departing earlier on October 9, and Hazrat Nizamuddin – Udaipur City and Tilak Bridge commuter services linking Sirsa, Bhiwani, and Shri Ganganagar, earlier scheduled for departure on October 10.

“Passengers are highly advised to verify their live train running status via official NTES app platforms before heading out,” railway officials have stated.

World.title: MLA, officials review public grievances in Visakhapatnam
World.content:
North Constituency MLA Vishnu Kumar Raju along with district officials visited Sanjeevayya Colony, Ward 46 on Friday as part of the ‘One Month, One Constituency, Four Visits’ programme to address public grievances.

The team received petitions and reviewed the action taken on earlier complaints. The MLA expressed concern over delays in resolving some grievances, particularly those concerning APEPDCL, and stressed the need for prompt action.

A key intervention concerned a schoolgirl whose father had met with an accident, leaving her family unable to pay her school fees. The MLA contacted the private school and directed its management to issue her Transfer Certificate to facilitate her admission to a government school.

Housing and pension-related issues were also raised. About 1,550 eligible beneficiaries in Tri-Junction Colony would be considered for house-site pattas, subject to verification and completion of prescribed formalities. The programme concluded with the distribution of house-site pattas to eligible beneficiaries.

World.title: CEC row LIVE updates: CJP leaders accuse govt. of imposing Emergency, 'Even if I am detained, the protest should not end', says   Dipke
World.content:
The Supreme Court on Friday (October 9, 2026) said the right to association and to protest peacefully is a fundamental right of every citizen, while reacting to a mention by senior lawyers of the apex court about the unprecedented “shutting down” of the national capital a day ahead of the CJP protests for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar on October 10. Supreme Court directed that there shall be “no complete prohibition” on the movement of metro trains, asking authorities to allow metro and other railway services to operate in a suitably regulated manner ahead of the protests.

Analysis | The Rahul Gandhi show and the Congress’s INDIA bloc dilemma

The Union Home Ministry has directed all States and Union Territories to coordinate with Delhi Police and take preventive measures to stop CJP supporters from mobilising towards the national capital. Citing potential law and order concerns, the MHA flagged intelligence inputs suggesting protesters could attempt to enter Delhi despite the police rejecting the group’s request to hold a gathering, and called for real-time intelligence sharing and strict implementation of preventive measures.

Also read | Opposition leaders ‘pray’ at Rajghat for government to ‘get wisdom’ to remove CEC

The Opposition INDIA bloc on Friday (October 9, 2026) urged President Droupadi Murmu to “repeal” all Assembly elections held over the last two years, saying they have “incontrovertible proof” of “vote chori” (theft). Before their meeting with the President, the Opposition leaders gathered at the central hall of Samvidhan Sadan, where according to sources, Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi claimed that the government is “rattled” and if the Opposition continues its campaign, the government could fall without completing its full term.

World.title: Sribharat urges Gadkari to take up Visakhapatnam Beach Road development
World.content:
Visakhapatnam MP M. Sribharat has urged Union Minister for Road Transport and Highways Nitin Gadkari to take up the development of Beach Road in Visakhapatnam to improve the city’s infrastructure and boost tourism.

Mr. Sribharat met Mr. Gadkari in New Delhi in the presence of Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu and discussed several infrastructure and industrial development proposals concerning Andhra Pradesh.

According to the release issued on Friday, Mr. Sribharat said that the discussions covered the proposed transfer of salt lands under the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT). The MP stressed the importance to facilitate the transfer to promote port-led industrialisation and strengthen Visakhapatnam’s position as a major industrial and commercial hub.

Mr. Sribharat also raised the need to expand export opportunities for key agricultural and marine products from Andhra Pradesh, particularly chillies, tobacco and aquaculture products.

He further discussed the proposed Outer Ring Road (ORR) for Amaravati, the capital city. The proposed iconic bridge associated with the Polavaram Project, both major infrastructure projects important to the State’s long-term development.

World.title: Telangana farmers shift to horticulture crops in Kharif
World.content:
Farmers in Telangana shifted their crop preferences during Kharif 2026, with the area under horticultural crops, particularly flowers, red chilli and other spices, registering significant increases. The shift comes amid concerns over the impact of El Niño on the southwest monsoon, deficient rainfall and irrigation stress.

The area under flower cultivation recorded the highest increase at 198%, followed by other spices at 192% and red chilli at 80%. The area under vegetable cultivation increased by 66%, while turmeric registered a 21% rise. In contrast, the area under fruit cultivation grew by just 1%.

It was learnt that the need to improve supply chain for vegetables export and cold storage units has come for discussion.

Agriculture Minister Tummala Nageswara Rao directed Horticulture Department officials to further encourage farmers to take up horticultural crops and provide them with high-quality seeds for vegetable cultivation. At a meeting held in Hyderabad on Friday , he said officials should work towards exporting vegetables to other States. The need to strengthen the supply chain for vegetable exports and establish cold storage facilities also came up for discussion.

Oil palm cultivation was another focus area. The Minister said some farmers were cultivating cocoa as an intercrop in oil palm plantations and called for the practice to be encouraged to improve farmers’ earnings.

World.title: Karnataka HC notice to govt. on BDA’s plan to construct new building for its headquarters by demolishing existing one
World.content:
The High Court of Karnataka has ordered the issue of notice to the State government and the Bangalore Development Authority (BDA) on a petition challenging the decision of the BDA to demolish its existing headquarters and construct a new building in its place.

A division bench comprising Anu Sivaraman and Justice K.S. Bharath Kumar passed the order on the petition filed by social activists, B.M. Shivakumar and H. Shivaram.

It has been pointed out in the petition that the BDA, in its board meeting held on December 30, 2025, passed a resolution with the board delegating powers to the Chairman and Commissioner for the demolition of the old building and the construction of a new one as part of the BDA’s 50th anniversary celebrations.

It has been contended in the petition that the existing building, which includes the 2004-built ‘Development Bhavan’ annexe, remains functional and has been substantially maintained using public funds.

It further alleges that no structural stability or condition assessment was conducted, no report from the Public Works Department was obtained, and no feasibility study was undertaken to examine whether repair, renovation, or structural strengthening could serve the purpose instead.

Claiming that the BDA is in debt, the petitioners have contended that spending crores of rupees of public money in such a financial situation is not in the public interest. The petitioners have also claimed that the authority has not audited its accounts for over five years and that its accounts have not been placed in the public domain.

Stating that the existing buildings should not be allowed to be demolished without a duly authenticated structural and technical assessment, the petitioners have said that the BDA is proceeding with its plan sans approval from the government.

World.title: Bilawal says PTI hurting itself by not abandoning its 'extremist politics', urges party to change its strategy
World.content:
PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari said on Friday that the PTI’s “extremist politics” were hurting the party itself, calling on it to reconsider its political strategy.

“The PTI is a party that has public supporters, but it keeps disappointing the people because of its decisions and extremist politics,” Bilawal said while addressing an event in Karachi.

“It has no political role in this city or in the federal government, and if it continues with its extremist politics, it will not remain in [power] in the province [Khyber Pakhtunkhwa] either.”

The comments come as the PTI has gone ahead with its long march, aimed to demand the release of jailed party founder and former prime minister Imran Khan, despite warnings from the Centre, which has vowed to prevent any gatherings in Islamabad.

“Instead of fulfilling their responsibilities and taking care of their province and its people, this party is stuck on the politics of hate,” Bilawal said.

He added that a week earlier, the federal government and the entire system had been prepared to impose an emergency in KP. The PPP, he said, had consistently maintained that imposing an emergency or introducing governor’s rule was a constitutional and legal option, but one that should be treated as a “legal atom bomb” and used only as a last resort.

In an apparent reference to talks between the government and opposition, he said, without explicitly naming anyone, that although all political parties including those in the opposition, had reached an agreement, the chief minister of one province had chosen “negative politics” instead of pursuing dialogue.

He said that sometimes “extremist politics” were preferred when one was in opposition, but said that this was ultimately affecting “the country, that province and its people, the youth and most of all the PTI”.

He called on the party to play its role in politics, adding that if it abandoned its current ways he would help to change the “political atmosphere” from Karachi itself. Bilawal said that Karachi had two political powers, the PPP and the PTI.

However, the PTI is fighting with other political parties, the federal government, the judiciary, Parliament and the establishment.

“When this is your politics, then your workers will also be disappointed,” he said. Bilawal said that the PTI had not participated in parliamentary proceedings.

He said after several months, the PML-N had agreed to form a parliamentary committee on electoral reforms.

“But it is expected that those crying the most about rigging … will not become a member of the committee. If you do not participate then how will we stop rigging in the future?” he asked.

Bilawal said that the PPP, from one political party to another, was insisting to the PTI to abandon its “extremist politics”. He said that once that happened, the space for dialogue would open and the party would be able to address its concerns.

“If they are true to their party and to their leader, if the chief minister who is so loud these days is true to Imran Khan, then he will abandon this extremist politics,” he said.

“It is Pakistan’s history; if someone is in jail today, it does not mean they remain there tomorrow,” he said. Bilawal said his father, President Asif Ali Zardari, held the “record” for being jailed the longest.

“If the PTI continues with its extremist politics, then Khan sahib will break Zardari sahib’s record and he will remain a prisoner. If the PTI leaves its extremist politics, then it will be able to achieve its political goals and save its workers from becoming disillusioned. Let’s see if they listen to what I am saying,” he said.

Bilawal said the country’s situation had deteriorated to the point where the public was facing hardships.

“Poverty is increasing to such an extent that the World Bank is now saying that Pakistan is bearing the heaviest burden of poverty and unemployment in the entire region,” Bilawal said.

“We want that whoever is the prime minister, in the federal government should be successful, so that the public gets relief. For creating those conditions, we need political stability, and this is only possible right now if political parties cooperate with each other on the country’s basic issues,” he said.

World.title: Centre done mulling emergency, option to be availed if KP does not cooperate on counter-terrorism: minister
World.content:
Parliamentary Affairs Minister Dr Tariq Fazal Chaudhry said on Friday that the Centre had finished deliberating on the imposition of an emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, warning that a lack of provincial government cooperation on counter-terrorism would lead it to enforce a state of emergency and then eradicate terrorism.

The minister made these remarks on Geo News programme ‘Aaj Shahzeb Khanzada Kay Saath’, during which he also refused to confirm reports that a high-level meeting was expected on Saturday to decide on the imposition of an emergency in KP.

The Centre has warned the PTI-led KP government in recent days of sending it packing through an emergency or governor’s rule as the party goes ahead with a protest march to demand the release of its jailed founder, Imran Khan. Federal ministers have cited the security situation in KP in this connection with the possibility of a state of emergency in the province.

Speaking on the programme, Chaudhry refused to verify that any meeting was taking place for the sake of making a final decision in any regard, noting that meetings took place at the Prime Minister’s House daily.

“The matter of any decisive meeting is not final, nor has it been notified,” he said.

Regarding the reports that the government was considering implementing an emergency in 12 districts, he added, “The reality is that the government has completed its deliberation regarding the implementation of an emergency. Now it is in the hands of the KP government what role it plays in imposing or not imposing an emergency in the province.”

The Centre and law enforcement agencies would end terrorism in KP no matter what, he said, adding that it would be better for the provincial government if they were to cooperate and play a part in this.

“But if they want to remain separate, then our other option is that after imposing an emergency, terrorism be cleaned up completely, terrorists be completely eradicated, and for that Article 232 … is for the whole province, not just 12 districts,” he added.

On the matter of these districts, Chaudhry said that “extraordinary measures are the need of the hour”.

However, when questioned, he categorically stated that the consideration of a state of emergency had “definitively no relation” to the PTI’s ongoing long march. He said that the federal government’s preparations for stopping the march were already complete, saying, “Bigger long marches than the one currently ongoing in KP have been brought to Islamabad, and they were stopped … We know how to deal with a long march. Neither is the long march a threat to us, nor is there any concern about it.”

More to follow

World.title: Govt reduces petrol price by Re0.66 per litre, raises high-speed diesel rate by Re0.52 per litre
World.content:
The government on Friday reduced the price of petrol by Re0.66 per litre, but increased that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Re0.52 per litre.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs398.30 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs396.24 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices are applicable for Oct 10 (Saturday) to Oct 12 (Monday).

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm and fuel allocations for official vehicles has been cut by 50 per cent for three months.

On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices.

Previously, on July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: PTI long march will go beyond Swabi, KP CM tells protesters on way to Charsadda
World.content:
PESHAWAR: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi was leading PTI protesters to Charsadda from Peshawar on sixth day of the party’s protest march that is being carried out to demand the release of jailed PTI founder Imran Khan.

The route plan for the march has undergone multiple changes since its launch on Oct 4. While the party initially vowed to march towards Islamabad, its final destination seemingly remains tentative as the KP CM has yet to announce the plan for the trek after Oct 11, beyond Swabi.

On the way to Charsadda, CM Afridi briefly addressed participants and told them not to worry as “we have to go elsewhere as well after Swabi”.

So far, the march has remained within KP, where the PTI is in power.

The PTI march began after weekend talks with the federal government failed to bridge their differences for multiple reasons , particularly over the counterterrorism policy. The federal ministers have warned the PTI not to lead the march beyond KP, and are also linking differences over the counterterrorism policy with the possibility of an emergency or governor’s rule in KP.

Afridi termed the federal government’s warnings “empty threats” and told the march participants that it “cannot harm the workers after they will cross the province’s boundary”.

Kundi’s challenge

Earlier in the day, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi challenged PTI protesters to dare and cross Swabi, a KP district that borders Punjab’s Attock and which the opposition party in the Centre has announced as the eventual destination of its long march..

Kundi raised doubt on the realisation of the PTI’s plan to reach Swabi on Oct 11.

“They are probably going to Charsadda today, then they might go to Mardan, and after that they might end up reaching Afghanistan through Dir,” he said while addressing a press conference in Peshawar. “Because whenever they turn towards Swabi, their legs start shaking, and their hearts tremble […] If they have any self-respect, reach Swabi tomorrow and cross it, or even step inside it. I will accept that you are a revolutionary party that aims to make a naya (new) Pakistan.”

Continuing to rail against the party, he said senior PTI leaders were “sitting in drawing rooms” in Islamabad while others were in “hiding”.

“They say that they have run successful mobilisation campaigns across Sindh and Punjab; did you see anyone from these provinces on their long march’s truck?” he questioned.

Reacting to the PTI’s claims that KP lawmakers and cabinet members were being “abducted”, Kundi said: “You (KP CM Afridi) should tell who is abducting your ministers as you are the chief executive of the province.

“You cannot protect your ministers, MPAs, and MNAs; how will you protect my people, the province and the nation? This is your position.”

Kundi added that the KP CM and his cabinet should resign on “ethical grounds”.

“They say that the SHOs do not listen to them; if no one listens to you, then why are you sitting [in the government]? Only to make money or for corruption,” he remarked, adding that presently, doctors, teachers, nurses, and municipal officers were observing strikes in KP.

The KP governor vowed that “we will protect our province and fight against terrorism on the front line. We will show such incompetent people […] how a province is run.”

Answering a question, Kundi contended that no province could run without the Centre. “But these people talk about confrontation with the federal government,” he said.

On the possibility of governor’s rule or an emergency in KP, the governor said that when the president or the prime minister deems that the situation in the province has worsened to the extent that these options should be availed, they would make a decision.

“Whenever the federal government will seek report on province’s situation; we will provide as per the information we have,” he added.

In response to another question, Kundi took a jibe at the PTI, saying the party had turned its long march into “Lucky Irani Circus, travelling from city to city […] But whenever they turn to Swabi, they opt to take a U-turn”.

He also commented on his recent meeting with KP’s chief secretary and inspector general (IG) to discuss the province’s law and order situation.

The KP CM has taken strong exception to the meeting and called for legislation to provide for the governor’s impeachment for “violating the Constitution”.

Kundi defended the meeting, saying: “I called the chief secretary and IG because we have no government on the ground in the province; they are busy in their circus.”

“My province is burning,” he continued, citing recent incidents of terrorism in KP.

“They (PTI) have never condemned terrorism. They cannot challenge the terrorists […] They don’t have any plan to fight terrorism,” he claimed.

He added that “terrorism is our red line,”, adding, “We cannot hand over this province to terrorists. This is our point agenda […] we will first talk about terrorism, and other things will follow.”

World.title: Sahibzada Farhan hits dazzling 89 as Pakistan down Sri Lanka in first T20I
World.content:
Sahibzada Farhan marked his first match as Pakistan’s full-time Twenty20 International captain with a commanding 89 as the hosts chased down Sri Lanka’s 182-8 to secure a four-wicket victory with seven balls to spare in the opening match of the three-game series at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on Friday.

Farhan struck 10 fours and four sixes in his 53-ball knock, while Maaz Sadaqat smashed a maiden T20I half-century to put Pakistan firmly on course for victory. Their 92-run second-wicket partnership proved decisive as Pakistan reached 187-6 in 18.5 overs.

The hosts made a flying start to the 183-run chase, with Farhan and Fakhar Zaman adding 54 for the opening wicket. Fakhar struck four boundaries in his 13-ball 21 before falling to Eshan Malinga in the final over of the powerplay, by which time Pakistan had raced to 70-1.

Maaz immediately maintained the momentum, taking advantage of loose deliveries to punish the Sri Lankan bowlers. He swept Maheesh Theekshana past fine leg for four before Farhan launched the spinner for six as Pakistan crossed the 100-run mark in the 10th over.

The left-hander continued to attack, smashing Dunith Wellalage over long-on for six before Farhan brought up his half-century off 33 balls. Maaz reached his maiden T20I fifty off just 21 deliveries in the 13th over, striking four fours and three sixes in an innings that gave Pakistan control of the chase.

Farhan then took Theekshana apart in the 14th over, sweeping him over long-on for six before adding two more boundaries. The spinner, however, ended Maaz’s 29-ball knock of 50 by trapping him leg-before, leaving Pakistan at 146-2.

Sri Lanka briefly threatened to turn the contest around as Hasan Nawaz was caught behind off Dushmantha Chameera for one and Theekshana bowled Saim Ayub for eight in successive overs. Pakistan slipped to 156-4, but Farhan remained the key to the chase.

After two quieter overs, the captain attacked Nuwan Thushara in the 18th, striking a boundary through square leg before launching a low full toss over extra cover for six. His innings ended at 89 when he was caught by Sahan Arachchige in the deep off the next delivery, with Pakistan needing just four runs for victory.

Shadab Khan fell for a duck, caught off Malinga, but Khawaja Nafay ensured there was no late drama. He finished unbeaten on 12 off seven balls, including a six over long-on, as Pakistan reached their target in 18.5 overs. Mohammad Imran remained not out on nought.

Earlier, Sri Lanka had posted 182-8 after winning the toss and electing to bat, with Lahiru Udara anchoring the innings through a superb 91 off 55 balls.

The batter struck 11 fours and a six, lifting Sri Lanka from 83-4 after Pakistan’s bowlers had made early inroads. Naseem Shah removed captain Kusal Mendis for one in the opening over, while debutant Mohammad Imran dismissed Kamil Mishara for six.

Udara then joined Kamindu Mendis in a counterattack that brought 60 runs for the third wicket. Kamindu made 23 off 18 balls, hitting four boundaries, before falling to Saim, caught by Fakhar at long-off. Two balls later, Sahan Arachchige departed for one after Shadab took a fine catch at point off Imran.

Undeterred, Udara brought up his maiden T20I half-century off 32 balls and continued to score freely. Dasun Shanaka contributed 18 off 15 balls, including two sixes, before Fakhar caught him off Shadab with Sri Lanka at 140-5.

Udara survived a missed chance on 77 when spinner Abrar Ahmed misjudged a high catch, but his innings ended nine runs short of a century when Naseem had him caught by Hasan at long-on in the final ball of the 19th over.

Naseem finished with 3-36 from four overs, while Imran claimed 2-21. Razaullah took his maiden T20I wicket in the final over, dismissing Theekshana for one, before Dushmantha Chameera struck a boundary off a free hit to help Sri Lanka finish on 182-8.

Despite Udara’s effort, Pakistan’s aggressive top-order batting proved decisive. Farhan’s captain’s knock and Maaz’s rapid half-century gave the hosts a winning start to the series, while Sri Lanka were left to rue their inability to stem the scoring during the middle overs.

World.title: FO says Pakistan has 'substantial number of forces, resources' in Riyadh
World.content:
Foreign Office (FO) spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan said on Friday that Pakistan already had “substantial number” of forces and resources in Riyadh and it was now up to the Makkah Defence Alliance to assess the threat in Saudi Arabia and make decisions accordingly.

The FO spokesperson remarks came in response to a query about the “active support” being offered by Pakistan to Saudi Arabia under the Makkah Defence Alliance amid an escalating conflict between the kingdom and Yemen-based Houthis.

The Makkah Defence Alliance is a tripartite arrangement that includes Turkiye as well. It was signed on Aug 7 and and aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empower its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.

Speaking during a weekly briefing, the FO spokesperson recalled that a joint statement by the three members of the alliance was “very clear in stating that the three countries are united in ensuring deterrence and safeguarding the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia”.

The three countries had decided to contribute and mobilise resources rapidly, he said, adding that Pakistan already had a “substantial number of forces, as well as resources, in Riyadh”.

“It is now up to the organisation to assess the threat perception and operate in accordance with its own mandate,” he said.

The spokesperson went on to say that providing further details on operational matters of the alliance, “including how the situation will be handled, would not be appropriate on my part. It would also be speculative on my part to suggest that certain countries could be involved”.

On the Houthis and escalation of the conflict, he said, “This is a militia that has been involved in such proxy activities and has contributed to regional instability. It has been actively fighting Yemeni forces for quite some time, and access to resources is possible these days. However, at this stage, I would not be able to provide you with specific names”.

Yemen’s civil war has rapidly emerged as the fiercest front in a wider regional conflagration triggered by the US and Israeli attack on Iran that started on February 28.

Saudi Arabia’s civil aviation authority said on Friday that three Saudi nationals ​were killed and several people were injured in ‌two attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on Thursday.

The strikes, which also injured several people, damaged a Saudia Airlines plane and sent smoke billowing over the airport, led many airlines to cancel flights to the Saudi capital days before it is due to host a major meeting of global oil chiefs.

Saudi airstrikes hit Houthi targets in the Yemeni capital Sanaa overnight, Houthi officials and affiliated media said, part of an intensifying air war against the Iran-allied group aimed at reversing its recent territorial ​gains, threats to international shipping, and attacks on the kingdom.

The Yemeni group says it is targeting the kingdom over its support for government forces in Yemen’s reignited civil war. Saudi Arabia says it is backing ​an offensive by ​Yemen’s UN-recognised ⁠government to take back territory from the Houthis.

Pakistan role, as part of the Makkah defence pact, has been a matter of discussion against this backdrop.

While Pakistan has expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia, it has also maintained that the Makkah alliance is intended for collective deterrence and defensive in nature.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday condemned recent Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, reiterating Pakistan’s commitment to the Gulf state’s “sovereignty, territorial integrity and security” under the Makkah Defence Alliance.

A day ago, the Ministry of Information dismissed on Thursday a news report claiming that Pakistan Air Force aircraft were being used against the Yemen’s Houthis as “fake and fabricated”. Earlier this week, the ministry also termed a Reuters report claiming the deployment of 30,000 to 40,000 Pakistani troops in Saudi Arabia as “speculative”.

Nevertheless, on Monday, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye agreed to the deployment of military forces and capabilities rapidly in the kingdom during an emergency meeting of the Makkah Defence Alliance in Riyadh. Monday’s meeting under the alliance was held to address the security developments and threats facing Saudi Arabia.

A statement issued by the Foreign Office after the meeting said the member states had “decided to move immediately to the practical implementation of the collective defence commitments and to take the necessary measures to provide the agreed military forces and capabilities and ensure their rapid deployment in the kingdom, in accordance with the approved arrangements and the national legislation of the parties, thereby enhancing readiness, military integration, and the collective capacity to confront and counter threats”.

Separately, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif, who was part of Pakistan’s delegation in the meeting, joined Geo News programme ‘Aaj Shahzeb Khanzada Kay Saath’ via telephone the same day and said Pakistan and Turkiye, the defence minister replied that both nations had a “presence in theatre”, but only Saudi troops were involved in combat operations.

He also said on Thursday that no stipulation of the Makkah Defence Alliance barred the member states from getting “directly involved” in case of a threat to one of the members.

Moscow Format meeting

The FO spokesperson also addressed the reason for the lack of a joint statement issued after the Moscow Format meeting, saying that it was due to the Afghan Taliban delegation’s departure from its previous position regarding the language on terrorism.

He noted that Pakistan had participated constructively in the meeting and “clearly conveyed its concerns” about terrorism emanating from Afghan territory, underscoring that it posed a serious threat to neighbouring countries.

“As you are aware, these concerns were duly reflected in the joint statement issued at last year’s Moscow Format meeting,” Khan said. “However, this year, the Afghan Taliban delegation did not agree to retain the previously agreed language and departed from its earlier position.”

He added, “We believe that any joint statement that does not adequately reflect this legitimate security concern would not present a fair picture of the ground realities. For Pakistan, this is a substantive security issue, not merely a matter of wording.”

However, the spokesperson highlighted that “the absence of a joint statement should not overshadow the value of regional dialogue”. He added that Pakistan had sufficient time to hold consultations regarding future participation in the Moscow Format, as the next meeting was a year away.

“As I have already mentioned, that is part of our engagement on the issue, and possibly we might continue to participate in the future as well,” he said, although he ruled out making any definitive commitments as “premature”.

New map issued by India

Additionally, the FO rejected the issuance of a new political map by India in which parts of India-occupied Jammu and Kashmir were depicted as a part of Indian territorial jurisdiction, terming it an “act of cartographic aggression” and noting that it did not make India’s occupation legitimate.

“Pakistan categorically rejects India’s latest act of cartographic aggression,” Khan said while answering a question.

He added, “Any motivated and unilateral cartographic exercise is legally void and in clear violation of the relevant United Nations Security Council resolutions. Such illegal actions cannot confer legitimacy on India’s occupation of large parts of Jammu and Kashmir.”

Noting that unilateral action by India could not alter the internationally-recognised disputed status of the region, he further said that these measures could not “prejudice the inalienable right of the Kashmiri people to self-determination”, which should be exercised via a free and impartial plebiscite under UN auspices.

“Instead of resorting to futile cartographic exercises, India must abide by international law, fulfill its obligations under the relevant UN Security Council resolutions, and allow the people of illegally occupied Jammu and Kashmir to exercise their right to self-determination,” the spokesperson added.

World.title: US imposes sanctions on International Criminal Court, hours after Nobel award to former judge
World.content:
The United States on Friday imposed sanctions on the International Criminal Court, vowing to cripple the tribunal’s operations just hours after the Nobel Peace Prize went to a former ICC judge who warned of mounting political attacks on the court.

The move came on the same day the Norwegian Nobel Committee awarded the peace prize to South Africa’s Navi Pillay, an 85-year-old jurist who headed the Rwanda genocide tribunal, served on the ICC and later led a UN commission that accused Israel of genocide in Gaza.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Washington would ban transactions with what he called a “rogue court,” escalating a long-running campaign by President Donald Trump’s administration against the Hague-based tribunal.

“Either the ICC will end its threats, or we will end the ICC,” Rubio said in a statement, claiming that the court wants more power at the expense of American sovereignty.

Rubio’s statement did not mention Pillay or the Nobel award. Instead, he said the sanctions were needed to protect security personnel and elected officials from prosecution by a court the United States has never joined.

“President Trump will never allow the International Criminal Court to prosecute Americans,” Rubio said, adding that the measures would cut off the court’s resources and cripple “its ability to operate”.

The top US diplomat said Washington had, for more than a year, spelt out “basic gestures of good faith” it expected from the court, and had held off on the designation in hopes that the ICC or its member states would change course. He said no “meaningful steps” were taken to address US concerns.

Rubio also called on US allies that belong to the court and “rely on American service members for their defence” to rein it in, warning that otherwise Washington would keep working to dismantle the ICC “brick by brick”.

The Trump administration had previously sanctioned individual ICC officials, including its prosecutor and several judges, over the court’s investigations involving the United States and Israel, which is also not a member.

Trump last month called on all ICC member states to quit the body, denouncing it as “out of control” and a “rogue institution. “

The court, however, rejected the US sanctions as an attack on international law and warned in a statement that “history will judge this moment”.

In a statement, the court called the sanctions “an assault on the rule of law and on the very foundations of the international legal order which strikes at the simple principle that no one stands above the law”.

It added that such actions were aimed at intimidating ICC staff and disrupting its activities, vowing it would not be deterred.

“The Court will continue to fully discharge its mandate, with independence and impartiality, acting only on the basis of the law and the evidence, for the sake of the countless victims of grave crimes,” ICC President Tomoko Akane was quoted as saying.

The statement called on the ICC’s 125 members to side with the institution, saying: “Its fate now rests also in the hands of the states that created it.

“Future generations, and above all the victims of mass atrocities, will ask how we responded when an institution created to protect them came under attack,” said the court.

States, rights groups back ICC

Following the move, several countries and rights groups issued statements condemning US sanctions on the court.

The foreign ministers of Canada, Denmark, France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Japan and the United Kingdom backed the ICC in a joint statement.

“As committed supporters of the ICC, we regret and strongly disagree with the announcement of sanctions to be imposed upon the Court by the United States,” it read.

Meanwhile, Amnesty International slammed the US “attack” on the ICC, calling on countries to “resist” after Washington imposed sanctions on the judicial body.

President Donald Trump’s “sanctions are designed to isolate and ultimately destroy the International Criminal Court,” Amnesty’s Erika Guevara Rosas said in a statement. “This existential attack must fail. States must take concrete action to resist the imposition of these measures.”

UN chief Antonio Guterres condemned Washington’s decision and said he was “deeply alarmed by the expected impact” of the measures.

“Today’s decision marks a serious blow to our collective pursuit of international criminal justice, of which the ICC is a key pillar,” his spokesman Stephane Dujarric told reporters.

“The secretary-general reiterates his unwavering support for the independence of the Court and its officials,” he added.

Similarly, UN human rights chief Volker Turk slammed the new sanctions, saying, “These sanctions — the latest in a series of retaliatory steps against the ICC and its personnel for the work they do every day to advance accountability for the very worst violations of human rights — are unacceptable.”

However, Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten said a six-month pause should be used to pursue negotiations with Washington before the sanctions take effect.

“The announced sanctions by the United States against the ICC are deeply regrettable. At the same time, these sanctions will not take effect immediately. And this is crucial because it provides us vital space for dialogue in the upcoming months,” Jetten told reporters.

World.title: Met Office predicts rain, thunderstorms in upper, central regions from Oct 10-15
World.content:
The Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD) on Friday predicted rain, wind, and thunderstorms, along with isolated hailstorms, in the upper and central parts of the country from the weekend with occasional gaps.

According to a press release issued by the PMD, a westerly wave is likely to enter upper parts of the country from Saturday and is likely to persist till Oct 15.

Under the influence of the weather system, rain-windstorms and thunderstorms with isolated hailstorms are expected in the upper and central regions, including Kashmir, Gilgit-Baltistan (GB), Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Punjab and the Islamabad region.

According to the Met Office, these storms are expected at “isolated places” in Kashmir’s Neelum valley, Muzaffarabad, Rawalakot, Poonch, Hattian, Bagh, Haveli, Sudhanoti, Kotli, Bhimber and Mirpur, as well as GB’s Diamer, Astore, Ghizer, Skardu, Hunza, Gilgit, Ghanche and Shigar, from Oct 10-15 with occasional gaps.

In KP, they are expected in Dir, Chitral, Swat, Kohistan, Shangla, Battagram, Mansehra, Abbottabad, Haripur, Buner, Malakand, Bajaur, Mohmand, Kohat, Peshawar, Charsadda, Nowshera, Mardan, Swabi, Khyber, Orakzai, Kurram, Hangu, Lakki Marwat, Karak, Bannu, Dera Ismail Khan and Waziristan for the same duration.

The PMD forecast the same rain-windstorms, thunderstorms and isolated hailstorms in Islamabad, Rawalpindi, Murree, Galliyat, Attock, Chakwal, Jhelum, Mandi Bahauddin, Gujrat, Gujranwala, Hafizabad, Wazirabad, Lahore, Kasur, Sheikhupura, Sialkot, Narowal Mianwali, Khushab, Bhakkar, Sargodha, Jhang, Toba Tek Singh and Faisalabad from Oct 10-11 and 13-14, with occasional gaps.

It added that they were also expected in Multan, Layyah, Dera Ghazi Khan, Bahawalpur, Bahawalnagar, Sahiwal, Okara, Pakpattan and Khanewal on Oct 10-11 and 13.

The press release forecast “mainly hot and dry weather” in Balochistan, but predicted rain-wind and thunderstorms in isolated places in Zhob, Barkhan and Musakhel on Oct 10-11 and 13.

“Mainly hot and dry weather is likely to continue” in Sindh in the coming days, the PMD added.

The Met Office warned of the potential impacts of the weather system, noting that wind, hail and lightning could damage weak structures such as electric poles, solar panels, and the roofs or walls of kaccha houses during the forecast period. It also warned that hail might damage standing crops in the plains of Punjab and KP.

The PMD also noted the possibility of light snowfall over high mountains and glaciers and added that daytime temperatures were likely to drop by 2-4 degrees Celsius during the forecast period.

“Farmers are advised to manage their crop activities keeping in view the weather conditions,” it said.

The Met Office further advised all concerned authorities to remain vigilant and take necessary measures to avoid any untoward situation during the forecast period.

Earlier this week, heavy rains, strong winds and thunderstorms, with isolated hailstorms, were predicted in the upper parts of the country for Tuesday and Wednesday.

A fresh spell of rain hit the country last month, particularly affecting Rawalpindi as inundated roads and knee-deep water at certain points exposed the city’s poor drainage system.

Islamabad and Rawalpindi received another burst of heavy rain at the end of September, with civic departments in the garrison city placed on high alert.

Earlier that month, KP also witnessed rain as heavy downpours lashed Mohmand, damaging and flooding roads and creating difficulties for residents. Rain coupled with strong winds and dust had also damaged vegetable and maize crops in Bajaur district, but no casualties were reported.
